Vectorization

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses AVX-2 instructions on all Xeon processors that support the AVX-2 instruction set— currently, the Haswell, Broadwell, and Skylake processors.

Machines with older processors continue to use the SSE2 instruction set as before. This change enhances the performance of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on the newer processors for simulations that make use of coupled solvers, though it does not have as much impact on simulations that make use of segregated solvers. You do not need to do anything special to use this feature—Simcenter STAR-CCM+ detects the hardware automatically and runs the appropriate level of vectorization.

What Is Vectorization?

Vectorization refers to the calculation of several arithmetic operations with a single instruction. To illustrate this, consider two vectors of arbitrary length that you wish to sum and store the result in a third vector. Scalar arithmetic (the opposite of vectorization) would add the first element in the first vector to the first element of the second vector and store the result in the first element of the third vector, then repeat the process for the second element, third element, and so on. Vectorization, however, makes it possible for the CPU to add, for example, the first and second element of the first vector to the first and second element of the second vector simultaneously and store the respective results in the first and second elements of the third vector, decreasing the time required for this particular calculation by a factor of 2.

What Are Different Levels of Vectorization, and How Do I Know What I Have?

Vectorization requires hardware support. If your hardware only has the capability to do one calculation at a time, then no amount of software manipulation can obtain any performance benefit from vectorization.

The different levels of available vectorization are as follows:

• SSE2 vectorization has been available since 2001 when Intel released its Pentium 4 processors.

• SSE2 vectorization allows simultaneous arithmetic operations on 2 double-precision floating point numbers or 4 single-precision floating point numbers.

• AVX vectorization was first released by Intel with its Sandy Bridge architecture in 2011 (which means that Sandy Bridge and Ivy Bridge computers are capable of both SSE2 and AVX). This level of vectorization allows simultaneous arithmetic operations on 4 double-precision floating point numbers or 8 single-precision floating point numbers—double what was available with SSE2.

• AVX-2 vectorization was first released by Intel with its Haswell architecture in 2013 (which means that Haswell and Broadwell are capable of all of AVX-2, AVX, and SSE2).

AVX-2 still only allows for 4 double-precision floating point numbers or 8 single-precision floating point numbers—the same as AVX—but it provides extra operations. For example, one new operation that is available in AVX-2 is called fused-multiply-add (or FMA for short). FMA is an instruction that allows the computer to calculate a ⋅b + c in one calculation instead of two (that is, first calculating a ⋅b and then adding c to the result).

How Vectorization Affects Results

Although vectorization does not cause any accuracy issues, it can cause a precision issue. That is, the final results are just as accurate as before, but instead of, for example, a temperature of 300.0001 K, the solver might return 299.9999 K when running with one level of vectorization versus another.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1182

To understand better how vectorization affects results, consider a primary issue with floating-point arithmetic: round-off error. Round-off error can produce a counterintuitive situation in which a + b + c ≠a + b + c . For details on round-off error, see the article on Wikipedia, Floating-point arithmetic > Accuracy problems.

Avoid Using Mixed-Vector Hardware in a Single Parallel Job

You are strongly advised to avoid using a heterogeneous compute cluster with respect to vectorization. That is, do not use a set of resources in which some nodes have AVX-2 capabilities while others do not. Variation in vectorization levels can lead to different round-off errors (as stated above). Moreover, for the same simulation, results computed on nodes with AVX-2 capabilities can be slightly different from those computed on nodes without them.


## References

[12] Wikipedia. [2018.] "Floating-point arithmetic", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floatingpoint_arithmetic.

Running Distributed Parallel Simulations on Multiple Windows Machines

On Windows platforms you can run distributed parallel simulations using cores from multiple machines, in conjunction with Intel MPI and IBM Platform MPI. To do this, use Windows PowerShell to launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ from within a shared directory, which is accessible to all machines that you want to use. You must have read/write access to the shared directory.

On Windows Server 2012 R2 with HPC Pack 2012 R2 or later, MS-MPI is advised. See Using Windows Server 2012 R2 or Later With HPC Pack.

To run distributed parallel simulations on multiple machines:

1. Make sure that your credentials are registered on all machines that you want to use. See Registering Your

Credentials for Distributed Simulations on Windows.

2. Click <Start> and type powershell in the search field.

3. Right-click on Windows PowerShell from the list of search results, and select Run as Administrator. You must have administrator privileges.

The Administrator: Windows PowerShell command prompt appears.

4. Change to the shared working directory:

> cd \\<MACHINE_NAME>\<SHARED_DIR>

5. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

◦ If Simcenter STAR-CCM+ has the same installation path on each machine, enter:

> "<STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR>\starccm+"

◦ If Simcenter STAR-CCM+ has a different installation path on each machine, use the UNC path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ executable:

> \\<MACHINE_NAME>\<STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR>\starccm+

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ GUI appears.

6. Create or load a simulation file as you normally would. See Creating a New Simulation Interactively and Loading an Existing Simulation Interactively.

7. In the Create a New Simulation or Load Simulation dialog, select Parallel on Named Hosts from the Process Options. See Using Parallel on Multiple Host Machines.

8. Enter the host names and the corresponding number of cores to use from each host.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1184

9. To use Intel MPI add -mpi intel and to use IBM Platform MPI add -mpi platform to the Command entry field.

10.If you are opening an existing file, select the file that you want to load.

11.Click OK.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ creates or opens the file, and uses the allocated cores from each machine. The relevant information is displayed in the Output window.

Job Manager

Job Manager allows you to submit simulation jobs on compute clusters directly from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client interface. A system administrator first installs and configures the Job Manager web service on the cluster and thereafter Simcenter STAR-CCM+ can submit jobs to it.

The submission of jobs on a set of compute resources, such as an HPC cluster, usually requires a detailed knowledge of the computing environment. Typically, for cluster runs, you must consider the following aspects:

• What is the path to the application installation directory?

• Which queuing system is installed on the cluster?

• Which MPI options are required?

Additionally, you must take care of the cluster login authentication and the file transfer between your local workstation and the cluster.

With Job Manager installed for your cluster, you do not require expert knowledge of your cluster environment. Job Manager provides an automated approach for user authentication, file transfer, job submission, and resource allocation and management.

Your system administrator installs Job Manager and configures it using the Administrator Web UI. Job Manager is part of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installer and does not require specific licensing. The Administrator Web UI consists of several panels that allow the system administrator to specify the compute resources, generate submission templates, and define user/group permissions.

You connect to Job Manager using the web address (URL) as provided by your system administrator. You authenticate yourself against Job Manager using either your cluster credentials or Job Manager specific credentials.

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you can use Job Manager for the submission of simulation runs and for design runs in Design Manager.

Job Manager supports HTTPS communication for encrypted communication and verification of the identity of the Job Manager server.

Supported Systems

Currently, the installation of Job Manager is only supported on Linux clusters.

The following queuing systems are supported:

• Torque

• Open Grid Engine

• Univa Grid Engine

• PBSPro

• Slurm

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1186

• LSF

Setting Up Job Manager (Admin)

After installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager on the compute cluster, you launch Job Manager from the command line and configure it using the Administrator Web UI.

Note: In the context of setup and troubleshooting of Job Manager, "you" refers to the Job Manager administrator.

To set up Job Manager (as a Job Manager administrator):

1. Launch Job Manager from the command line.

2. Log in to Job Manager using the Administrator Web UI.

3. In the Web UI, create a resource group that represents the compute resources, such as an HPC cluster.

4. Create one or more submission templates that define how jobs are submitted to the resource group.

5. Create user groups and assign specific permissions.

6. Create users and assign them to the user groups.

Defining Resource Groups

A resource group represents a set of compute resources—typically an HPC cluster.

For a new installation with Internal Authentication, you must create a new resource group. For a new installation with OS Authentication, a resource group that represents a Torque cluster is available by default. You can edit this resource group according to your requirements.

To create a resource group for a set of compute resources:

1. On the main administration panel, in the Server Configuration group box, click Resource Groups.

2. In the Resource Groups panel, click New Resource Group.

3. In the New Resource Group panel, set the following properties:

Property Description

Name The name of the resource group.

Resource Type The type of resource represented by the resource group.

The following resource types are available:

◦ Grid Engine Cluster

◦ Torque Cluster (default)

◦ PBSPro Cluster

◦ Slurm Cluster

◦ LSF Cluster

Login Node The host name of the cluster login node that is used for the SSH connection.

System Service The service used to transfer files from/to the login node of the resource group and to execute commands on the login node.

The following system services are available:

◦ SSH without Password—use this option in the following situations:

▪The authentication mode of Job Manager is Internal Authentication

▪SSH with password is prohibited

◦ SSH with Password

Application Launch RSH The remote shell command used to launch applications on the cluster.

If you leave the text-box empty, Job Manager uses ssh by default.

User Directory Template (use $user_name variable to substitute the user name)

The path to the directory on the compute resource where Job Manager stores job-related files.

Examples:

1. /home/$user_name/job_manager_data, where Job Manager substitutes the $user_name variable with the respective login name of the user.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1190

Property Description

2. /$HOME/job_manager_data, where $HOME is substituted with home directory of the user.

For more information, see User Directory.

4. Click Create.

5. To edit the properties of an existing resource group, click next to the resource group entry.

For an installation with OS Authentication, you cannot edit the name of the default resource group—this name is used as reference to the resource group used for authentication in the Job Manager configuration file jobmanager.cfg file. See Installation Guide > Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager > Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager on Linux.

6. To delete a resource group, click next to the resource group entry.

For an installation with OS Authentication, you cannot delete the default resource group.

User Directory

For each user, when running a job, Job Manager stores the job-related files in a user-specific directory on the compute resource.

You can customize the location and name of the user directory in the Job Manager Web UI.

Job Manager creates the following subdirectory structure within the specified user directory:

Directories Description

job_manager_data Job Manager user directory

jobs

[jobID_1]

[jobID_2]

...

Sub-directories associated with each job

Each job sub-directory [jobID_n] contains the following files:

• Submission script

• Job output

tasks

[taskID_1]

[taskID_2]

...

Sub-directories associated with each task

Each task sub-directory [taskID_n] represents the working directory for the task and contains the following files:

• Task input files, such as the reference simulation file and a Java macro file

• Task output files, such as scenes that are written to files

common Job Manager cache directory

When several tasks use the same input file, such as the reference simulation file when running design simulations

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1191

Directories Description

simultaneously in Design Manager, Job Manager first copies the file from the local filesystem to the common directory. The file is then copied from the common directory into the respective task directory. Job Manager uses this procedure to avoid repeated uploads of the same file.

Creating Submission Templates

A submission template specifies the complete set of commands that are required to submit a job to a resource group. You can create multiple submission templates for a resource group, for example to allow users to choose from different versions of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ or from multiple cluster manager queues.

Job Manager uses submission templates to generate a submission script for your queuing system—Torque, Grid Engine, PBSPro, Slurm, or LSF. The submission script reflects the settings that you specify in the submission template panel. Submission template variables of the form $jm_<variable name> are replaced with job and system properties specific to the queuing system. The syntax of the script depends on the specified interpreter, such as bash or tcsh, and includes pre-processing directives that act as parameters for the queuing system. Be aware that:

• The syntax of the pre-processing directives are specific to the queuing system.

• The pre-processing directives are processed during job submission, not at execution time.

The submission script reflects the resource request from Job Manager. However, the exact number of resources allocated for a job may be greater than the number requested in order to satisfy constraints from the queuing system.

If required, you can customize submission templates according to your needs—see Customizing Submission Templates.

To create a submission template:

1. On the main administration panel, in the Server Configuration group box, click Submission Templates.

2. In the Submission Templates panel, click New Submission Template.

3. In the New Submission Template panel, set the following properties:

Property Description

Name The name of the submission template as it appears in the drop-down menu of the Submission Template property in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and in Design Manager.

Resource Group The resource group for which you want to use the submission template.

Install Path The path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ bin directory on the selected resource group:

Example: [STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1192

Property Description

Job Launch Options Command line options to pass to rmlaunch.bat—the launch script for Resource Manager executed from the generated submission script.

Example: -vv for verbose output or redirect the output to the log file.

For information on Resource Manager, see Installation Guide > Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager > Installation Prerequisites > Installation Location.

Partition Name (for Slurm)/ Queue Name (for all other systems)

The name of the cluster manager queue used for the submission. For a Slurm cluster, this is the name of the partition used for the submission.

To use the default cluster queue/partition, leave this text-box empty.

Parallel Environment (for Grid Engine only) The name of the parallel environment.

For example: mpich

Default Walltime The default requested wall time in the format of HH:MM:SS.

To use the default cluster manager wall time, leave this text-box empty.

Script Template

(leave empty to get it filled with the default template)

The template for the submission script generation. For a new job submission on the cluster, to create the start script, variables in the template are initialized with job-specific values.

To use the default submission template for the selected resource group, leave this field empty. See Submission Template Reference.

Keep Job and Task Repositories (for troubleshooting purposes)

When ON, keeps the temporary jobs and tasks folders within the Job Manager user directory.

See Installation Guide > Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager > Installation Prerequisites > Temporary Folder Considerations.

4. Click Create.

5. To edit the properties of an existing submission template, click next to the submission template entry.

6. To delete a submission template, click next to the submission template entry.

The submission templates in Job Manager support the following applications:

◦ Design Manager Design Run

◦ STAR-CCM+

Job Manager allows you to edit the application configurations, for example to add additional command line options to the application executables.

8. In the Application Configs panel, next to the application configuration of interest, click .

9. In the Edit Application Config panel, set the following properties:

Property Description

Application (read only) The type/name of the application for which this configuration applies. Only one configuration for each application is allowed for any given submission template.

Submission Templates Reference

Customizing Submission Templates

The default submission template accounts for various scenarios in job submission. However, in certain situations, the generated submission template requires manual customization.

For example:

• Setting environment variables, such as LICENSE_SERVER.

• Adding expert settings for the queuing system, such as:

# PBS -Wx=NACCESSPOLICY:SINGLEJOB # PBS -E

• Passing application options to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ executable during job submission. This is particularly useful when the application options depend on runtime attributes. See Example.

NOTE: When editing the submission template, be aware of the following:

• Do not omit lines of the submission template.

• Always verify that the customized submission template works correctly. See Verifying the Job Manager Setup.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1194

• A syntax error in the submission template does not necessarily cause jobs to fail. If the submission template exits before running $command, jobs fail.

Example

In this example, you set the -power licensing option for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ jobs on a Grid Engine cluster that use more than two compute slots.

First, you define a shell variable to pass to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ executable:

1. In the App. Configs column of the submission template entry, click Edit.

2. In the Application Configs panel, next to the application configuration for STAR-CCM+, click .

3. In the Edit Application Config panel, for Additional Option, set a shell variable using the $ character, such as $LICENSE_OPT.

4. Click Save.

Next, you modify the default submission script template so that the shell variable is set to -power if the number of requested slots for the job is greater than two. To query the number of slots, you use the submission template variable $jm_nslots (see Submission Template Variables):

5. Next to the submission template entry, click .

6. In the Edit Submission Template panel, edit the default code in the Script Template (leave empty to get it filled with the default template) text box as follows:

Code Explanation

#!/bin/bash #$ -S /bin/bash

# run in local directory #$ -cwd

# specify parallel environment and number of # slots # example: #$ -pe <pe_name> 42 $jm_pe_slots_line

# specify max walltime # example: #$ -l h_rt=<walltime> $jm_walltime_line

# specify queue # example: #$ -q <queue_name> $jm_queue_line

# set job name # example: #$ -N <name> $jm_name_line

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1195

Code Explanation

if [ $jm_nslots -gt 2 ]; then LICENSE_OPT="-power" else LICENSE_OPT="" fi export LICENSE_OPT

Here you set the shell variable LICENSE_OPT to be empty or equal to -power depending on the number of requested slots.

# combine stdout and stderr in outfile # The next four lines are required by # Job Manager #$ -j y #$ -o $jm_outfile export STAR_API_KEY=$jm_apikey $jm_command

7. Click Save.

Updating Submission Templates after Changing the Resource Type

If you created submission templates using a resource group with an incorrect resource type, you must correct both the resource type and the submission templates explicitly.

To set the correct resource type for the resource group:

1. On the main administration panel, in the Server Configuration group box, click (Resource Groups).

2. In the Resource Groups panel, click next to the resource group that uses the incorrect resource type.

3. In the Edit Resource Group panel, set the correct Resource Type.

4. Click Save.

To update the submission template:

5. On the main administration panel, in the Server Configuration group box, click (Submission Templates).

6. In the Submission Templates panel, click next to a submission template that uses the corrected resource group.

7. In the Edit Submission Template panel, delete the code in the Script Template text box.

8. Click Save.

The Script Template text box is filled with the correct submission template for the specified resource type.

9. Repeat Steps 5-8 for all submission templates that use the corrected resource group.

Assigning Groups and Permissions

Job Manager manages authorization with a user-group-permission system.

The user-group-permission authorization system grants permissions to perform certain actions according to groups. Users are assigned to particular groups and, through those group assignments, the users acquire the permissions to perform particular actions.

Job Manager provides the following permissions:

create jobs

Permission to create new jobs.

use [template] submission template

Permission to create jobs using the [template] submission template.

For each submission template, Job Manager automatically provides the corresponding permission to use it.

manage jobs

As create jobs, but adds the permission to view, manage, and delete jobs—regardless of the job ownership. To delete jobs, the group of users who acquire this permission must also acquire the permission from the queuing system to manage jobs.

manage system

The permission to log into the Administrator Web UI to set up and manage Job Manager (Job Manager administrator).

The following table lists the groups that are available by default and the permissions that are assigned to them:

Group Name Permissions

job creators create jobs

job managers create jobs, manage jobs

administrators manage system

You can create new groups, edit the group names and the permissions that are assigned to the groups, and delete existing groups.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1203

Note: You must explicitly add the use [template] submission template permission to the group of users that you want to be able to create jobs using that template. This group must also have the create jobs permission assigned to it.

To create a new group:

1. On the main administration panel, in the Users and Groups group box, click Groups.

2. In the Groups panel, click New Group.

3. In the respective New / Group panel, set the following properties:

Property Description

Group Name The display name of the group.

Permissions The permissions assigned to the group.

Using <Ctrl>, you can select multiple permissions for a group.

4. Click Create.

5. To edit the properties of an existing group, click next to the respective resource group entry.

6. To delete a group, click next to the group entry.

Creating Users

Regardless of the type of authentication (Internal Authentication or OS Authentication), each user of Job Manager requires a user account in the Job Manager database.

For both types of authentication, the user name must correspond to the OS user name on the cluster login node.

To create a user:

1. On the main administration panel, in the Users and Groups group box, click Users.

2. In the Users panel, click New User.

3. In the New User panel, set the following properties:

Property Description

User Name The name of the user that corresponds to the OS username on the cluster login node.

Email Address The email address of the user. Job Manager uses this email address to communicate with the user, for example when resetting the password.

Display Name The name of the user as displayed in the Job Manager Web UI.

Groups The user groups to which the user is assigned.

Using <Ctrl>, you can assign the user to multiple user groups. This way, the user receives all permissions of the selected user groups.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1204

Property Description

Password (optional) For Internal Authentication, allows you to specify the initial user password. The user can reset this password as required—see Resetting the Job Manager User Password for Internal Authentication.

For OS authentication, leave this field empty—the user uses his or her OS password as required by the login node of the represented resources.

4. Click Create.

5. To edit the properties of an existing user, click next to the user entry.

6. To delete a user, click next to the resource group entry.

Importing User Credentials

Importing User Credentials

The Job Manager Web UI allows you to import user credentials in tabular form.

Importing user credentials in tabular form is particularly useful for a large number of Job Manager users, where it would be very time-consuming to create each user individually.

The user credentials table must be in *.csv file format and must have four columns that contain the following information in order:

<user name>,<email address>,<display name>,<groups>

where <groups> must be a semicolon separated list of the groups to which you want to assign the user. For more information, see Creating Users.

Example:

user1,user1@gmail.com,User1,administrators;job managers;job creators user2,user2@gmail.com,User2,administrators;job managers user3,user3@gmail.com,User3,administrators user4,user4@gmail.com,User4,job creators user5,user5@gmail.com,User5,job managers;job creators user6,user6@gmail.com,User6,job managers user7,user7@gmail.com,User7,job creators user8,user8@gmail.com,User8,job creators user9,user9@gmail.com,User9,job creators user10,user10@gmail.com,User10,job creators user11,user11@gmail.com,User11,job creators user12,user12@gmail.com,User12,job creators user14,user13@gmail.com,User13,job creators user14,user14@gmail.com,User14,administrators;job managers;job creators

Note: For Internal Authentication, the import of initial user passwords is not supported. You can set the password in the Job Manager Web UI after the import. Alternatively, the user sets the password directly—see Resetting the Job Manager User Password for Internal Authentication.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1205

Note: To import properly into Job Manager, a table that contains special characters (including accented characters) requires UTF-8 encoding rather than ANSI.

To import the *.csv file of user credentials:

1. In the menu, click Admin > Bulk Users Import.

2. In the Bulk Import Users from the CSV File panel, next to the CSV Users File property, click Browse....

3. In the Choose File to Upload dialog, navigate to the folder that contains the *.csv file.

4. Select the file and click Open.

5. To handle the import of user credentials in case of duplicate or non-existent credential data, set the following properties:

Property Description

If User with the Name Exists Specifies how to handle the import of user credentials in case of a duplicate user name.

The following options are available:

◦ Skip CSV user (don't do anything)

◦ Overwrite the properties and replace the group membership

◦ Overwrite the properties and merge the group membership

◦ Abort the import

If Different User with the Email Exists Specifies how to handle the import of user credentials in case of a duplicate email address. The following options are available:

◦ Skip CSV user (don't do anything)

◦ Abort the import

If Group does not Exist Specifies how to handle the import of user credentials in case of a non-existent group.

The following options are available:

◦ Skip the group assignment (don't do anything)

◦ Add the new group and add user to it

◦ Abort the import

6. If your *.csv file contains a header row, activate Skip the first row (heading).

7. Click Import.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1206

Verifying the Job Manager Setup

After the installation and setup of Job Manager, you can verify Job Manager from the command line. The command line verification provides feedback on the status of Job Manager and reports potential problems or errors.

The command line verification runs a simple Hello World macro in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using Job Manager. The procedure is as follows:

• Locally writes the Java macro

• Instructs Job Manager to copy the Java macro to the compute resources

• Instructs Job Manager to submit a job to the cluster management queue

• As a task within the job, runs the Java macro in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ (% starccm+ new -batch macro.java)

• Looks for the expected output: Hello World

You can run the command line verification on a local workstation or on the represented compute resources. Running the command line verification on a local workstation allows you to additionally check the network connectivity to the compute resources.

To run the command line verification:

1. Open a command prompt and enter the following line:

[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin/jmverify [JobManager_URL] --user [username] --passwd [passwd]

where:

◦ [STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR] is the path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation directory.

◦ [JobManager_URL] is the URL of Job Manager, such as https://[hostname]:[portnumber].

◦ [username] is your Job Manager username, which corresponds to the OS username that you use to login to the cluster login node (optional). If not specified, sets the name of the current user.

◦ [passwd] is the password of the user (optional). If not specified, you are prompted for the user password. For OS authentication, this user password is the OS password as set on the login node of the represented compute resources. For Internal Authentication, it is the Job Manager specific user password.

2. If multiple submission templates are available (see Creating Submission Templates), enter the submission template of your choice:

Example:

[user1@cluster1 ~]$ ./star/bin/jmverify https:// cluster1.koeln.siemens.com:443 --user user1 Enter your password associated with ./star/bin/jmverify https:// cluster1.koeln.siemens.com:443 Job Manager https://cluster1.koeln.siemens.com:443/api/v1 pinged in 0.0s API Version: 1 User identity: user1 Time to ping: 0.0s Submission Templates available to user1 queried in 0.0s: ----------------- | template name |

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1207

| ------------- | | Submit_v1     | | Submit_v2     | ----------------- Enter the Submission Template to use:

The command prompt gives feedback on the status of the job submission using Job Manager:

◦ If Job Manager is successfully verified, you receive the following information—using the Example in Step 2:

https://cluster1.koeln.siemens.com:443 has been successfully verified for user user1

◦ If a problem occurs, the command prompt provides you with guidance on how to resolve the problem.

3. Repeat Step 1 and Step 2 for all available submission templates.

Note: By default, jmverify submits a single job with a single Simcenter STAR-CCM+ task on two slots.

If you want to run a high-load test, you can increase the number of tasks and slots. For example, to run a job with 8 tasks on 64 slots, where each job runs on 8 slots, you enter the following line in the command prompt:

[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin/jmverify [JobManager_URL] --user [user] --passwd [passwd] --slots 64 --tasks 8 --task_slots 8

Running jmverify --help gives you additional information about the verification application.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1208

Running a Simulation with Job Manager

With Job Manager set up for your Linux cluster, you can run simulations without requiring expert knowledge of your cluster environment. To access Job Manager, you must run the simulation from the Graphical User Interface (GUI)—you can not access Job Manager from a batch client.

To access Job Manager, you require the URL of the Job Manager web server as provided by your Job Manager administrator. If the URL begins with https://, the communication between the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client and the Job Manager web server is encrypted.

Note: If the communication is encrypted (that is, using HTTPS), you must make sure that the root certificate of the certificate authority (CA) is installed in the Java JDK trust store. For detailed instructions, see the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Installation Guide at the following location: Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager > Installation Prerequisites > Client-Web Server Communication > Generating a Trusted Certificate > Importing the CA Root Certificate into the Client Trust Stores.

Before you run a simulation with Job Manager, be aware of the following:

• If Job Manager is installed in Internal Authentication mode, the public key of the Job Manager system account must be imported in your authorized keys file on the cluster login node. The public key of the system account, such as jmadmin, is stored in the ~jmadmin/.ssh/id_rsa.pub file. The authorized keys are usually stored in the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys file in your home directory.

• If you use Job Manager for the first time, and Internal Authentication applies, consider changing your password. See Resetting the Job Manager User Password for Internal Authentication.

• Simulations are only saved at the end of a batch run if you either activate Autosave Batch Runs within the File > Auto Save panel, or if you supply a macro file that contains commands for doing so.

To run a simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager:

1. Add a Job Manager connection to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Adding a Job Manager Connection .

2. Submit the simulation using the Job Manager connection:

a) In the Servers window, right-click the Job Manager Servers > [username]@[Job Manager URL] node and select Submit Simulation.

b) In the Submit Simulation dialog, set the following properties:

▪Submission Template

▪Simulation File

▪Macro File (Optional)

▪Number of Processes

For more information, see Job Manager Servers Reference.

c) Click OK.

Under the [username]@[Job Manager URL] node, a server process node labeled Status ([status]) - [simulation] is displayed for each serial server process or parallel master process.

Note: DO NOT shut down your local workstation as long as the status shows Uploading. The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client must remain active on your local workstation until the upload is complete.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1209

3. To monitor the progress of the simulation, you can use a web browser to connect remotely to the Job Manager job. See Monitoring a Simulation under Job Manager.

4. When the simulation is complete, download the results from the cluster:

a) Right-click the Status ([status]) - [simulation] node and select Download Results.

b) In the Select Files to Download dialog, select the files you want to download.

You can download the starting and final simulation files (*.sim) and the simulation log file (*.out).

c) To remove the selected files from the cluster after download, activate Permanently delete the files on Job Manager after downloading (cannot be undone).

d) Click OK.

e) In the Download Location dialog, navigate to and select the directory, where you want to write the files.

f) Click Open.

Resetting the Job Manager User Password for Internal Authentication

For Job Manager with Internal Authentication, you require a Job Manager specific user password.

When your Job Manager administrator sets up Job Manager, he or she can optionally specify a initial user password for you. You are advised to reset your user password before you use Job Manager. If your Job Manager administrator does not set an initial user password for you, you must set your user password before you can use Job Manager.

Note: For Job Manager with OS Authentication, you use the same credentials as when you log in to the login node of the represented cluster using SSH.

The request for password reset is sent to your email-address.

Job Manager Connection Dialog

URL

Sets your Job Manager username. This username corresponds to the OS username that you use to login to the cluster login node.

Depending on the Job Manager authentication mode set by your Job Manager administrator, set one of the following passwords:

Submit Simulation Dialog

Submission Template

From the drop-down menu, select the Job Manager submission template that suits your requirements. The submission template determines how the simulation is submitted to the cluster, such as which cluster

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

queue or which Simcenter STAR-CCM+ version to use. The available submission templates are provided by your Job Manager administrator.

Status

Displays the run status of the simulation. The following statuses are available:

• Uploading—the simulation file is uploading to the cluster.

• Pending—the job was created but has not launched, yet.

• Queued—the job is waiting for compute resources in the queue.

• Starting—the job is starting.

• Executing—the simulation is running.

• Complete—the simulation completed successfully.

• Failed—the simulation failed with errors.

• StartFailed—the simulation could not be started.

• Terminated—you terminated the simulation before completion.

• Interrupted—the server terminated the simulation before completion.

• Disconnected—you exited the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client while the simulation was running. The simulation continues running with Job Manager.

Web Monitor

When you submit a simulation to Job Manager, you can monitor the status and progress of the simulation using the Web Monitor. Web Monitor is a web-based client that you can access from any compatible browser.

When connected to Web Monitor, you can select a running job and view plots and scenes that were already defined in the simulation before you submitted it to Job Manager.

For scenes, you can manipulate the view using zoom, pan, and rotate.

If you decide that there is no reason for the simulation to continue running, the Web Monitor allows you to stop and save the simulation, and end the job.

Monitoring a Simulation under Job Manager

Using a web browser, you can check the status and monitor the plots and scenes of your simulation as it runs on the Job Manager server.

For security reasons, both Job Manager and the Web Monitor App must be installed within an corporate private network. See the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Installation Guide for details (Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager > Installation Prerequisites, "Installation Location" and "Client-Web Server Communication").

1. In the Servers window, right-click the Job Manager Servers > [username]@[Job Manager URL] node and select Open in Web Monitor.

▶Alternatively, to use the link on a different device or to e-mail it to someone else, select Copy Link to Web Monitor.

2. In the login web page, enter the same credentials that you use for your Job Manager server.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1215

The Web Monitor shows all simulation jobs on the Job Manager server, divided into two tables. The top table (Live Monitor) includes jobs that you can monitor now ("Executing") or soon ("Queued" or "Pending"). The bottom table (Status & Log) contains jobs that either completed successfully or failed. You can also sort and filter using any of the table column headers.

If you submitted a job to Job Manager in the previous version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+, that job is also accessible in the Web Monitor.

Details about the various controls in the Web Monitor UI are available in Web Monitor Reference.

3. To make sure that the list of jobs and their status is current, near the upper left corner of the page, click

(Refresh List).

Note: The lack of immediate updates is largely due to the process for conveying information: Web Monitor connects to the App Server which in turn connects to Job Manager. The App Server prevents continuous polling to Job Manager.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1216

5. To access simulation job data, including plots and scenes, in a job monitoring session, click the link of the monitor job in the Job column.

By default the Residuals plot is shown.

To prevent a monitoring session from using excessive computing time on the cluster, after the session is idle for a period of time, the Web Monitor automatically returns to the job list.

Once the job has reached "Complete" status, the job data is no longer available through the Web Monitor.

a) To view the updates of plots and scenes, click the links to them in the Scenes/Plots list of displays.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1217

You can manipulate a scene or plot view (for example zoom or pan) as you would in a standard Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client.

You cannot create or modify plots or scenes, for example add or remove parts. All post-processing must be prepared in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client before the job is submitted.

The Web Monitor uses server rendering with a single thread—that is, the graphics capabilities of the machine where the master process is running are used (typically the head node of the cluster on which Job Manager is running). Activities that depend on hardware graphics or multiple render threads for best

performance may suffer: for instance, opening a scene with advanced rendering can result in long delays before the first frame displays.

If, after reviewing solution progress, you decide that the simulation can be discarded, you can terminate the simulation without saving the simulation file.

6. Within the job list, click under the Terminate column in the row for that particular job.

To download the simulation file after the run is complete, see the instructions for downloading the results from the cluster in Running a Simulation with Job Manager.

Resolving the Error: Unable to Find a Valid Certificate for SSL

To access Job Manager, you require the URL of the Job Manager web server as provided by your Job Manager administrator. If the URL begins with https://, Secure Sockets Layer (SSL)/Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocols are used to encrypt the communication between the Job Manager client—such as Simcenter STAR-CCM+, Design Manager, or a web browser—and the Job Manager web server.

To establish the encrypted connection, the root certificate of the certificate authority (CA) must be installed in the trust store of the client. If you try to connect to Job Manager and the CA root certificate is not added to the client trust store, an error message appears.

Example: The following error message appears when you are Adding a Job Manager Connection in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and the CA root certificate is not available in the Java JDK trust store:

For information on how to import the CA root certificate into the client trust stores, see the following section in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Installation Guide:

Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Job Manager > Installation Prerequisites > Client-Web Server Communication > Generating a Trusted Certificate > Importing the CA Root Certificate into the Client Trust Stores.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1221

Monitoring and Deleting Jobs and Tasks

You can monitor Job Manager jobs and tasks using the rmclient application. This application also allows you to delete jobs and terminate the tasks that are owned by the job.

You can run the rmclient application from a local workstation or on the represented compute resources.

To monitor your Job Manager jobs:

1. Open a command prompt and enter the following line:

[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin/rmclient [JobManager_URL] -u [username] -p [password] get jobs -table -format fields id,owner,status

where:

◦ [STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR] is the path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation directory.

◦ [JobManager_URL] is the URL of Job Manager as provided by your Job Manager administrator.

◦ [username] is the username of the Job Manager user, which corresponds to the OS username used to login to the cluster login node (optional). If not specified, sets the name of the current user.

◦ [passwd] is the password of the user (optional). If not specified, you are prompted for the user password. For OS authentication, this user password is the OS password as set on the login node of the represented compute resources. For Internal Authentication, it is the Job Manager specific user password.

For each job, the command prompt displays the job id, the owner of the job, and the status of the job, where the following job statuses are available:

◦ pending—the job is not yet submitted.

◦ queued—the job is submitted and waiting in the queue.

◦ running—the job is being executed.

◦ done—the job completed successfully.

◦ interrupted—the job was interrupted and terminated. Example: the job ran out of walltime.

◦ failed—the job failed to start. Example: the submission start script failed.

Example:

[user1@cluster1 ~]$ ./star/bin/rmclient https:// cluster1.koeln.siemens.com:443 -u user1 get_jobs --table --format_fields id,owner,status password: ------------------------------ | id   | owner     | status  | | ---- | --------- | ------- | | 276  | user1     | done    | | 284  | user2     | pending | | 287  | user3     | pending | | 294  | user2     | done    | | 297  | user3     | queued  | | 298  | user3     | running | | 301  | user1     | done    | | 304  | user1     | queued  | | 305  | user2     | done    | | 307  | user2     | running | | 308  | user2     | running | | 310  | user3     | running | | 311  | user3     | done    |

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1222

| 312  | user2     | done    | ------------------------------

To delete a job and terminate the tasks that are owned by the job:

2. In the command prompt, enter the following command:

[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin/rmclient [JobManager_URL] -u [user] delete job -jobid [jobid]

where:

◦ [jobid] is the id of the job you want to delete as provided in Step 2.

The rmclient command provides additional expert functionality for handling Job Manager and the related jobs and tasks. For more information, run rsverify --help.

Increasing the Verbosity Level of Job Manager Logging

To obtain additional debug information for Job Manager, you can increase the verbosity level of logging in the Job Manager configuration file.

The Job Manager configuration file uses the python logging config file format, which allows you to configure logging per python package. For each package, the file contains a specific section that starts with [logger_package name], where you can set the verbosity level and handler of the package logger.

The following verbosity levels of logging are available, in increasing level of detail:

• ERROR

• WARNING

• INFO

• DEBUG

The handler determines where the debug information is written—to console or to a logfile.

For more information, see https://docs.python.org/2/library/logging.config.html#configuration-file-format.

By default, the Job Manager package inherits its logging configuration from the root logger [logger_root], which sets the following level and handler:

[logger_root]

level ERROR

handler console

Before you increase the logging level, be aware of the following:

• Increasing the logging level increases the amount of data that is written, which can create large logfiles.

• Job Manager and Resource Manager are two different processes with different logging. Each process has its own configuration file to control the logging—jobmanager.cfg and resourcemanager.cfg.

• Resource Manager is run per user. When you change the logging for Resource Manager, take care to set a user dependent logfile location.

• Enabling the DEBUG verbosity level for the python authorization package in [logger_auth] can reveal sensitive data, such as user passwords.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1223

To increase the logging level for Job Manager and change the logging handler:

1. Navigate to [STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin, where [STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR] is the path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation directory on your cluster.

2. Open the Job Manager configuration file jobmanager.cfg file in a text editor and look for the section that starts with [logger_root].

3. In the section [logger_root], set the logging level as required, such as level = DEBUG.

4. Depending on where you want to write the logging information, set handlers to console, file, or both.

Example: The following section writes debug information to console:

[logger_root] # *** Change this level to control overall logging level (ERROR, WARNING, INFO, DEBUG) level = DEBUG # *** Uncommment one of the following three lines to route the output to console, logfile or both # Change the log file path in the [handler_logfile] section handlers = console #handlers = logfile ##handlers = console, logfile

Note: If you are running Job Manager as a service, you can only write the logging information to a file.

5. If you write the logging information to a logfile, you can customize the file path in the section [handler_logfile]:

[handler_logfile] class = FileHandler level = NOTSET formatter = generic # *** Change the first parameter below to modify the path to the log file args=(__import__("datetime").datetime.now().strftime('jobmanager_%%Y-%%m-% %d_%%H-%%M-%%S.log'), 'a')

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1224

Command-Line Reference

The starccm+ command can start either the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client:

starccm+ [options] [simulation]

or server process:

starccm+ -server [options] [simulation]

Without any arguments, the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ GUI client is started. No server process is started, as that is only required when a simulation is created or loaded.

If a simulation file is named without any options, both the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client and a server are started, and the named file is loaded into the server.

If the -server argument is specified, only the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server process is started. Any server option can also be specified on the command-line to start the client; the client passes those options on when it starts the server process.

General Options

Argument Description

-info Prints information about the simulation file: the version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with which that file was saved (in this example 15.06.###), number of partitions, file size, and number of iterations in the file:

STAR-CCM+ 15.06.### (linux-x86_64-2.5/gnu4.6) Serial 680.34 KB  Iter 66

-ini <file> Activates an .ini file that contains general and client options.

-loc For the client, this option turns off broadcasting of queries to locate servers on the network; it also prevents the server from responding to any locator queries. The broadcast from the client is a UDP multicast, along with TCP pings, to known hosts. This multicast search is started by default when you launch the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client without a simulation file. In Windows this option can cause network access warnings from your personal firewall.

-new Launches the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ workspace and starts a new simulation without accessing a simulation file.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1225

Argument Description

-printpids Prints process IDs. An example of the output format is as follows:

Host ID 0 Rank 0 on marlin32 with process ID 7270 Host ID 0 Rank 1 on marlin32 with process ID 7422 Host ID 0 Rank 2 on marlin32 with process ID 7591

-v, -vv, -vvv Activates Verbose mode, prints environment changes and sub-commands.

-version Prints the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ version information (in this example 15.06.###):

15.06.###

License Options

Argument Description

-lite Requests a Lite Session license as opposed to a full license. Only a reduced functionality set is available.

-power Starts Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with the Power Session license feature.

-doepower Uses a Power Session license for the optimization session license.

-nosuite Prevents main licenses from being used to enable cores for parallel computation. Only parallel licenses are used to enable cores for parallel computation.

-powerpre Uses 10 DOEtoken licenses to launch a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ preand postprocessing session.

-tokensonly Specifies to only use DOEtoken licenses for optimization studies. With this option, you can also use DOEtoken licenses for regular parallel runs in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

-notokens Specifies to not use DOEtoken licenses for optimization studies.

-doe-preferhpcdomains Changes the order in which the DOEtoken license feature is checked out. Using this option checks out the hpcdomains license feature before the DOEtoken license feature for optimization studies.

-podkey <value> Specifies a Power on Demand license key.

-doeuuid <value> Specifies a DOE UUID (universal unique identifier).

-licpath <path:...> Specifies a license path that overrides the default license path. When this option is used, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the path to define a new CDLMD_LICENSE_FILE environment variable for the spawned server session.

-reserve <lic1[,lic2,...]> Allows you to specify add-on licenses that can be automatically checked out.

-noreserve Prevents add-on licenses from being checked out unless a model operation requires them.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1226

Argument Description

-noretry Prevents add-on licenses from being retried when a significant operation is carried out.

-norelease Prevents add-on licenses from being released after importing geometry.

Client Options

Argument Description

-batch [command] Starts Simcenter STAR-CCM+ in batch mode (without a GUI). The following additional commands are available:

• mesh — runs the meshing pipeline

• run — runs the solver until the stopping criteria are satisfied

• step — steps the solution

• <macro>.java — runs the specified Java macro file

If no command is specified, the default action is to run the solver. In each case, the simulation is auto-saved through the auto save feature (unless that property is turned off).

When applying simulation operations, if a chain of simulation operations is set active, the - batch without any [command] executes the operations in batch mode. If no chain of simulation operations is active, - batch steps the simulation by ignoring the simulation operations. However, once an additional command is included, the batch execution will NOT include simulation operations, no matter there is an active chain or not.

You can specify multiple commands within the -batch argument. In the following example, three macros are run in order before running the mesh pipeline and the solver:

-batch macro1.java,macro2.java,macro3.java,mesh,run

-batch-report Generates a summary report of a batch simulation. The report appears in .html format. This report includes details about the computer system where the simulation was run, as well as details about the simulation itself.

-classpath <classpath> Overrides the User macro classpath setting from the Options dialog. This option only affects the macro compilation in the current session of Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

-clientldlibpath <path>:<path>:<pat h>

This option permits you to add directory paths explicitly to the Simcenter STARCCM+ client library search path (LD_LIBRARY_PATH) for the client runtime environment.

-config <id> Accesses a saved configuration of server options. (These options are also listed in the Saved Configurations list of the dialog that loads a simulation or creates a new one.)

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1227

Argument Description

-save-config <id> Saves a configuration of server options and adds it to the Saved Configurations list of the dialog that loads a simulation or creates a new one.

-fontsize <size> Adjusts the size of the font that is used in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client workspace, such as dialogs and the object tree, for that session. Add the desired font size with this command.

For example, a command of starccm+ -fontsize 16 sets the font size to 16 points.

-host <host> -port <port> Specifies the host and port of a running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server process to which the client connects. If the -host and -port options are used, a simulation file cannot be specified.

-locale <locale> Overrides the default locale of your operating system. You can run Simcenter STARCCM+ in the following languages:

• English US: en:US

• Japanese: ja

• Chinese (simplified): zh

• Korean: ko

• Russian: ru:RU

-macro <file> Runs the macro file upon client startup. This option is similar to -batch in that a macro file is read, but in this case a GUI is opened. This option requires specification of a simulation file. Since it is impossible to record a macro that includes the opening of a simulation file, there is never a conflict.

-nbuserdir <dir> Lets you specify a location, other than $HOME, in which the .star-*-*-* directory is written. Enter this command after client startup.

This option changes the location of key Simcenter STAR-CCM+ information, including the user settings directory and client log messages. Consider using this option when you do not have write access to your $HOME directory, or when you want to share modules.

-noexit Prevents the server process from shutting down after batch file execution has completed. By default, the client and server processes both shut down after the macro completes.

-on <host> Specifies the hostmachine on which to start the server process. By default, when a new simulation is created or an existing simulation file is opened, the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client starts a server process on the local machine. If the -on option is specified however, the client attempts to start the server process on the named host machine using the appropriate remote shell.

Additionally, this option can be used directly as a parallel option to specify the hosts that the parallel server uses.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1228

Argument Description

-param <global parameter name> <value>

Specifies the value of a global parameter that already exists in the target simulation. You can set scalar and vector parameter values using either fixed values or expressions, and can also set file paths for file parameters. Multiple instances are allowed.

If either argument (name or value) contains spaces or reserved characters such as '$', surround the argument in quotes, either single or double, depending on the command shell and your objective.

Examples

starccm+ -param MaxTime 10.0 demo.sim

starccm+ -param MinWidth 2cm demo.sim

starccm+ -param Sample [0.1,0.2,0.15] demo.sim

starccm+ -param MaxTime 10.0 -param MinWidth 2cm demo.sim

Linux Quoted Example

starccm+ -param MaxWidth '$MinWidth * 2' demo.sim

Windows Quoted Example

starccm+ -param MaxWidth "$MinWidth * 2" demo.sim

To set a file parameter for a specific simulation:

-param <file parameter name> <path to file> <path to simulation>

When you enclose the <path to file> in quotes, the path can use separators of either type (forward slash or back slash). Without quotes, the <path to file> must use forward slash separators for Linux, and back slash separators for Windows.

Example

starccm+ -param demoparameter demofile.txt demo.sim

-reset Restores the default client layout (including window positions) and settings (options and mounted directories).

-time Prints server-elapsed and CPU times after a batch run. Specifically, it prints a summary of computational resource use of the server on close-down.

In serial:

Saving: /home/ncr/sims/suprBump@00077.sim Server Elapsed Time :          5.362  (s) Server CPU Time     :          0.830  (s) Closing connection to server and exiting

In parallel:

Auto save: /home/ncr/sims/suprBump@00077.sim Saving: /home/ncr/sims/suprBump@00077.sim |Global Rank|Server Elapsed Time (s)|Server CPU Time (s)| MPI Overhead (s)|MPI Overhead %Elapsed Time (s)| |          0|                  7.120| 1.250|           0.461|                         6.476| |          1|                  7.120| 5.150|           2.371|                        33.302| |          2|                  7.120| 5.120|           2.425|                        34.056| |          3|                  7.120| 5.160|           2.451|                        34.421| Maximum worker communication time on rank     : 3 Minimum worker communication time on rank     : 0 Average worker communication time             : 1.927 Standard deviation worker communication times : 0.847 Closing connection to server and exiting

-userdir <name> On Linux, adds a user settings directory to your home directory with name optionally added to the folder name.

-nbuserdir <name> On Linux, specifies the NetBeans directory.

-clientcore On Linux, reserves one core for running the client in a batch system. Use this flag if you perform a lot of post-processing while running in parallel.

-clientldpreload <file:...> On Linux, sets the client LD_PRELOAD environment variable.

Server Options

Argument Description

-arch <architecture> This option allows you to override the automatic determination of the architecture of the machine. The specified architecture must exist within the installation and must be compatible with the machine architecture. If these conditions are not met, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ exits, or runtime errors occur.

For example, this argument can work when a 32-bit Linux installation is executed on a 64-bit Opteron-based architecture:

-arch linux-x86-2.2.5

-batchsystem <system> This option can be used to aid the startup of parallel Simcenter STAR-CCM+ under the control of a supported Batch Management System (for usage see Using Batch Management Systems).

Currently the supported systems are:

• PBS (<system>=pbs)

• LSF (<system>=lsf)

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1230

Argument Description

• Sun Grid Engine (<system>=sge)

• Load Leveler (<system>=ll)

• SLURM (<system>=slurm)

-collab In the startup of a server, allows others to connect to it. (By default only the user who starts a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server is allowed to connect to it.)

-cout Messages are directed to the console rather than to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client.

-jobmanager <URL> Specifies the URL of the Resource Manager that controls the resources for the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. The Resource Manager automatically adds this option to the server.

-ldlibpath <path>:<path>:<pa th>

This option permits you to add directory paths explicitly to the Simcenter STAR-CCM + server library search path (LD_LIBRARY_PATH) for the server runtime environment.

The -ldlibpath option is required when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ relies upon thirdparty software that is installed in custom locations. In addition, consider using it for user code in the following instances:

• Linking against a math library like IMSL or NAG. (Getting access to the functions in them is one reason to write user code.)

• Most compilers that can build a .so file dynamically link it against their own runtime libraries. Add paths to these libraries, unless they happen to be the system libraries (as they are with GNU compilers on Linux).

-load Loads the specified simulation file as soon as the server starts. Without this option, the simulation database is loaded on demand when the client connects to the server.

-msjob[:<opt>] Submits a cluster job to the Windows Server job scheduler. This functionality is available only on Windows Server 2012 machines.

-noconnect In the startup of a server, specifies a session that is exclusive to the Simcenter STARCCM+ console session that launched it. No other users can connect to that server.

-port <port> Specifies server port for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to open.

-portrange <range> Specifies the number of ports the server can attempt to bind to.

-server Starts the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server with an automatically generated port number.

-rsh <option> -svrrsh <option> The -rsh <option> option can be used to specify:

• the remote shell used to start remote servers from the client

• the remote shell used in the server to launch parallel processes, co-simulations, and so on.

The -svrrsh <option> specifies the server's remote shell only.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1231

Argument Description

When starting a server using -server, the -rsh or -svrrsh options default to ssh.

In a new client session the remote shell settings default to those set by the environment options, Generic Remote Process Launch Command and the Server Remote Process Launch Command.

-taskid <pid> Specifies the task ID of the Resource Manager that controls the resources for the server. The Resource Manager automatically adds this option to the server.

-ldpreload <file:...> On Linux, for the server, sets the shared libraries list to LD_PRELOAD.

Visualization Options

Argument Description

-graphics <option> For the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer, uses one of the following options:

• auto – (default) prefers supported native OpenGL over Mesa OpenGL; this option has the same effect as not using any -graphics option.

• native – enforces native OpenGL

• mesa – enforces Mesa OpenGL; uses the alternative mesa graphics libraries

-hardwarebatch Uses hardware acceleration for rendering graphics scenes when running in batch. This option can provide faster performance when post-processing large numbers of scenes. Hardware drivers must be installed properly and be in use on the machine where the client process of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is running. For Linux/Unix machines, run an X server on the machine where the client process of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is running. This X server could be your interactive X session, or another X session that you have permission to run.

-rgraphics For the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server (remote rendering), uses one of the following options:

• auto – (default) prefers supported native OpenGL over Mesa OpenGL; this option has the same effect as not using any -rgraphics option.

• egl – enforces native OpenGL on EGL (Linux only)

• native – enforces native OpenGL

• mesa – enforces Mesa OpenGL; uses the alternative mesa graphics libraries

-rthreads N Client option. Sets the number of threads N available for visualization tasks, including advanced rendering. When using this setting, consider the following:

• If you specify a high value for render threads, you can incur resource contentions that interfere with the proper functioning of your computer.

• Increasing render threads is expected to scale performance linearly. However, linear scaling can fail with high thread counts on hyper-threaded or multi-CPU systems, although performance can still increase. Complexity of the scene can also impact performance and prevent scaling.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1232

Argument Description

• The value specified with the -rthreads command line option takes precedence over the corresponding setting that is available through Tools > Options.

• Cannot be used in conjunction with the -batchsystem option. If it is, then - rthreads defaults to a value of 1. If you attempt to specify a -rthreads value greater than 1 when using -batchsystem, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ generates a warning message.

-rr [hostname:port] Client option that tells the (batch) client to use a separate rendering service on either the local machine or a remote machine. The argument [hostname:port] is optional. Without hostname:port, the client tells the server to spawn a rendering process on the same (local) machine. With hostname:port, the client tells the server to connect to the rendering service already running on the remote machine (launched using starrenderer).

-rrthreads N Server option which controls the number of threads N used by the rendering processes that can be spawned by the server for clients connecting with -rr. If Simcenter STARCCM+ is started with -rr -rrthreads N then the (batch) client uses remote rendering and the server that is launched uses N threads for remote rendering

Parallel Options

Argument Description

-benchmark Assesses performance capabilities of your hardware. For detailed information about options, use -benchmarkhelp. For more information about benchmarking, see Performance Benchmarks.

-machinefile <file> MPI machine resource file name. Only used with parallel operation. The processes are allocated to the machines in the resource list starting with the first entry. If the number of requested processes (defined by -np) exceeds the number of machines that are listed, the remaining processes continue to be allocated starting with the first entry in the resource list. Cannot be used with - on.

-mpi <driver>

-mpidriver <driver>

Specifies the MPI driver to use <ms, platform>. If omitted, Simcenter STARCCM+ uses a default driver.

In addition, this command can help if you do not know the specific inter-connect hardware available on a machine.

-mpiflags <options> MPI driver expert options.

-mpitest [:<options>] Performs MPI tests and exits.

-np <np> Number of processes to use. Only used for parallel operation. If the -np option is omitted and -machinefile or -on is specified, the number of processes is assumed to be the number that the resource list prescribes. If neither -on or - machinefile is specified with this option, then -on localhost:<np> is assumed.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1233

Argument Description

-np <np[,npcosim]> Number of processors to use for co-simulation, where np is the number of processes for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and npcosim is the number of processes for the other tool.

-on <host[:np] [,host[:np]]> List of hosts to run parallel processes on. If :np is specified, then np processes are put on that machine. There must be no spaces in the list of hosts. The processes are allocated to the machines in the resource list starting with the first entry adding np processes before moving on to the next machine in the list. If the number of requested processes (defined by -np) exceeds the number of machines that are listed, the remaining processes continue to be allocated starting with the first entry in the resource list. Cannot be used with - machinefile.

-pio Activates parallel input/output on RAID-5 file systems. When this flag is included, the given simulation file is restored using parallel I/O, and all subsequent simulation files are saved using parallel I/O.

-cpubind <policy> Specifies what binding policy <off, bandwidth, latency> to use when binding CPUs.

You can request a report to display the binding layout by entering: -cpubind v

Working with .ini Files

You can use an .ini file as a shortcut for general and client command line options when starting local Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulations.

To use this feature, add the -ini option to your line command:

% starccm+ -ini myinifile.ini <simfile>

The file contains simple listed commands, with any line beginning with # considered a comment. For instance, if you usually prefer to use rsh rather than ssh on your system, the .ini file could look like the following:

# set default rsh command -rsh rsh

A more complex .ini file could be constructed as follows:

# set default rsh command -rsh rsh # set batchsystem and always allocate the controller process to a cpu/core shared with a worker process -batchsystem pbs: # MPI options #   - Intel MPI #   - PSM2 fabric -mpi intel -fabric psm2

Arguments that are passed on the command line take precedence over the ones that are listed in the .ini file. For example, suppose that you issue the following command line:

% starccm+ -ini myinifile.ini <simfile> -rsh ssh

The -rsh argument in the command line takes precedence over the one in the .ini file. Currently there is no way to merge these two arguments.

Your system administrator can create a global .ini file that applies these options to all servers.

Contents:

Creating a Global .ini File

See Also:

Creating a Global .ini File

Creating a Global .ini File

System administrators can create a global .ini file that contains command line options that affect all users. This ability is particularly useful if there are system-wide options that all users should be using.

For a list of command line options, refer to Command Line Reference.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 1235

Create the global .ini file as described in Working with .ini Files and place it in the following directory of your Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation:

[INSTALL_DIR]/star/config/ini

Name the .ini file according to the architecture of the system where it is installed, for example:

[INSTALL_DIR]/star/config/ini/starccm+-<arch>.ini

Where <arch> is the architecture of your system.

Naming the Linux Global .ini File

On Linux, you can find the architecture by using maparch, which is located in [INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin/ maparch. An example command to run maparch is:

% ./star/bin/maparch linux-x86_64-2.5

The .ini file is then named:

[INSTALL_DIR]/star/config/ini/starccm+-linux-x86_64-2.5.ini

Naming the Windows Global .ini File

On Windows, the .ini file is named:

[INSTALL_DIR]\star\config\ini\starccm+-windows.ini

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solves physics problems on a computational mesh. To provide this mesh, you first define geometry using internal or external tools, and then create a mesh pipeline whose operations generate the mesh in repeatable steps.

Modeling Geometry

This part of the User Guide describes how to use 3D-CAD, the parametric solid modeler available within Simcenter STAR-CCM+. It also describes the features and tools available for further preparation of the geometry model and its surfaces.

For many simulations in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, the first step involves preparing the geometry of the case under investigation. This geometry could come from a model that was prepared previously in a CAD package, or could be created directly using the 3D-CAD module within Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3D-CAD

This fully integrated CAD tool allows you to build geometry from scratch within the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ environment, as well as import external CAD models and modify them before running a simulation. 3D-CAD is tailored to suit the needs of a CFD analysis and allows you to change the geometry quickly and easily, before rerunning the simulation.

The chapters in this section covering 3D-CAD are as follows:

• Creating geometry with 3D-CAD

• Importing geometry into 3D-CAD

• Exporting geometry from 3D-CAD

• Using 3D-CAD models in a simulation

Preparation of the Geometry Model

The concepts that are associated with manipulating and preparing geometry have been distinguished from the ones that relate to regions and boundaries through the introduction of geometry parts. Geometry parts are contained within the Geometry Parts node of the object tree. They are fully described in the section Using Geometry Parts.

The other parts of the documentation cover the following:

• An introduction to using Simcenter STAR-CCM+

• How to generate or import meshes and work with them

• Modeling physics -- the concepts, theory, and implementation details of the models

• Using tools in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to facilitate your work

• A wizard guide that shows how Simcenter STAR-CCM+ features are combined in customized interfaces for special applications
