Job Manager

Adding a Job Manager Key

A Job Manager key authenticates you against Job Manager on the clusters.

To add a Job Manager key:

1. Select the Compute Resource > Job Manager node and click (Custom Editor) for Job Manager Key.

2. In the Job Manager Keys dialog, set the following properties:

◦ URL

◦ Username

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6795

◦ Password

For more information, see Job Manager Servers Reference.

3. Click Add.

Design Manager allows you to add multiple Job Manager keys, which is particularly useful if you want to switch between multiple clusters where a Job Manager is installed.

4. To delete a Job Manager key, select the key in the list and click Delete.

5. Click OK.

You are authenticated against Job Manager on the cluster. Depending on the URL of Job Manager, Design Manager communicates your username and password to Job Manager using http or https:

The Job Manager connection is listed in the Servers window. If authentication fails, an error message appears.

Note: When you save the Design Manager project, the specified URL and username of the key are saved as design study properties in the Design Manager project file (*.dmprj). The password is NOT saved.

When you reload the *.dmprj file to rerun the design study, you are prompted to enter the password again.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6796

Running on a Windows HPC Cluster Using General Job Submission

To run a Design Manager project on a Windows HPC cluster, you must submit the project in general job submission mode. General job submission means that Design Manager submits each design simulation individually to the HPC Job Manager.

Note: All file system paths that you specify in your Design Manager project file must be network shared between the node that submits the jobs to the HPC Job Manager, such as the head node, and the compute nodes. Always use the full network path using uniform naming convention (UNC).

Additionally, you must provide Design Manager with the UNC path to the Design Manager project file (*.dmprj). There are two options to satisfy this requirement:

• Load the Design Manager project file using the UNC path, such as \\cluster\data\home\user1\work \DesignManager\project1\project1.dmprj. See Saving, Closing, and Loading a Design Manager Project.

• Load the Design Manager project file using the local path, such as H:\home\user1\work \DesignManager\project1\project1.dmprj. Then select the Design Manager project node at the root of the object tree and set Project Artifact Directory to the UNC path of your project artifact directory on the cluster.

The first option offers the advantage that Design Manager keeps using the relative path to the project artifact directory that contains the *.dmprj file. This approach allows you to move the file without having to update the Project Artifact Directory entry.

To run a design study using general job submission on a Windows HPC cluster:

1. For each design study in your Design Manager project, define the run and resource settings:

a) Select the Design Studies > [design study] > Settings > Run Settings node and set the following properties:

▪Save Simulation Files: Specify the designs whose Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation files you want to save.

▪Save Log files: Choose whether to save log files to the design directories or not. This option is enabled by default.

▪Output Auxiliary File Types: Specify the extensions of simulation output files that you want to preserve for each design. Output files whose extensions you do not specify are deleted.

▪Simultaneous Jobs: Set the number of design simulations to run concurrently.

▪Compute Processes: 1. This value disables the Compute Processes property. Instead, you specify the cores to run with each design simulation in the Job Submit Command. See step 1c.

When setting the numbers for Simultaneous Jobs and Compute Processes, check that you have enough cores available (simultaneous jobs * compute processes).

For more information, see Run Settings Reference.

b) Select the Compute Resource node and set the following properties:

▪Type: Windows HPC Cluster

▪STAR-CCM+ Command Line Options: Set command line options to pass to the design simulations, such as License Options or other Simcenter STAR-CCM+ options, see Command-Line Reference.

Example: -power (Power Session licensing).

c) Select the Compute Resource > Windows HPC Cluster node and specify the following cluster settings:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6797

▪Job Submit Command: Set the command to submit each design simulation to the cluster queue.

The default value (job submit /numcores:8) is set up for a cluster running the HPC Job Manager, where each design simulation is submitted on eight cores. The scheduler allocates the requested cores from the available nodes.

▪Script File: Set the UNC path and the full name of your job submission script on the cluster. Make sure that the job submission script meets the General Job Submission Script Requirements and has execute permission.

For more information, see Compute Resource Reference.

2. Select File > Save and save the project file.

3. Transfer the Design Manager project file (*.dmprj) and associated input files such as the reference simulation file (*.sim) and custom Java macro files (*.java) to your cluster project root directory.

4. Run the design studies.

As the general job submission mode leverages the client-server capability of Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you can run design studies directly from the Graphical User Interface (GUI) on your workstation. Alternatively, you can run design studies on your cluster from a batch client.

Method Procedure

Running directly from a local GUI client

For more information, see Working With Remote Servers.

If you want to run the Design Manager server remotely from your local workstation, you require remote shell access to the cluster without password prompting.

1. On your local workstation, launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and click (Load a File).

2. In the Load a File dialog, set Type to Design Manager Project.

3. Activate the Remote Server option and set the remote server properties:

▪Remote Host: Specify the name of a cluster node that has the ability to submit jobs to the queue, such as the head node. If you require the domain name to connect from your local machine, include it here.

▪Remote User: Specify the user name that is required to log into the specified remote host.

▪Remote Shell: Choose the type of remote shell command.

4. In the File text box, specify the UNC path and the full name of the Design Manager project file in your cluster project root directory.

5. In the Command text box, insert the UNC path and the name of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ executable on the cluster.

To activate the Unlicensed Design Manager Server license scheme, add - dmnoshare (optional). For more information, see Design Manager Licensing.

6. Click OK.

The Design Manager object tree loads.

7. Run the design studies interactively:

▪To run a specific design study, right-click the design study node and select Run Study.

▪To run all design studies sequentially from first to last, right-click the Design Studies manager node and select Run All Studies.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6798

8. If your local workstation restarts or shuts down during the night, you can disconnect from and reconnect to the remote Design Manager server from your local client, see Making Client-Server Connections.

The Design Manager server remains active on the head node until you close the project.

Running from a batch client

For more information, see Running the Client in Batch.

1. On a cluster node that has the ability to submit jobs to the Windows HPC scheduler, such as the head node, submit the Design Manager project in batch from the command line.

Example:

[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]\star]bin\starccm+ -batch run [PROJECT_ROOT_DIR]\[PROJECT].dmprj [-dmnoshare] [- passtodesign <options>]

where:

▪[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR] is the UNC path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation directory on your cluster.

▪[PROJECT_ROOT_DIR] is the UNC path to the project root directory.

▪[PROJECT] is the name of your Design Manager project file.

▪-dmnoshare activates the Unlicensed Design Manager Server license scheme. Omitting this option uses the Default license scheme. For more information, see Design Manager Licensing.

▪-passtodesign <options> allows you to pass additional simulation command line options, such as license options, to the design simulations. Passing simulation command line options directly from the command line is useful for machine-specific or user-specific options, which you do not want to save within your Design Manager project file (see step 1b). However, command line options that require double quotes are not supported—you must set these options in the STAR-CCM+ Command Line Options property. For more information, see Design Manager Options.

Note: If [PROJECT_ROOT_DIR] or [PROJECT] contains spaces, you must pass the Design Manager project file with quotes:

[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]\star\bin\starccm+ -batch run "[PROJECT_ROOT_DIR]\[PROJECT].dmprj" [-dmnoshare] [- passtodesign <options>]

2. To follow the progress of your design studies, you can connect to and disconnect from the running Design Manager server, see Making Client-Server Connections.

The Design Manager server shuts down automatically as soon as all design simulations are complete.

The Design Manager server submits the specified number of simultaneous design simulations to the queue. As soon as one design simulation completes, Design Manager submits the next design simulation. This job submission procedure continues until all design simulations are complete.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6799

The output from the Design Manager server is displayed in the Output window. The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ servers for each design simulation are visible in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server list.

Note: The Design Manager server does not have any capabilities to interact with the job scheduler on your cluster. Design Manager can not detect what type of scheduler is used on your cluster. The tracking of each design—the detection of failure or completion—solely relies on files that are written to disk by each design simulation. Therefore, when a Design Manager project submits a design simulation to the cluster and the submission of the simulation fails or anything unexpected happens in the scheduler, the Design Manager server can not detect this failure. However, as soon as a resource is assigned and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is executed, then Design Manager can detect failures. Design Manager marks the design simulation as failed and moves to the next design simulation to complete the design study.

Contents:

General Job Submission Script Requirements

General Job Submission Script Requirements

When running a design study, the Design Manager server passes specific instructions to each design simulation. These instructions are communicated via files that are written to the temporary directory .mdxruntime that is located in the same directory as the project artifact directory. When a design simulation is submitted to the HPC Job Manager, the Design Manager server executes the user job submission script in the temporary directory .mdxruntime\$project\$study\$design. The .mdxruntime\ $project\$study\$design directory contains all the files that Design Manager requires to execute the design simulation.

The Design Manager server does not interact with the HPC Job Manager on your cluster. For this reason, in the job submission script, you must read the following files from .mdxruntime\$project\$study\$design and redirect them to the Design Manager server:

• dm_design_execute_options.txt

This file contains additional command line options, such as license details, and other options that you define in the design study settings.

• dm_design_output_info.msg

This file contains the name of the log file that Design Manager expects to be available when the design simulation executes.

Design Manager automatically changes to the job working directory to read these two files.

Example

The following script code shows an example of a Windows Batch Script (*.bat) for general job submission:

@echo off

REM Design Manager definitions REM ---------------------------------- REM dm_design_execute_options.txt contains starccm+ command line arguments. REM dm_design_output_info.msg contains log output file name to dump. set /p STARTCASE=< dm_design_execute_options.txt

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6800

set /p CASELOG=< dm_design_output_info.msg

REM Set STAR-CCM+ installation directory REM ---------------------------------- REM For [STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR], set the full network path (UNC) to the STARCCM+ installation directory on the cluster set STARCCMHOME=[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]

REM Log node information to the design log REM ---------------------------------- echo Job nodes: %CCP_NODES% >> %DMLOGS%

REM Call STAR-CCM+ REM ---------------------------------- %STARCCMHOME%\star\bin\starccm+ -mpi ms -np %CCP_NUMCPUS% %STARTCASE% >> %CASELOG%

The script code checks for the files dm_design_execute_options.txt and dm_design_output_info.msg and assigns the content to the following independent variables:

• STARTCASE—contains the additional command line options

• CASELOG—contains the name of the log file

These two variables are then used when calling Simcenter STAR-CCM+ at the end of the script, where:

-mpi ms allows you to run design simulations across multiple nodes using Microsoft MPI. -np %CCP_NUMCPUS% specifies the number of cores to run with each design simulation. %CCP_NUMCPUS% automatically detects the number of cores from the Job Submit Command property.

Re-Running a Design Study with Modified Settings

After running a design study you can re-run the design study with modified settings.

You can modify every property of a design study, such as the study type, the input parameters, the responses, the scenes and plots for post-processing, or the run and resource settings.

To re-run a design study with modified settings:

1. In the Design Manager project, right-click the respective design study node and select Clear Study.

The result data are removed from the Design Manager project.

2. Clearing a design study does not remove the Design Manager output files from the disk.

▶If you want to remove the output files from the disk, navigate to the study artifact directory and delete it manually.

▶If you keep the previous output files, Design Manager uses subscripts for the new design artifact directories in your study artifact directory.

3. Modify the properties of the design study as required.

4. Select File > Save and save the project file.

5. Run the design study.

Stopping, Extending, and Resuming a Design Study

You can stop, extend, and resume one or more design studies in a single action.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6801

To stop a design study:

1. In the Design Manager project, right-click the respective design study node and select Stop Study.

Executing this action on multiple selected studies stops all the studies in sequence.

Stopping a design study prevents Design Manager from starting new design simulations. Design simulations that are already running are not killed but run until completion.

If you stopped a design study, you can resume it where it picks up from the last completed design:

2. Right-click the design study node and select Run Study.

Design Manager submits the outstanding design simulations.

If a design study completes but further design simulations are needed to achieve the desired results, you can extend the design study:

3. Adapt the settings of the design study as required.

Example: To extend a study, you can decrease the increment of the input parameter values or increase the number of designs to run.

4. Select File > Save and save the project file.

5. Run the design study.

Design Manager automatically detects which designs are already evaluated and submits design simulations for the additional designs.

Resuming a Design Study after Abort

Design Manager can abort for reasons such as hardware conflicts or lack of system resources. When it does abort, you can resume the aborted design study from the last completed design.

You can also manually abort one or more running design studies. In contrast to stopping a design study, where the running design simulations run until completion, aborting a design study kills the running design simulations. This is particularly useful if you want to cancel a design study without having to wait until the running design simulations complete.

To manually abort one or more running design studies from the UI:

1. Right-click the design study node, (or one of a selection), and select Abort Study.

To manually abort a running design study in batch mode:

2. Depending on your operating system, do one of the following:

▶On Windows, place a file with the file name DM_ABORT in the run directory; an empty text file is sufficient for this purpose.

▶On Linux, use the following line command:

% touch DM_ABORT

You can customize the abort file name in your Design Manager project, see Design Manager Reference.

Design Manager kills the running design simulations. The results of the completed designs are available in the study artifact directory.

To resume after abort:

3. Run the design study.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6802

Design Manager automatically detects the completed designs and runs the remaining design simulations until the design study completes.

Note: Design Manager can only resume from the last completed design, if the Design Manager project is automatically saved when each design simulation completes. For this reason, you are advised to always activate the Auto Save option (see Run Settings Reference).

Re-running Selected Designs

Design Manager allows you to re-run selected designs of a design study. This is particularly useful for designs that failed during the study run due to runtime or licensing failures.

Design Manager uses the settings of the design study to re-run selected designs. Re-running a design updates the design results, such as responses, performance value, or feasability. Note, that re-running a baseline design can change the performance value of other designs in the design study.

In Pre-Allocation Mode, the license reservation for the selected designs is either based on the specified number of Simultaneous Jobs or on the number of selected designs:

• If the number of selected designs is smaller than the number of simultaneous jobs, then the license reservation is based on the number of selected designs.

• If the number of selected designs is higher than or equal to the number of simultaneous jobs, then the license reservation is based on the number of simultaneous jobs.

You can add and remove responses in the design study before you re-run selected designs. Adding and removing paramaters is not supported.

Design Manager allows you to re-run designs using one of the following methods:

• Re-running all designs of a design set

• Re-running selected designs from an output table

• Re-running selected designs from a plot

To re-run all designs of a design set:

1. Right-click the Design Sets > [design set] node, such as Design Sets > Error, and select Rerun Designs.

For information on creating additional design sets, see Analyzing the Results of a Design Study.

Using <Ctrl>, you can select multiple design sets within a design study. Designs that are listed in several of the selected design sets are run only once.

To re-run selected designs from an output table:

2. Open the output table for a design set that contains the designs of interest. See Tabulating Designs.

3. In the output table, select a row of a design that you want to re-run.

Using <Ctrl>, you can select multiple rows.

4. Right-click and select Rerun Designs.

To re-run selected designs from a plot:

5. Open a plot that displays the designs of interest. See Creating XY Plots and Creating Parallel Coordinates

Plots.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6803

6. Select the data point (XY plot) or data line (Parallel Coordinates plot) of a design that you want to re-run. Use <Ctrl> to select multiple designs.

7. Right-click and select Rerun Designs.

To stop or abort a design run, you must stop or abort the respective design study:

8. Right-click the Design Studies > [design study] node and select Stop Study or Abort Study, respectively.

Running a Design Study with Local CAD Update

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, CAD Clients provide bi-directional communication between CAD packages and Design Manager. When running a design study, Design Manager modifies the design parameters imported from the CAD package as required by the study. The CAD geometry is then updated natively in the CAD package and re-imported in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for the mesh and solver stages.

Before you begin, check whether the following pre-requisites are fulfilled:

• CAD package, CAD Clients and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are installed on the same Windows machine.

• Job Manager server is installed on the Linux cluster. User accounts are set up for the Job Manager server. For more details, refer to Adding a Job Manager Connection.

This process of updating geometry, meshing, solving, and extracting the final results, is controlled by Job Manager.

The entire workflow is outlined in the following steps:

• CAD geometry is updated locally on the Windows machine with Design Manager server and CAD package.

• The simulation file is saved after the native CAD update.

• The saved simulation file is transferred automatically using Job Manager to the registered Linux cluster where the meshing and solving stages are executed.

A flowchart of the process is shown as follows:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6804

To set up a design study with Local CAD Update through Job Manager:

Launch and set up CAD Client in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. In the CAD package, under Simcenter STAR-CCM+ tab, select Transfer Geometry. For more details see "Transferring Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+" in the documentation for the specific CAD client.

The CAD data are transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and can be viewed under the Geometry > CAD Client Models node. The CAD parameters and responses transferred with the model can be accessed by Design Manager.

2. In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation file, select the Geometry > CAD Client Models > [cad model] node and review the following properties:

Properties Setting

CAD file

Specifies the full name of the CAD geometry file, including the extension, which is updated in the CAD package required by Design Manager.

The file name is transferred automatically from the CAD package. An example of a NX file name is: geometry.prt

CAD File Location

Specifies the location of the CAD file on your local machine (for the CAD package to access).

If necessary, set the location of the CAD file. An example path is: C:\NX_geometry

CAD-Client Update Mode

Specifies whether Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for the CAD package is located on the local machine or on a remote machine.

To execute Local CAD update, select Local.

3. Save the simulation file so that any changes to setup are updated for Design Manager.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6805

Set up the Design Manager Project to execute Local CAD Update:

4. Create a Design Manager project based on the simulation file. For the detailed workflow, refer to Creating a

Design Manager Project.

5. In the Design Manager project file, set up a design study where you can add the imported CAD parameters. For more details refer to Setting Up a Design Study.

6. Select the Design Studies > [design study] > Settings > Compute Resources node and set Type to Local CAD Update.

A Local CAD Update node is added underneath Compute Resources.

Note: The Local CAD Update option is not applicable to a CAD Robustness Study. To run a CAD Robustness study locally, choose the Direct option.

7. Local CAD Update requires one Direct compute resource for the CAD update and one Job Manager compute resource for meshing and solving. See also: Compute Resource Reference.

a) By default, you have one Default Direct compute resource created in the Design Manager project. If necessary for your setup, for example because you must specify additional Command Line Options, you can create your own Direct compute resource. For more details refer to STAR-CCM+ Command Line Options.

b) To add a Job Manager compute resource, right-click the Tools > Compute Resources node and select New Resource > Job Manager.

c) Proceed to configure the Job Manager compute resource. Refer to Job Manager Configuration for details.

Note: For the Job Manager configuration, you must use the Submission Template that provides the same version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ that was used to save the simulation file.

8. To specify the compute resources for Local CAD Update, select the Design Studies > [design study] > Settings > Compute Resources > Local CAD Update node and set the properties as follows:

Property Setting

Compute Resource for CAD Update [Default Direct]

Compute Resource for successive Design run [Job Manager]

For more details, refer to Compute Resource Reference for Local CAD Update.

9. Select the Design Studies > [design study] > Settings > Run Settings node and set the properties. For more details refer to Run Settings Reference.

Note: You specify a suitable number of Compute Processes for your Linux cluster.

10.Right-click on the Design Studies > [design study] node and select Run Study.

Monitoring a Design Study

In the GUI, you can check the progress of a running design study in the progress and status bar beneath the explorer window. You can also view post-processing objects while a design study runs, allowing you to view progress interactively.

To track the status of all the design simulations of a design study in tabular form:

1. Select the Design Sets > All node and select Open Output Table.

The output table opens in the Graphics window and displays all designs of the design study together with their respective input parameter and response values. The State of a design indicates the current stage of the design simulation. The Performance value of a design is a rating value that allows you to judge the design. For more detail, see Output Table Reference.

As soon as a design simulation completes successfully, that is when State equals , you can view the exported scenes and plots of that particular design:

2. In the output table, right-click the design of interest and select Open Scenes > [scene], where [scene] is the scene you want to visualize. For plots, you select Open Plots > [plot].

The scene or plot opens in the Graphics window.

Once you open a scene or a plot, a snapshot is created automatically. See Snapshots Reference.

If you prepared project plots before the run, you can monitor the progress of the design study using these plots:

3. In the object tree, right-click the respective Plots > [project plot] node and select Open.

The project plot opens in the Graphics window. Once a design simulation completes, a new data point appears in the plot.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6807

Design Manager automatically updates the marker of the best design and the path to the best design during the run. For more information, see Plots Reference.

Analyzing the Results of a Design Study

In Design Manager, post-processing objects reference design sets. Design sets contain one or more designs, according to how you define them. You can view results in tables, scenes, plots, or project plots.

The following predefined design sets are available:

• All—contains all designs evaluated during the study.

• Successful—contains all designs apart from those that encountered an error.

• Feasible (not for DOE and CAD Robustness studies)—contains the designs that meet all constraints in the study.

• Error—contains the designs that encountered an error during the run.

For more information, see Design Sets Reference.

To create additional design sets for a design study:

1. Right-click the Design Studies > [design study] > Design Sets node, and select New Design Set.

In the Graphics window, the associated output table opens and displays all designs of the design study.

2. To define a subset of designs, you can set the designs manually or use the filter capabilities of the output table:

Method Procedure

Setting the designs manually 1. In the project tree, select the associated design set node.

2. Set Designs to the designs of interest using the object selector.

Using the filter capabilities of the output table

1. In the output table header, next to the design property of interest, click .

2. In the Set Query Rule dialog, set the property to the desired range and click OK. For more information, see Output Table Filter Query Rules.

The design set and its output table is updated to match the query rule.

Design Manager also allows you to create designs sets interactively from project plots or from output tables of other design sets. For more information, see Exploring the Analysis in Design Manager.

Tabulating Designs

In Design Manager, output tables allow you to tabulate the designs of a design set and their properties in the Graphics window. You can also export the designs of a design set to a *.csv table file.

To open the output table of a design set in the Graphics window:

1. Right-click the Design Sets > [design set] node and select Open Output Table.

The output table appears in the Graphics window and displays the properties of each design—such as its parameter and response values. For more information, see Output Table Reference.

If a study response has a constraint defined and the constraint is not satisfied for a particular value, the affected value is highlighted in red in the design table. A tool tip explains the violation as illustrated in the following example:

Design Manager allows you to reorder the designs in an output table. For example, to find the best design in a design set, you can order the designs according to their performance value.

To reorder the designs in an output table:

2. In the output table, click the header of the design property by which you want to reorder the table, such as Performance.

The designs are reordered to display the property in ascending order. Clicking the header again reverses the order.

If an output table contains many columns, it can be useful to hide or change the position of columns to improve the readability of the table.

To toggle the visibility of columns in an output table:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6810

3. In the upper right corner of the output table, click .

A drop-down menu opens that lists the headers of the columns.

4. Deselect or select the columns that you want to hide or show, respectively.

5. To close the drop-down menu, click anywhere off the menu in the Graphics window.

Design Manager stores the visibility of the columns for the output table.

When you add an input parameter or a response to the design study of the tabulated design set, Design Manager automatically adds the corresponding column to the output table. Removing an input parameter or a response, removes the corresponding column. The first three columns in an output table always list Design#, Name, and State of the designs—you can not change the position of these columns.

To change the position of a column that lists a parameter, a response, or Performance:

6. Click the header of the column that you want to move and, while still holding down the left mouse button, drag the mouse until the pointer hovers over the target position.

7. To finish moving, release the mouse button.

Design Manager stores the positions of the columns in the output table. However, the following actions restore the default column order:

◦ Changing the study type of the design study

◦ Adding or removing input parameters or responses in the design study

For more information on interacting with designs in output tables, see Exploring the Analysis in Design Manager.

To export the design information of a dataset to a table file:

8. Right-click the Design Sets > [design set] node and select Export to CSV....

9. In the Export to CSV dialog, save the design set as *.csv.

Visualizing Scenes and Plots

When each design simulation completes, Design Manager exports chosen scenes and plots and makes them available for you to view.

In Design Manager, a snapshot allows you to display a specific scene or a specific plot for the designs within a design set. Locking a snapshot to a specific design allows you to compare the design with other designs in the design set.

To create a snapshot:

1. Right-click the Snapshots node and select New > [snapshot type], where [snapshot type] can be Scene Snapshot or Plot Snapshot.

2. Select the new snapshot node and set the following properties:

◦ Design Study: The design study from which to extract the snapshot data.

◦ Design Set: The design set within the specified design study from which to extract data.

◦ Scene/Plot: The scene or plot of interest.

Design displays the name of the design that is visualized in the specified scene or plot.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6811

To add additional information to the snapshot display in the Graphics window, such as the name or the performance value of the visualized design:

3. Select the Snapshots > [snapshot] > Annotations node and set Annotations to Design Name or Performance Value, respectively.

Design Manager allows you to create and add additional simple text annotations. For more information, see Tools Reference—Annotations.

You can step through the designs of the specified design set using the Design Manager Snapshot toolbar, see Toolbar Reference:

Alternatively, you can select a design of interest in an output table or in a project plot. The snapshot is then updated automatically to reflect the selected design. For more information, see Exploring the Analysis in Design Manager.

To compare snapshots for different designs:

4. Create multiple snapshots, where each snapshot displays the same scene or plot.

5. In the Graphics window, arrange the snapshot panels side by side.

6. For each snapshot, select the snapshot node and set the following properties:

◦ Lock Design: Activate (activates the Design property).

◦ Design: Set the design you want to compare.

When you unlock one of the snapshots, you can step through the designs of the specified design set and compare the locked designs with the remaining ones.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6812

You can interact with snapshots that refer to scenes and plots that are exported as STAR-View File (see Setting Up a Design Study) as you would with the respective scene or plot in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. For example, you can rotate the view, zoom in and out, or play animations. To improve understanding of results, you can link multiple snapshots so that they move in tandem as you interact with one of them.

To set up a link among snapshots:

7. Using <Ctrl>, multi-select the snapshots you wish to link.

8. Right-click and select Linked View.

9. Interact with one of the snapshots.

Creating XY Plots

XY plots are two-dimensional graphs that allow you to display the relationship between two variables. These plots can show history, 2D relations, or Pareto analysis.

You can create XY plots before you run a design study, while it is running, and when it is complete. If you create an XY plot before you run the design study or while it is running, it is updated continuously as the study progresses.

1. To create an XY plot:

▶Right-click the Plots node and select New Plot > XY Plot.

▶Alternatively, right-click Design Studies > [design study] and select Create Plot to choose one of the following XY plot you want to create:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6814

Plot Type Example

History Plot

A history plot shows by default a parameter or a response against the design number.

Parameter vs Response Plot

A parameter vs response plot shows by default the first listed response against the first listed parameter.

Response vs Response Plot

A response vs response plot shows by default the second listed response against the first listed response.

Pareto Plot

A Pareto plot shows by default the second listed response against the first listed response. This plot is particularly useful for multi-objective optimization, where you want to display the tradeoff between two competing objectives.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6815

Plot Type Example

Bubble Plot

In addition to the information shown by a Response vs Response Plot, a bubble plot shows (by default) the first design parameter as bubble size and the second parameter as bubble color. .

For more details of the bubble plot refer to Bubble Plot Objects Reference.

The latter method is a quicker approach since it automatically assigns the predefined data types to its axes on the selected XY plot. You can adjust the data type under Plots > Data Series. See Axis Data Type for details on each type.

For bubble plots you can also adjust the date used for under Plots > [bubble plot] > Bubble Style > Size Scaling Data / Color Scaling Data.

To add data to the plot:

2. Right-click the Plots > [project plot] > Data Series node and select Add Data.

3. In the Add Data Providers to Plot dialog, select the design study from which to extract data and click OK.

Alternatively, you can drag-and-drop the respective Design Studies > [design study] node onto the Data Series node of the plot or into the visualization display of the plot.

A new data series, which is named after the selected design study, is added to the Data Series node. If you select multiple design studies, multiple data series are created automatically.

4. Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] node and set Input Design Sets to the design sets whose data you want to display in the plot.

Alternatively, you can drag the respective Design Studies > [design study] Design Sets > [design set] node into the visualization display of the plot. When you drop the design set, a menu opens that allows you to add the design set to an existing data series in the plot or to create a new data series.

To set the type of data that you want to display on the plot axes:

5. Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Bottom Axis Data node and set Type to one of Parameter, Response, Design Number, Design Status and Design Performance. See Axis Data Type for details on each type.

Note: If Design Status is chosen as an axis type, the corresponding axis automatically sets the range from 0 to 1.

You can drag and drop parameters and responses onto an axis in an XY plot.

6. Repeat the last step for the Left Axis Data node.

When you add a new data series with the same input design study as a previously added data series, then the new data series uses the same axis data by default.

For a Multiple objective tradeoff study (Pareto front), you can visualize the Pareto ranking for the designs of each Pareto cycle:

7. Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] node and set Render Mode to Pareto.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6816

By default, Design Manager displays the design ranking for the last cycle:

8. To plot the ranking for another cycle, select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Pareto Ranks node and set Cycle to the cycle of interest. You can select multiple cycles if required.

Alternatively, you can step through the cycles using the Design Manager Snapshot toolbar. See Toolbars Reference.

You can also create XY plots directly from the design study of interest:

9. Right-click the respective design study node and select Create Plot > [plot type], for more details of the XY plot type refer to XY Plot Type.

Additionally, you can create a History Plot directly from a response or a parameter:

10.Right-click the respective response or parameter node and select Create History Plot.

The plot opens in the Graphics window.

Depending on the study type, Design Manager allows you to mark specific designs in an XY plot.

To mark the data point of the best design, where the best design is the design with the highest performance value:

11.Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Best Design node and activate Visible.

The respective data point is marked in the plot and is listed in the legend.

In a history plot, you can display the path that the design study follows in reaching the best design:

12.Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Best Design History node and activate Visible.

A line displays the path from the first to the best design.

To mark the data point of the baseline design, where the baseline design is the first design that Design Manager runs in the design study:

13.Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Baseline Design node and activate Visible.

The following screenshot displays a history plot, where the best design, the best design history, and the baseline design are visible:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6817

To determine the value of a particular data point:

14.Hover the mouse over the data point of interest.

The coordinates are displayed next to the pointer.

You can export the data series that are displayed in an XY plot:

15.To export data series, do one of the following:

▶To export all data series in a plot, right-click the plot node and select Export.

▶To export specific data series, multi-select the respective data series nodes, right-click, and select Export.

16.In the Export to CSV dialog, save the design set as *.csv.

Plotting Multiple Data Series in an XY Plot

Design Manager allows you to add multiple data series to a single XY plot. These data series can refer to the same design study or to different design studies within your Design Manager project.

Referring to the same design study is useful when you want to display multiple variables of a design study— parameters, responses, design numbers, design status or design performance—in a single chart display. For example, you can view two different responses versus a parameter in the same plot. Viewing the variables on different axes improves the readability of such plots, especially when the variables have widely different scales of values, such as meters and Pascals.

Example:

Referring to various design studies is useful mainly for optimization studies. Suppose you run a weighted sum of multiple objectives optimization study. By looking at the responses it appears that there is possibly a competitive relationship between them. To explore this possibility, you run a Pareto optimization study. Showing the data from both of these studies on the same plot can indicate the part of the Pareto front on which the weighted sum study was focused.

Example:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6819

To plot multiple variables from the same or from different design studies:

1. Create an XY plot.

2. For each pair of variables that you want to display for a certain design set:

a) Add a data series and select the design study and design set from which you want to extract the variables.

b) Set the axes data that you want to display, such as parameters and responses, for the default axes—at the bottom and at the left.

To use multiple axes:

3. Right-click the [project plot] > Axes node and select New Axis > [position], where [position] can be Right or Top.

4. For the variable that you want to display on the new axis, select the respective [data series] > [axis] Data node, where [axis] Data can be Left Axis Data or Bottom Axis Data, and set Axis to Right Axis or Top Axis, respectively.

For more information, see Plots Reference.

Creating Parallel Coordinates Plots

Parallel Coordinates plots are two-dimensional graphs that allow you to display the relationships between multiple variables at the same time.

You can create Parallel Coordinates plots before you run a design study, while it is running, and when it is complete.

1. To create a Parallel Coordinates plot:

▶Right-click the Plots node and select New Plot > Parallel Coordinates.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6820

▶Alternatively, right-click Design Studies > [design study] and select Create Plot > Parallel Coordinates.

The latter method is a quicker approach since it automatically assigns the responses to its axes on the Parallel Coordinates plot. You can adjust the responses or add parameters to the plot under Plots > Data Series.

To add data to the plot:

2. Right-click the [project plot] > Data Series node and select Add Data.

3. In the Add Data Providers to Plot dialog, select the design study from which to extract data and click OK.

Alternatively, you can drag-and-drop the respective Design Studies > [design study] node onto the Data Series node of the plot or into the visualization display of the plot.

A new data series, which is named after the selected design study, is added to the Data Series node. If you select multiple design studies, multiple data series are created automatically.

By default, a Parallel Coordinates plot displays all designs in the selected design study. To display a specific design set:

4. Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] node and set Input Design Sets to the design sets of interest.

Alternatively, you can drag the respective Design Studies > [design study] > Design Sets > [design set] node into the visualization display of the plot. When you drop the design set, a menu opens that allows you to add the design set to an existing data series in the plot or to create a new data series.

For each variable that you want to display, add an axis to the plot:

5. Right-click the [project plot] > Coordinates node and select New Axis.

The Graphics window updates to display the plot axis. The following nodes are added to the object tree:

◦ [project plot] > Coordinates > Axis [n]: Allows you to specify how the respective axis is plotted (such as the axis title, labels and ticks).

◦ [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Axis [n] Data: Here, you specify what should be plotted along the axis.

6. To assign data to an axis, select the respective Axis [n] Data node and set Type to one of Parameter, Response, Design Number, Design Status and Design Performance. See Axis Data Type for details on each type.

You can drag and drop parameters and responses onto an axis in a Parallel Coordinates plots.

When you add a new data series with the same input design study as a previously added data series, then the new data series uses the same axis data by default.

The plot displays a single data line for each design in the selected design study.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6821

For a Multiple objective tradeoff study (Pareto front), you can visualize the Pareto ranking for the designs of each Pareto cycle:

7. Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] node and set Render Mode to Pareto.

By default, Design Manager displays the design ranking for the last cycle:

8. To plot the ranking for another cycle, select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Pareto Ranks node and set Cycle to the cycle of interest. You can select multiple cycles if required.

Alternatively, you can step through the cycles using the Design Manager Snapshot toolbar. See Toolbars Reference.

You can also create a Parallel Coordinates plot directly from the design study of interest:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6822

9. Right-click the respective design study node and select Create Plot > Parallel Coordinates. By default, the plot shows an axis for each response in the design study. You can modify the default settings as required.

Depending on the study type, Design Manager allows you to mark specific designs in the plot.

To mark the best design, where the best design is the design with the highest performance value:

10.Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Best Design node and activate Visible.

The respective data line is marked in the plot and is listed in the legend.

To mark the baseline design, where the baseline design is the first design that Design Manager runs in the design study:

11.Select the [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] > Baseline Design node and activate Visible.

The following screenshot displays a Parallel Coordinates plot, where the best design and the baseline design are visible:

To determine the variable values for a design:

12.Hover the curser over the data line of interest.

The hovered-over line is emphasized, the other lines are muted. A tooltip appears next to the curser.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6823

13.To control the information that is displayed in the tooltip, select the [project plot] node and set Tooltip Display to one of the following options:

◦ Aggregated Totals Only: Displays the number of aggregated data lines under the curser for each data series.

◦ First Hit: In addition to the aggregated hit totals, displays the variable values of the first data line under the curser. The first data line is the last rendered line in the last rendered data series.

◦ First Two Hits: Displays the aggregated hit totals and the variable values of the first two data lines under the curser.

◦ First Three Hits: Displays the aggregated hit totals and the variable values of the first three data lines under the curser.

When you select a data line, notations of the variable values of the design are displayed at the axes.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6824

If you select multiple designs within the same data series, notations are hidden to avoid plot clutter.

By default, the axes are spanned across the entire plot area with equal distance between the axes.

14.To change the position of an axis, do one of the following:

▶Select the [project plot] > Coordinates > Axis [n] node and set x-Position to the relative x-position in the Graphics window, defined over the interval [0,1].

▶In the Graphics window, select the axis of interest, drag it horizontally to the desired position, and drop it.

You can move an axis to any position, which allows you to change the order of the axes in the plot.

15.To respan the axes, right-click the [project plot] node and select Respan Axes.

To look at smaller changes of the plotted data, you can zoom in/out between two axes (which affects the two surrounding axes) or on a single axis:

16.In the Graphics window, click on a space between the two axes of interest or select a single axis, respectively, and use the middle mouse button to zoom in/out.

For more information, see Plots Reference.

Speeding Up the Setup of Parallel Coordinate Plots

Speeding Up the Setup of Parallel Coordinate Plots

Depending on the number of axes and data series that you want to display in a Parallel Coordinates plot, the setup can be time consuming and require multiple mouse clicks. For this reason, Design Manager provides various options to accelerate the setup.

You can accelerate the setup in the following situations:

• Defining the Initial Setup

• Plotting all Responses in a Design Study

• Editing all Axis Data

To speed up the initial setup of a Parallel Coordinates plot:

1. Right-click the Plots node and select New Plot > Parallel Coordinates.

2. Right-click the Plots > [project plot] node and select Quick Setup.

The following Parallel Coordinates Quick Setup dialog opens:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6825

3. In the dialog, set the following properties:

◦ Data Providers: Select the design study whose designs you want to display in the plot. By default, a parallel coordinates plot displays all designs in the design study.

◦ Axis Data: Select the data type that you want to extract from the designs and display on the axes of the plot. For more details of the data type refer to [axis] Data.

4. In the Axis Order group-box, define the order of the axes in the plot—the first entry in the list is the leftmost axis in the plot:

a) Select the axis in the list whose position you want to change.

b) Use the Order buttons on the right side of the group-box to modify the axis position.

5. To hide axis labels and ticks in the plot, deactivate Show axis labels and ticks.

Plots without axes labels and ticks allow a faster interaction with the plot in the Graphics window (for example when interactively changing the position of an axis).

6. Click OK.

Design Manager automatically adds the required axes and data series to the plot.

When you use the Quick Setup option on a non-empty plot, the entire plot is reconstructed as defined in the Parallel Coordinates Quick Setup dialog. All plot settings, such as line style or font size, are reset to their default values.

To retain your previous plot settings, use the Quick Setup option on the data series of the plot:

7. Right click the Plots > [project plot] > Data Series > [data series] node and select Quick Setup.

The Parallel Coordinates Quick Setup dialog opens. The Data Providers box is greyed out.

8. Modify the axis data, the axis order, or the visibility of the axis labels and ticks as required and click OK.

Design Manager updates the project plot accordingly.

To quickly create a Parallel Coordinates plot that displays all responses in a design study:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6826

9. Right-click the respective Design Studies > [design study] node and select Create Plot > Parallel Coordinates.

For a CAD Robustness study, this action creates a Parallel Coordinates plot that displays all input parameters and the Design Status.

To quickly edit all referencing axis types of the axis in the plot:

10.Multi-select the [project plot] > Coordinates > Axis [n] nodes, right-click, and select Edit referencing axis types....

11.In the Multiple Objects dialog, click Expand/Contract Tree, then Expand/Contract Values.

The dialog gives you quick access to all the axis types and displayed variables. You can modify the referenced axes separately.

12.Edit the axes as required and click OK.

Asynchronous Post-Processing

Design Manager allows you to create additional post-processing objects in a single simulation (design or reference) after a design study has been run, and then executes an update on all designs so that their simulation files also receive the additional objects. This methodology works best when you save the simulation files for each design.

To create and apply post-processing after a design study has completed its run:

1. Right-click the Design Sets > [design set] node and select Open Output Table.

2. For a design within whose simulation file you wish to insert additional post-processing objects, right-click the entry in the Output Table and select Open for Post Processing.

Note: This option is disabled if you chose to not save the design simulations files.

3. In the Open simulation for post processing window, select any process options and click OK.

The corresponding simulation file opens in post-processing only mode. In this mode, you can only add or modify post-processing objects such as reports, scenes and plots. You can also add or modify derived parts.

4. In the design simulation file, create any additional derived parts that you require (or modify existing ones) and similarly add or modify reports, scenes or plots.

5. When you are done with making changes to the chosen design simulation, do the following:

a) Close the design simulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6827

b) In the Apply Changes? dialog click Apply.

Design Manager applies the changes you made in the design simulation to the reference simulation. In a later step you apply the changes from the reference simulation to all the other design simulations so that they are synchronized.

Because the reference simulation now contains objects that the other design simulations do not, all designs are marked out of date as shown:

6. Before you update all the designs with the new objects, you can add or modify post-processing objects within the design study itself in order to view them once you update the results. You can do this as follows:

a) To add additional scenes, select the Design Studies > [design study] > Scenes node and update scenes using the Custom Editor within the Properties window.

b) To add additional plots, select the Design Studies > [design study] > Plots node and update plots using the Custom Editor within the Properties window.

7. To propagate the post-processing changes throughout the designs, right-click the Design Studies > [design study] node and select Update Results.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6828

Alternatively you can update results for selected designs only as follows:

▶In the Output Table, multi-select target designs using the <ctrl> key, then right-click and select Update Results.

▶Right-click the Design Studies > [design study] > Design Sets > [design set] node and select Update Results.

Note: You are advised to do the synchronization step using the same version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ as you used for adding or modifying post-prcessing objects.

When running the Update Results operation Design Manager opens each simulation, synchronizes the postprocessing changes and extracts the new output to the Design Manager project. If there is no Simulation file present for a particular design, Design Manager re-runs the designs to generate the results.

As an alternative to Step 1, if you do not have the design simulations saved while running the study you can open the reference simulation for post-processing. To do this step, right-click the Simulations > [reference simulation] node and select Open for Post Processing..

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6829

After making changes in the reference simulation, you can propagate these changes to the design simulation as described above.

Exploring the Analysis in Design Manager

Follow these steps to assess the design connectivity between output tables, snapshots, and project plots.

In Design Manager, output tables, snapshots, and project plots are connected to each other. When you select a specific design in one of these post-processing objects the others are synchronized automatically to reflect the selected design.

To visualize the design connectivity:

1. Arrange multiple panels in the Graphics window. A panel is an individual section of the Graphics window that contains an output table, a project plot, or a snapshot (scene or plot). You can save a window layout to make the current Graphics display available for restore. For more information, see Guide to the Graphics Window.

2. Using the Design Manager Snapshot toolbar, step through the designs one by one. See Toolbars Reference.

3. In an output table or in a project plot, click a specific design item:

▶In an output table, select the respective row.

▶In a project plot, select the respective data point (XY plot) or data line (Parallel Coordinates plot).

The other panels are updated automatically to reflect the selected design.

Output tables and project plots provide further features for interacting with a selected design item. You can open scene and plot snapshots, define design sets, or display design details.

To open a scene or plot snapshot from a selected design item:

4. Right-click the design item and select Open Scenes/Open Plots > [scene/plot] > [snapshot], where [snapshot] can be a new snapshot or a previously created snapshots for the respective scene or plot.

To create a new design set from specific designs or to add specific designs to a previously created design set:

5. Using <Ctrl>, multi-select the designs of interest.

6. Right-click and select Set Design Set > [design set], where [design set] can be a new design set or a previously created design set.

To display design details:

7. Right-click and select Show Design Details....

The Design Details dialog displays the following information:

◦ Design#

◦ Name

◦ State

◦ Performance (not for DOE and CAD Robustness studies)

◦ Artifact Directory

◦ Design Log File

◦ Simulation File

◦ Messages

For more information, see Output Table Right-Click Actions and Plots Right-Click Actions.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6830

Example: The following video displays the connectivity between output tables, project plots, and snapshots for an airfoil pareto optimization study.

Analyzing the Results of a Design Study in HEEDS|post

HEEDS|post is a plotting and graphing package that offers enhanced post-processing capabilities for your design studies. You can analyze the study results in HEEDS|post while the study is running, as well as when it completes.

Whenever possible, perform the post-processing for your design studies in Design Manager. Only use HEEDS| post if the post-processing capabilities of Design Manager do not suit your requirements. For the analysis of study results in HEEDS|post, you require a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Intelligent Design Exploration license.

To analyze the results of a design study in HEEDS|post:

1. In Design Manager, right-click the design study node and select Open in HEEDS|post....

Design Manager writes the HEEDS|post project file [design study]0.rpt in the study artifact directory. Depending on the study type of your design study, Design Manager writes additional output files, such as:

◦ [design study]0.res

◦ [design study]0.gph

◦ [design study]0.hst

◦ [design study]0.plot

◦ DOE_0_[response].out

HEEDS|post uses the structure of the project artifact directory to refer to the scene, plot, and log files of your design study.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6831

Note: HEEDS|post can only view scenes and plots that are written as *.png files. *.sce files are not supported.

After the data export, Design Manager automatically launches HEEDS|post, which loads the written project file.

If your design study is still running, you can enable HEEDS|post to reload the project file as soon as a design simulation completes:

2. Within HEEDS|post, in the Study toolbar, activate Auto Refresh.

Note: If the Design Manager server is running on a remote server—that is, if you are running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ locally and connecting to a remote Design Manager server, Open in HEEDS| post... only exports the HEEDS|post project data. You can launch HEEDS|post at a later time and load the exported HEEDS|post project manually. See Launching HEEDS|post.

Launching HEEDS|post

You can launch HEEDS|post from Design Manager and analyse the exported results of a design study in HEEDS| post.

To launch HEEDS|post manually and open an exported HEEDS|post project:

1. In Design Manager, select Tools > Launch HEEDS|post.

2. In HEEDS|post, select File > Open.

3. In the HEEDS|post - Open Project dialog, set the file type to HEEDS POST Project (*.rpt).

4. Navigate to and select the exported [File name]0.rpt file, and click OK.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6832

Design Manager Reference

The following properties and right-click actions are available for a Design Manager project.

Design Manager Project Properties

The following properties are available for the Design Manager project node at the root of the object tree.

Name

Displays the name of the Design Manager project (read only).

Connection Mode

Displays whether and how other users can connect to the server running the Design Manager project (read only). For more information, see Server Connection Mode.

Project Artifact Directory

Specifies the path to the project artifact directory, which contains all the outputs of the design studies— such as simulation files, log files, scene files, and plot files. For more information, see directory file structure.

By default, Design Manager uses the relative path to the directory that contains the *.dmprj file.

Study Execution Abort File Name

Allows you to specify the name of a file that, once placed in the project root directory, causes the design studies in your Design Manager project to abort. This action is useful for stopping a batch run. The default file name is DM_ABORT.

Auto Save

When On, Design Manager saves the Design Manager project file (*.dmprj) after each design simulation completes.

Retain Temporary Artifacts

When activated, allows you to store temporary artifacts created by study execution in the .mdxruntime folder. The .mdxruntime directory structure and file contents are subject-to-change. For more information, see directory file structure.

Design Manager Project Right-Click Actions

The following specific actions are available when you right-click the Design Manager project node. For information on the common right-click actions, see Common Pop-Up Menu Items.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6833

View Log

Allows you to view the log file of the Design Manager project.

Whenever you save the Design Manager project, an entry is added to a project log. The project log is a record of each save operation through the life of the project, which specifically records the following for every save operation:

• Date

• Time

• Version number

• Architecture that was used.

The information is stored in the project file itself, and not in a separate file. The log could be useful if you are checking compatibility issues between architectures, or between greatly disparate version numbers, for example.

You can also intersperse a log with comments of your own, see Adding Comments.

Collapse Tree

Shrinks the object tree back to its default size.

Design Studies Reference

The following properties and right-click actions are available for design studies in Design Manager.

Design Study Properties

Object Properties

Design Studies Design Studies

Displays the number of design studies in the Design Manager project (read-only).

[design study] Study Type

Controls the type of design study that you want Design Manager to run. For information on the various study types, see Study Types.

• Manual

Activates the Design Table node, which allows you to create the designs to run in tabular form. See Creating Manual Designs.

• Sweep

Activates the Design Table node. Edit this node to display the list of designs that are created based on the Input Parameters settings. The number of designs to run is determined by the number of variables and how many values are used for each variable.

• DOE

Activates the DOE Settings node that allows you to set the DOE Type to run:

◦ 2 Level Full Factorial: Carries out a two-level full factorial DOE study.

◦ 3 Level Full Factorial: Carries out a three-level full factorial DOE study.

◦ Latin Hypercube Sampling: Carries out a DOE study that uses Latin Hypercube sampling to determine the input parameter values. Activates the Sampling Settings node that allows you to set the total number of Designs to Run in the design study. The specified value must be equal or smaller than the number of possible designs as defined by the input parameters.

• Optimization

Activates the Optimization Settings and Design Seeds nodes.

The Optimization Settings node controls the following properties:

◦ Optimization Type: Specifies the type of optimization to run.

Weighted sum of all objectives specifies a design study where all objectives are combined into a single objective, which is optimized by the algorithm. The objectives are combined using the performance function given by Eqn. (577).

Multiple objective tradeoff study (Pareto front) specifies a design study where each objective is independently considered by the algorithm.

This option activates the Archive Size child node. The archive size is the number of non-dominated designs that you want the algorithm to find during the search in order to resolve the Pareto front.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6836

Object Properties

The value of the archive size must be evenly divisible by four and greater than or equal to 12. This value should also be greater than or equal to the number of input parameters in the design study. As an example, a Pareto optimization study with 8 variables would have an archive size of 12, while one with 13 variables would have an archive size of 16.

Single-objective and multi-objective studies use the SHERPA algorithm.

◦ Designs to Run: Specifies the total number of designs to run in the design study. For single-objective Optimization studies, run at least 30 to 35 designs. As a guideline, set this value to 10 times the number of input parameters in your design study. For multi-objective Optimization studies, run at least 40 designs, which is the default value. As a guideline, for multi-objective Optimization studies, set this value to 8 to 12 times the archive size. If the archive size is larger than 20, the number of designs to run is multiplied by 2 to give 40 designs. The SHERPA algorithm works best when it can learn as many times as possible.

The Design Seeds node controls seed values for the optimization study. You can seed an optimization study with manually entered designs or with design sets of a prior design study. See Design Seeds Reference.

• Stochastic

Activates the Stochastic Settings node that allows you to set the total number of Designs to Run in the design study.

• CAD Robustness

Activates the CAD Robustness Settings node that allows you to set the Sampling Type for the input parameters:

◦ Manual: Activates the Design Table node, which allows you to set the input parameter values for the designs to run in tabular form. See Creating Manual Designs.

◦ Sweep: Activates the Design Table node. Edit this node to display the list of designs that are created based on the Input Parameters settings. The number of designs to run is determined by the number of variables and how many values are used for each variable.

◦ Latin Hypercube: Uses Latin Hypercube sampling to determine the input parameter values. Activates the Sampling Settings node that allows you to set the total number of Designs to Run in the design study. The specified value must be equal or smaller than the number of possible designs as defined by the input parameters.

Simulations

Specifies the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ reference simulation that provides the inputs for the design study.

Tags

Specifies the tags for the design study. For more information, see Tagging Simulation Objects.

Input Parameters Reference

The following properties and right-click actions are available for input parameters.

Input Parameters Properties

Object Properties

Input Parameters Parameters

Specifies the parameters from the reference simulation to use as input parameters for the design study.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6839

Object Properties

[input parameter] Parameter Type (only for Sweep, Optimization, Latin Hypercube Sampling DOE, and CAD Robustness studies)

Controls how Design Manager sets the input parameter values.

• Continuous

Allows Design Manager to set the input parameter to values within a specified range. This option activates the Continuous child node, which controls the following properties:

◦ Range: Specifies the minimum value and the maximum value that Design Manager can set for the input parameter.

◦ Baseline Value (only for Optimization): Specifies the value for the input parameter in the baseline design. The baseline design is the first design that Design Manager runs in the design study.

◦ Increment (only for Sweep and Optimization): Specifies the increment size. When set, Resolution is automatically updated.

◦ Resolution (only for Sweep and Optimization): Specifies the number of different values to look at for the input parameter. When set, Increment is automatically updated.

• Discrete

Sets the input parameter to discrete values. This option activates the Discrete child node, which controls the following properties:

◦ Values: Specifies the list of values for the input parameter, separated with commas or spaces.

◦ Baseline Value (only for Optimization): Specifies the value for the input parameter in the baseline design. The baseline design is the first design that Design Manager runs in the design study.

• Constant

Sets the input parameter to a constant value, without exploring other values. This option activates the Constant child node, where you set the Value of the constant.

Reference Parameter (read only)

Displays the associated parameter in the reference simulation.

Simulation Effect (read only)

Displays the value of the Simulation Effect property of the associated parameter in the reference simulation:

• Unknown: Implies the parameter affects everything (that is, geometry, meshing, and solver).

• Geometry: The parameter affects the geometry (which implies it also affects meshing and solver).

• Meshing: The parameter affects meshing (which implies it also affects the solver).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6840

Object Properties

• Solver: The parameter affects the solver only.

Reference Value (read only)

Displays the value of the associated parameter in the reference simulation.

Input File Directory

Specify the directory of the list of files and only apply to file path study parameter.

Lock Name

When On, preserves the name of the selected input parameter.

When Off, the name of the input parameter is linked to the name of the associated parameter from the reference simulation. When you change the name of the parameter in the reference simulation and update the reference simulation in Design Manager, the input parameter name is updated automatically.

Tags

Specifies the tags for the input parameter. For more information, see Tagging Simulation Objects.

Factor Value (only for 2-level/3-level full factorial DOE studies)

Factor Mode

Controls whether the lower and upper values for the input parameter are absolute or relative to a mid value.

• Absolute

Activates the Absolute child node, where you set absolute values for the lower value (Low), mid value (Mid), and upper value (High). The Mid property is only available for 3 Level Full Factorial DOE studies.

• Relative

Activates the Relative child node, where you set a constant mid value (Mid) and relative low and high values (Low(-%) and High(+%)). The low and high values are relative to the specified mid value.

Stochastic Value (only for Stochastic studies)

Baseline Value

Specifies the value for the input parameter in the baseline design. The baseline design is the first design that Design Manager runs in the design study.

Distribution

Specifies the type of probability distribution to use for the input parameter. The probability distribution is centered around the Baseline Value of the input parameter.

• Normal: Specifies a normal distribution. The standard deviation is specified through the St. Deviation property in the corresponding child node.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6841

Object Properties

• Triangular: Specifies a Triangular distribution. The lower and upper limits of the distribution are specified through the Min Variation and Max Variation properties in the corresponding child node, respectively.

• Uniform: Specifies a uniform distribution. The maximum variation in either direction is specified through the Max Variation property in the corresponding child node.

Mode

Specifies whether the distribution properties (Min Variation, Max Variation, and St. Deviation) are absolute, or relative to the baseline value.

• Relative

All property values are specified as a percentage of the Baseline Value.

• Absolute

All property values are specified as absolute values.
