Responses Reference

The following properties and right-click actions are available for responses.

Responses Properties

Object Properties

Responses (not for CAD Robustness studies) Response

Sets the reports from the reference simulation to use as responses for the design study. See Study Outputs—Responses.

[response] Reference Report (read only)

Displays the associated report in the reference simulation.

Is Objective (only for Optimization and Sweep studies)

When On, instructs Design Manager to use the response as an objective for the design study.

Activating this property activates the Objective Properties child node.

Is Constraint (not for DOE studies)

When On, instructs Design Manager to use the response as a constraint for the design study.

Activating this property activates the Constraint Properties child node.

Note: In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 12.04, the Is Objective and Is Constraint properties were supported for all study types. From version 12.06 onwards, if you play a macro recorded in version 12.04 that activates one of these properties for an unsupported study type, the property is activated as read-only but no longer used.

Units

Displays the unit of the selected response.

Lock Name

When On, preserves the name of the selected response.

When Off, the name of the response is linked to the name of the associated report from the reference simulation. When you change the name of the report in the reference simulation and update the reference simulation in Design Manager, the response name is updated automatically.

Tags

Specifies the tags for the response. For more information, see Tagging Simulation Objects.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6843

Object Properties

Specify Valid Minimum

When On, allows you to set a valid minimum for the response value. A design with a response value below the value that you specify in the corresponding Valid Minimum child node is classed as Error design.

Specify Valid Maximum

When On, allows you to set a valid maximum for the response value. A design with a response value above the value that you specify in the corresponding Valid Maximum child node is classed as Error design.

Objective Properties Goal

Sets the analysis goal for the selected response. You can choose to Minimize or Maximize the value of the response.

The specified goal sets the Signi in the performance evaluation of each design

(see Eqn. (577)). The value is -1 for objectives being minimized and +1 for objectives being maximized.

Normalization Type

Sets the type of normalization to use for the selected response. The specified value determines the normalization value Normi in the performance evaluation

of each design (see Eqn. (577)).

• Baseline Normalization: Sets the normalization value automatically to the objective's value in the baseline design. The baseline design is the first design that Design Manager runs in the design study. For the various study types, this design is determined as follows:

◦ Manual: The first design that you specify in the list of designs to run.

◦ Sweep/DOE: The design that combines the minimum values for all of your input parameters.

◦ Optimization/Stochastic: The design that combines the values that you set as Baseline Value for each input parameter.

• Normalization Value: Allows you to specify the normalization in the Normalization Value child node. Only use this property if there are multiple objectives. Set this property so that all normalized objectives are of a similar order of magnitude.

Weight

Allows you to take into account the difference in importance between objectives. For example, the mass of a cooling device can be of less importance than its cooling rate.

The specified value determines the linear weight of the objective LinWti in the

performance evaluation of each design (see Eqn. (577)).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6844

Object Properties

Constraint Properties Type

Sets the type of the constraint. You can set a Minimum or a Maximum constraint for the response. You can also combine both limits (Minimum/ Maximum). Any designs with a response value outside of the range that you specify in the corresponding child node is classed as infeasible. You specify the constraint values in the corresponding child nodes.

Run Settings Reference

The following properties are available for the run settings of a design study in Design Manager.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6846

Run Settings Properties

Save Simulation Files

Specifies the designs whose Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation files you want to save.

• None: Does not save any *.sim files.

• All Best Designs (for Optimization studies only): Saves all best designs in the design study. Each time Design Manager finds a design that is better than any previous design, it saves the *.sim file of the design.

The best design in a set of designs is the design with the highest performance value as given by Eqn. (577).

• Last Best Design (for Optimization studies only): Saves the *.sim file for the last best design that Design Manager finds during the run of the design study. At any time during the run, the *.sim file for the best design so far is available.

• All Designs: Saves the *.sim files for all designs in the design study.

Save Log files

Controls whether to save log files to the design directories. This option is enabled by default for newly created studies.

Output Auxiliary File Types

Specifies the extensions of simulation output files to be preserved for each design. Example: [png, csv, jpg, sce, simh]

The specified files are copied from the .mdxruntime directory to the artifact directory. Non-specified files are deleted. See Directory and File Structure.

The following output file types are supported:

• Scene (png, jpg, tif, pnm, bmp, ps, sce)

• Plot (png, jpg, ps, csv, eps)

• Solution history (simh)

• Summary report (html, xml)

• Table (csv)

• Track file (trk)

• Mesh and solution data (ccm, case, fvuns, plt, cel, sbd, ntl, trn, bdf, cgns, cga)

In the reference simulation, you must set the output directories for the files relative to the simulation file— absolute paths are not supported. Design Manager preserves the directory and sub-directory structure relative to the simulation file.

Example: Setting the output directory for hardcopies of a temperature scene to ./Scenes/ Temperature/ stores the hardcopies for each design in Design_[n]/Scenes/Temperature/.

Note: For track files (trk), you must save the design simulation files along with the track files using Save Simulation Files.

Note: For a CAD Robustness study, the design simulations do not write any auxiliary output files.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6847

Simultaneous Jobs

Specifies how many design simulations are run at the same time. When running an Optimization study, this value must not be greater than the value specified in Designs to Run divided by 10. If computational and license resources permit, set this value to 1/5 to 1/7 of the value set in Designs to Run.

Compute Processes

Specifies how many cores to run with each Simcenter STAR-CCM+ design simulation.

Compute Resource Reference

The following properties are available for the compute resources of a design study in Design Manager.

Compute Resource Properties

Type

Controls the type of compute resource that you want Design Manager to use for the design study.

• Direct: Runs the design study using direct execution, such as a local machine or workstation.

• Linux Cluster: Runs the design study on a Linux cluster using a generic scheduler.

This option activates the Linux Cluster child node, where you specify the following properties:

Job Submit Command

Command that is used to submit each design simulation on the cluster.

The default value qsub -l nodes=1:ppn=8 is set up for a cluster running OpenPBS where each design simulation is submitted on one node running eight cores per node.

To avoid underloading or overloading of compute resources, set Compute Processes to 1. This value disables the Compute Processes property.

Name Identifier

Specifies the flag for the name identifier of a design simulation being submitted to the queue.

The default value -N is set up for a cluster running OpenPBS.

Prefix

Specifies the value for the name identifier that is passed on to the job scheduler. The default value is dm_study_design.

Script File

Allows you to use a submission script that contains the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ execution command and common command line options.

You specify the absolute path and the full name of the script file, which must be available on the cluster drive.

Make sure that the script file has execute permission.

• Windows HPC Cluster: Runs the design study on a Windows HPC cluster using the HPC Job Manager.

This option activates the Windows HPC Cluster child node, where you specify the following properties:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6848

Job Submit Command

Command that is used to submit each design simulation on the cluster.

The default value job submit /numcores:8 is set up for a cluster running the HPC Job Manager, where each design simulation is submitted on eight cores. The scheduler allocates the requested cores from the available nodes.

To avoid underloading or overloading of compute resources, set Compute Processes to 1. This value disables the Compute Processes property.

Name Identifier

Specifies the flag for the name identifier of a design simulation being submitted to the queue.

The default value /jobname is set up for a cluster running the HPC Job Manager.

Prefix

Specifies the value for the name identifier that is passed on to the job scheduler. The default value is dm_study_design.

Script File

Allows you to use a submission script that contains the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ execution command and common command line options.

You specify the full UNC path and the full name of the script file, which must be available on the cluster drive.

Make sure that the script file has execute permission.

• Job Manager: Runs the design study on a Linux cluster using Job Manager.

This option activates the Job Manager child node, where you specify the following properties:

Job Manager Key

Specifies the key to authenticate against Job Manager on the cluster.

Clicking (Custom Editor) opens the Job Manager Keys dialog, where you specify the following properties.

URL

Specifies the URL of Job Manager on the cluster as provided by your Job Manager administrator.

Username

Specifies your Job Manager username. This username corresponds to the OS username that you use to login to the cluster login node.

Password

Depending on the Job Manager authentication mode set by your Job Manager administrator, specifies one of the following passwords:

◦ For OS Authentication mode, specifies your cluster login password.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6849

◦ For Internal Authentication mode, specifies your password that is specific to Job Manager. The initial password can optionally be provided by the Job Manager administrator.

Once the key is added, it is available in the drop-down menu for all design studies in your Design Manager project.

Submission Template

Specifies the Job Manager submission template that suits your requirements. The submission template determines how the design simulations of the design study are submitted to the cluster, such as which cluster queue or which Simcenter STAR-CCM+ version to use. The available submission templates are provided by your Job Manager administrator.

• Local CAD Update

This option activates the Local CAD Update child node, where you specify the following properties:

Compute Resource for CAD update

Specifies the compute resource that handles the CAD update. This resource must be your local machine on which the native CAD package is installed. Only compute resource type Direct is allowed. By default Default Direct is chosen.

Compute Resource for successive Design run

Specifies the compute resource for successive design run. Only compute resource type Job Manager is allowed. The Job Manager resource is created under Tools > Compute Resources.

STAR-CCM+ Command Line Options

Specifies simulation command line options to pass to the design simulations—such as License Options or other Simcenter STAR-CCM+ options, see Command-Line Reference.

This property is useful for general simulation command line options that you want to save within your Design Manager project.

Example:-pio -power (parallel I/O and power licensing).

Alternatively, you can pass simulation options from the command line, see Design Manager Options, which is useful for machine-specific or user-specific options.

As Design Manager controls the resource management for the design simulations, you must not pass resource management options to the design simulations. Therefore, the following resource specification options are not supported:

• -batchsystem

• -bs

• -hostregexpr

• -machinefile

• -np

• -on

Macro Files Reference

A macro is a Java program that is compiled and executed within the Design Manager workspace. Macro files are Java language files that can be recorded as a journal of your interaction with the application.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6850

The File > Macro menu in Design Manager contains the same options for recording and running macros as the corresponding menu in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. For a full description of the available options, see Scripting the Application.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulations and Design Manager projects have separate Recent Macro lists. Macros that are played when a Design Manager project is active are added to the Design Manager Recent Macro list, and macros that are played when a simulation is active are added to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation Recent Macro list.

The following properties and right-click actions are available for macros in Design Manager.

Macro File Properties

Object Properties

Macro Files None.

[macro] Macro Insertion Point

Controls the stage in the workflow of a design simulation where Design Manager performs the custom steps that are defined in the macro.

• Before Meshing: Runs the macro immediately before executing the meshing pipeline.

• After Meshing: Runs the macro immediately after executing the meshing pipeline.

• After Running: Runs the macro immediately after the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver completes, and before any results are returned to Design Manager.

Macro File

Specifies the path to the macro file (*.java). By default, Design Manager uses the relative path to the project root directory.

Tags

Specifies the tags for the macros. For more information, see Tagging Simulation Objects.

Macro Right-Click Actions

Object Right-Click Actions

Macro Files New

Adds a new macro to the workflow of a design simulation.

In the Open dialog, you select the appropriate macro file (*.java) and set the macro insertion point (see Macro File Properties, above). The file must exist already: this option does not allow you to create a new macro file.

You can record macro files using the File > Macro menu or create macro files manually in a text editor.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6851

Output Tables Reference

The following properties and right-click actions are available for the output table of a design set.

Output Table Properties

Design#

Displays the identification numbers of the designs in the design study.

Name

Displays the names of the designs.

State

Displays the run states of the designs. The following states are available:

• No icon: This design has not started.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6854

• This design is queued to run.

• This design has been assigned to run.

• This design has started to run.

• This design is running. This state includes updating the CAD data and parameter values, meshing, and solving.

• This design has executed.

• This design is processing outputs.

• This design has completed successfully.

• This design has failed.

In most cases, the states and change so quickly that you do not notice them in the GUI.

Performance (not for DOE and CAD Robustness studies)

Displays the performance values of the designs, which allow you to rate the designs. The formulation of the performance value is given by Eqn. (577).

Parameter/Response

Displays the values of the respective input parameter or response.

Output Table Filter Query Rules

The following filter operators are available for the design properties in an output tables of a user-defined design set:

Properties Available Operators

Name contains

Matches all designs with names that include the specified text string.

does not contain

Matches all designs with names that do not include the specified text string.

matches

Matches all designs with the specified name.

does not match

Matches all designs with names other than the specified name.

starts with

Matches all designs with names that begin with the specified text string.

does not start with

Matches all designs with names that do not begin with the specified text string.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6855

Properties Available Operators

ends with

Matches all designs with names that end with the specified text string.

Note: A name can include a trailing number which is considered part of the name, such as Design 1 . Therefore, for example, an entry of ign does not find the Design 1.

does not end with

Matches all designs with names that do not end with the specified text string.

State All

Matches all designs in the design study.

Successful

Matches the designs that have completed successfully.

Error

Matches the designs that encountered an error when they ran.

Not Started

Matches the designs that have not started.

Feasible (not for DOE and CAD Robustness studies)

Matches the designs that meet all constraints.

Design# Performance Parameter Response

all values

Matches all designs in the design study.

less than

Matches all designs with respective quantity being smaller than a specified value.

greater than

Matches all designs with respective quantity being larger than a specified value.

between

Matches all designs with respective quantity being in a specified range.

Output Table Right-Click Actions

The following actions are available when you right-click the row of a specific design in the output table:

Show Design Details

Opens the Design Details Dialog.

Design Details Dialog Reference

The Design Details dialog provides information for a design that you select in a table or in a project plot.

Design#

The identification number of the designs in the design study.

Name

The name of the design.

State

The simulation state of the design, see State.

Performance (not for DOE and CAD Robustness studies)

The performance value of the design, see Eqn. (577).

Artifact Directory

The path to the design artifact directory where the simulation results of the design are stored—see directory file structure. Clicking the hyperlink opens the directory in your default file browser.

Design Log File

The log file of the design simulation—see Save Log files. The log file gives a text description of developments within the simulation. Clicking the hyperlink opens the file in your default text editor.

Simulation File

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation file—see Save Simulation Files. Clicking the hyperlink opens the Load a File dialog, which allows you to load the simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Messages

Information about the design simulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6857

If the design reused an existing cached mesh, an information message indicates the design from which the mesh was reused. For more information, see Mesh Reuse in Design Studies.

If the design fails, error messages show the reasons for the failure of the simulation.

Note: For files and file paths on remote machines, Design Manager displays the respective information but does not provide hyperlinks.

Object Properties

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6859

Object Properties

Animation Target Frame Rate (fps)

Maximum number of animation frames that are displayed in one second (less for complex scenes, or when less computing power is available).

Annotations Annotations

A list of the annotations added to the snapshot. Editing the property accesses the inplace object selector to add or remove annotations.

[annotation] Width Stretch Factor

Scales the width of the annotation, with the default of 1.0 equaling 100% of the original width

Height

The height of the annotation as a fraction of the visualization display height, where 1.0 equals the full height

Position

The position of the lower left corner of the text in the Graphics window based on the specified Coordinate System.

Visible

When On, shows the annotation in the display. When Off, the annotation is hidden.

Coordinate System

Selects the type of coordinates to use for Position.

• Normalized Viewport: Shows x-y values as fractions of the length and height of the Graphics window display, respectively. The origin is the lower left-hand corner of that display.

• World: Shows x-y-z values as global coordinates. As you rotate the object, the annotation keeps its position relative to that object.

Interactive

When On, allows you to move the annotation in the display using the mouse. When Off, locks the position of the annotation in the display.

Location

Controls the visibility of the annotation relative to the objects in the display.

• Background: Shows the objects in front of the annotation.

• Foreground: Shows the annotation in front of the objects.

Data Series Reference

Design Manager data series specify the designs of a design study that are displayed in a project plot.

Data Series Properties

Object Properties

[data series] Input Design Study

Specifies the design study whose designs you want to analyze.

Input Design Sets

Specifies the design set of the selected design study that you want to display in the project plot.

Render Mode

Controls how the plot displays the designs of the selected design set:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6867

Object Properties

• Default: Displays all designs of the selected design set using the same symbol style for all designs.

• Pareto (only for Multiple Objective Tradeoff Optimization studies): Displays the designs of a specific Pareto Cycle that you specify in the Pareto Ranks child node. You can select multiple cycles if required. By default, Design Manager displays the last cycle.

For an XY plot, Design Manager displays the designs using a specific symbol style for each Pareto rank. For a Parallel Coordinates plot, Design Manager uses a specific line style. You can control the styles in the Pareto Ranks > Rank [n] > Symbol Style / Line Style child nodes. See Line and Symbol Style Properties.

Legend Name

Changes the legend text in the project plot display.

Lock Legend Name

When On, prevents any automatic changes to the legend name. The legend name is linked to the node name which in turn reflects the name of the part that the data series represents. Therefore, name changes to the part are automatically reflected in the name of the data series node and the legend name. If this property is activated, the current legend name is locked, effectively unlinking the property from the node name. Setting the legend name automatically activates this lock.

Tags

Specifies the tags for the design study data set. For more information, see Tagging Simulation Objects.

[axis] Data Axis

Controls the axis on which the data is plotted. The choice of axes depends on the total number of axes in the project plot.

Type

Controls the type of data to be displayed on the axis:

• Parameter: Displays a specific input parameter of the design study, that you specify in the corresponding Parameter child node. See Input Parameters Reference.

• Response: Displays a specific response of the design study, that you specify in the corresponding Response child node. In an XY plot, when you activate the Show Constraints property, the plot highlights the field of feasible designs, where the field is determined by the constraints that you set for the specified response. See Responses Reference.

• Design Number: Displays the identification number of the design in the design study.

• Design Status: Displays 1 for a successful design and 0 for a design that encountered an error when it ran.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6868

Object Properties

• Design Performance: Displays the performance value calculated by SHERPA based on constraints and objectives. A higher performance value indicates a better design. For the formulation of the performance value, see also: Performance Rating.

Tags

Specifies the tags for the axis data. For more information, see Tagging Simulation Objects.

Best Design History (not for Parallel Coordinates plots and not for DOE, CAD Robustness, and Multiple Objective Tradeoff Optimization studies in XY plots)

Visible

When On, the project plot displays the path of the design study to the best design. This path passes the designs that are identified as best designs at one point during the run of the design study. The best design in a set of designs is the design with the highest performance value (see Eqn. (577)).

You specify the style of the path in the Line Style child node. See Line and Symbol Style Properties.

Legend Name

Specifies the legend text that is associated with the best design history.

Best Design (not for DOE, CAD Robustness, and Multiple Objective Tradeoff Optimization studies)

Visible

When On, the project plot marks the best design in the design study, where the best design is the design with the highest performance value (see Eqn. (577)).

You specify the style of the mark in the Symbol Style child node. See Line and Symbol Style Properties.

Legend Name

Specifies the legend text that is associated with the best design.

Baseline Design (not for DOE, Stochastic, and CAD Robustness studies)

Visible

When On, the project plot marks the baseline design. The baseline design is the first design that Design Manager runs in the design study. For the various study types, this design is determined as follows:

• Manual: The first design that you specify in the list of designs to run.

• Sweep: The design that combines the minimum values for all of your input parameters.

• Optimization: The design that combines the Baseline values that you specify for each input parameter.

You specify the style of the mark in the Symbol Style child node. See Line and Symbol Style Properties.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6869

Tools Reference

The Tools manager node contains various objects that facilitate your analysis.

The following objects are available:

• Annotations

• Color Maps

• Compute Resources

• Custom Trees

• Filters

• Layouts

• Tags

• Units

• Views

Annotations

An annotation is an object that you can use to add information to a snapshot display in the Graphics window. The following annotations are available by default:

• Design Name: Displays the name of the respective design that is analysed within a design study.

• Performance Value: Displays the performance value of a design given by Eqn. (577). The perforamans value is a rating value that allows you to judge the design.

Additional simple text annotations allow you to place customized text labels in snapshot displays.

For more information, see Annotations.

Color Maps

Color maps let you create custom color and shade configurations. For more details refer to Color Maps.

Compute Resources

This object is a collection of all the defined compute resources in a Design Manager Project. By default, a Direct compute resource named Default Direct is defined. New compute resources can be added to the Design Manager Project by right-clicking this node.

Custom Trees

If you have a large simulation with many objects in the tree, custom trees allow you to quickly access the objects that you use most.

For more information, see Using Custom Simulation Trees.

Filters

A filter uses queries to narrow groups of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ objects. A query consists of one or more conditional statements, also called "predicates", by which Simcenter STAR-CCM+ searches among the objects in the simulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6873

For more information, see Object Filters.

Layouts

A window layout is an arrangement of windows in the graphics display, which consists of one or more modes. They can be used to save, restore, and edit a specified visual display.

For more information, see Preserving the Window Layout.

Tags

Tags can help you find and select objects easier. Once a tag has been created, it can be applied to one or more objects to flag them as being different from other objects.

For more information, see Tagging Simulation Objects.

Units

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ has flexible and customizable support for engineering units. The standard SI and USCS systems are built in, and you can add new units as desired.

For more information, see Engineering Units.

Views

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, every scene has a camera to convert the three-dimensional objects in a scene into the two-dimensional image visible on the screen. The information defining the orientation, position and projection of the three-dimensional objects is stored in a view object.

For more information, see Working with Views.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6874

Toolbars Reference

The following toolbars are specific to Design Manager projects.

: Design Manager Animation toolbar

: Design Manager Snapshot toolbar

: Design Manager Vis toolbar

For information on the toolbars that are common in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, see STAR-CCM+ Toolbar Reference.

Design Manager Animation

This toolbar resembles the controls of a common video player to animate scene snapshots, where the scenes are exported as Scene Files (*.sce).

(Play/Pause)

Toggles between playing the scene animation and pausing it.

(Stop)

Stops the animation in the scene.

(Single Step Forward)

Moves the paused animation forward one frame.

(Single Step Backward)

Moves the paused animation backward one frame.

Design Manager Snapshot

This toolbar lets you step through the designs of a design set in snapshots, output tables, and study plots. For Pareto plots, you step through the Pareto cycles.

(First Design)

Jumps to the first design in the design set.

(Previous Design)

Steps backward to the previous design in the design set.

(Next Design)

Steps forward to the next design in the design set.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6875

(Last Design)

Jumps to the last design of the design set.

(Reset Current Design)

Resets the design, that is, no design is displayed.

Design Manager Vis

This toolbar lets you work interactively with scene snapshots, where the scenes are exported as Scene Files (*.sce).

(Reset View)

Restores the view to a zoom factor such that the model takes up most of the display. The view angle is unchanged. Use this function if the model has somehow zoomed or panned to such a position that you can no longer see it on the display.

(Rotate)

Rotates the view around a focal point that your most recent mouse click in the display sets.

(Rubberband Zoom)

Allows you to zoom to a specific area in the display by clicking two points that define the opposing corners of the zoomed area. Press <Esc> to cancel.

(View)

Opens a drop-down menu that allows you to set, save or restore a view.

• Store Current View

Records properties about the projection mode, zoom factor, pan position and view angle and adds a node to the Views node of the simulation tree. It is named View N, where N is the first available number that is not used by existing views with the same prefix. So if you have a view, View 1, then this operation creates a view, View 2.

• Restore View

Contains a submenu of saved views, including a thumbnail of the view. Select one of the submenu items to restore that view.

• Projection Mode

Contains a submenu that toggles between perspective and parallel mode for the current view.

• Views

Contains a submenu of standard view angles using the axes as reference vectors.

• Standard Views

Contains a submenu of standard views using the aspects of the object in the scene.

• View Coordinate System

Contains a submenu of coordinate systems in the simulation that a view can use.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6876

(Previous View)

Reverses the latest change to the view.

(Next View)

Repeats a change that was subjected to the Previous View command.

Command Line Options Reference

The following command line options are available for Design Manager.

Note: Some commands accept arguments with embedded quotes. When using C-shell on Linux, add set backslash_quote to the ~/.cshrc file. This variable ensures that embedded quotes are correctly escaped.

Design Manager Options

The starccm+ [project] command launches the Design Manager server and loads the specified Design Manager project file (*.dmprj). The following Design Manager server options are available:

-dmnoshare

Specifies the Unlicensed Design Manager Server Licensing Scheme.

Note: This option is not supported when running Design Manager in Pre-Allocation Mode.

-passtodesign <options>

Specifies simulation options to pass to the design simulations, such as License Options or other Simcenter STAR-CCM+ options, see Command-Line Reference.

Passing simulation options from the command line is useful for machine-specific or user-specific options— such as a Power on Demand license key.

Example: starccm+ [project] -dmnoshare -passtodesign "-power -podkey <value> - licpath 1999@flex.cd-adapco.com"

Alternatively, you can pass command line options from the GUI, see STAR-CCM+ Execution Command. Passing command line options from the GUI is useful for general simulation command line options that you want to save within your Design Manager project.

As Design Manager controls the resource management for the design simulations, you must not pass resource management options to the design simulations. Therefore, the following resource specification options are not supported:

• -batchsystem

• -bs

• -hostregexpr

• -machinefile

• -np

• -on

Note: The -passtodesign <options> option does not support arguments that require double quotes, such as -mpidriver platform:"-aff:automatic:bandwidth". You must pass these options from the GUI.

-preallocpower

Specifies to use only Power Session licenses when running in Pre-Allocation Mode.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6878

Similar to -dmnoshare, the specified option instructs the Design Manager server to not pull any licenses.

Additionally, it implicitly passes -power to the design simulations. The option -passtodesign "- power" is not required.

Example: starlaunch jobmanager --command "starccm+ [project] -preallocpower"

-doepower

Specifies to pull a Power Session license (ccmppower) instead of a ccmpsuite license as session license when using the Default Licensing Scheme. Using this option together with -podkey <value> uses a Power on Demand license.

When running Design Manager in Pre-Allocation Mode and using the -doepower option, you must pass this option also to the Design Manager server.

Example: starlaunch jobmanager --command "starccm+ [project] -doepower - passtodesign \"-doepower\""

-notokens

Specifies to not use doetoken licenses for the design simulations.

When running Design Manager in Pre-Allocation Mode and passing the -notokens option to the design simulations, you must pass this option also to the Design Manager server.

Example: starlaunch jobmanager --command "starccm+ [project] -notokens - passtodesign \"-notokens\""

Resource Manager Options

When running Design Manager in Pre-Allocation Mode, Resource Manager provides the actual resource management functionality. The following command line options are available for starlaunch jobmanager:

--command <batch_command>

Specifies the command that runs your Design Manager project in batch.

--slots 0

Specifies to allocate no processor for the jobmanager process.

--batchsystem <system>

Specifies the batch management system on your cluster.

Specifies a group of network machines on which Design Manager is allowed to run the design simulations.

Specifies an MPI file that lists the machines on which Design Manager is allowed to run the design simulations.

License Options

The following options control the license usage when running a design study in Design Manager:

-doepower

Uses a Power Session license (ccmppower) instead of a ccmpsuite license as session license when using the Default Licensing Scheme. Using this option together with -podkey <value> uses a Power on Demand license.

-licpath <path:...>

Specifies a license path that overrides the default license path. When this option is used, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the path to define a new CDLMD_LICENSE_FILE environment variable for the spawned server session.

Example: -licpath 1999@flex.cd-adapco.com (Power on Demand license server)

-nosuite

Prevents ccmpsuite licenses from being used to enable cores for parallel computation. Only parallel licenses, such as Power Tokens, are used to enable cores for parallel computation.

-notokens

Specifies to not use doetoken licenses for the design simulations.

-podkey <value>

Specifies a Power on Demand license key.

-power

Specifies to check out Power Session licenses for each design simulation. Using this option together with - podkey <value> enables Power on Demand licensing.

Note: This option is not supported when running Design Manager in Pre-Allocation Mode. To check out Power Session licenses in pre-allocation mode, use the Design Manager Option - preallocpower.

-tokensonly

Specifies to only use doetoken licenses for the design simulations. With this option, you can also use doetoken licenses for regular parallel runs in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

For the Default Licensing Scheme, the following table displays the supported combinations of license option and the associated license usage:

Troubleshooting Design Manager

If you encounter problems when setting up or running a design study, check these common problem scenarios for advice on how to proceed.

Connection to Job Manager fails due to invalid proxy settings

You can encounter problems with invalid proxy settings in the following situations:

• Situation 1: Opening or creating a Design Manager project

• Situation 2: Running a Design Manager project in pre-allocation mode

In these cases, Design Manager displays the following error message:

ERROR: Connection to Job Manager failed. Check http proxy settings, use command line option or change configuration to bypass proxy, or contact your system administrator.

There are typically two environment variables that control the usage of an HTTP proxy on a computer:

• http_proxy—contains the address (and optionally the user name and password) of the proxy to be used

• no_proxy—defines the host names or patterns to be contacted without use of the proxy

For example:

export http_proxy=http://10.203.0.1:5187/ export no_proxy="localhost,127.0.0.1,localaddress,.localdomain.com"

There are some OS specific places (for example the Windows registry) where the proxy can be defined as well.

Problems occur when the HTTP proxy is not set up correctly, for example:

• http_proxy is set but points to an unavailable or non-existent proxy server.

• http_proxy is set but no_proxy is not set. In this case, the http_proxy server is also used for communication to the local host, which is not allowed.

To resolve the error in Design Manager:

• In Situation 1:

Navigate to [INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin, open the starlaunch.cfg configuration file in a text editor, and un-comment the line bypassproxy = true.

• In Situation 2:

Add the --bypassproxy option to the starlaunch command.

Example: starlaunch jobmanager --command <batch_command> --slots 0 --batchsystem -- bypassproxy

For more information, see Pre-Allocation Submission Script Requirements.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6882

Interacting with CAE Software

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ can integrate a wide range of other computer-aided engineering (CAE) tools into a simulation.

The basic import and export features let you use external geometry, surface and volume mesh data, as well as export such data from a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation. Therefore you can incorporate a host of external file formats and CAE models into your simulation.

A more advanced integration of CAE with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is coupling. This capability allows you to use Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to obtain part of the solution, and a second code to obtain another part of the solution. By coupling the two codes together, solution data is passed between them at specified intervals during the simulation, and you can obtain a solution for the whole model. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ offers two methods of coupling: file-based coupling, whereby data is exchanged between codes via files stored in the computer disk, and co-simulation, in which data is exchanged automatically while the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation and the partner simulation are running.

File-based coupling is very versatile and can be used for most types of coupled simulation. It relies on the user to manually execute the coupling steps via the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ interface, although the process can be automated via scripts. Co-simulation allows for data exchange between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and the following:

• Simcenter STAR-CCM+ (co-simulation between two Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulations)

• Simcenter Nastran

• Simcenter Amesim

• FMU

• Abaqus

• GT-SUITE

• WAVE

• RELAP

• Reacting Channel (1D Plug Flow Reactor in DARS)

For co-simulation with GT-SUITE, Simcenter Amesim, WAVE, and RELAP, coupling works best if the interfaces are located where the flow is largely one-dimensional, as this will reduce errors due to averaging. The worst place for a coupling interface is where there is partial reverse flow, because the mean flow is not representative of either the forward or reverse flows.

The methods available for each coupling technique depend on which third party software you are coupling with Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Note: Currently, co-simulation does not support host specification using the IPv6 communication protocol.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6883

On Windows version 7 or older, the length of the PATH environment variable can affect the co-simulation functionality. You are advised to reduce the length of the PATH by storing the path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation in a separate environment variable:

CCM=[path to STAR-CCM+ INSTALL_DIR] PATH=%CCM%\lib;%CCM%\vtk;...

Importing into Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ allows you to import models from a number of other CAE packages so that you can use data associated with the model in your Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation.

You can use an imported CAE model in a standalone Simcenter STAR-CCM+ analysis, or for coupling Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with other codes using file-based coupling. You can also import data from STAR-CD for post-processing in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Importing Mesh and Solution Data from STAR-CD

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ allows you to import mesh and solution data from STAR-CD, in order to post-process the STAR-CD solution data using the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ visualization tools. This import option does not support Lagrangian solution data.

Since the STAR-CD v4.04 release, the solution data provided by STAR (the solver) has been stored in two files: the .ccmp file for standard (restart) solution data, and the .ccmt file for transient solution data. Both of these files contain a link to the corresponding .ccmg file for the mesh data; if this .ccmg file is missing, it is not possible for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to read either the .ccmp or the .ccmt file. This import option does not support solution data from moving mesh calculations.

The procedure for importing both mesh and solution data from STAR-CD is described as follows (assuming that the necessary STAR-CD files have been copied into the working directory):

1. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and start a new simulation in the manner appropriate to your environment.

2. Select File > Import > Import Volume Mesh...

3. In the Open dialog, select the desired .ccmp or .ccmt file. Make sure that the corresponding .ccmg file is also available.

4. Click Open.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6886

If solution data is successfully read from the file, information on the process is displayed in the Output window. This information includes details of the solution data found in the file, and details of the scalar fields in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to which the solution has been mapped. An example of this output is shown below.

CCM file version 20617

Importing CAE Models

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ allows you to import CAE models that have been prepared in other CAE products. You can use imported CAE models for standalone Simcenter STAR-CCM+ analyses or for coupling Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with external CAE codes using the file-based coupling technique.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ supports the import of CAE models containing shells, surfaces, beams, and volumes from the following codes:

• Abaqus

• ANSYS

• Nastran

• RadTherm (shells only)

• es-ice or pro-STAR

It is also possible to import a CAE model in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary format (.sbd). These files are used in the same way as CAE models imported from the codes that are listed above, but you cannot import them as regions. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ also supports the import of Ensight input files, which can be used to visualize and compare multiple solutions in one simulation. For more information, see Working with the STARCCM+ Boundary Data (.sbd) Format and Working with Ensight.

For Nastran models, you can import data that was defined in local coordinate systems. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ transforms the data into a global coordinate system during the import process. All other formats are imported in a global coordinate system, as importing from local coordinate systems is not supported.

To import a CAE model:

1. Select File > Import > Import CAE Model...

2. In the Open dialog, select the file to import and click Open.

3. In the Import Options dialog, set the Import Mode to one of the following options:

▶Create New Region(s)—this option allows you to import the CAE model as a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ region. The imported region can then be used in the same way as any other region in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

▶Create New Region(s) and Imported Model(s)—this option imports the CAE model as a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ region and, additionally, adds the Imported Models node to the simulation tree, for file-based coupling. From this node, you can export solution data from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to a file format that can be read into the third-party CAE code. Similarly, you can import solution data from the CAE code into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and use the data to define boundary conditions in the simulation. See File-Based Coupling.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6888

You can use the Units menu to specify the units of the CAE model.

4. Click OK.

The progress is shown in the Output window. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ recognizes geometrical elements that are defined in the imported file, and adds a geometry part for each volume that is defined in the CAE model. All geometry parts are automatically assigned to a single region. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ also adds corresponding boundaries and part surfaces for any surface that is defined in the CAE model. If the CAE model contains vertex specifications, including single feature vertices or groups of vertices, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ creates associated part points (which can be used for stress analysis with the Solid Stress model. See Solid Stress: Preparing the Geometry).

Note: When you import a CAE model, do not delete or modify the association between the region and the parts that represent the imported CAE model. For imported CAE models, part-region associations cannot be restored once they are deleted.

If you set Import Mode to Create New Region(s) and Imported Model(s), Simcenter STAR-CCM+ also adds the imported model under the Imported Models node, for file-based coupling with the corresponding CAE code.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6889

The imported CAE model node typically contains two subnodes, Imported surfaces and Imported elements. These nodes show the imported surfaces and elements that are defined in the CAE model file.

Note: When you import a CAE model containing a volume, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically extracts the free surface of the imported body and creates a corresponding boundary. When you import a model containing shells, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically locates the positive and negative side of each shell.

An imported CAE model can be visualized in a scene, in the same way as regions, boundaries, and parts. For more information, see Visualizing an Imported CAE Model.

Note: The import procedure is different when importing a CAE model from pro-STAR or es-ice.

Exporting Mesh and Solution Data

This section outlines the steps for exporting Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mesh and solution data to formats that can be used in other CAE packages.

While this topic covers general export of mesh and solution data, other topics provide instructions and format information for exporting the following:

• 3D-CAD geometry

• Mesh surfaces

• Mesh and Solution Data to CGNS

To export mesh and solution data:

1. Select File > Export ...

This menu item opens a modified form of the standard Save To File dialog. In this dialog, you can specify the file type, the name of the new file, and which types of data to export to the file.

2. Choose the scope of the data to select from the Export Type drop-down list.

The following options are available:

◦ Mesh Only

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6891

◦ Mesh and Solution Data

◦ Solution Data Only

3. Use the Files of Type drop-down list to choose the output format.

The currently supported export formats include:

Type of File Type of Data Exported Further Information

CCM (*.ccm) Mesh data and solution data Exports volume mesh and solution data. If you select the CCM format, you can activate Append to existing file to add the exported information to a .ccm file that you select. For example ESI/VA One, FFT/Actran, and LMS/Virtual.Lab (used in noise propagation cases), can read this format.

When exporting a user-defined field function, make sure that the function property, Function Name, only contains characters of the following types:

◦ A-Z, a-z, 0-9

◦ special characters other than the forward slash "/" (that is, ASCII values from 32 to 126, except for 47)

Note:In CCM files, mesh indices are written as 32-bit integers. This approach sets a limit to the size of meshes that you can export using the CCM format. Estimated upper limits are ~700 million cells for trimmed meshes and ~350 million cells for polyhedral meshes.

CGNS, CFD General Notation System (HDF5) (*.cgns) Mesh data and solution data Legacy option. For CGNS export, see Exporting Data to CGNS Files .

Exports volume mesh and solution data. Open format, CFD General Notation System.

Appending is allowed. When exporting polyhedral volume meshes to CGNS format, regions and boundaries can import into some third-party codes as a single region and single boundary. This limitation only applies to meshes containing polyhedral cells.

CGNS has two internal data formats, HDF5 and ADF. HDF5 is the default and preferred standard over the older ADF format.

For automatic export of transient data, set Trigger to either Time Step or Delta Time, as required. Also, make sure that the file Base

CGNS, CFD General Notation System (ADF) (*.cga)

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6892

Type of File Type of Data Exported Further Information

Name does not contain any special characters, such as _ and @.

When you export solution data, but not mesh data, make sure that the mesh does not change during the analysis. If the mesh changes, choose to export both mesh and solution data.

Siemens Virtual.Lab Custom CGNS (HDF5) (*.cgns) Mesh data and solution data Exports volume mesh and solution data in a format that is suitable for LMS Virtual.Lab.

This option is intended for exporting transient pressure data to Siemens Virtual.Lab, for aeroacoustic analysis.

As LMS Virtual.Lab does not support polyhedral meshes, do not export regions with polyhedral meshes to this file format. However, you can export boundaries with polygonal surface meshes. Before exporting to CGNS, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ merges the boundaries and triangulates any polygonal faces.

For automatic export of the transient data, set Trigger to either Time Step or Delta Time, as required. Also, make sure that the file Base Name does not contain any special characters, such as _ and @.

When you export solution data, but not mesh data, make sure that the mesh does not change during the analysis. If the mesh changes, choose to export both mesh and solution data.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically appends the exported data to the file that is saved during the first export. See Automatically exporting Mesh and Solution data at Regular Intervals.

Ensight Gold (*.case) Mesh data and solution data Exports volume mesh and solution data. You can export solution data from either cells or vertices. When you select a region, the surface mesh is also exported.

Appending to an existing file is allowed.

Automatically Exporting Mesh and Solution Data at Regular Intervals

When running a long simulation (either interactively or in batch mode) it is useful to enable the auto export feature. This feature causes Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to export the solution data automatically at regular intervals during the run, when the Export... command is disabled. This section includes a description of the properties of the Auto Export dialog.

• For automatic export to CGNS files, follow the instructions in Exporting Data to CGNS Files .

• For automatic export to other file formats, follow the instructions provided in this section.

1. Select File > Auto Export... from the menu.

The Auto Export dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6896

2. Expand the Auto Export > Update node and activate Enabled .

To specify the file format that you want to export to:

3. Select the file format from the drop-down list in the Values column of the File Format property.

4. Specify the Base Name.

The base name is the prefix of the name of the file that you want to export your data to.

5. Specify the Export Directory if necessary.

This directory is the location of the file that you want to export your data to. The default path is the same as

the path of your simulation file. Clicking (Custom Editor) activates a dialog similar to the Save dialog. You can use this dialog to navigate to a new location for the file.

6. Enter the type of separator that should be used in the Separator property.

By default, when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ saves copies of the simulation file, it places a @ character to separate the base file name and the number of the trigger event. If the use of this character in this manner causes any problems with your system, you can enter a different one as the separator. If you attempt to leave this field blank, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ puts the @ character there by default.

7. If you want to add the exported data to an existing file, activate Append To File.

8. If you prefer not to export the mesh data, activate Export Solution Data Only.

9. To export vertex data, activate Export Data on Vertices.

This option is only available when your export includes solution data, and when you are exporting to an Ensight Gold file.

To select the scalar values that you want to export:

10.Click (Custom Editor) next to Scalar Functions.

11.In the Auto Export - Scalar Functions dialog, select the desired functions and click OK.

12.Using the same method as defining the scalar functions, you can select vector functions, regions, boundaries, derived parts, and parts surfaces.

13.Select the trigger type from the drop down menu of the Trigger property.

This property specifies how the auto export operation is triggered. Unless you are running a transient analysis, leave the setting at Iteration. For more information, see Trigger Types.

14.To control the number of intervals that pass between auto exports, expand the Trigger > Frequency node and enter the value that you want. See Trigger Properties.

15.Click Close.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically exports during the next run at the intervals you specified. To deactivate this feature, simply reopen the Auto Export dialog and deactivate Enabled.

Auto Export Properties

You can use the following properties to activate and customize this feature:

File Format

Selects the format of the file from a drop-down list.

Base Name

The prefix of the file name to use when exporting your data.

Export Directory

The directory that contains your file with exported data.

Separator

Specifies the character that appears between the base file name and the number of the trigger event (@ by default).

Format Width

Width of the iteration, time, or step number in the formatted file name.

Append to File

When activated, adds the exported information to an existing file. This file would be the one you specify in the Base Name, Export Directory and File Format properties.

This option works for .ccm, Ensight and .trn file formats only.

Export Solution Data Only

When activated, exports solution data and the mesh for the first designated time step or iteration and thereafter exports solution data only without the mesh. However, in cases with mesh motion, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ does export the mesh when there are significant topological changes between the designated exports.

Export Data on Vertices

When activated, exports vertex data. This option is only available when your export includes solution data, and when you are exporting to an Ensight Gold file.

Scalar Functions

Determines which scalar values to export.

Vector Functions

Determines which vectors to export.

Regions

Selects regions to export. See Exporting Region and Boundary Data.

Boundaries

Selects boundaries to export. See Exporting Region and Boundary Data.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6898

Derived Parts

Selects derived parts to export. See Accessing Solution Data through Derived Parts.

Part Surfaces

Selects part surfaces to export.

Update

When expanded, this property makes available the controls listed below.

Enabled

When activated, enables the auto export feature.

Trigger

Provides choices for triggering the automatic export. See Trigger Types.

Iteration Frequency

Controls the number of trigger events between exports. See Trigger Properties.

The settings are saved in the simulation database.

Exporting Region and Boundary Data

The following rules apply when exporting region and/or boundary data:

• If no regions and no boundaries are selected, data for all the regions (including the boundaries) in the simulation is exported.

• Selecting a region automatically selects the boundaries that are associated with that region. Data for the selected region (including the associated boundaries) is exported. This action has the same effect as manually selecting a region and the boundaries in that region.

• Selecting a boundary does not automatically select the region that is associated with that boundary. Data for the selected boundary is exported.

• Selecting boundaries without also selecting regions results in a .ccm file that contains only boundary data. This option is not compatible with pro-STAR.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6899

CGNS File Import and Export

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ allows for import or export of data through CGNS files. CGNS (CFD General Notation System) is a standard data format that can can contain both mesh and solution data.

As the CGNS standard is widely used by a variety of software packages, CGNS import/export enables data exchange between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and external software. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ allows you to:

• Import mesh and solution data from a CGNS file and apply it to regions or boundaries.

• Export mesh and solution data from regions or boundaries to a CGNS file.

Preparing the Simulation for CGNS File Exchange

To import or export data through CGNS files, you require an additional physics continuum with the File Import/Export model. This continuum represents the external CGNS file and is not related to the physics that are solved in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation.

To enable CGNS file exchange in a simulation:

1. Create a new physics continuum with the following models:

Group box Model

Optional Models External Continuum

External Continuum External Application (selected automatically)

External Application File Import/Export

Space Select one of the following:

◦ For import or export of boundary data (surface mesh and, optionally, solution data), select Surface Three Dimensional.

◦ For import or export of region data (volume mesh and, optionally, solution data), select Three Dimensional.

When you create the external physics continuum, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ adds a CGNS link node to the simulation tree, External Links > [Link 1]. The link is automatically configured for CGNS export:

Assign the CGNS link to the external continuum. The Space model selected in the associated continuum determines whether the data are exchanged at boundaries or regions.

2. Select the External Links > [Link 1] > Conditions > External Continua node and select the external continuum.

You can use a link for import or export, but not both. However, you can create multiple CGNS links and external continua in the same simulation.

3. To set up the link for import or export, follow the instructions in:

▶Exporting Data to CGNS Files

▶Importing Data from a CGNS File

Exporting Data to CGNS Files

You specify all export settings in a CGNS link under the External Links node. Export settings include the mesh and solution data that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ exports to CGNS, the data export frequency, and the CGNS file format and location.

To set up a CGNS link for export:

1. Follow the instructions in Preparing the Simulation for CGNS File Exchange .

2. Expand the relevant CGNS link node, for example, External Links > [Link 1].

3. Select the Conditions > Transfer Direction node and set Option to Export.

To specify the mesh and solution data that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ exports to CGNS, you set up an export zone. You can use the default zone node, Zones > [Zone 1].

A zone can export boundary data (surface zone) or region data (volume zone), depending on the space model selected in the associated external continuum (see Preparing the Simulation for CGNS File Exchange). Although a link node accepts a combination of volume and surface zones, you are advised to only have one type in each link node, particularly for 2D simulations.

To export mesh data, specify the relevant surface parts (boundaries) or volume parts (regions) for export:

4. Select the [Zone 1] > Conditions > Surface Parts or Volume Parts node and set Parts to the relevant boundaries, or regions, respectively.

Optionally, you can export solution data. To export solution data:

5. Right-click the [Zone 1] > Conditions > Exported Fields node, select Add Auxiliary Field and choose Scalar or Vector, as appropriate.

6. Select the Exported Fields > [Auxiliary Field] node and set the following properties:

Property Setting

Field Stencil Select a mesh stencil for data mapping (see Field Stencil ). All the exported fields within a given zone must have the same stencil.

Scalar/Vector Function Select the field function whose data you want to export to CGNS.

The remaining properties are read-only.

If required, you can add other fields for export. If you do not add any fields under the Exported Fields node, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ exports only mesh data.

When exporting boundaries with polygonal meshes, you can choose whether Simcenter STAR-CCM+ retains the original surface mesh or converts the mesh faces to triangular faces. Unlike polygonal meshes, triangular meshes are supported by most software packages.

7. Select the [Zone 1] > Conditions > Boundary Triangulation node and set Option as required.

For more information, see Boundary Triangulation.

When exporting multiple boundaries, you can choose whether Simcenter STAR-CCM+ retains the individual boundaries or merges the boundaries into one:

8. Select the [Zone 1] > Conditions > Merge Boundaries node and set Option as required.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6902

◦ If you select Merge Boundaries Into One, specify the boundary name under the [Zone 1] > Values > Merged Boundaries Name node.

For more information, see Merge Boundaries.

The CGNS standard provides two file formats, ADF (.cga) and HDF5 (.cgns). By default, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the newer HDF5 format. To change the file format:

9. Select the [Link 1] > Conditions > Database Format node and select the required format.

For more information, see Database Format.

In a simulation, you can have one or more export events. While Simcenter STAR-CCM+ exports solution data at every export event, you can restrict the export of mesh data based on mesh changes:

10.Select the [Link 1] > Conditions > Mesh Mode node and select one of the following:

▶Always Enabled—exports mesh data at every export event.

▶Initially and on Mesh Change—exports the mesh in the first export event. In subsequent events, mesh export occurs only if the mesh has changed.

You can instruct Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to create new CGNS files at each export event or append data to existing files:

11.Select the [Link 1] > Conditions > File Mode node and select one of the following:

▶File Series—creates new files at every export event. The number of files depends on the specified Mesh Mode. See Output CGNS Files.

▶Single File—creates a single file each for mesh and solution data during the first export event. In subsequent export events, appends data to the same file.

For more information, see File Mode.

You can trigger export events manually or instruct Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to export data automatically at regular time intervals. Automatic export is suitable for transient simulations, while steady simulations rely on manual export.

To define a trigger for automatic data export:

12.Select the [Link 1] > Conditions > Trigger node and set Option to one of the following:

▶Time-Step—specify the number of time-steps between export events under the [Link 1] > Values > Time-Steps per Transfer node.

▶Delta-Time—specify the time interval between export events under the [Link 1] > Values > Delta-Time node.

Optionally, you can restrict automatic data export to a specified time range by specifying the times at which Simcenter STAR-CCM+ starts or stops exporting data:

13.Select the [Link 1] > Conditions > Time Range node and select the desired Option.

Depending on the selected option, set the relevant times using the [Link 1] > Values > Start Time and Stop Time nodes.

To trigger an export event manually:

◦ Right-click the [Link 1] node and select Export File.

By default, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ exports the relevant files to the current working directory. For the exported files, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the name prefix, solution. To change these settings:

14.Select the [Link 1] > Values > File node and set its properties.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6903

For more information, see File.

Importing Data from a CGNS File

You specify all import settings in a CGNS link under the External Links node. Import settings include the mesh and solution data that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ imports from CGNS, and the CGNS file details.

To set up a CGNS link for import:

1. Follow the instructions in Preparing the Simulation for CGNS File Exchange.

2. Expand the relevant CGNS link node, for example, External Links > [Link 1].

3. Select the Conditions > Transfer Direction node and set Option to Import.

Specify the CGNS file from which Simcenter STAR-CCM+ imports data. You can import data from a single file or from multiple files:

4. Select the Conditions > File Mode node and set Option to either Single File or File Series, as appropriate.

When importing from multiple files, the files must have the same name prefix. For example, the file series LinkExp@00001.cgns, LinkExp@00002.cgns, LinkExp@00003.cgns has the same name prefix, LinkExp.

5. Select the [Link 1] > Values > File node and set the following properties:

Property Setting

Directory Select (Custom Editor) and navigate to the folder containing the CGNS file. You can either select the directory or the file itself. When selecting the file, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically updates the Base Filename and Extension properties.

Base Filename ◦ For single file import, enter the name of the file, without path or file extension.

◦ For multiple files, enter the name prefix of the file series.

Before you can specify the data that is imported from the CGNS file, you instruct Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to parse and index the data available in the file:

6. Right-click the [Link 1] node and select Scan.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ parses the base nodes in the CGNS file and retrieves the available zones and solution states. Each solution state corresponds to solution data at a particular time or iteration. For more information on the structure of a CGNS file, see the official documentation, CGNS File Structure.

7. Select the [Link 1] > Values > Import Link State node.

The State Name property lists the solution states from the CGNS file. Each state is named <Solution State Time>:<Base Filename>:<CGNS Base Node Name>. For each state, the other properties of the Import Link State node display information on the solution time or iteration and an index assigned by Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

To import the data at a specified solution state:

8. Select the Import Link State node and select the relevant solution state by selecting either the State Name, Solution State Time, or Iteration under the corresponding property.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6904

These three properties are dependent, so you only need to set one of the properties to select a solution state.

To set up the link node based on the selected solution state and to create the required external regions and boundaries:

9. Right-click the [Link 1] node and select Create External Parts.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically performs the following operations:

◦ Checks that the CGNS file contains zones that are consistent with the space model that you selected in the external continuum.

◦ Creates external regions and boundaries based on the volume and surface zones that are defined in the CGNS file.

◦ Creates the required zone nodes under the [Link 1] > Zones node. For each zone, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically selects the External Volume Parts or External Surface Parts, and the Imported Fields, as defined in the CGNS file.

For more information, see Import Settings.

Unlike export events, you can only trigger import events manually. To import the mesh data from the file:

10.Right-click the [Link 1] node and select Import Meshes.

To import solution data from the file:

11.Right-click the [Link 1] node and select Import Fields.

CGNS Link Reference

You specify the CGNS import/export details in a link node under the External Links node. A CGNS link node represents a connection to a CGNS file.

The following settings are always available and apply to both import and export.

[Link 1] Properties

Link Type

Describes the type of connection. Read-only.

[Link 1] Models

Link models configure the connection to a partner application or file. The link icon changes based on the application, or file, that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ connects to through the link. The link model must be appropriate for the co-simulation or file export model selected in the physics continuum.

[Link 1] Conditions and Values

CGNS Version (Read-Only)

Specifies the version of the CGNS standard in use. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ currently supports version 3.2.1.

Transfer Direction

Specifies whether Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses this link for import or export of data to the CGNS format.

Mapping Option (Read-Only)

Automatically set to No Mapping.

Verbosity Level

Controls the amount of information that is printed to the Output window.

External Continua

Allows you to select the external physics continuum in which you chose the File Import/Export model.

Zones Manager Properties

Number of Zones

Displays the number of zones defined for this link. Read-only.

Zones Manager Right-Click Actions

New

Adds a zone under the Zones node.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6907

[Zone] Properties

Index

Specifies a unique index which identifies a zone. Read-only.

Zone Type

Set automatically based on the space model you select in the external physics continuum. CGNS export supports surface zones (for export of boundary data) and volume zones (for export of region data).
