Exporting Pressure Loads

For co-simulation, export the pressure load on a wall boundary using one of two field functions: Static Pressure or Absolute Pressure. The Absolute Pressure in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is the absolute static pressure, which is the sum of the static pressure and the reference pressure. The Static Pressure is equal to the absolute pressure minus the reference pressure, and is often termed the "gauge" pressure in literature. The following diagram illustrates the relationship between these values.

Note: Use consistent applications of pressure in both Abaqus and Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In Abaqus, the reference pressure is the pressure at which the structure is considered to be unloaded, with no displacements. It is the variation of the absolute static pressure with respect to the reference pressure that causes deformations and strains in the structure.

As an example of how to ensure consistency, consider a cylinder that is loaded on the inside diameter (ID) and the outside diameter (OD). Simcenter STAR-CCM+ models the fluid on the inside of the cylinder. Assume that the OD of the cylinder is subject to 1 bar (atmospheric conditions), and that the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ reference pressure is 1 bar (which is the default value). If Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is set to export the Static Pressure as the load on the ID, then, in Abaqus, load the OD of the cylinder with zero load to be consistent.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7157

In effect, this means that no load is required in Abaqus at the OD. If, however, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is set to export the Absolute Pressure as the load on the ID of the cylinder, then, in Abaqus, load the OD with 1 bar (that is, the same value as the reference pressure in Simcenter STAR-CCM+).

If the absolute static pressure within the cylinder is 10 bar when the fluid velocity is zero, it is convenient for the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ reference pressure to be set to 10 bar. With the 10-bar reference pressure, if you export Static Pressure as the load on the ID, in Abaqus the OD must be loaded with a pressure of -9 bar (that is, a tension load) to be consistent. If, however, you choose to export Absolute Pressure from Simcenter STAR-CCM+, load the OD in the Abaqus with a pressure of 1 bar.

This procedure of loading the OD of the cylinder with the pressure that will give the correct net loading on the structure is correct only for elements where through-thickness behavior is not considered (for example, shell elements). If solid elements are used to model the cylinder, then applying fictitious loads to the OD will produce the correct bulk loading, but incorrect behavior in the walls of the cylinder. In this case, absolute pressure should be exported to Abaqus for the ID and the ambient pressure should be applied on the OD within the Abaqus model.

Model Dimensions and Coordinate Systems

Co-simulation between two-dimensional and axisymmetric models is not supported. Represent twodimensional models as a three-dimensional slice of unit thickness, or wedge element, with the appropriate symmetry boundary conditions applied.

Vector fields are transferred according to Abaqus and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ conventions. The first component represents the quantity along the x-axis, the second component represents the quantity along the y-axis, and the third component represents the quantity along the z-axis. All fields are transferred in the global coordinate system (the Laboratory Coordinate System in Simcenter STAR-CCM+). If a local coordinate system is applied in the Abaqus model, the incoming and outgoing fields are transformed appropriately.

Co-Location of the Abaqus and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Models

Co-locate the Abaqus and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ models. Place the fluid-structure interface regions of both models in the same geometric positions in space. Ensure that the coupled wall boundaries in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are not larger or smaller in extent than the corresponding interface in the Abaqus model.

Supported Abaqus Elements

Abaqus supports first-order and second-order continuum, shell, and membrane elements. Modified tetrahedral elements are not supported due to mapping limitations.

Supported Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Cells

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ supports tetrahedral and trimmed mesh cell types, as well as cells of arbitrary polyhedral type in 3D for co-simulation with Abaqus.

Known Limitations

This section lists the known limitations of co-simulation using Abaqus and Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• Run Abaqus and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on binary compatible platforms.

• The coupled boundaries must be of the same spatial extents - the coupled boundaries cannot be larger or smaller in extent than their counterpart in either code.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7158

• If coupling both sides of a double-sided structure, a separate surface must be created for each side of the structure and assigned to a separate coupling zone in the fluid domain.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7159

GT-SUITE Co-Simulation

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ allows for two-way co-simulation with GT-SUITE, a multiphysics simulation tool from Gamma Technologies. GT-SUITE provides a modeling framework for the design and analysis of engineering systems, such as engines, vehicles, and thermal-hydraulic networks.

During the co-simulation, GT-SUITE drives the overall one-dimensional system simulation, while Simcenter STAR-CCM+ models the flow within components that require a three-dimensional analysis. For example, you can use Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to model an intake manifold that forms part of an engine analysis designed in GT-SUITE.

Co-Simulation Interface

In GT-SUITE, you define the co-simulation interface using the following objects:

• CFD Component—represents the component that is modeled in 3D using Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• CFD Interfaces—mark the 1D/3D interfaces between GT-SUITE and Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• CFD Connections—define the physical conditions and values at the 1D/3D interfaces.

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you couple the relevant boundaries with GT-SUITE using co-simulation zones. Each co-simulation zone uniquely associates a GT-SUITE CFD connection with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7160

Co-simulation zones and CFD connections must match in number and name.

Exchanged Fields

Co-simulation supports coupling between CFD connections (either CFDFlowConn or CFDFlowConnBeta connections) and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundaries of type Mass Flow Inlet, Velocity Inlet, or Pressure Outlet.

The fields that are exchanged between the CFD connection and the coupled Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary depend on:

• the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary type

• the GT-SUITE CFD Interface Condition that you define for the CFD connection

Simcenter STAR-CCM + Boundary Type

GT-SUITE CFD Connection GT-SUITE CFD Interface Condition Imposed by GT

Imported from GTSUITE Exported to GTSUITE

Velocity Inlet CFDFlowConn Flow (velocity or mass flow rate) Velocity Static Pressure

CFDFlowConnBeta Flow (CFD imposes GT pressure): Velocity

Mass Flow Inlet CFDFlowConn Flow (velocity or mass flow rate) Velocity Density Static Pressure

CFDFlowConnBeta Flow (CFD imposes GT pressure): Velocity

Flow (CFD imposes GT pressure): Mass Flow Rate

Mass

Pressure Outlet CFDFlowConn Pressure Depending on the flow direction, either:

• Static Pressure, when flow is leaving the Simcenter STARCCM+ boundary

• Total Pressure, when flow is entering the boundary

Velocity

CFDFlowConnBeta Pressure (CFD imposes GT velocity)

Pressure (CFD imposes GT mass flow) Mass

At a Mass Flow Inlet boundary, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ applies the mass flow rate that is calculated from the imported fields (either velocity and density, or mass).

Depending on the flow direction, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ also imports or exports the following fields, regardless of the type of coupled boundary and CFD connection:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7161

Flow Direction Imported from GT-SUITE Exported to GT-SUITE

Entering the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary Temperature Mass Fractions --

Leaving the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary -- Temperature Mass Fractions Passive Scalars

At a Mass Flow Inlet boundary, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ applies the total temperature that is calculated from the imported static temperature and velocity. At a Velocity Inlet boundary, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ directly applies the static temperature imported from GT-SUITE.

GT-SUITE and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ do not exchange turbulence values. Turbulence values are specified in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ at the boundary level, in the usual manner.

Before sending data back to GT-SUITE, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ averages the computed fields across sampling volumes adjacent to the coupled boundaries, to convert the three-dimensional fields to one-dimensional values. Volume averaging is important when significant three-dimensional effects occur near the coupled boundary. The co-simulation provides optimum results when the flow in the sampling volumes is approximately one-dimensional.

GT-SUITE co-simulation uses an explicit coupling scheme, that is, data exchange occurs once per time-step.

Multi-Component Gases: Coupled Material Components

In co-simulation with GT-SUITE you can model single-component gases and liquids, and multi-component gases. When you model multi-component gases, GT-SUITE defines the components of the fluid mixture in the co-simulation. These components include unburned species and burned species, which result from the products of reaction between the unburned species. The combustion products consist of 13 components with varying composition:

prod_ar: Argon prod_co: Carbon Monoxide prod_co2: Carbon Dioxide prod_h: Monatomic Hydrogen prod_h2: Hydrogen prod_h2o: Water prod_n: Monatomic Nitrogen prod_n2: Nitrogen prod_no: Nitric Oxide prod_o: Monatomic Oxygen prod_o2: Oxygen prod_oh: Hydroxide prod_so2: Sulphur Dioxide

You associate the GT-SUITE species with corresponding mixture components or passive scalars in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Mixture components represent GT-SUITE species that influence the bulk flow, that is, species that have non-trace quantities. Passive scalars represent GT-SUITE species that do not influence the bulk flow, that is, species that have trace quantities.

The species mass fractions are exchanged at the co-simulation interface, as described in the previous section.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7162

GT-SUITE Coupling Libraries

In order to communicate with GT-SUITE, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ requires the location of the double precision GT-SUITE coupling library. By default, the coupling library file is located at:

Platform Library File Location

Linux [GTIHOME]/[GT-SUITE_version]/GTsuite/bin/linux_x86_64/ coupling/libgtlink_dp.so

Windows [GTIHOME]/[GT-SUITE_version]/GTsuite/bin/win64/coupling/ gtlink_dp.dll

where [GTIHOME] is the path to the GT-SUITE installation and [GT-SUITE_version] is the version of GT-SUITE.

Preparing the GT-SUITE Simulation for Co-Simulation

Starting from a fully set up GT-SUITE simulation, you define the co-simulation interface by adding CFD objects to the model map.

The following instructions outline the general workflow and may vary based on the version of GT-SUITE that you are running.

• For a step-by-step example using GT-SUITE v2017, refer to the tutorial GT-SUITE Co-Simulation: 1D Coupling.

• For more information on setting up a simulation in GT-SUITE, refer to the GT-SUITE User Guide.

Before you define co-simulation settings:

1. Launch GT-ISE and load the GT-SUITE simulation that you want to couple with Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

2. Run the standalone GT-SUITE analysis until converged.

This practice allows you to:

◦ Check that the GT-SUITE simulation is set up correctly.

◦ Determine the number of cycles that are required to achieve convergence.

◦ Use the results from the standalone GT-SUITE analysis as initial conditions in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, in order to speed up convergence of the coupled problem.

3. Analyze the results in GT-POST, making note of the average values for pressure, temperature, and, when modeling multi-component gases, species mass fractions.

To prepare the simulation for coupling, you add CFD objects to the GT-SUITE model. CFD objects allow you to define the interfaces with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and to control the co-simulation settings. To create CFD objects, you require the corresponding templates:

4. In the Templates and Search ribbon, click Template Library.

5. In the Template Library tree, expand the Flow > General Flow node.

6. Drag and drop the following templates from the template library tree onto the project tree:

◦ Components > CFDComponent

◦ Components > CFDInterface

◦ either:

▪Connections > CFDFlowConn

▪Connections > CFDFlowConnBeta

The CFDFlowConnBeta object exposes additional controls for setting pressure relaxation and tracking mass continuity at the interface.

Defining CFD Objects

Using the CFD templates, add the required CFD objects to the project tree.

To represent the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundaries, add CFD interfaces to the model map:

1. In the model map, locate the components of type 'Pipe*' that you want to couple with Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

2. For each pipe section, replace the default 1D orifices with 1D/3D CFDInterface objects using the following procedure:

a) Delete the default 1D orifices.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7165

b) Drag and drop the Components > CFDInterface > def node from the project tree onto the model map, then place it at the original orifice position.

c) Right-click the CFDInterface on the model map and select Start New Link.

d) Use the Start New Link tool to join the CFDInterface to the adjacent pipes, making sure that the arrows point in the direction of the flow.

CFD interfaces serve as 1D/3D switches. When GT-SUITE and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are uncoupled, GT-SUITE solves the flow in the one-dimensional components. When coupled, the GT-SUITE solver supplies boundary conditions to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and no longer solves the flow in the one-dimensional components.

To define the characteristics of the 1D/3D interfaces, add CFD connections to the model map. To create a CFD connection:

3. In the project tree, right-click either the Connections > CFDFlowConn node or the Connections > CFDFlowConnBeta node and select Add Object...

CFDFlowConnBeta connections allow you to control pressure relaxation and mass continuity at the interface.

4. Define the properties of the CFD connection as follows:

Property/Attribute Setting

CFD Domain Sampling Length Specify the length of the volume-averaging zone, across which Simcenter STAR-CCM+ averages the three-dimensional fields, before sending values to GT-SUITE.

The specified length is rounded up or down to cover the nearest complete mesh cell.

Make sure that the sampling volume length covers an area of the simulation where there is one-dimensional flow.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7166

Property/Attribute Setting

You can visualize the sampling volumes in Simcenter STAR-CCM + using the Average Zone Flag field function in a scalar scene. See Preparing the STAR-CCM+ Simulation for Co-Simulation.

CFD Boundary Cross-section (be precise) Specify the cross-section of the coupled Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary. Set this option so that the areas of the coupling interface between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE match. For a mismatch of more than 5%, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ stops the simulation.

In general, GT-SUITE allows for pipes with circular or rectangular cross-sections. For cross-sections that do not meet these requirements, you can calculate the area of the coupled boundary in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using a Sum report of the Area field function.

Species Map Override def

5. Define the remaining properties based on the type of connection:

▶For a CFDFlowConn object, set Interface Conditions Imposed by GT at the CFD Boundary to one of the following:

▪To couple with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ velocity inlet or mass flow inlet, select Flow (velocity or mass flow rate).

▪To couple with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ pressure outlet, select Pressure.

This choice determines the fields exchanged during the co-simulation. See Boundary Types and Exchanged Fields.

▶For a CFDFlowConnBeta object, set CFD Interface Condition Imposed by GT to one of the following:

▪To couple with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ velocity inlet, select Flow (CFD imposes GT pressure): Velocity.

▪To couple with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mass flow inlet, select either Flow (CFD imposes GT pressure): Velocity or Flow (CFD imposes GT pressure): Mass Flow Rate.

▪To couple with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ pressure outlet, select either Pressure (CFD imposes GT velocity) or Pressure (CFD imposes GT mass flow).

This choice determines the fields exchanged during the co-simulation. For more information, see Boundary Types and Exchanged Fields.

6. Define any remaining properties as appropriate to your case.

To represent the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ region, add a CFD component to the model map:

7. In the project tree, right-click the Components > CFDComponent node and select Add Object...

8. In the Create Object dialog:

a) Set Object Name to the name of the coupled Simcenter STAR-CCM+ region.

b) In the Simulation Phases tab, set Engine Cycles or Time Before CFD (or "cfdreload") Started to the number of pre-cycles that GT-SUITE runs independently before coupling with Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Pre-cycles improve stability in GT-SUITE, providing more accurate boundary conditions from GT-SUITE and therefore reducing the time to reach a converged solution.

9. Complete the set up by defining the GT-SUITE species. See Defining a CFD Species Map in GT-SUITE.

Defining a CFD Species Map in GT-SUITE

CFD species maps determine how the gas components are transferred between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE.

To define a CFD species map:

1. Right-click a CFD component, and select Edit Properties...

2. In the Edit Object dialog, click the ellipsis (...) next to the Species Mapping Object attribute.

3. In the Value Selector dialog, select CFDSpeciesMap from the Create New Object group box and click OK.

4. In the Create Object dialog, set Object to the name of the species map.

5. Set User Defined Species Map to one of the following options:

◦ def — Uniquely associates all GT-SUITE species with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ gas component or passive scalar.

◦ CFDDefinedSpeciesMap — The user-defined CFDDefinedSpeciesMap reference object defines the association of one or more GT-SUITE species with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ gas component or passive scalar. For example, you can map all harmful gases to a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ passive scalar called Pollutants.

6. Set each CFD species to one of the following options:

◦ ign — Ignores the CFD species and does not send it to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. The mass fraction of this species is redistributed between the other species to maintain mass conservation. This option is only recommended for trace components.

◦ CFDSpecies — Associates the GT-SUITE species with the user-defined CFDSpecies in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7168

Defining a CFDDefinedSpeciesMap

A CFDDefinedSpeciesMap is similar to a CFDSpeciesMap, but you can map multiple GT-SUITE species to a single Simcenter STAR-CCM+ species. You can also define the mapping for the intake charge species.

The following steps assume that you are defining a CFD species map, as detailed in the previous section.

To define a CFDDefinedSpeciesMap:

1. In the Edit Object dialog of the CFDSpeciesMap, click the ellipsis (...) next to the User Defined Species Map attribute.

2. In the Value Selector dialog, select CFDDefinedSpeciesMap from the Create New Object group box and click OK.

3. In the Create Object dialog, set Object to the name of the CFDDefinedSpeciesMap.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7169

4. Set each entry in the GT-SUITE Species Name column to the GT-SUITE species that you want to include in the map.

5. Set each entry in the CFD Species Name column to one of the following options:

◦ ign — Ignores the CFD species and does not send it to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. The mass fraction of this species is redistributed between the other species to maintain mass conservation. This option is only recommended for trace components or species that are not used in the GT-SUITE case that you are analyzing.

◦ CFDSpecies — Associates the GT-SUITE species with the user-defined CFDSpecies in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Defining a CFDSpecies.

Defining a CFDSpecies

A CFDSpecies is the species that GT-SUITE passed to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ during a coupled simulation. GT-SUITE writes the material properties for these species when you run the simulation preprocessing.

The following steps assume that you are defining a CFD species map, as detailed in the previous section.

To define a CFDSpecies:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7170

1. In the Edit Object dialog of the CFDSpeciesMap, click the ellipsis (...) next to a CFD species.

2. In the Value Selector, select the relevant species from the GT-SUITE Library tab and click OK.

Set up a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation for co-simulation with GT-SUITE.

You can select further models from the Optional Models group to meet individual simulation requirements.

Simulation preprocessing in GT-SUITE generates a material database file, <GTPOWER_case_name>.chemkin_GT.dbs. To use the same material properties as GT-SUITE, import this file into Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

2. Right-click the Tools > Material Databases node and select New Material Database.

3. Right-click the new material database and select Import Properties.

4. In the Open dialog, select the <GT-POWER_case_name>.chemkin_GT.dbs file and click OK.

5. In the Import Properties dialog, select Import properties for all materials and click OK.

7. In the Import Properties dialog, select Import properties for all materials and click OK.

When modeling multi-component gases, define a mixture component or passive scalar for each species defined in GT-SUITE. In general, use gas components to represent GT-SUITE species that have non-trace quantities, and passive scalars to represent GT-SUITE species that have trace quantities. A mixture component influences the physical properties of the simulation, thus providing the most accurate and realistic solution. A

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7172

passive scalar has no effect on the physical properties of the simulation, which reduces processing times. If you use passive scalars for all species, specify a background fluid in the region.

To add a mixture component to the simulation:

8. Expand the [physics continuum] > Models node.

9. Right-click the Multi-Component Gas > Gas Components node and select Select Mixture Components...

10.In the Select Mixture Components dialog, select gas components from the GT-POWER Materials database, then click Apply.

Note: Although the “fuel-combust” species is a liquid, you can represent it with a gas in the MultiComponent Gas model. This modeling approach does not affect results, as the gas only represents the species in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, with the physics values received from GT-SUITE.

To add a passive scalar to the simulation:

11.Right-click the Passive Scalars node and select New.

To reduce the numerical round-off, set the reference pressure to the average pressure in GT-SUITE. You can identify the average pressure in GT-SUITE by running a standalone GT-SUITE analysis and using GT-POST to analyze the results.

To set the reference pressure:

12.Select the [physics continuum] > Reference Values > Reference Pressure node and set the Value property.

Note: All pressures in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are defined relative to the reference pressure. In GT-SUITE, all pressures are absolute. Take these differences into consideration when defining pressure values.

For best initialization, set the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ initial conditions to the average values from GT-SUITE, which you can obtain by running a standalone GT-SUITE analysis and using GT-POST to analyze the results:

13.Expand the [physics continuum] > Initial Conditions node, and specify the initial conditions as follows:

a) As the initial pressure in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is relative to the reference pressure, set the Pressure value to the difference between the average pressure from GT-SUITE and the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ reference pressure.

b) As the initial temperature in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is an absolute value, set the Static Temperature value to be the same as the average temperature from GT-SUITE.

c) When you model multi-component gases, set the species mass fractions to the average values from

GT-SUITE, by setting the Species Mass Fraction value. Click (Custom Editor) to enter the mass fractions in an array.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7173

Specify boundary types in the usual manner. The coupled boundary types determine the fields exchanged between GT-SUITE and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ during the co-simulation, as explained in Exchanged Fields.

14.Specify the boundary types. For the boundary that couple with GT-SUITE, set the Type to either Mass Flow Inlet, Velocity Inlet, or Pressure Outlet.

The recommended practice is to set the boundary type to mass flow inlet for all coupled boundaries— regardless of whether they are inlets or outlets. If you use a mass flow inlet, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the boundary area, normal velocity, and density from GT-SUITE to determine the mass flow rate at the boundary. Small changes in density are reflected in the mass flow rate across the boundary.

For coupled boundaries that have large negative flows (such as flows that are leaving the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ domain), use coupled velocity inlet boundaries. Using coupled mass flow inlet boundaries can sometimes lead to instabilities for some models. If you use a velocity inlet, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ takes the normal velocity from GT-SUITE and applies it uniformly at the coupled boundaries.

Note: Setting all the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ coupled boundaries to mass flow or velocity inlets does not have the same negative numerical repercussions that would occur in a standalone CFD model. The absolute pressure of the CFD model drives the GT-SUITE solution and sets the mass flux or velocity at the boundary.

15.Specify boundary conditions in the usual manner. On the coupled boundaries, only specify turbulence settings, as all the other values are set by GT-SUITE.

16.Complete the set up by specifying co-simulation settings, including the coupled boundaries, coupled species, and connection settings. For instructions, refer to the section, Specifying Co-Simulation Settings.

Specifying Co-Simulation Settings

Before connecting to GT-SUITE, you couple the GT-SUITE CFD connections with the corresponding Simcenter STAR-CCM+ objects. You also specify co-simulation global settings, such as the connection method and the location of the GT-SUITE case file.

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you define co-simulation settings in a link node under the External Links node. This node is created automatically when you activate the GT-SUITE Co-Simulation model.

To couple GT-SUITE CFD connections with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundaries, you define co-simulation zones:

1. Expand the External Links > [Link 1] > Zones node.

2. Create a zone for each CFD connection defined in GT-SUITE.

By default, the [Link 1] > Zones node contains one zone. To create additional zones, right-click the Zones node and select New.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ matches co-simulation zones and CFD connections by name. To successfully couple Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with GT-SUITE:

3. Rename each co-simulation zone to the name of the corresponding GT-SUITE CFD connection.

Use the co-simulation zones that you created to couple Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundaries with GT-SUITE. To couple a boundary with a GT-SUITE CFD connection:

4. Expand the relevant boundary node, [Fluid Region] > Boundaries > [Boundary].

5. Select the Physics Conditions > External Code Coupling Specification node.

6. Set External Code Coupling Specification to the co-simulation zone associated with the CFD connection of interest.

When you assign a boundary to a co-simulation zone, the Coupled Model Parts property for the zone automatically updates to display the name coupled boundary.

7. Repeat the previous steps as required, to specify all coupled boundaries. The type of coupled boundary and CFD Connection determines the fields that are exchanged during the co-simulation (see Exchanged Fields).

For multi-component gases, associate the GT-SUITE species with corresponding gas components or passive scalars in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

8. Right-click the Link 1 > Values > Partner Material Components node and select New Partner Material Component.

9. Repeat the previous step to create a material component node for each of the species defined in GT-SUITE.

10.Rename each material component node to the name of the corresponding GT-SUITE species.

11.Select each of the Partner Material Components > [Material Component] node and set Coupled STARCCM+ Mixture Component/Passive Scalar to the corresponding gas component or passive scalar.

Note: Make sure that each GT-SUITE species is coupled with a unique mixture component or passive scalar. If you assign two GT-SUITE species to the same gas component, the solver stops with an error message before the first iteration.

Coupling to GT-SUITE

Specify the settings for launching and connecting to GT-SUITE, then initiate coupling.

1. Expand the External Links > Link 1 node.

2. Select the Conditions > GT-SUITE Version node and select the version of GT-SUITE that you are running.

3. Select the Conditions > Partner Filesystem node and specify the location of the GT-SUITE model file:

▶When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE run on the same machine, set Option to Local Filesystem.

▶When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE run on different machines, set Option to Remote Filesystem.

For remote locations, the GT-SUITE model file must be located in the directory from which you execute the GT-SUITE command, gtlink.

4. Select the Values > GT-SUITE Model File node and set GT-SUITE Input File to either the .gtm or .dat model file, as follows:

▶When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE run on the same machine, click (Custom Editor) and use the dialog to select the file in the local filesystem.

▶When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE run on different machines, specify the full name of the model file, including the extension (either .gtm or .dat), without including any folder path.

To initiate the communication with GT-SUITE, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ requires the location of the GT-SUITE coupling libraries (see GT-SUITE Coupling Libraries):

5. Select the Conditions > Load Partner Library Option node and set Option to one of the following:

▶When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE run on the same machine:

1. Select Use environment variable.

2. Select the Values > GTIHOME Environment Variable and set GTIHOME to the path to the GT-SUITE installation. For more information, see Load Partner Library Option.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ looks for the library file in the default location (see GT-SUITE Coupling Libraries) within the specified GT-SUITE installation.

▶When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE run on different machines:

1. Select Specify library file.

2. Copy the coupling library file (for information on the default location, see GT-SUITE Coupling

Libraries) to the machine where Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is running.

3. Select the Values > GT-SUITE Library node and set GT-SUITE Library to the library file that you copied.

Specify the method for launching GT-SUITE:

6. Select the Conditions > Launch Partner Option node and set Option to one of the following:

▶To launch GT-SUITE manually, select Do Not Launch. If GT-SUITE runs on a remote host, this is the only suitable option.

▶To instruct Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to automatically launch GT-SUITE:

1. Select Launch Default Application.

2. Select the Values > GTIHOME Environment Variable node and set GTIHOME to the path to the GT-SUITE installation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7176

3. Select the Values > GTISOFT_LICENSE_FILE Environment Variable node and set GTISOFT_LICENSE_FILE to the path to the directory containing the license file.

For more information, see Launch Partner Option.

When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches GT-SUITE (that is, Launch Partner Option is set to Launch Default Application), Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically uses the launching details for connection. When you launch GT-SUITE manually (that is, Launch Partner Option is set to Do Not Launch), the coupling library requires the host and port on which GT-SUITE is running. The host and port information is stored in a connection file, gtlink.prm. To create this file:

7. Select the Conditions > Connect Option node and set Option to Partner Code Creates Connection File.

When launched, GT-SUITE automatically creates the required gtlink.prm connection file in the directory containing the gtlink command.

8. Copy the gtlink.prm file to the directory containing the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation file.

Note: Versions of GT-SUITE older than v2017 do not create the connection file automatically. In this case, you can instruct Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to create the connection file in the simulation directory, based on the host and port that you specify using the Values > Partner Host:Port node. For more information, see Connect Option.

9. To run the co-simulation, click Run (Ctrl+R).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically loads the coupling library and, based on the specified launch and connect methods, connects, or launches and connects to, to the specified GT-SUITE server.

On connection, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ matches the co-simulation zones with the corresponding GT-SUITE CFD connections.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ also allows you to manually load or unload the coupling library, and manually control the launch and connect steps. For more information, see Link Right-Click Actions.

To terminate the connection:

10.Right-click the Link node and select Terminate.

11.To restart the co-simulation:

▶If the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ session is active, select Solution > Clear Solution. You can then start GT-SUITE using the previous method.

▶If you close Simcenter STAR-CCM+, perform a restart-run by modifying the GT-SUITE model file to restart from a user-defined time-step. Restart the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation from an autosave file.

Contents:

Running a Co-Simulation with GT-SUITE on Parallel Hosts

Running a Co-Simulation with GT-SUITE on Parallel Hosts

If you intend to run on parallel hosts (a multiple node cluster or several machines over a network), the procedure for running the co-simulation must meet certain criteria. The following examples demonstrate coupling over parallel hosts using two machines or nodes; A is the master host and B is the slave host.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7177

Running GT-SUITE on the Master Host

The easiest way to run a coupled simulation is to allow Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to launch the GT-SUITE server automatically on the master host. However, the master host must have access to the GT-SUITE installation.

To run the GT-SUITE server on the master host, A:

1. Launch a parallel simulation using the procedure in Using a Remote Multi-Core Workstation, ensuring that the master host is the first entry in the table. Alternatively, from the command line:

starccm+ -server -on A:x,B:y -np x+y

where:

◦ x – is the number of processes on A

◦ y – is the number of processes on B

Running GT-SUITE on a Slave Host

If the master host does not have access to a GT-SUITE installation, run the GT-SUITE server on one of the slave hosts. This scenario requires a different coupling procedure.

To run the GT-SUITE server on the slave host, B:

1. Launch a parallel simulation using the procedure in Using a Remote Multi-Core Workstation, ensuring that the master host is the first entry in the table. Alternatively, from the command line:

starccm+ -server -on A:x,B:y -np x+y

where:

◦ x – is the number of processes on A

◦ y – is the number of processes on B

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7178

Setting Up STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE for a Restart Run

On occasion, it is necessary to stop the solver prematurely, or continue running an existing analysis for more time-steps. To meet these requirements, GT-SUITE co-simulation provides facilities to perform a restart run. This section details this procedure for a case that has been stopped before completion.

To continue an analysis for more time-steps, the following steps can also be followed, but increase the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ stopping criteria to extend the duration of the simulation.

Before running the solver, enable the Auto Save feature in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to save the simulation at regular intervals. The autosaved files provide an exact time-step from which you can restart the solver, thus ensuring the two codes begin at the same point in the analysis. The autosave file has a name that corresponds to the current time-step, for example, casename@01000.sim is the saved simulation at time-step 1000.

To enable Auto Save:

1. From the menu bar, select File > Auto Save....

2. In the Auto Save dialog, set Trigger Type to Time Step, as the restart time-step must be specified in the GT-SUITE case.

3. Set Frequency and Max Autosaved Files as required.

4. Start the GT-SUITE solver and obtain a solution in the usual manner.

To restart the simulation in GT-SUITE, modify the case setup so that the solver restarts from a user-specified time-step:

5. Right-click a CFD component, and select Edit Properties...

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7179

6. In the Edit Object dialog, select the Advanced tab.

7. Set Read to CFD Time Step Number to def.

8. Save the GT-SUITE case file and create a .dat file, by selecting Run > Run-Simulation Utilities > Create .dat file from the menu bar.

To restart the simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

9. Load the autosaved file into Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

▶If you perform a restart from a different directory, make sure that you copy the relevant files from the previous working directory (that is, the *.cfdreload, *.sim, *.gtm, and *.gdx files).

10.Run the solvers in the usual manner.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver restarts from the last time-step and the GT-SUITE solver restarts from the user-specified time-step.

GT-SUITE Link Reference

GT-SUITE Link Reference

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you specify the settings for co-simulation with GT-SUITE in a link node under the External Links node.

A link node, External Links > Link 1,appears in the simulation when you activate the GT-SUITE Co-Simulation model. This node allows you to specify co-simulation global settings, such as the connection method, as well as to define and set up co-simulation zones, which couple the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundaries with the corresponding GT-SUITE CFD Connections.

This section describes the global settings available for co-simulation with GT-SUITE. For details on the cosimulation zone settings, see Co-Simulation Zones Reference.

Link Properties

Link Type

Describes the type of connection. Read-only.

Link Models

In a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation, you access the co-simulation framework by activating co-simulation models in the physics continua. These models determine the physics of the coupling, including the fields that can be exchanged with the partner simulation.

Link models configure the connection to a partner application or file. The link icon changes based on the application, or file, that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ connects to through the link. The link model must be appropriate for the co-simulation or file export model selected in the physics continuum.

Link Conditions and Values

You specify the general settings of the co-simulation under the Link > Conditions and Link > Values nodes.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7182

GT-SUITE Version

Allows you to specify which version of the partner software you are running. The available options include the recommended versions (see the section External Packages Support of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Release Notes), as well as a Custom option. The Custom option allows you to specify a version other than the recommended. In general, you are advised to use one of the recommended versions, as compatibility for other versions is not guaranteed. When using the Custom option, set the version using the Values > Custom Code Version node.

Load Partner Library Option

Allows you to specify the location of the GT-SUITE coupling library (see GT-SUITE Coupling Libraries).

Method Corresponding Condition/Value Nodes

Specify Library File

Allows you to manually specify the path to the GT-SUITE library file. This option is suitable for cases where the location of the library file is not the default. See Coupling to GT-SUITE.

GT-SUITE Library

Specifies the path and name of the GT-SUITE library file. You can type the full path and name manually, or you can

click (Custom Editor) and navigate to the file using the file selection dialog.

Use environment variable

Instructs Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to load the library from the default location (see GT-SUITE Coupling Libraries). This option requires you to save the path to the GT-SUITE installation in the environment variable, $GTIHOME.

GTIHOME Environment Variable

Specifies the path to the GT-SUITE installation. You can

type the full path manually, or you can click (Custom Editor) and navigate to the installation directory using the file selection dialog.

This setting overwrites any existing $GTIHOME environment variable, for the current co-simulation run.

When restoring a simulation containing the GTIHOME Environment Variable setting, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the $GTIHOME environment variable, if this is set on the system. If not set, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the GTIHOME Environment Variable setting that is found in the simulation.

Launch Partner Option

Allows you to specify which method Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses to launch GT-SUITE.

Method Corresponding Value Nodes

Launch Default Application

Automatically launches GT-SUITE on cosimulation run. This option requires you to specify the path to the GT-SUITE installation and license file using the environment variables $GTIHOME and $GTISOFT_LICENSE_FILE.

The following settings allow you to overwrite the $GTIHOME and $GTISOFT_LICENSE_FILE environment variables defined on your system, for the current cosimulation run:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7183

GTIHOME Environment Variable

Specifies the path to the GT-SUITE installation. You can

type the full path manually, or you can click (Custom Editor) and navigate to the installation directory using the file selection dialog.

GTISOFT_LICENSE_FILE Environment Variable

Specifies the GT-SUITE license file.

When restoring a simulation that contains these setting, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the environment variables, if these are set on the system. If not set, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the settings that are found in the simulation.

Do Not Launch

Requires you to manually launch GT-SUITE.

None

Connect Option

Allows you to specify which method Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses to connect to GT-SUITE.

When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches GT-SUITE (that is, Launch Partner Option is set to Launch Default Application), Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically uses the launching details for connection.

When you launch GT-SUITE manually (that is, Launch Partner Option is set to Do Not Launch), the coupling library requires the host and port on which GT-SUITE is running. The host and port information is stored in a connection file, gtlink.prm, which can be created using the following methods:

Method Corresponding Value Nodes

Partner Code Creates Connection File

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ does not create the connection file.

From v2017, when you launch GT-SUITE in server mode using the gtlink command, GT-SUITE creates the required gtlink.prm connection file in the directory from which you instantiate gtlink.

To use this file for connection, copy it to the directory containing the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation file.

None

STAR-CCM+ Creates Connection File

When co-simulation starts, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically writes the specified host and port details to a file and saves the file in the simulation directory as gtlink.prm.

Partner Host:Port

Specifies the host and port where GT-SUITE is running. Provide these details in the format [Host Name]: [Port Number]

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7184

GT-SUITE Partner Connection File

Displays the name of the connection file created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ (readonly).

Partner Filesystem

Specifies whether the GT-SUITE files are located on a local or remote file system. See GT-SUITE Model File.

GT-SUITE

Displays the status of the connection between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE and the GT-SUITE library that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses to communicate with GT-SUITE.

GT-SUITE Model File

Specifies the location and name of the GT-SUITE case file. You can provide either the .gtm file or the .dat file. When providing the .dat file, make sure it is up-to-date. See Coupling to GT-SUITE.

Partner Material Components

For multi-component gases, allows you to couple the fluid components defined in GT-SUITE with gas components and passive scalars defined in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

The [Material Component] nodes must match the species defined in GT-SUITE in number and name. See Specifying Co-Simulation Settings.

Link Right-Click Actions

Load Partner Library

Loads the specified GT-SUITE library file. See Load Partner Library Option.

Launch and Connect

Launches the specified partner simulation and starts the connection, coupling the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation with the partner simulation.

Connect

Starts the connection, coupling the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation with the running partner simulation that you specified.

Terminate

Terminates the connection between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and GT-SUITE.

Unload Partner Library

Unloads any GT-SUITE library file that was previously loaded.

Co-Simulation Zones Reference

Co-simulation zones allow you to couple Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundaries with the partner GT-SUITE CFD connections.

Zones Manager Properties

Number of Zones

Displays the number of zones defined for this link. Read-only.

Zones Manager Right-Click Actions

New

Adds a co-simulation zone under the Zones node. For coupling to be successful, the name of a cosimulation zone must match the name of the corresponding GT-SUITE CFD connection.

Zone Properties

Index

Displays a unique identifier for this zone. Read-only.

Zone Type

Specifies what type of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ objects are assigned to this co-simulation zone. The available option is Surface Zone, which allows you to couple Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundaries to their surface counterparts in the partner simulation (surface-to-surface coupling).

Zone Conditions and Values

Coupled Model Parts

Displays the parts on the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ model that exchange data with the partner simulation, through this co-simulation zone. As this type of co-simulation only supports surface-to-surface coupling, the coupled model parts can only be boundaries.

This property is read-only. To assign a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary to a co-simulation zone, use the External Code Coupling Specification boundary condition.

GT-SUITE Zone Data

Displays the settings defined for the coupled CFD connection in GT-SUITE. As these settings are defined in GT-SUITE, all the properties are read-only:

Area: displays the CFD cross-section that is specified for the coupled CFD connection in GT-SUITE (readonly). ID: displays the ID number that is given to the CFD connection within the GT-SUITE case (read-only). This index is not used to match the co-simulation zone with the corresponding CFD connection. Cosimulation zones and CFD connections are matched by name. Sampling Length: displays the length of the sampling volume across which Simcenter STAR-CCM+ averages the computed fields before sending them to GT-SUITE. The sampling volume length is defined in GT-SUITE (read-only).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7186

WAVE Co-Simulation

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ allows for two-way co-simulation with WAVE, a 1D engine and gas dynamics simulation tool from Ricardo Software.

For more information on WAVE, visit the official website.

In a co-simulation between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and WAVE, WAVE computes a full engine-power analysis and allocates a portion of the flow to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for solving in 3D. Co-simulation reduces the computational times in both Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and WAVE. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ receives time-accurate boundary conditions from WAVE, and WAVE receives space-accurate boundary conditions from Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Co-Simulation Interface

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you define co-simulation zones that couple the CFD orifices defined in WAVE with corresponding Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mass flow inlet boundaries. Each co-simulation zone uniquely couples a WAVE CFD Orifice with a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary. Co-simulation zones and CFD orifices must match in number and name.

During the co-simulation, WAVE sends the computed flow quantities and species mass fractions to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, which then applies them uniformly at the coupled boundary. Before sending data back to WAVE, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ averages the computed fields in order to provide one-dimensional values.

You can also exchange additional single-value data, for example shaft speed, torque, and flow rate, by associating Simcenter STAR-CCM+ auxiliary field specifications with WAVE control links.

WAVE co-simulation uses an explicit coupling scheme, that is, data is exchanged once per time-step.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7187

Exchanged Fields

Co-simulation zones allow coupling between WAVE orifices and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mass flow inlets. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically sets the boundary conditions based on the imported fields.

For exchange of single-value data using Simcenter STAR-CCM+ auxiliary fields and WAVE control links, you manually set the relevant boundary conditions using the field functions that store the imported data.

Option Fields Sent to WAVE Fields Received from WAVE

Co-simulation zones • Density

• Temperature

• Pressure

• Mass Flow

• Species Mass Fractions

• Density

• Temperature

• Pressure

• Mass Flow

• Species Mass Fractions

Single-value data exchange Auxiliary fields representing single-value data Control link data

Coupled Species

WAVE uses combustion models to determine the products of reaction between fuel and air. WAVE uses five active scalars in modeling the combustion process:

• air—Air, with gas composition aN2, bO2, cCO2, dH2O (defined in WAVE pre-processing).

• burnedAir—Products of combustion, with gas composition aN2, bO2, cCO2, dH2O.

• burnedFuel—Remaining products of combustion, with gas composition eCO, fNO, gOH, hN, iO, jH, kH2.

• fuelLiquid—Fuel in liquid form, with molecular composition CCHHOONN (specified in WAVE preprocessing).

• fuelVapour—Fuel in vapor form, with molecular composition CCHHOONN (specified in WAVE preprocessing).

In a co-simulation with WAVE, you couple the WAVE active scalars with corresponding mixture components or passive scalars defined in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. The mass fractions are exchanged at the co-simulation interface.

Additionally, you can couple passive scalars defined in WAVE with mixture components or passive scalars defined in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Preparing the WAVE Simulation for Co-Simulation

Modify a WAVE simulation for co-simulation with Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

The following instructions assume that you start from a fully set up WAVE simulation. Also, some of the following instructions may vary based on the version of WAVE that you are running. For more information on setting up a case in WAVE, refer to the WAVE User Guide.

Before specifying co-simulation settings, it is good practice to run a standalone WAVE analysis. You can use the results from the standalone WAVE analysis as initial conditions in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

1. Run the WAVE simulation independently until converged.

2. Using a text editor, open the .out file that is associated with the WAVE simulation. This file is typically located in the same directory as the WAVE simulation file.

3. Note the average pressure and temperature for the adjacent duct to the CFD inlet.

For example:

You can now modify the WAVE simulation for co-simulation with Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

For each CFD orifice in WAVE, specify the diameter of the coupled zone in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If the zone cross-section is non-circular, use the effective diameter, that is, the diameter of an equivalent circle with the same cross-sectional area as the zone. In the example below, the diameter at the manifold intake is 50 mm.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7189

To set the CFD orifice diameter in WAVE:

4. Double-click External CFD Orifice.

5. In the External CFD Orifice dialog, set the value in the Diameter textbox to match the zone diameter in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Specify WAVE as the child process. This parameter allows Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to start the WAVE solver when obtaining a solution:

6. From the WAVE menu bar, select Model > External > CFD...

7. From the Parameters group, select Child.

Specify the number of pre-cycles that WAVE runs independently before sending data to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Pre-cycles improve stability in WAVE, providing more accurate boundary conditions to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and, therefore, reducing the time to reach a converged solution.

8. From the WAVE menu bar, select Model > External > CFD...

9. From the Process Control group, select Postponed.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7190

10.Specify the number of coupled cycles in the Coupled Duration textbox.

This value is subtracted from the total number of simulation cycles, to determine the number of pre-cycles.

The WAVE solver runs independently until it reaches the number of pre-cycles. When the number of precycles is met, WAVE starts sending data to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

The transfer of data to WAVE from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ can be delayed until a defined time-step. This facility allows the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver to reach a level of stability while receiving data from WAVE, before sending data back to WAVE. To set a transfer delay:

11.From the WAVE menu bar, select Model > External > CFD...

12.Enter the number of time-steps in the One Way Steps textbox.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7191

Preparing the STAR-CCM+ Simulation for Co-Simulation

Set up a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation for co-simulation with WAVE.

1. Before you set up the physics continua, prepare the required geometry, regions, interfaces, and mesh, as appropriate to your analysis.

For more information on these general operations, see General Simulation Process.

2. In the co-simulation physics continuum, activate the following physics models:

Group Physics Model

Space Three Dimensional

Time one of Implicit Unsteady, PISO Unsteady

Material Multi-Component Gas

Reaction Regime Non-Reacting

Flow any

Enabled Models Gradients (selected automatically)

Equation of State any

Energy any

Viscous Regime any

Optional Models Co-Simulation

Co-Simulation Models WAVE

Optional Models Passive Scalar

Note:This model can be neglected if you represent all species of a multi-component gas with gas components.

You can select further models to meet specific analysis requirements.

3. Define a mixture component or passive scalar for each active scalar defined in WAVE.

The choice between using a mixture component or passive scalar to represent a WAVE active scalar depends on user requirements. A mixture component influences the physical properties of the mixture, providing the most accurate and realistic solution. A passive scalar has no effect on the physical properties of the mixture and so reduces compute time. If passive scalars are used for all species, a background fluid must be present in the region.

To add a mixture component to the simulation:

a) Expand the Continua > [Physics Continuum] > Models node.

b) Right-click the Multi-Component Gas > Gas Components node and select Select Mixture Components...

c) In the Select Mixture Components dialog, select the gas components, then click Apply.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7192

Note: Although the WAVE fuelLiquid species is a liquid, it can be represented by a gas in the MultiComponent Gas model. This does not affect results, as the gas simply represents the species in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, with the physics values received from WAVE.

To add a passive scalar to the simulation:

a) Right-click the Passive Scalars node and select New.

If you wish to couple WAVE passive scalars with Simcenter STAR-CCM+, use the same procedure to define the required mixture components or passive scalars in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

To reduce the numerical round-off, set the reference pressure to the average pressure in WAVE. You can identify the average pressure in WAVE by running a standalone WAVE analysis. You can then read the average pressure in the CFD component in the relevant WAVE .out file (see Preparing the WAVE Simulation for CoSimulation).

To set the reference pressure:

4. Select the [Physics Continuum] > Reference Values > Reference Pressure node and set Value to the average pressure in WAVE.

Note: All pressures in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are defined relative to the reference pressure. In WAVE, all pressures are absolute. Take these differences into consideration when defining pressure values.

The initial conditions in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are used to reduce the time that it takes for the solution to converge. For best initialization, set the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ initial conditions to the average values from WAVE, which you can obtain by running a standalone WAVE analysis.

5. Expand the [Physics Continuum] > Initial Conditions node and specify the initial conditions as follows:

a) As the initial pressure in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is relative to the reference pressure, set the Pressure value to the difference between the average pressure from WAVE and the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ reference pressure.

b) As the initial temperature in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is an absolute value, set the Static Temperature value to be the same as the average temperature from WAVE.

c) Set the species mass fractions to the average values from WAVE, by setting the Species Mass Fraction

value. Click (Custom Editor) to enter the mass fractions in an array. Initial mass fractions must sum to the value of 1.

As an example, if coupling to a component on the intake side of an engine, it would be intuitive to initialize the region with air. Hence, the mass fractions would be as follows:

Mixture Component Value

air 1.0

fuelVapour 0.0

fuelLiquid 0.0

Exchanging Predefined Fields at Co-Simulation Zones

Exchanging Single-Value Data

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7193

Exchanging Predefined Fields at Co-Simulation Zones

To couple Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mass flow inlet boundaries and WAVE CFD orifices, you define co-simulation zones. When coupling Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and WAVE through co-simulation zones, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically defines the exchanged fields and boundary conditions.

For information on the predefined fields exchanged at co-simulation zones, see Exchanged Fields.

To couple a mass flow inlet with a WAVE CFD orifice:

1. Right-click the External Links > [Link 1] > Zones node and select New.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ adds a co-simulation zone, [Zone 1], under the Zones node.

Assign the relevant mass flow inlet boundary to the co-simulation zone:

2. Expand the relevant Regions > [Region] > Boundaries > [Mass Flow Inlet Boundary] node.

3. Select the Physics Conditions > External Code Coupling Specification node and set External Code Coupling Specification to [Link 1]: [Zone 1].

For the coupled boundaries, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically sets the boundary conditions based on the fields imported from WAVE, except turbulence. When modeling turbulent flow, define the Turbulence Specification at the coupled boundaries as appropriate to your analysis.

4. Select the [Link 1] > Zones > [Zone 1] > Values > Fluid Link node and set External CFD Interface Number to the interface number of the associated CFD External orifice (defined in WAVE).

5. Define the boundary conditions at the boundaries that are not coupled to WAVE in the usual manner.

Couple each of the WAVE active scalars with the corresponding Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mixture component or passive scalar.

6. Right-click the Link 1 > Values > Coupled Species node and select New Coupled Species.

7. Repeat the previous step to create a coupled species node for each of the active scalars defined in WAVE.

8. Rename each coupled species node to the name of the corresponding WAVE active scalar.

9. For each Coupled Species > [Species] node, set Mixture Component/Passive Scalar to the relevant Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mixture component or passive scalar.

All the active scalars defined in WAVE must be coupled to either Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mixture components or passive scalars. Similarly, all the mixture components defined in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ must be coupled to either an active scalar or a passive scalar in WAVE.

Optionally, you can use the same procedure to couple WAVE passive scalars with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mixture components or passive scalars. You can leave passive scalars in either WAVE or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ as uncoupled.

Exchanging Single-Value Data

You can exchange single-value data between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and WAVE by associating Simcenter STAR-CCM+ auxiliary field specifications with WAVE control links.

In each code, you specify the data that is exported to the partner code. To export single-value data from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to WAVE:

1. Expand the External Links > [Link 1] > Conditions node.

2. Right-click the Exported Fields node and select Add Auxiliary Field > Scalar.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7194

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ adds an auxiliary field specification under the Exported Fields node.

3. Select the [Scalar Auxiliary Field] specification node and select the Scalar Field Function that you want to send to WAVE. The selected field function must represent a single value. For example, you can select the field function associated with a report.

Similarly, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ can import single-value data from WAVE control links. When the two codes connect, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically adds auxiliary field import specifications based on the export settings specified in WAVE. Alternatively, to manually create import specifications:

◦ Right-click the Imported Fields node and select Add Auxiliary Field > Scalar.

Once you define export (and, optionally, import) specifications in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you associate them with the corresponding WAVE control links using pin associations. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically adds pin associations for each export or import field specification.

Pin association nodes have the same name of the corresponding auxiliary field specifications, preceded by either Export: or Import:.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7195

To specify the WAVE control links:

4. For each export specification, select the relevant Conditions > WAVE Control Pin Associations > [Export: Scalar Auxiliary Field] node.

5. Set Associated ID to the pin number of the WAVE control link that receives the data.

6. For each import specification, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically defines the association based on the export settings specified in WAVE. Alternatively, you can manually set the Associated ID for each [Import: Scalar Auxiliary Field] node.

When the two codes connect, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ checks that the settings are consistent. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ deletes any import specification that is not associated with an export control link. For export specifications that are in conflict with export control links, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ modifies the control pin associations, in order to restore a valid association setup.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ stores the imported data in field functions that are named after the corresponding WAVE control link, [WAVE Control Pin #], where # is the control link pin number.

7. Use the imported data field functions to set boundary conditions in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Coupling STAR-CCM+ to WAVE

Specify the WAVE launching details and connect to the WAVE simulation.

To couple to WAVE, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ requires the path to the WAVE co-simulation libraries, the path and name of the WAVE simulation file, and the path to the WAVE executable.

1. Expand the External Links > [Link 1] node.

For more information, see WAVE Version.

3. Expand the [Link 1] > Values node.

5. Select the RSimlink Libraries Folder node and specify the path to the folder containing the co-simulation RSimlink libraries.

See RSimlink Libraries.

6. Select the WAVE Input File node and specify the path and name of the WAVE simulation file.

8. To run the co-simulation, click (Run) in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ automatically disconnects from WAVE at the end of the co-simulation analysis.

Link models configure the connection to a partner application or file. The link icon changes based on the application, or file, that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ connects to through the link. The link model must be appropriate for the co-simulation or file export model selected in the physics continuum.

The available options include the recommended versions (see the section External Packages Support of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Release Notes), as well as a Custom option. The Custom option allows you to specify a version other than the recommended. In general, you are advised to use one of the recommended versions, as compatibility for other versions is not guaranteed. When using the Custom option, set the version using the Values > Custom Code Version node.

RELAP Coupling

The RELAP Coupling feature provides the ability for two-way transfer of data between three-dimensional Simcenter STAR-CCM+, and one-dimensional RELAP. For example, the natural convection currents in coolant fluid can be analyzed in detail in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, with RELAP providing the boundary conditions.

This provides increased detail in specified areas of the RELAP case, by adding a three-dimensional element to a one-dimensional simulation. Similarly, processing times can be reduced in a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation, by utilizing the speed of one-dimensional codes.

Note: RELAP is only available on Linux. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ can run on Windows or Linux and connect to RELAP running on Linux.

What is RELAP Coupling?

RELAP coupling provides a means of data exchange between three-dimensional Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and one-dimensional RELAP. This allows for a compromise between the speed of one-dimensional code, with the detail of three-dimensional code. The feature provides optimum results when coupling occurs at a flow zone where the flow is expected to be largely one-dimensional. This recommendation does not apply to zones, as they apply thermal data to a wall boundary.

When running the solver, the flow or thermal data received from RELAP are applied at the coupled Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary. If there is outflow at the boundary, the temperature is averaged at the flow zone, and sent back to RELAP. The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver typically uses a smaller time step than RELAP. Data is exchanged at each RELAP time step, and the boundary conditions for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are interpolated between these time steps.

The following table summarizes how Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and RELAP boundaries couple to one another:

STAR-CCM+ RELAP

Wall Heat Structure

Mass Flow Time Dependent Volume and Junction

The RELAP node, located within the External Links node, becomes available when the RELAP Coupling model is activated. It holds subnodes, which are populated with zones and flow zones, once the simulation is coupled to RELAP.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7203

What is a RELAP Zone or Flow Zone?

A RELAP zone or flow zone represents the equivalent of a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary in RELAP. Each RELAP zone and flow zone must be assigned to a coupled boundary in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation.

A RELAP zone is a specified wall boundary in the CFD region, which provides a means of exchanging thermal data between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and RELAP. Similarly, a RELAP flow zone is a mass flow boundary, which provides a means of exchanging flow data between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and RELAP. The physics values at the zones or flow zones are averaged, providing a single value used to determine the equivalent boundary conditions in the one-dimensional code.

RELAP zones transfer thermal data based upon the axial discretization in RELAP. This means that multiple constant values from RELAP are applied at the wall boundary. The direction and distribution of the onedimensional discretization is determined by the Orientation property. The RELAP discretization on the coupled boundary can be visualized as a scalar displayer using the AvgZoneFlag field function.

RELAP flow zones transfer flow data, with a uniform value applied at the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary. This value can be multiplied by a flow multiplier to modify the received value. A field function or table can also be used to multiply the received value by a variable scale factor. For example, this can be used with cell positions or wall distance to model the effect of a boundary layer at the flow boundary.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7204

The RELAP Zones and RELAP Flow Zones nodes hold the individual zone nodes, which become available when RELAP Coupling is activated and started.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7205

Preparing the RELAP Case

In order to couple RELAP to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you must create a .control file that specifies the port number and which parts of the RELAP model are to be coupled to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

This file must have the same case name as the RELAP case input file and be located in the same directory. For example, if the RELAP case input file is casename.i, then the file required by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ must be called casename.i.control.

The .control file must follow a certain format, with an example and explanation below:

PORT 5555 NUMCOUPLED,5,1,0 DEBUGOUTPUT PRESBC TDV 980 JUN 979 FLUXBC HS 9000 SIDE 1 FLUXBC HS 9001 SIDE 1 TEMPBC HS 9700 SIDE 2 TEMPBC HS 9701 SIDE 2 TEMPBC HS 9702 SIDE 2

PORT 5555 Set the port number for communication, which must match the RELAP node property.

NUMCOUPLED,5,1,0 Specifies the number of zones, followed by the number of flow zones. In the example, five thermal boundaries (zones) and one flow boundary (flow zone).

DEBUGOUTPUT Makes RELAP write debug output when running

PRESBC TDV 980 JUN 979 Define a pressure boundary condition at a specified time dependant volume ID (e.g. 980) and a junction ID (e.g. 979). This will be represented by a flow zone in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

FLUXBC HS 9000 SIDE 1 Define a heat flux boundary condition at a specified heat structure ID (e.g. 9000) and side (e.g. 1). This will be represented by a zone in Simcenter STAR-CCM + that sends temperature data and receives heat flux.

TEMPBC HS 9700 SIDE 2 Define a temperature boundary condition at a specified heat structure ID (e.g. 9702) and side (e.g. 2). This will be represented by a zone in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ that sends heat flux data and receives temperature.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7206

Setting Up the STAR-CCM+ Simulation

The following section details the process of setting up a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation for coupling with RELAP.

Contents:

Activating the RELAP Co-Simulation Model

Setting the STAR-CCM+ Boundary

Activating the RELAP Co-Simulation Model

The RELAP co-simulation model is selected from within the Physics Model Selection dialog on the relevant continuum.

To select the RELAP model, the following models are required:

1. Select Three Dimensional from the Space group box.

2. Select Implicit Unsteady from the Time group box.

3. Select any material from the Material group box, except Solid.

◦ If you select Multi-Component Gas or Multi-Component Liquid, select Non-Reacting from the Reaction Regime group box.

◦ If you select Eulerian Multiphase, select Volume of Fluid (VOF) from the Multiphase Flow Model group box.

4. Select either Segregated Flow or Coupled Flow from the Flow group box, depending on the required solver type.

The Segregated solver is recommended in most cases.

5. Select Co-Simulation from the Optional Models group box.

6. Select RELAP from the Co-Simulation Models group box.

To fully define the physics continua used in a RELAP coupled simulation, the following additional models must also be activated:

7. Either a Segregated Energy or Coupled Energy model from the Optional Models group.

8. Any model from the Equation of State group box.

9. Turbulent from the Viscous Regime group box.

10.Any turbulence model from the Reynolds-Averaged Turbulence group, depending on simulation requirements.

Further models can be selected from the Optional Physics Models group, to meet individual simulation requirements.

Setting the STAR-CCM+ Boundary

The boundary type determines the physics values exchanged between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and RELAP. RELAP coupling is capable of transferring thermal data at walls and flow data at inlets and outlets.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7207

The first step in setting the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary is to specify the boundary as coupled. For thermal data, you must specify whether the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ wall boundary will send temperature and receive heat flux, or vice versa. For flow data, there is an option to multiply the received data by a scale factor.

Contents:

1D Coupling Specification

Coupling a STAR-CCM+ Mass Flow Boundary to a RELAP Time Dependant Volume and Junction

Flow Multiplier

1D Coupling Specification

The 1D Coupling Specification property determines whether the boundary in question is coupled to RELAP.

To set a boundary as coupled:

1. Select the 1D Coupling Specification node, within the Physics Conditions node.

2. In the Properties window, set 1D Coupling Specification to Coupled.

Coupling a STAR-CCM+ Wall Boundary to a RELAP Heat Structure

To transfer thermal data, a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ wall must be assigned to a RELAP heat structure at a zone.

There are then two coupling options available:

• Simcenter STAR-CCM+ receives temperature and sends heat flux.

• Simcenter STAR-CCM+ receives heat flux and sends temperature.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7208

To couple a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ wall boundary to a RELAP heat structure:

1. Select the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ boundary Physics Conditions > Thermal Specification node.

▶To set Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to receive temperature data, set Method to Temperature.

▶To set Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to receive heat flux data, set Method to Heat Flux.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7209

2. In the casename.i.control file (see Preparing the RELAP Case):

▶If you set Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to receive temperature, set RELAP to receive heat flux by specifying the FLUXBC boundary condition.

▶If you set Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to receive heat flux, set RELAP to receive temperature by specifying the TEMPBC boundary condition.

Coupling a STAR-CCM+ Mass Flow Boundary to a RELAP Time Dependant Volume and Junction

To transfer flow data, a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ mass flow boundary must be assigned to both a RELAP time dependant volume and a junction, at a flow zone.

A summary of the data transferred at a flow zone is included below:

• Pressure sent from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to the RELAP time dependant volume.

• Mass flux sent from the RELAP junction to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• If there is inflow into Simcenter STAR-CCM+, temperature is sent from the RELAP time dependant volume to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• If there is outflow from Simcenter STAR-CCM+, temperature is sent from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to the RELAP time dependant volume.

The majority of boundary conditions at a flow zone are governed by RELAP, except turbulence. Therefore, the boundary is set as coupled, with turbulence specification required.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7210

Flow Multiplier

The Flow Multiplier allows you to multiply the data received from RELAP at the coupled boundary with a scale factor. For example, if the RELAP simulation modeled one tube, but the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation models two tubes, you could use a multiplier of 2 to double the received flow data at the coupled boundary.

To set a flow multiplier:

1. Select the Physics Values > Flow Multiplier node and set the Method.

The Method menu allows you to select Constant, Field Function, Tabular or User Code input.

2. Select the sub-node of the Flow Multiplier node and enter the required input in the Properties window.

The example below shows use of the Constant option to double the received data.

The main use of this property is to take the one-dimensional, uniform flow data, and provide a parabolic profile at the coupled boundary, which takes the boundary layer at the wall into consideration. As an example, you can use a field function to multiply the data by a varying scale factor dependant on cell position.

The following field function uses the cell centroid in the radial direction, relative to a cylindrical coordinate system located at the centre of a pipe. This value is put to the power of 25 to give a parabolic shape, representative of an arbitrary boundary layer. The profile is then flipped and transposed so that the majority of the flow is given a flow multiplier of approximately 1.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7211

This example profile is illustrated below by displaying the flow multiplier field function on the inlet of a cylindrical pipe:

A similar effect can also be achieved on a per-cell basis by using tabular data with reference to cell IDs.
