7. Save the simulation .

Setting Up the Valve Motions

For the motion of the valves, you import tables that describe the valve lifts as a function of crank angle.

To define the motion for the exhaust valve:

1. Right-click the Engine > Exhaust Valve 1 node and select Edit.

2. In the Edit dialog, next to the Valve Lift File drop-down menu, click Import.

3. In the Import Valve Lift Table dialog, navigate to the inCylinder folder of the downloaded tutorial files.

To define the motion for the intake valve:

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11426

6. Right-click the Engine > Intake Valve 1 node and select Edit.

The Valve Lifts plot displays the lift curves for the exhaust and intake valves:

Defining Operating Conditions and Time-Step Size

Here, you set the crank angle at which the simulation begins and the duration of the analysis. You enable automatic time-step control, which adjusts the time-step size based on preset valve lift thresholds.

To set the start crank angle and the duration of the analysis:

1. Right-click the Operating Conditions node and select Edit.

2. In the Operating Conditions group box, set the following properties:

Property Setting

Start Angle 300.0 deg

Duration 420.0 deg

In general, you run an analysis over multiple engine cycles to reduce the effect of initial conditions on the final results. If your processing time is limited, you are advised to start the analysis some crank angles before the intake valve opens—for example at 300 deg crank angle. At this stage, you can assume that the flow in the cylinder is relatively steady compared to the intake and combustion phases.

3. Click Apply, then Close.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11427

The Graphics window still displays the engine geometry at TDC position. However, in the bottom left corner, the red-colored starred text indicates that the displayed imported geometry no longer represents your settings of 300 deg crank angle.

To set up the automatic time-step control:

4. Right-click the Solvers node and select Edit.

The Edit dialog displays the default time step settings, solver settings, auto-save settings, and wall treatment.

5. In the Time Step Settings group box, activate Automatic.

6. Click Apply, then Close.

7. Save the simulation .

Aiding Solution Convergence

To prevent reversed flow and to aid solution convergence, you extend the volume mesh with orthogonal extruded cells at the inlet and outlet boundaries. Additionally, you move the valve curtain interfaces to a position that is more suitable for this engine geometry.

The valve curtain interfaces are the curved surface areas that are located on the surfaces of the valves; they separate the cylinder volume from the port volumes. See Valves Opening and Closing.

To move the valve curtain interfaces:

1. Right-click the Mesh node and select Edit Mesh Settings.

The Graphics window displays the valve curtain interface for each valve in yellow color.

2. Within the Edit Mesh Settings dialog, in the Normalized Valve Curtain Interface Position group box, set the value to 55.0.

3. To preview the valve curtain interfaces in the Graphics window, click Apply.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11428

To extrude the mesh at the inlet and outlet boundaries:

4. In the Extrusion group box, set Extrude I/O Boundaries to On.

By default, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder extrudes the mesh for a distance of 1.0 mm using two cells in the direction of the extrusion.

5. Click Apply, then Close.

6. Save the simulation .

Preparing the Plots and Scenes for Visualization

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder provides several plots and scenes by default. To watch the solution develop, open the plots for cylinder turbulence kinetic energy and tumble-y. Also open the scenes for velocity magnitude and absolute pressure. Write the scenes to image files at regular intervals.

To open the plots:

1. Right-click the Results > Plots > Cylinder Turbulence Kinetic Energy node and select Open.

In the Graphics window, the Cylinder Turbulence Kinetic Energy plot opens and displays the mass-averaged turbulence kinetic energy in the cylinder as a function of crank angle.

2. Repeat Step 1 for the Results > Plots > Tumble-Y node.

This plot displays the tumble about the y-axis as a function of crank angle.

To open the scenes and write them to image files:

3. Using <Ctrl>, multi-select the Results > Scenes > Absolute Pressure 1 and Velocity Magnitude 1 nodes.

4. Right-click and select Open.

The scenes open in the Graphics window.

5. Right-click the selected nodes again and select Edit.

6. In the Multiple Objects dialog, activate Attributes > Update > Save To File.

By default, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder writes the scenes to files after each crank angle.

7. Click Close.

8. Save the simulation .

Running the Simulation

The simulation is now set up and ready to run.

You are advised to run this tutorial on a multi-core machine with 8 cores or more. Depending on the specifications of the machine, this tutorial takes approximately 5 hours to complete.

To run the simulation

1. Click (Play/Resume "In-Cylinder").

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder updates the geometry to represent your settings and starts the meshing process. While the simulation is running, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder saves the image files for the velocity and pressure scenes to your working directory. The base name of each image file is combined with the number of the update to ensure that each file is unique.

2. After the run is finished, save the simulation .

Gasoline Engine: Charge Motion

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder provides methods for predicting the charge motion in an internal combustion engine, including the injection of liquid fuel and the subsequent evaporation and mixing process.

In this tutorial, you investigate the spray formation resulting from a direct fuel injection into a single engine cylinder. The fuel composition is as follows:

Fuel Component Mass Weighting

Iso-C8H18 (iso-Octane) 0.6

C7H8 (Toluene) 0.35

C7H16 (Heptane) 0.05

After injection, the fuel droplets mix with the in-cylinder gas and start to evaporate to form a flammable mixture. The goal of this tutorial is to predict the mass of vapor arising from the injected fuel and the liquid and vapor spray penetration. Additionally, you analyse the absolute pressure, velocity, and fuel/air equivalence ratio in the cylinder.

The engine geometry, the operating conditions, the initial and boundary conditions, and the motion of the piston and the valves are the same as introduced in the Gasoline Engine: Motored tutorial.

For the half engine model, you create a fuel injector on the symmetry plane and position it close to the intake valve. Three nozzles on the tip of the injector introduce the fuel into the cylinder—one hollow cone nozzle and two solid cone nozzles. One of the solid cone nozzles is oriented such as to direct its spray of fuel droplets towards the intake valve.

For all three nozzles, the hydraulic diameter of the nozzle hole is 0.2 mm and their cone angles are as follows:

Nozzle Outer Cone Angle Inner Cone Angle

Nozzle1 30.0 deg 0.0 deg

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11435

Nozzle Outer Cone Angle Inner Cone Angle

Nozzle 2 35.0 deg 0.0 deg

Nozzle 3 33.0 deg 15.0 deg

The simulation starts at 300 deg crank angle. The fuel injection starts at 420.0 deg crank angle and ends at 469.41 deg crank angle.

You specify the injection conditions in the form of tables that describe the fuel mass flow rate and the injection temperature as functions of crank angle. To specify the diameter of the injected fuel droplets, you import a table that describes the distribution of the droplet diameter using a cumulative distribution function (CDF).

Starting from the final Gasoline Engine: Motored simulation file, you clear the mesh and re-run the simulation using automatic time-step control. For charge-motion simulations, automatic time-step control adjusts the time-step size based on the preset valve lift thresholds and on the start and end of fuel injection.

After the run, you analyze the simulation results using the charge-motion specific post-processing capabilities that are available in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder.

The following image displays the updated target of the nozzle:

To increase the outer angle of the injection cone for Nozzle 2:

5. Edit the Engine > Injector > Nozzle 2 node.

6. In the Injector Nozzle : Nozzle 2 dialog, set Outer Cone Angle to 35.0 deg.

7. Click Apply, then Close.

8. Edit the Engine > Injector > Nozzle 3 node.

Setting the Duration of the Analysis and the Time-Step Size

The simulation starts at 300 deg crank angle and runs until 600 deg crank angle. For the automatic time-step control, you adjust the time periods before and after fuel injection. Additionally, you reduce the time-step size that is used during fuel injection.

For a motored-test simulation as described in the Gasoline Engine tutorial, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder runs 10 inner iterations per time-step. For a charge-motion simulation, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder increases the number of inner iterations to 20 to improve convergence and mass conservation. However, the increased number of inner iteration increases the runtime of the simulation. To reduce the runtime of this tutorial, you decrease the duration of the analysis from 420 deg crank angle to 300 deg crank angle.

To set the duration of the analysis:

1. Right-click the Operating Conditions node and select Edit.

2. In the Operating Conditions group box, set Duration to 300.0 deg.

3. Click Apply, then Close.

To adjust the time periods for the automatic time-step control:

4. Right-click the Solvers node and select Edit.

5. In the Time-Step Settings group box, click Settings.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11444

6. In the Auto Time-Step Settings dialog, click the Injectors tab and set the following properties:

Period Time Step

Before Injection 1.0 deg 1.0E-6 (default value)

During Injection 7.5E-7

After Injection 20.0 deg 5.0E-6 (default value)

7. Click OK.

8. Click Close.

9. Save the simulation .

Preparing the Plots and Scenes for Visualization

For a charge-motion simulation, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder provides several injection specific plots and scenes by default. To watch the solution develop, you open the plots for the injected mass of fuel and for the liquid and vapor spray penetration. You also open the scenes for velocity magnitude, absolute pressure, and fuel/air equivalence ratio. You write the scene for fuel/air equivalence ratio to image files at regular intervals.

To open the plots:

1. Right-click the Results > Plots > Injector Mass Injected node and select Open.

In the Graphics window, the plot opens and displays the mass of the injected droplets, the mass of the vapor arising from the droplets, and the total mass of the fuel (droplets and vapor) in gram as a function of crank angle.

2. Repeat Step 1 for the Injector Liquid Spray Penetration and Injector Vapor Spray Penetration nodes.

These plots display, for each nozzle, the distance interval that contains 95% mass of the injected droplets and of the vapor arising from the droplets measuring from the nozzle origin.

To open the scenes:

3. Multi-select the Results > Scenes > Absolute Pressure 1, Fuel Distribution 1, and Velocity Magnitude 1 nodes, right-click on one of the selected nodes, and select Open.

The scenes open in the Graphics window.

The Fuel Distribution 1 scene allows you to visualize various definitions of air-fuel mixture ratio. By default, the scene displays the air/fuel ratio.

To display the fuel/air equivalence ratio:

4. Right-click the Fuel Distribution 1 > Air/Fuel Ratio Derived Parts Scalar 1 node and select Toggle Visibility.

The displayer is rendered invisible.

5. Repeat Step 4 for the Fuel/Air Equivalence Ratio Derived Parts Scalar 1 displayer.

The previously hidden displayer is rendered visible.

To get a clear view of the injected parcels:

6. Select the Absolute Pressure 1 > Absolute Pressure Derived Parts Scalar 1 node and set Opacity to 0.4.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11445

7. Repeat Step 6 for the Fuel Distribution 1 and the Velocity Magnitude 1 scenes using the Fuel/Air Equivalence Ratio Derived Parts Scalar 1 and the Velocity: Magnitude Derived Parts Scalar 1 displayers, respectively.

To write the fuel/air equivalence ratio scene to image files:

8. Select the Results > Scenes > Fuel Distribution 1 > Attributes > Update node and activate Save To File.

By default, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder writes the scene to file after each crank angle.

9. Save the simulation .

Running the Simulation

The simulation is now set up and ready to run.

You are advised to run this tutorial on a multi-core machine with 12 cores or more. Depending on the specifications of the machine, this tutorial takes approximately 11 hours to complete.

To run the simulation:

1. Click (Play/Resume "In-Cylinder").

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder updates the geometry and starts the meshing process. While the simulation is running, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder saves the image files for the velocity, pressure, and fuel/air equivalence ratio scenes to your working directory. The base name of each image file is combined with the number of the update to ensure that each file is unique.

2. After the run is finished, save the simulation .

After the simulation is complete, you visualize the results.

Examine the plots for injected mass and spray penetration:

The following plots display the results after the run:

Summary

The Gasoline Engine: Charge-Motion tutorial demonstrates how to run a charge-motion simulation for a fourstroke gasoline engine using Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder.

The tutorial introduced the following features:

• Defining the engine models for a charge-motion simulation

• Setting up a multi-component fuel

• Setting up the injector

• Adjusting the cone angles and targets of the nozzles

• Defining the injection mass flow rate, the injection temperature, and the droplet diameter using tables

• Adjusting the automatic time-step control

• Plotting the injected mass of fuel and the liquid and vapor spray penetration as a function of crank angle

• Analyzing the fuel/air equivalence ratio in the cylinder

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11449

Gasoline Engine: ECFM-3Z Combustion

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder, you can simulate the combustion process in a gasoline engine using the Extended Coherent Flame Model Three Zone (ECFM-3Z).

The ECFM-3Z model is a general-purpose combustion model that is capable of simulating the complex mechanisms of turbulent mixing, flame propagation, and diffusion combustion that characterize modern internal combustion engines. In this tutorial, you use the ECFM-3Z model to investigate the spark ignition and combustion process of a fuel directly injected into a single engine cylinder. The engine setup and the fuel injection are the same as introduced in the Gasoline Engine: Charge Motion tutorial.

You create an ignitor on the symmetry plane and position it in the center of the cylinder head.

You set the ignition timing to 20.0 deg CA (degree crank angle) before top dead center (BTDC).

The simulation starts at 300 deg CA. You set the initial gas composition in the cylinder and ports using automatic composition initialization.

To ensure good cell quality for all crank angles during the run of the simulation, you set re-mesh criteria that are suitable for this engine geometry.

Starting from the final Gasoline Engine: Charge Motion simulation file, you clear the mesh and re-run the simulation until 800 deg CA using automatic time-step control. For combustion simulations, automatic timestep control adjusts the time-step size based on the preset valve lift thresholds, the start and end of fuel injection, and the ignition timing.

After the run, you analyze the simulation results using the post-processing capabilities that are available in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder.

Summary

Prerequisites

This tutorial guides you through the setup of the combustion simulation using the dedicated Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder add-on in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

You require a double-precision version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to complete this tutorial.

Make sure that the (Open Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder) button is visible in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ toolbar. For information on how to include the button in the toolbar, see Accessing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder.

Loading an Existing Simulation

You start from an existing simulation file that contains objects and solution data from the tutorial Gasoline Engine: Charge Motion.

To start this tutorial, you can either:

• use your own version of the simulation file from the Gasoline Engine: Charge Motion tutorial, if you have already worked through it; or,

• use the version from the tutorials files bundle located on the customer success portal.

To obtain the simulation file from the bundle:

1. Follow the instructions in Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal.

2. After extracting the package to disk, navigate to the inCylinder folder of the downloaded tutorial files and copy the file GasolineEngineChargeMotion_final.sim into your working directory.

To open the simulation file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder:

1. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

2. Select File > Load Simulation....

3. In the Load a File dialog, select an appropriate parallel option and set Compute Processes to at least 16.

4. At the bottom of the dialog, click Browse....

5. In the Open dialog, navigate to your working directory, select GasolineEngineChargeMotion_final.sim, then click Open.

6. In the Load a File dialog, click OK.

7. From the top menubar, select Mesh > Clear Generated Meshes.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11451

8. In the Clear Generated Meshes dialog, click Yes.

9. From the toolbar, click (Open Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder).

10.In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder, click Update.

11.Select File > Save As... and save the simulation as GasolineEngineCombustion.sim.

Setting Up the Combustion Models

Here, you select the combustion and ignition models. To save runtime, you de-activate the combustion model until the start of fuel injection at 420 deg CA.

To select the models for a combustion simulation:

1. Edit the Models node and select the following models:

Group Box Model

Optional Models Combustion

Combustion Model ECFM-3Z Spark Ignition (selected automatically)

Spark Ignition Model FI Spark-Ignition

To de-activate the combustion model until the start of fuel injection:

2. Edit the Models > ECFM-3Z node and set ECFM Start Time to 420.0 degCA.

3. Click Apply, then Close.

4. Save the simulation .

Setting Up the Ignitor

For the ignition of the air-fuel mixture, you create an ignitor Engine Part, which provides a template for defining the ignition location and timing. You set the ignition timing to 700.0 deg CA, which is 20.0 deg CA BTDC.

To create the ignitor:

1. Right-click the Engine node and select Create Ignitor.

The Edit tab opens and displays the ignitor template. The Graphics window updates and displays the ignitor as a red sphere. By default, the ignitor is centered in the cylinder head.

2. In the Graphics window, change the view to obtain a similar engine position to the one shown below:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11452

To position the ignitor:

3. In the Edit dialog, set the following Position properties:

Property Setting

Y 1.0E-9 m

Z 0.008 m

The specified Y value slightly offsets the ignitor from the symmetry plane to make sure that the ignitor is located inside the simulation domain.

4. To preview the ignitor in the Graphics window, click Update at the bottom of the dialog.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder updates the position of the ignitor:

To set the ignition timing:

5. Within the Edit dialog, in the Physics group box, set Spark Start Time to 700.0 degCA.

6. Click OK.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11453

7. Save the simulation .

Setting Analysis Duration and Initial Gas Composition

The simulation starts at 300 deg CA and runs until 800 deg CA. To set the initial gas composition in the cylinder and ports, you use Automatic Composition Initialization.

Automatic Composition Initialization automatically determines the initial gas composition in the intake port, the exhaust port, and the cylinder based on the fuel-air mixture and the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) composition. For information on the calculation of the initial mass fractions for the chemical species, see Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder Formulation—Automatic Composition Initialization.

The calculated initial mass fractions in the intake port and the exhaust port are also set as boundary conditions at the inlet and the outlet, respectively.

To set the duration of the analysis:

1. Right-click the Operating Conditions node and select Edit.

2. In the Operating Conditions group box, set Duration to 500.0 deg.

To automatically initialize the gas composition:

3. Make sure that Automatic Composition Initialization is activated.

The default settings assume that the simulation starts during the exhaust stroke. In that case, the cylinder and the exhaust port contain only exhaust products and the intake port contains pure air. The EGR for the intake port and thereby the intake boundary is set to 0.0, which means that no exhaust gas enters the engine through the inlet due to recirculation.

4. Click Apply, then Close.

5. Save the simulation .

Reducing Under-Relaxation Factor and Time-Step Size

To aid solution convergence, you reduce the under-relaxation factor for the pressure solver. For the automatic time-step control, you reduce the time-step size after fuel injection and decrease the time period in which the reduced time-step is used.

To set the pressure under-relaxation factor:

1. Right-click the Solvers node and select Edit.

2. In the Solver Settings group box, set Pressure Under-Relaxation Factor to 0.5.

To set the time-step size:

3. In the Time-Step Settings group box, click Settings.

4. In the Auto Time-Step Settings dialog, click the Injectors tab and set the following properties:

Period Time Step

After Injection 13.0 deg 2.0E-6

5. Click OK.

6. Click Apply, then Close.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11454

7. Save the simulation .

Setting the Re-Mesh Criteria

During the running simulation, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder re-meshes the geometry based on certain remesh criteria to ensure good cell quality for all crank angles. The default re-mesh criteria are based on best practices and are suitable in most cases. Here, you set re-mesh criteria that are more suitable for this engine geometry.

To set the re-mesh criteria:

1. Right-click the Mesh node and select Edit Mesh Settings.

2. In the Edit tab, click Re-mesh Criteria.

3. In the Bad Morphed Cell Criteria (all must be satisifed) group box, set the following properties:

Property Setting

Min Cell Aspect Ratio 2 0.82

Min Cell Quality 2 0.025

4. Click Apply, then Close.

5. Save the simulation .

Preparing the Plots and Scenes for Visualization

To watch the solution develop, you open the plots for the temperature and for the pressure in the cylinder. Additionally, you create a scene that displays the reaction progress variable.

To open the plots:

1. Multi-select the Results > Plots > Cylinder Temperature and Cylinder Pressure nodes, right-click on one of the selected nodes, and select Open.

The scenes open in the Graphics window.

For the scene that displays the reaction progress variable, you copy the Fuel Distribution 1 scene and modify the displayed scalar field. The Fuel Distribution 1 scene is already set up in such a way as to write image files at regular intervals after each deg CA. To create the reaction progress variable scene:

2. Right-click the Scenes > Fuel Distribution 1 node and select Copy.

3. Right-click the Scenes node and select Paste.

4. Rename Copy of Fuel Distribution 1 to Reaction Progress Variable 1.

5. Rename Reaction Progress Variable 1 > Fuel/Air Equivalence Ratio Derived Parts Scalar 1 to Reaction Progress Variable Derived Parts Scalar 1.

6. Select the Reaction Progress Variable Derived Parts Scalar 1 > Scalar Field node and set Function to ECFM > Progress Variables > Premix Progress Variable.

7. Save the simulation .

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11455

Running the Simulation

The simulation is now set up and ready to run.

You are advised to run this tutorial on a multi-core machine with 16 cores or more. Depending on the specifications of the machine, this tutorial takes approximately 28 hours to complete.

To run the simulation:

1. Click (Play/Resume "In-Cylinder").

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder updates the geometry and starts the meshing process. While the simulation is running, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ In-Cylinder saves the image files for the velocity, pressure, fuel/air equivalence ratio, and reaction progress variable scenes to your working directory. The base name of each image file is combined with the number of the update to ensure that each file is unique.

2. After the run is finished, save the simulation .

Analyzing the Results

After the simulation is complete, you visualize the results.

Examine the plots for the temperature and the pressure inside the cylinder:

1. In the Graphics window, click through the Cylinder Temperature and Cylinder Pressure tabs.

The following plots display the results after the run:

At 741.7 deg CA, the temperature in the cylinder reaches its maximum value of 2597.3 K.

The pressure in the cylinder reaches its maximum value of 58.9 bar at 737.4 deg CA.

Examine the scene for the reaction progress variable:

2. In your working directory, click through the saved image files for the reaction progress variable. The saved scene files can be animated with a media program of your choice:

What Is Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer?

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer is a light-weight, license-free standalone scene and plot viewer for Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

You can use it to examine a scene or plot as you would in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, when the display contents are exported to a three-dimensional .sce graphics file.

As an alternative to running the full Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client, this file format is strictly for interactive viewing. You cannot make scene or plot modifications as you would in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as adding parts to be displayed, changing the coloring or using a different scalar.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 3

Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer is included among the components selected by default in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation on Windows and Linux 64-bit platforms.

It is also available to download as a separate installable package from the Siemens Digital Industries Software support site.

As no licensing is required for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer, it is possible to use it for viewing the results of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulations without needing to purchase the software.

Instructions are provided on how to install the downloaded package on Windows and Linux.

Product Excellence Program

The Product Excellence Program collects information about our customers and their use of Siemens Digital Industries Software. This information helps us improve our product features and functionality to better meet customer needs. No personal or intellectual property information is collected or shared. Product performance is not affected and participation in the program is voluntary.

Privacy statement

The Product Excellence Program helps Siemens Digital Industries Software understand how customers use our products and assists us in improving our products. The program is anonymous and participation is voluntary.

The Product Excellence Program is designed to protect the privacy of the user and the intellectual property created through the use of Siemens Digital Industries Software products.

How does it work?

The Product Excellence Program is used to collect data about your installation, the features you use and how you use them. The data is sent to Siemens Digital Industries Software for analysis. By examining usage patterns from a large number of people, we gain insight into how the products are used and how to improve the software in future releases. Data collection occurs in the background as you use the software and does not affect performance or functionality.

What data is sent?

The data collected can vary by product and by release as we gain more insight or add new capabilities. The Product Excellence Program may collect information on the functions utilized, the operating environment (e.g. OS, RAM, graphics, etc.), product version, or other indications of user interaction. The data may also include the company name that is using the product. This data is solely for use by Siemens Digital Industries Software to improve our products and is never shared with any third party.

There is no contact information in the data and Siemens Digital Industries Software will not contact you by phone or email as a result of the data collected. No information about the data you create or manage is collected.

Participation is optional.

You can control your participation during installation or reinstallation of the software by using the Product Excellence Program option in the interactive installer.

Exporting a Scene or Plot to a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer File

You can export the contents of a scene or plot to a scene file (.sce) from Simcenter STAR-CCM+. You can open the .sce file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer and work with the same interactive image that you had in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Be sure to use the same version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer as the version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ that you used to create the scene file. You can interact with the image to rotate (in scenes), pan, and zoom. If you are exporting a scene that includes sweep animation, you must activate the Precompute Steps option on the relevant animation control beforehand.

1. To save the scene or plot contents to a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer file, do one of the following within the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation:

▶For a scene, right-click the scene node or the scene display, and select Export 3D Visualization File....

Note: This option is deactivated if more than one scene node is selected.

▶For a plot, right-click the plot node or the plot display, and select Export as Scene (*.sce).

This action activates a dialog, in which the Files of Type: filter is used to select the format of the saved file. The file type is set to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer file (*.sce) format by default. This format is the only option available for plot export.

2. To customize the information that appears in the thumbnail preview of the scene file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer, enter a title or a description, or both, in the corresponding text boxes.

3. To compress the data that is saved in the scene file, activate the Use Compression option.

4. Navigate to the location where you want to save the file, enter the file name in the File Name: text box, and click Save.

You can auto-export a scene (but not a plot) into a scene file while the simulation is running. This capability is especially useful for transient simulations as it generates framesets within the scene file. To auto-export the scene:

5. Open the node of the scene and select the Attributes > Update node.

6. Set File Format to sce.

See Also:

Creating Framesets

Creating Framesets

You can create a frameset, or "book", of scenes and/or plots in a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer file.

A frameset lets you flip through multiple scenes and plots in a single scene file. This capability is useful for assembling a set of related 3D images. Examples include a scalar scene with different values of the function, different scalar functions, or even combinations of different scenes (such as mesh and scalar) and plots (such as XY and histogram) of the object that you are simulating.

To create a frameset:

1. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, when saving to a scene file, select the file of the same scene or plot as the one that you are exporting.

Note: It is not possible to append to .sce files that were exported from a version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ prior to 10.02.

2. In the dialog that appears asking you if you want to overwrite the file, click Append.

3. To append a different type of scene or plot, for example to append a scalar scene to the file of a geometry scene, edit the Title text box in the dialog so that the same title is used.

Note: You can append scenes or plots to a scene file without editing the title, but the resulting file does not work as a frameset. Rather, it is simply a group of images that appear together in a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer preview.

To view a frameset:

4. Open the scene file as you would any other.

The preview shows a thumbnail preview of the frameset with the title and description that you specified.

5. To view the frameset, double-click its preview as you would for any other scene file.

6. To scroll through the frameset, click (Step Forwards) or (Step Backwards), or use the slider bar, near the bottom of the display.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 9

These buttons are available only in a scene file that has scenes or plots appended using the same title.

Animating framesets

7. To animate a frameset, click (Play Frameset Animation). To stop the frameset animation, click (Pause Frameset Animation).

8. To have the frameset animation repeat in a loop, activate the checkbox to the right of the slider bar.

9. To adjust the frameset animation speed:

a) Select Tools > Settings.

b) In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer Settings dialog, you can specify the following:

▪Target FPS for frameset animation—maximum number of animation frames that are displayed in one second (less for complex scenes, or when less computing power is available). The minimum FPS is 0.0001.

▪Target frameset animation length—defines the total time of the animation. The actual time can vary depending on your specification of FPS, the complexity of the scene file, and available computing power. The minimum length of an animation is 0.0001 s.

▪Refresh Rate—specifies the rate (frames per second) of refreshing the display during interaction. The higher the value, the less time Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer allocates to drawing an image. If this time is exceeded, surfaces are demoted to a simpler representation. A higher number leads to a smoother interaction, but with less detail.

▪Camera Perspective Angle—adjusts the viewing angle of your scene view. Alternatively, press <Ctrl> while turning the mouse wheel; you can see the view angle change as the numerical setting changes. For details, see "Setting the Camera Angle of View" in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ User Guide.

▪GPU Utilization—functions similarly to this feature in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, except custom settings are not available in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer. For details on GPU utilization, see "Controlling Graphics Performance" in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ User Guide.

c) Click OK.

See Also:

Exporting a Scene or Plot to a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer File

Working with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer

This section provides instructions on launching the standalone scene viewer Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer, and looking at scene files.

Starting Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer

Assuming you have followed the instructions for the installation, start Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer one of the following ways, depending on your platform:

• On Windows, in the Start menu, launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer (earlier versions: Simcenter STARView+) by selecting its menu item in the Siemens Simcenter STAR-CCM+ submenu. (If you installed Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer as a standalone product, then it has its own submenu.)

• On Linux, point to the proper directory for starting Simcenter STAR-CCM+, and enter the following command line:

starview+

Alternatively, you can include the name (and path if necessary) of the specific .sce file to open:

starview+ file.sce

For a complete overview of all Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer command line options, run with -help.

Opening a File

To open a .sce file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer:

1. Start the viewer.

2. Select File > Open.

3. In the Open Scene file dialog, navigate to the .sce file. Click Open.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer automatically opens the scene.

For a scene file that has additional scenes and/or plots appended to it, all those images are previewed.

If images were appended using the same title, a frameset is present, and will appear accordingly in the preview.

5. To return to the preview, click the arrow in the upper right corner of the scene.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer 2020.3  |  User Guide

6. To close the preview, select File > Close.

Note: Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer opens one file per session. To view multiple files, run multiple sessions.

Scene Operations

Once you have the scene open you can move around a scene, hide and show scene objects, and restore a scene. Use the mouse for manipulating scenes within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer. If your exported scene contains animations, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer can replay them. Such animations include streamlines, vectors, and sweeps.

Moving Around a Scene

The techniques for examining a scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer are similar to interacting with the scene display in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Graphics window.

Panning To pan the image in the visualization display, hold down the right mouse button and drag the mouse in the direction where you want to move the object.

The image appears to change its view angle as you pan. This effect is because the view is in the Perspective projection mode, which depicts three-dimensional space. In the Parallel projection mode, the view angle stays the same.

Rolling To roll the scene, hold down the <Ctrl> key, and click and drag the mouse upward or downward.

Using the <Ctrl> key rotates the object along an axis perpendicular to your screen.

Rotating Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses a point on a part to rotate. If you select a point somewhere other than on a part, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses the depth to that last point; the depth is normal to the view plane.

The scene can be rotated around various axes, vertical, horizontal, or arbitrary, depending on the direction you move the mouse.

To rotate, choose a point on or near the object in the visualization display, and click and drag (holding down the left mouse button) from that point.

This technique rotates the object around the axis perpendicular to the direction of your drag. You set the location of the axis when you choose a point to begin clicking and dragging.

Zooming There are two ways to zoom with the mouse:

• Choosing a focal point:

Choose a point inside the display, then click and drag downward using the middle mouse button. This action brings your view closer to that point.

Moving the mouse straight up has the opposite effect.

• Using the mouse wheel:

Turning the mouse wheel toward you brings your view closer to the visualization display; the opposite wheel movement takes your view farther away.

The mouse pointer must be within the visualization display for this operation to work. Its particular position within the display determines the direction of this type of zooming.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 14

Note: Vectors in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer look as they did when you exported the scene; the vector lengths do not update when you zoom in. This is due to the fact that exported vector scenes do not retain all vector data.

Setting Predefined Views

The following options are available for predefined views in the View menu:

• Side View, also <S>

• Top View, also <T>

• Front View, also <F>

• Flip vertical, also <C>

Changing the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer Projection Mode

Each scene can be viewed in either of two projection modes: parallel or perspective. The perspective projection provides a realistic view of the scene whereas the parallel mode looks less realistic and is similar in style to technical diagrams.

By default the scene is set to Perspective Projection. To change to parallel mode in the current view, select View > Parallel Projection. The view of the scene updates automatically.

Hiding and Showing Scene Objects

• To hide an object in a scene, right-click on that object and select Hide object.

• To restore hidden objects, right-click in the scene and select Show All.

Restoring a Scene

• To restore the default settings of the view, right-click on the display and select Reset View. Alternatively:

◦ Select View > Reset View.

◦ Press <R>.

Playing Scene Animations

The controls for the scene animation become available only when the active scene contains an animation. To replay sweep animation, you must have activated the Precompute Steps option on the animation control before exporting the scene from Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See "Sweeping Parts Animation" in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ User Guide.

Note:

Note: For a frameset, a file with multiple scene images, you can set Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer to flip from one scene to the next in an animation. See Animating framesets.

1. To play a scene (or inframe) animation, open the scene file.

At the bottom of the scene, the controls are available.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 15

2. To start the animation, click (Play Inframe Animation).

This animation includes the same types of basic controls as the animations in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

(Pause Inframe Animation) as well as (Stop Inframe Animation).

Viewing Advanced Rendering

You can toggle between normal (OpenGL) rendering and advanced rendering, even in scene files created before the current version. Advanced rendering lets you depict your project in a photorealistic display at an economic computational cost.

If you exported a scene with Enable Advanced Rendering deactivated:

1. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer opens the scene file with normal rendering. To activate advanced rendering, select Render Mode > Advanced Rendering. A progress bar appears in the upper left corner of the scene to show the progress of rendering.

2. To adjust the advanced rendering appearance, select Render Mode > Advanced Rendering Settings.

3. In the Advanced Rendering Settings dialog, adjust the following:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 16

◦ Quality—controls quality of the final image using a slider, with higher quality requiring longer rendering time.

◦ Min Samples Per Pixel—specifies a lower limit for the sampling coverage of each pixel. The value sets a minimum bound for samples shot per pixel. The actual number of samples shot per pixel varies depending on the quality settings, but it is always at or above the bound set with this parameter.

◦ Render Threads—specifies the number of compute threads on the machine that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer is allowed to use for rendering scenes. This value is not saved in the scene file, so Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer always uses half the maximum system value by default.

◦ Noise Reduction—specifies the amount of smoothing applied to the final image. Higher values remove more noise but might filter out fine details.

If you exported a scene with Enable Advanced Rendering activated, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer opens the scene file with advanced rendering activated by default.

To deactivate advanced rendering, select Render Mode > Normal.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 17

Saving Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer Scene Data

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer you can produce output of the contents of a scene file in a variety of ways.

Saving Scene Image Files

You can save a scene to an image file. To do this:

1. Click (Camera).

Alternatively, select File > Hardcopy.

2. In the Export Hardcopy dialog:

a. Navigate to the location for the graphic file.

b. Enter a name for the file in the File name: text box.

c. Select the graphics format from the Save as type: drop-down list.

d. Click Save.

Saving Scene Files

You can export the contents of a scene file to another scene file using Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer.

1. With a scene open, select File > Export.

2. In the Export Hardcopy dialog:

a. Navigate to the location for the scene file.

b. Enter a name for the file in the File name: text box.

c. Click Save.

Recording Interaction with the Scene

You can record your movements of the scene view in an .avi video file. This feature lets you create a visual tour of the scene.

1. To begin the recording, click (Record).

Alternatively, select Tools > Record Movie.

2. In the Save Movie File dialog:

a. Navigate to the location for the video file.

b. Enter a name for the file in the File name: text box.

c. Click Save.

Once you finish saving the file, the recording starts. During the recording, a message appears in the scene display.

3. Carry out the actions in the scene.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Viewer 2020.3  |  User Guide

4. When done, click (Stop Recording).

Alternatively, select Tools > Stop Recording.

Overview

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality Client allows you to explore Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation solutions in a virtual reality environment. You can stand inside a solution and examine how flow, energy, and other quantities interact with the digital prototype.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality is designed to work with HTC Vive. HTC Vive is a virtual reality headset that uses room scale tracking technology to capture your movements in 3D space. Along with the base stations and headset, HTC Vive provides two wireless controllers that act as hands in the virtual reality environment. These controllers provide multiple input methods including a trigger, buttons, and a track pad.

When activated, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality applies a floor below the model and a ceiling above. The floor that appears in the display corresponds to the real floor under your feet—you calibrate the location of your floor when you set up HTC Vive. The ceiling is set at a fixed distance above your head.

Capabilities:

• Standalone and connected modes

◦ Standalone: view the contents of .sce files that you previously exported from Simcenter STAR-CCM+

◦ Connected: interact with scenes on a running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server

• The following capabilities require scenes in which resampled volume parts are applied to a scalar or vector displayer, as applicable:

◦ Particle tracers—release particles into the vector scene flow and watch how they behave in real time

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 2

◦ Plane Section—create an interactive plane section by slicing the scalar volume with a plane

◦ Isosurface—create an interactive isosurface representing constant scalar values in a scalar volume

• Clip planes—remove surfaces in order to view geometry behind

Setup

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality requires that you first set up the HTC Vive equipment and the associated SteamVR software. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality itself comes within the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installer or as a separate download.

Requirements

• Operating system: Windows 10 64-bit

• Graphics card: NVIDIA Quadro P4000 or better (RTX 8000 is optimal)

• Virtual reality equipment (see sections below)

• SteamVR software (installed as part of HTC Vive setup)

HTC Vive Setup

• Follow the HTC Vive setup instructions available from the HTC Vive website. These steps require that you install the SteamVR client with a Steam user account (free of charge).

• Obtain and install the latest driver for your NVIDIA graphics card.

• In the NVIDIA Control Panel, set Threaded optimization to Off.

Windows Mixed Reality Setup

• Follow the Windows Mixed Reality setup instructions from Microsoft.

• Obtain and install the latest driver for your NVIDIA graphics card.

The thumbstick as used by Windows Mixed Reality is supported and has the same functionality as the HTC Vive controllers. Icons and annotations are adapted to fit Mixed Reality.

Oculus Rift S Setup

If Oculus Rift S hardware is detected upon startup of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality client, the relevant .ini file is automatically chosen so that the Oculus Rift controller look-and-feel appears immediately in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality display. No further input is required from you.

You can choose between two options for installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality—either on its own, or as part of an overall Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation.

Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality on Its Own (No License Required)

1. In a web browser, log in to the Support Center portal.

2. In the customer success portal, click Products > Downloads. Your browser is redirected to the Global Technical Access Center (GTAC) of Siemens Digital Industries Software.

3. In the Product Filter box, enter Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 4

4. To begin the download, expand the Full products folder then click the link to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality.

5. When the download completes, open Windows Explorer and navigate to the folder that contains the downloaded executable file.

6. Either run the installer interactively or use the command line:

◦ To run interactively:

1. Right-click the .exe file and choose Run.

2. Follow the on-screen prompts.

◦ To run from the command line:

1. Open a command prompt and navigate to the folder that contains the installer.

2. Run the installer using one or more of the following options:

-i console runs the installer in console mode, which installs Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality with the default settings. Output from this installation is shown in the console window. Note that you are required to accept the license agreement and choose the location for the installation in the console. -DINSTALLDIR=<path> provides an alternative location for the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality installation. -DNOADMIN=true allows the installation and execution of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality without administrator privileges. You must choose an installation location that is not protected by administrator privileges.

Installing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality with Simcenter STAR-CCM+

1. In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Installation Guide, follow the steps for downloading and extracting Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

2. Continue by following the steps within Installing STAR-CCM+ on Windows > Installing STAR-CCM+ Using the Interactive Installer > Custom Install.

3. When you see the list of STAR-CCM+ Components from which to choose, include Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality in your selection.

4. Complete the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation.

Customizing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality

You can customize the environment and rendering quality of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality display. To do this, in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality desktop client, select Tools > Settings. In the Settings dialog, you can specify the following:

• Volume Rendering Quality—sets rendering accuracy for direct volume rendering and isosurfaces.

• Precise Volume Bounds—allows clean clipping of the volume boundaries with the geometry. This clipping is designed to work with all three volume rendering modes (plane sections, isosurfaces, and direct volume rendering).

• Ceiling Texture—sets the holodeck ceiling texture, which consists of a .png image replicated over the ceiling tiles. To use a different image, click Choose and navigate to the replacement file.

• Ceiling Texture Scale—adjusts the scale of the repeated image in the holodeck ceiling texture.

• Floor Texture—sets the holodeck floor texture, which consists of a .png image replicated over the floor tiles. To use a different image, click Choose and navigate to the replacement file.

• Floor Texture Scale—adjusts the scale of the repeated image in the holodeck floor texture.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 5

• Swap Left/Right Controller—switches left and right controller annotations and functionality.

• Preserve Scene Orientation—preserves a prepared view when the scene is loaded. This view can be either the orientation stored in a .sce or simulation file, or the view orientation of a scene opened in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client. This orientation is used when you reset the view. Scale and distance of the model are set to default values and are never preserved.

Product Excellence Program

The Product Excellence Program collects information about our customers and their use of Siemens Digital Industries Software. This information helps us improve our product features and functionality to better meet customer needs. No personal or intellectual property information is collected or shared. Product performance is not affected and participation in the program is voluntary.

Privacy statement

The Product Excellence Program helps Siemens Digital Industries Software understand how customers use our products and assists us in improving our products. The program is anonymous and participation is voluntary.

The Product Excellence Program is designed to protect the privacy of the user and the intellectual property created through the use of Siemens Digital Industries Software products.

How does it work?

The Product Excellence Program is used to collect data about your installation, the features you use and how you use them. The data is sent to Siemens Digital Industries Software for analysis. By examining usage patterns from a large number of people, we gain insight into how the products are used and how to improve the software in future releases. Data collection occurs in the background as you use the software and does not affect performance or functionality.

What data is sent?

The data collected can vary by product and by release as we gain more insight or add new capabilities. The Product Excellence Program may collect information on the functions utilized, the operating environment (e.g. OS, RAM, graphics, etc.), product version, or other indications of user interaction. The data may also include the company name that is using the product. This data is solely for use by Siemens Digital Industries Software to improve our products and is never shared with any third party.

There is no contact information in the data and Siemens Digital Industries Software will not contact you by phone or email as a result of the data collected. No information about the data you create or manage is collected.

Participation is optional.

You can control your participation during installation or reinstallation of the software by using the Product Excellence Program option in the interactive installer.

Preparing Scenes for Use in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality operates on existing scenes that you define within Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

To prepare scenes, use any of the displayer types in constructing scalar or vector scenes. To introduce certain visualization features in real time within the virtual environment, you must first prepare a scene with an appropriate displayer that includes a resampled volume derived part:

• For releasing particles, a vector displayer is required.

• For adding a plane section or an isosurface, a scalar displayer is required.

These scenes can be exported to .sce files.

Some features are not currently supported, including:

• Advanced rendering

• Depth peeling (Transparency Mode option)

• Line integral convolution

• Isoline labels

• Scene grid annotations

• Uniform Screen setting for vector glyphs

Scenes in which you intend to release particles, or add a plane section or an isosurface, require a resampled volume part for the regions of interest.

1. To create a resampled volume part:

a) Right-click Derived Parts and choose New Part > Resampled Volume.

b) Set Input Parts to one or more regions whose solution you wish to view.

c) Define a bounding box for the volume. Either activate Snap to part or set the properties directly (Origin, Size, Rotation Axis, Rotation Angle).

d) Click Create.

2. To apply the resampled volume part in the scene, do either of the following depending on what you want to add:

▶To release particles, select a vector displayer in the scene and set Parts to the resampled volume part. Set the Function of the Vector Field, for example to the Velocity vector.

▶To add a plane section or an isosurface, select a scalar displayer in the scene and set Parts to the resampled volume part. Set the Function of the Scalar Field, for example to the Velocity Magnitude scalar.

To improve default performance of volume rendering, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality automatically reduces quality by half. ("Quality" in this context refers to the accuracy with which the resampled volume is processed during raycasting.)

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 9

Before exporting, you can adjust the quality manually in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with the Quality property of the Volume Rendering Settings sub-node of the scene displayer that includes the resampled volume.

3. To export scenes for use in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality standalone:

a) Right-click on the scene node or the scene display, and select Export 3D Visualization File.

b) In the Save Scene File dialog, you can set the Title and Description of the scene, and activate Compression (for a reduced file size).

Other quality and performance notes:

◦ If your scene includes a 2D annotation, such as a plot annotation, its foreground has an aspect ratio of 4:3. To avoid distortions, set the Aspect Ratio property of the scene node in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to 4:3.

◦ To prevent graphical artifacts, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality automatically increases line width to at least 2.0 pixels.

◦ When creating a resampled volume part that is used in a scalar scene, set the Minimum Voxel Size and Cell Size to Voxel Ratio such that the final number of voxels is less than 50 million. To get the voxel count, click Preview in the in-place dialog of the resampled volume part. Beneath the Preview button, the voxel count appears.

◦ Avoid using local lighting in a scene that uses volume rendering.

◦ Leave the Contour Style property of a scalar displayer set at Automatic.

4. To auto-export scenes to file while a simulation is running, (for example, scenes at regular intervals in a transient simulation):

a) Open the node of the scene and select the Attributes > Update node.

b) Set File Format to sce.

c) Set the update properties to save at the frequency you require.

Standalone Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality: Launching and Loading Scenes

Note: The virtual reality hardware must be connected before you attempt to launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality. Otherwise Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality exits with an error.

1. To launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality in standalone mode:

▶From the Windows Start menu, locate the CD-adapco submenu, then select Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality.

▶From the command line, enter:

[INSTALLDIR]\starvr

2. In standalone mode, to open scenes:

a) Select File > Open.

b) Choose a .sce file.

c) Select a scene from the list that appears and click OK.

Connected Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality: Launching and Loading Scenes

Prerequisites:

• Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and load the simulation file that you wish to view. If you want to allow other users to connect to the same Virtual Reality session in collaboration mode, be sure to set the Connection Mode of the simulation to Collaboration.

• The virtual reality hardware must be connected before you attempt to launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality. Otherwise Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality exits with an error.

1. To launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality in connected mode, interactively:

a) From the Windows Start menu, select Siemens > Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality.

b) In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality, select File > Connect.

c) In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality server dialog, specify the following:

▪Host—If you are running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on the same computer as Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality, enter localhost. For any other computer, enter the name that appears in the Host property of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server node. In some cases you must use the fully qualified domain after the hostname, for example, mycomputer.siemens.com.

▪Port Number—Enter the number that appears in the Port property of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server node.

To obtain the hostname and portnumber for a running Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ UI, select Window > Servers.

2. In the Servers panel, select the local server for the simulation to which you wish to connect.

3. From the properties, obtain the Host and Port.

2. To launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality in connected mode from the command line:

In a command prompt window, enter:

[INSTALLDIR]\starvr hostname portnumber

Where hostname and portnumber are as described above.

3. In connected mode, to open scenes, choose from the list that you see after connecting to the server. If there is only one scene, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality connects to that scene automatically.

If you are connecting to a colleague's server in collaboration mode, then from the list of scenes on the remote server, choose the one that your colleagues are also using.

4. If you are connecting to a collaborative virtual reality session that has already been set up:

a) Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality.

b) Have the correct host and port number for the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality session.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 12

Note: Depending on how your network is configured, you may need additional information to connect to the host computer, such as the network path.

c) Select File > Connect.

Note: Depending on network bandwidth, connecting to the remote session can take some time.

Exploring the Virtual Scene

After loading a scene into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality, you can enter the virtual environment that the headset now displays.

To get brief, helpful information right in the scene view, access the Quick Start guide using either of the following techniques:

• Select Help > Quick Start from the top menus of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality.

• Press the menu button on top of either controller. Press again to view the next slide. To turn off Quick Start, press both menu buttons simultaneously.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality controllers provide a palette of options for controlling view, movement, and other aspects of the scene. For details, see Controller Action Reference.

To explore the environment:

1. Stand or sit approximately in the center of the designated floor area, put on the headset, and hold the controllers.

Note: For better responses from the controllers, press the virtual controls in the interior of the touchpads, not directly on the edges.

2. To move the model closer to you, point one of the controllers so that the controller handle and the hoop are aligned with your forward line-of-sight. Using your thumb on the same controller, press Pull. To move the model away from you, press Push.

3. To move the model sideways, or up and down:

a) Point the controller hoop in the corresponding direction.

b) Press Push or Pull.

4. To fly around the model while it remains stationary:

a) Press a grip button on one of the controllers; the palette appears. A laser beam shines from the front of the other controller.

b) Point the laser beam of the other controller at the (Static/Fly) icon on the palette; squeeze the controller trigger at the same time.

You are now in Fly mode; the controller buttons update to show +Fly and –Fly, and the Fly mode icon appears in the scene.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 14

c) Hold one controller at arms length in front of you; point the hoop in the direction in which you wish to move.

d) Press +Fly to move forwards in that direction; press –Fly to move backwards in the opposite direction.

e) To return to Static mode, repeat the action with the controller palette.

5. To release particles into the flow:

a) Using the pan, move, and fly controls, move to a position where you can place one of the controller hoops into the flow domain.

b) Hold one of the controller hoops in the flow at the point from which you want particles to appear.

c) On the same controller touchpad, press Flow. Particles now enter the scene through the hoop.

d) To make this injection point a continuous source, press + on the touchpad of the other controller.

e) While particles are entering, control the speed at which they travel using the Increase Particle Speed and Decrease Particle Speed actions on the palette.

f) Control the diameter of particles using the Increase Particle Diameter and Decrease Particle Diameter actions on the palette.

g) To remove a continuous source of particles, point a controller hoop at the source, press Flow, and then press - on the other controller.

6. One or multiple plane sections can be used to create slices through the scalar volume. To add a plane section in the scene:

a) Press Plane on the right controller.

The plane section icon and a temporary plane section appear, moving as you move the controller.

b) Position the plane section where you want it.

c) With the left controller, press +.

The plane section remains in the selected position, with scene data displayed on it.

d) To remove the nearest plane section, press Plane, and press - with the left controller.

7. One or multiple isosurfaces can be used to represent constant scalar values in the scalar volume. To add a isosurface in the scene:

a) Press Iso on the right controller.

The iso color bar, with a pointer, and a temporary isosurface appear, moving as you move the controller.

b) Position the iso color bar where you want it, with the pointer at the desired scalar value along the bar.

c) With the left controller, press +.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 15

The isosurface remains, with the scalar value displayed on it.

d) To remove the nearest isosurface, press Iso, and press - with the left controller.

8. To view volume rendering in the scene:

Note: The resampled volume derived part must be included in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ scene.

a) Press a grip button on one of the controllers; the palette appears. A laser beam shines from the front of the other controller.

b) Point the laser beam of the other controller at the (Volume Rendering) icon on the palette; squeeze the controller trigger at the same time.

The resampled volume appears in the scene.

c) To deactivate the volume rendering, repeat the action with the controller palette.

9. To hide surfaces using clip planes:

a) Press Clip on the right controller.

b) Position the clip plane icon in the plane where you want the clipping to occur.

As you move the icon, the part of the model beyond that plane becomes invisible.

c) With the left controller, press +.

The part of the model beyond the clip plane remains invisible.

d) To remove the nearest clip plane, point at it with the right controller, press Clip, and press - with the left controller.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Collaborating in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality

If you connect to the same Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server as other colleagues, then you can see their position as an avatar when you view the same scene. Use cases are collaborative exploration, tutoring (an experienced user introduces a novice user to virtual reality), or demonstrations (for example at a car show).

1. To set up a collaborative virtual reality session, follow the procedure for a session that is connected to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, but be sure to specify Collaboration when launching the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Server. For details of the procedure, see Connected Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality: Launching and Loading Scenes.

When multiple users have joined a virtual reality session, the following information becomes available to all users:

◦ The position and orientation of each user and their controllers are transmitted to all other users in the scene —using a different-colored hard hat avatar for each user. Interactive tools such as particle injection and palette settings are also transmitted. Hence you can see the immediate actions of all others users in the scene.

◦ All interaction items (plane sections, iso surfaces, clip planes, or particle seed points) are shared globally. The addition or deletion of an item is transmitted to all other users.

◦ Palette settings that you use to customize your virtual reality experience can be optionally shared.

All users can perform standard Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality actions, including addition or removal of clip planes, plane sections, isosurfaces, and particle sources. You can remove such elements regardless of which user created them.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 17

2. To share your virtual reality settings with other users, select Tools > Collaborative and choose from the options in the Shared Settings dialog. The options you activate cause your changes to those settings to be transmitted to other users.

◦ Show/Hide HUD (heads-up display, or visibility of 2D scene elements in the foreground, such as the color bar and annotations)

◦ Enable/Disable Fly Mode

◦ Show/Hide Floor and Ceiling

◦ Show/Hide Volume Rendering

◦ Increase/Decrease Particle Radius

◦ Increase/Decrease Particle Speed

When you share a setting with other users, link symbols, with colors corresponding to the other users, appear on the palette icon of that setting to indicate that it is shared.

3. To follow another user:

a) Press a grip button on one of the controllers; the palette appears. A laser beam shines from the front of the other controller.

b) Point the laser beam at the bounding box of the user's avatar and press the trigger. As long as the trigger is pressed, you are connected to the other user in follow mode.

c) If your finger grows tired from holding down the trigger, switch to the other controller by pressing and holding its trigger.

As a user moves the model (scale, translate, rotate), these transforms are transmitted to the other users in follow mode.

4. To stop following a user, release the trigger of your controller.

5. To locate a user who is not in view, look for an arrow with that user's color that points to the user's location.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 18

When a user is behind an object in the view, the location is indicated by a diamond.

6. To move closer to another user, point the controller in that user's direction and press Pull. To move farther away, press Push.

7. To move the current viewpoint instantly, or teleport, to the viewpoint of another user:

a) Press a grip button on one of the controllers; the palette appears. A laser beam shines from the front of the other controller.

b) Point the laser beam of the other controller at the (Teleport) icon on the palette.

c) Point at the left or right arrow alongside the icon to cycle to the target user.

d) When the laser beam points to the desired user, squeeze the controller trigger.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Controller Action Reference

Use the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality controller palette to modify particle speed and size, control visibility of scene elements, choose movement modes, and reset the view.

Action What It Does

Decreases or increases the relative speed of tracer particles as they move through the scene. These actions do not control the rate at which particles are released into the scene.

Decrease Particle Speed Increase Particle Speed

Decreases or increases the diameter of the tracer particles in the scene (all at once).

Decrease Particle Diameter Increase Particle Diameter

Toggles the visibility of 2D scene elements in the foreground, such as the color bar and annotations.

Toggle Visibility of 2D Scene Elements

Toggles between Static (Push/Pull) and Fly modes. In Static mode, you are standing still and pushing or pulling the object. In Fly mode, you appear to be moving.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Virtual Reality 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 20

Action What It Does

Toggle between Static and Fly Modes

Toggles the visibility of the floor and ceiling. When this action is activated, the floor and ceiling are visible. When you deactivate it, you see yourself floating in a white void.

Toggle Visibility of Floor and Ceiling

Toggles the visibility of a resampled volume derived part, provided that part is included in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ scene. By default this option is deactivated.

Toggle Volume Rendering

Resets the following:

• The scene view, that is, the size and position of the model

• Particles

• Seed locations

• Clip planes

Reset

Moves the current viewpoint instantly to the viewpoint of another user.

Click left and right arrows to cycle through all users present in the same scene. The color of the glasses and arrows match the user colors.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Add-on provides you with straightforward access to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver from within the CATIA environment.

Standard physics models, including turbulence, ideal gas, heat transfer, and gravity are supported for single body cases. Multiple body simulations involving conjugate heat transfer, rotating reference frames, and porous media are also supported. Advanced physics models can be added to the simulation by either launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and selecting them directly, or by implementing additional Java macro commands.

Introducing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 provides you with straightforward access to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver from within the CATIA environment.

Standard physics models, including turbulence, ideal gas, heat transfer, and gravity are supported for single body cases. Multiple body simulations involving conjugate heat transfer, rotating reference frames, and porous media are also supported. Advanced physics models can be added to the simulation by either launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and selecting them directly, or by implementing additional Java macro commands.

Contents:

What are the Capabilities?

Getting Started

Common Functions

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on Different Machines

See Also:

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

What are the Capabilities?

This section highlights the capabilities of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 enables you to:

• Define flow characteristics for the simulation

• Specify mesh parameters and controls

• Execute the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, with specified solution controls

• Post-process results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

• Use parallel processing

Problem Definition

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 provides an interface for the specification of continua, regions, and boundaries in order to define the CFD simulation. This information is then used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to calculate a solution and present results.

The particular solver options that you can currently select through the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 interface include:

• Turbulence

◦ k-e Model

◦ Laminar

• Temperature

◦ Thermal Modelling

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 4

◦ Conjugate Heat Transfer

• Equation of State

◦ Constant Density

◦ Ideal Gas

• Porous Media

◦ Isotropic

◦ Uni-Directional

• Moving Reference Frames

• Energy Source

• Gravity

• Passive Scalar

Meshing

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 provides you with a transparent interface to Simcenter STAR-CCM+’s surface and volume meshing tools. This allows you to generate high-quality meshes using a solid model that was built within the CATIA environment. The specific meshing functionality includes:

• Surface meshing using the surface remesher for optimum mesh quality

• Prismatic subsurface meshing in the volume mesh for capturing near-wall boundary layers

• Volume meshing of parts with either:

◦ Tetrahedral core mesh generation

◦ Polyhedral core mesh generation

◦ Trimmed hexahedral core mesh generation

• Automatic handling of region-to-region interfaces

Running the Solver

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 allows the generation of solutions with varying accuracy and speed by providing the following solver controls:

• Number of iterations

• Stopping criterion at which to assume convergence

• Discretization scheme (1st or 2nd order)

• Solver under-relaxation factors

• Additional commands using Java macros

Post-processing

As post-processing is carried out in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, a wide range of tools are available for analysis. These include:

• Scalar scenes

• Vector scenes

• Streamlines

• Isosurfaces

• Plane sections

• Reports

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 5

• Plots

Parallel Processing

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 supports parallel processing for mesh generation and solver calculations. You can set up parallel processing in the Preferences dialog. The different Simcenter STAR-CCM+ licensing options can also be selected here. See Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing.
