Launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

To launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5:

1. Start CATIA using the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 desktop icon that was created by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installer.

For version 15.06.###, this will be STAR-CAT5 Rxx 15.06.###. In the unlikely event that a desktop shortcut was not created during the installation process, you can create a new shortcut manually. See Creating a STAR-CAT5 Shortcut Manually.

2. Select File > Open and open the CATPart or CATProduct that you want to analyze.

3. Select Start > Analysis & Simulation > STAR-CAT5.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 tree is located on the top-left of the window, and the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Info App window launches.

Contents:

Manually Creating a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Shortcut

Manually Creating a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Shortcut

If a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 shortcut is not created by the installer, you can manually generate one yourself by following the steps outlined below.

1. Open a Command Prompt:

a) Click Start.

b) Type cmd in the search field at the bottom of the Start menu and select cmd.exe from the search results.

2. Enter the following line in the Command Prompt, taking care to preserve the correct spacing:

<setcatenv> -e "<shortcutname>" -p "<catiainstalldir>;<starcadinstalldir>" - a global -icon no -menu yes -cs CATIA

where:

◦ <setcatenv> is the full path to setcatenv.exe. The default location for a 64-bit installation is: C:\Program Files\Dassault Systemes\Bxx\win_b64\code\bin\setcatenv.exe

◦ <shortcutname> is the name of the new shortcut that will be generated.

◦ <catiainstalldir> is the full path to the CATIA Bxx directory. The default path is: C:\Program Files\Dassault Systemes\Bxx

◦ <starcadinstalldir> is the full path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Bxx directory. The default path for a 64-bit installation is: C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\STAR-CAD[VERSION] \STAR-CAT5\win64\bin\Bxx where x is the relevant version of your installation.

An example is shown below. In this case a new shortcut for a 64-bit installation of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 15.06.### is shown. In this case the shortcut name is STARCAT5_R21_TEST.

"C:\Program Files\Dassault Systemes\B21\win_b64\code\bin\setcatenv.exe" -e "STAR-CAT5_R21_TEST" -p "C:\Program Files\Dassault Systemes\B21;C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-CAT5\win64\bin\B21" -a global -icon no - menu yes -cs CATIA

A new shortcut will be generated and placed in the Start menu of CATIA. The default location is Start > CATIA.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Info App Window

The STAR-Works Info App window automatically appears when you start Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Initially, this window only contains the Status tab which displays the version and licensing information for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5. More tabs appear as you create or load geometry files in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, allowing you to perform more actions.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7

You cannot close the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Info App window while CATIA or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 are running. Attempting to close the window by clicking the X button returns a message in the Status tab informing you of this. You can maximize and minimize the window by clicking the - and _ buttons respectively.

Use the Clear button to clear all the information that is displayed in a particular tab.

Use the Abort button to stop active processes, such as surface/volume meshing, or the solver. This button only appears when you can stop a process — it is grayed out at all other times.

A clock is displayed in the bottom-left of the window. This clock displays the current time on your machine. A progress bar is located next to the clock and reports the progress of various processes, such as mesh generation and the solver.

More information on the various tabs is provided in the following sections:

• The Status Tab

• The Output Tab

• The Model Checker Tab

• The Residuals Tab

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 8

The Status Tab

The Status tab displays the licensing information for your current session, informing you whether the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 license checked out successfully. The version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 is also displayed in this tab. This tab appears by default when you launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 without a geometry file.

The Output Tab

The Output tab appears once you create or open a geometry file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 9

During the meshing process, this tab displays status information along with a brief report on the generated mesh. If errors were encountered during the meshing process, they are reported here with suggestions as to what can be causing them.

When the solver is running, the Output tab behaves like the output window in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, displaying the data for each residual per iteration. When the solver finishes running, the same information is also displayed in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Output window.

You can control the amount of information that is displayed in the Output tab by editing the verbosity in the config.xml file. See Modifying the Config.xml File.

To abort the mesher or solver, click the Abort button.

The Model Checker Tab

The Model Checker tab displays information from the live model checker, where the case setup is actively monitored for any problems. See Checking the Model for Errors.

The following example reports that the case has no inlet boundary defined.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 10

The Residuals Tab

The Residuals tab appears when you launch the solver. Use the residuals to monitor the convergence of the solution being calculated.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11

Typically, a drop in three to five orders of magnitude in the residuals indicates that the solution has converged to an acceptable level. The residuals that are displayed in this tab also appear in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ under the Plots node.

You can zoom in to the residuals by clicking and holding the left mouse button in the graph area and drawing a box around the area you want to view. To zoom out, right-click in the graph area. You can hide individual residuals from the Residuals tab by clicking their label at the top of the plot window.

Modifying the config.xml File

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ requires a configuration file to enable it to find the appropriate components to run correctly. This configuration file is created during installation. An explanation of the file and settings within it is given here.

The configuration file is called config.xml. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 searches for this file in the installation directory.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 12

Typical config.xml content is shown below. In this example Simcenter STAR-CCM+ version 15.06.### is shown.

<CAD> <STAR_HOME>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\star</ STAR_HOME> <SOLVER>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\star\bin \starccm+.exe</SOLVER> <LOGFILE>starcad.log</LOGFILE> <WWHELP>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.### \win64\Intel11.1\wwhelp.exe</WWHELP> <MANDIR>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\doc\en \online</MANDIR> <VERBOSITY>Normal</VERBOSITY> <!-- Can be Verbose, Log or Normal. Default Normal --> </CAD>

You can edit the following lines:

• <SOLVER> provides the location of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver executable. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ licensing options are set in the Preferences dialog in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 user interface. See Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing.

• <LOGFILE> is the log file that will automatically be created and saved when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 is run. A path of your choice can be used.

• <VERBOSITY> is the verbosity of the output window in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Info App. This can be set to one of the following:

◦ Normal—This is the default setting and will display the least amount of information in the Output panel.

◦ Verbose—This will display a moderate amount of information in the Output panel.

◦ Log—This will display all available information in the Output panel.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Object Tree

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 uses an object tree as the primary method for setting parameters.

The object tree consists of nodes, each one of which represents a particular component of the simulation. This approach to the user interface complements the method that is used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+, allowing for an easy transition between the two software packages.

The object tree appears slightly different in assembly mode as it must accommodate multiple parts, but the principles of operation remain the same.

Nodes are arranged in an order that follows the recommended workflow for setting up a simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5. At each stage, you typically right-click on a particular node in the tree and choose the appropriate action from the pop-up menu.

Certain functionality within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 applies to the simulation as a whole, rather than to individual objects. These operations are provided in either the menu or toolbar.

A complete list of all functions and their respective location is included in Understanding the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Interface.

Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing

The licensing options and the options for setting up parallel processing are located in the Preferences dialog.

This dialog provides two sets of options: server preferences and server settings.

• Server preferences are applied whenever Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 starts a server.

• Server settings are saved in the CAD file and are applied only to that CAD file. Click Save as Default Server Settings to save the current server settings as the default settings to be applied to all CAD files.

To modify the run mode and licensing options:

1. Select STAR-CAT5 > Preferences from the menu.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 16

The Preferences dialog appears.

2. Select the run mode:

▶For serial, set Run Mode to Serial (the default setting).

▶For parallel, set Run Mode to Parallel and Compute Processes to the desired number of cores.

You can use the up/down buttons or you can type in the number of cores that you want to use.

▶For advanced licensing options, such as Power on Demand, enter the appropriate argument in the Command field.

For Power on Demand, enter:

-licpath 1999@flex.cd-adapco.com -podkey <pod_key>

Where:

▪1999@flex.cd-adapco.com is the default CD-adapco Power on Demand server.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 17

▪<pod_key> is the Power on Demand license key.

For more information on Power on Demand licensing, see the section User Guide > Using STAR-CCM + > STAR-CCM+ Licensing > Power on Demand Licensing.

A full list of command-line arguments is available in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ User Guide at User Guide > Using STAR-CCM+ > Command-Line Reference.

The Command field updates automatically to reflect the selections you make. Manual entries are not affected by these selections.

3. Select a licensing option:

▶To use a Power Session license, select Power Session.

This license is designed for parallel simulations, where you can use an unlimited number of cores in this session.

▶To use a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Lite license, select Lite Session.

A limited set of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ features are provided when you activate this option.

If you select no licensing option, the default CAD client license is used.

4. Click OK.

If the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server is running when you modify the preferences, a message box appears informing you that both Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ must be closed for the changes to take effect.

5. Click OK to proceed.

6. Close the active Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ sessions.

7. Restart Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Note: The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server only starts when it is required, such as during surface meshing or volume meshing. It does not start when you launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

If an option in the Preferences dialog conflicts with an option in the config.xml file, the option that is set in the Preferences dialog takes precedence. An example of such a situation is if the Compute Processes property is set to 4 in the Preferences panel, while it is set to 2 in the config.xml file; the simulation runs using four processors. See Modifying the config.xml File

Note: IBM Platform MPI must be installed on your local machine for you to run in parallel. This program is included with the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ package installer.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 18

To change the units system:

1. Bring up the Choose Units System dialog:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 19

The Choose Units System dialog appears.

Automatic Unit Conversion in Dialog Panels

Note: Specific values that you have already modified the units on are not affected by a change of units system.

Transferring Units to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Units that are used in the CAD geometry file are also used in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation. Less common units, such as those listed below, are not supported in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

• Micrometers

• Angstroms

• Nanometers

• Mils

• Microinches

• Footinches (this unit may be converted to inches in Simcenter STAR-CCM+)

• Miles

Note: This list may not be exhaustive and is subject to change.

These units are converted to meters when the CAD geometry is imported into Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Transferring the CAE Model to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

You can transfer your geometry and the simulation setup to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ at any time from within the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 environment. If you want to transfer only the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, refer to Transferring Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

To transfer the geometry with the simulation set up:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, select Transfer CAE Model.

The version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ that is affiliated with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 launches.

Note: A surface mesh is required in order to visualize the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If you have not generated a mesh before clicking Transfer CAE Model, the geometry is tessellated with a medium density.

Editing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Settings While the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client is Running

If you make a change in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 while the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client is running, such as adding or deleting a boundary, you may need to update the volume mesh.

Scenes in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ session will not display the model correctly unless you keep the volume mesh up to date. A list of changes that require you to re-mesh the geometry is provided below:

• For boundaries and regions: changing the type, adding or deleting

• For mesh pipelines and mesh controls: editing, adding or deleting

When adding or removing regions and boundaries in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, the scenes in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ may be missing some parts, as shown below, even after re-meshing the geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 21

To update the scene, you need to manually add the modified regions and boundaries to the scene in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client. You can do this by dragging and dropping the region or part from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ object tree, or by adding the region or part using the Part Selector. An alternative method would be to create a new scene, as this will automatically pick up the new regions and boundaries added to the simulation.

Product Excellence Program

The Product Excellence Program collects information about our customers and their use of Siemens Digital Industries Software. This information helps us improve our product features and functionality to better meet customer needs. No personal or intellectual property information is collected or shared. Product performance is not affected and participation in the program is voluntary.

Privacy statement

The Product Excellence Program helps Siemens Digital Industries Software understand how customers use our products and assists us in improving our products. The program is anonymous and participation is voluntary.

The Product Excellence Program is designed to protect the privacy of the user and the intellectual property created through the use of Siemens Digital Industries Software products.

How does it work?

The Product Excellence Program is used to collect data about your installation, the features you use and how you use them. The data is sent to Siemens Digital Industries Software for analysis. By examining usage patterns from a large number of people, we gain insight into how the products are used and how to improve the software in future releases. Data collection occurs in the background as you use the software and does not affect performance or functionality.

What data is sent?

The data collected can vary by product and by release as we gain more insight or add new capabilities. The Product Excellence Program may collect information on the functions utilized, the operating environment (e.g.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 23

OS, RAM, graphics, etc.), product version, or other indications of user interaction. The data may also include the company name that is using the product. This data is solely for use by Siemens Digital Industries Software to improve our products and is never shared with any third party.

There is no contact information in the data and Siemens Digital Industries Software will not contact you by phone or email as a result of the data collected. No information about the data you create or manage is collected.

Participation is optional.

You can control your participation during installation or reinstallation of the software by using the Product Excellence Program option in the interactive installer.

Assigning Surfaces and Parts to Objects in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

Regions, boundaries, mesh pipelines, and mesh controls are all represented as objects on the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 object tree. You can assign parts and surfaces to these objects when their property dialog is open.

Assigning Surfaces to Objects

The selected surfaces are highlighted on the CAD geometry. By default, CATIA only highlights the edges of selected surfaces. This behavior can be changed so that the surface is highlighted as well, as is shown in the following screenshot.

2. On the CAD geometry, click the part that you want to assign to the object. You can add multiple parts by clicking more parts on the CAD geometry.

Removing Surfaces and Parts from Objects in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

Regions, boundaries, mesh pipelines, and mesh controls are all represented as objects on the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 object tree. You can remove parts and surfaces from these objects when their property dialog is open.

A surface that is removed from a boundary is returned to the default boundary. Similarly, removing a part from a region returns it to the default region.

Removing Surfaces from Objects

To remove a surface from an object (when its property dialog is open):

2. On the CAD geometry, click the part that you want to remove.

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on Different Machines

You can run Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on two different machines.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ operates on a client-server architecture, where Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is the server and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 is the client. A benefit of client-server architectures is that the client and the server do not have to be running on the same machine. Typically, CAD packages run on Windows operating systems. You can choose to run Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on any remote machine with a supported or certified platform, including Linux platforms.

Transferring Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

With Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, you can transfer your CAD geometry directly to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ from within the CATIA environment. Along with the geometry data, you can also transfer design data, such as CAD parameters, coordinate systems, and reference planes.

The Transfer Geometry feature imports your geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+. This function provides an alternative method to the CAD translator add-ons for importing geometry. This method of transferring geometry can provide a faster workflow when performing a design analysis.

To transfer geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, select Transfer Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and imports the CAD geometry. You are now at the same stage in the workflow as if you imported the surface mesh directly into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using the CAD translators (File > Import > Import Surface Mesh...).

2. Set up your case in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Caution: Do not click Transfer CAE Model if you have previously used the Transfer Geometry method and set up your case in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. This action results in the loss of your settings in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Saving Simulation Files

or

Transferring Design Data to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Design data consists of CAD parameters, coordinate systems, and reference planes that you can transfer to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ along with the geometry.

CAD parameters control the feature dimensions, for example extrusion depth, and are useful for modifying the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ after running the analysis. You can use reference planes in scalar scenes and reports in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. You can use coordinate systems to define motion in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation.

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, CAD parameters appear within the Expressions Editor dialog as single-values with units. You can select these for use in expressions, which in turn can be used in the following contexts:

• In 3D-CAD, for expressions that apply to design parameters

• Expression reports

• Coordinate parameters

Additionally, after transfer, you can set a CAD parameter in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to reference global scalar parameters.

To transfer design data to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, click Design Data.

The Design Data dialog appears.

Note: Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 only recognizes native CAD features as CAD parameters. Only recognized CAD parameter are displayed in the list.

▶Coordinate Systems—Click the Coordinate Systems tab and select the coordinate systems that you want to transfer from the list. You can select multiple items at once.

▶Reference Planes—Click the Reference Planes tab and select the planes that you want to transfer from the list. You can select multiple items at once.

3. In each tab, activate the Transfer to STAR-CCM+ option.

Once you transfer a CAD parameter to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you can modify the geometry from within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with respect to that parameter. This feature is useful for quickly modifying a geometry after performing an analysis in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ without needing to return to the original CAD software.

In the following example, the geometry of a diffuser is modified.

To modify a geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

2. Transfer the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Transferring Geometry to STAR-CCM+.

Transferred geometries are located under the Geometry > Parts node.

Transferred CAD parameters are located under the Geometry > CAD Client Models > [part_name] > CAD Parameters node.

3. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, save the geometry file. The simulation file is also saved.

▶To update the part without updating the parameters in the CAD file, right-click Geometry > CAD Client Models > [part_name] and select Update Model.

The geometry updates according to the CAD parameter changes.

This workflow maintains an active link between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and Simcenter STAR-CCM+. When working with Geometry Transfer, you can modify the geometry in either package and the geometry in the relevant package is updated accordingly.

Updating the Geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with CATIA Closed

You can close CATIA and continue working with the simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Doing so, however, breaks the link between the two software packages. Any further updates that you make to the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are not transferred back to the geometry in CATIA. Instead, these changes are stored in memory, which allows you to include the CAD parameters in your optimization scripts.

This workflow also allows you to release the CATIA and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 licenses when performing tasks in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In this case, the CATIA and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 licenses are temporarily checked out only when the updates to the geometry are stored in memory.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 37

Transferring the geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 will overwrite the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Transferring CATIA Publications to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

You can transfer published entity names from CATIA to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using the Transfer Geometry feature of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

When you transfer geometry that contains CATIA publication data, the published names are transferred instead of the default entity name.

You can transfer the published names for the following entities:

• Surfaces—by default, surface names are extracted from the last feature that created them, for example Pad.1. Transferring the published name allows you to control the names of the surfaces.

• CAD Parameters—by default, CAD parameters are transferred with a generic name that describes what they are, for example Length.19. If the CAD parameter is published, then the name of the published CAD parameter is transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, CAD parameter names are concatenated with the part or assembly name that they come from, for example Part\CAD Parameter.

• Features—by default, the feature name is transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If the feature contains published data, then this name is transferred instead.

• Bodies—by default, body names are not used in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. When a part contains more than one body, the bodies are transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ as parts inside a composite part. The published name of these parts will be transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

If the same entity, feature, or body is published more than once in the assembly tree, then the top-most publication is used for that entity, feature, or body respectively.

You can control how the geometry is transferred from CATIA to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ through the Geometry Transfer Settings dialog.

To access the Geometry Transfer Settings dialog:

1. Right-click the STAR-CAT5 > CAE Model Case > Solution and select Geometry Transfer Settings.

Create Part Contacts from Coincident Faces Controls whether the geometry transfer feature searches for pairs of coincident faces on the CAD faces. For each pair found, part contact data is created and stored in the Contacts property (in Simcenter STAR-CCM+). See the Creating Part Contacts from Coincident Entities section in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ user guide.

Transfer Multi-Body Parts as Composites Specifies whether to transfer a single part containing multiple solid bodies as a composite part. Part contacts are created for each pair of coincident faces. Leaving this option deactivated merges all solid bodies in the part.

Transfer Hidden Geometry Specifies whether to transfer hidden parts. By default, hidden parts in CATIA are not transferred. For files saved in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 v10.06 and earlier, this option is activated by default.

Transfer Sheet Geometry Specifies whether to transfer sheet bodies as part of the transfer process. This option is turned off by default.

A simple message is displayed in the output window which states if the surface mesh is valid. For example: Body 2 is not valid.

Understanding the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Process

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 the typical workflow for running a simulation is as follows:

1. Ensure that the CAD model is suitable for analysis

2. Extract the fluid volume

3. Define the material properties for each part of the model, for example, air, water, aluminum

4. Define model physics, for example, turbulence, temperature, gravity

5. Specify boundary conditions, for example, inlets, outlets, symmetry planes

6. Specify mesh settings

7. Define solution controls

8. Run the case

9. Post-process the results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Once you have obtained an initial solution you may wish to re-run the case with some different settings, or with some changes to the geometry. To do this you can:

1. Return to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and change settings or modify the geometry

2. Re-run the case

Using Suitable CAD Models in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 only supports the use of solid bodies. If a geometry is made up entirely of surfaces then it will not be possible to define any boundary conditions, and the meshing options will be greyed out.

It is good practice to create copies of the original geometry file(s) before importing them into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Suppressed or deactivated parts and features are not supported by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and will have no effect on the analysis. Hidden parts, however, are used in the analysis. Ensure that all desired parts and features are active before using them with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Extracting the Fluid Volume

A CAD model usually represents a component made from solid material. However, in the case of flow simulation, a model representing the fluid volume is needed, requiring a different CAD model to be created. This is illustrated below:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 41

In some instances, a simulation will require multiple regions, such as:

• Moving Reference Frames

For rotating flow, such as turbines.

• Porous Media

For representing regions with fine geometric structures

• Energy Source

For simulating thermal specifications, such as conjugate heat transfer

These types of simulation require each region to be represented by individual contiguous parts within an assembly.

Defining Material Properties

Continua determines the characteristics of the fluid and solid entities used within the simulation. The behavior of a single continuum is primarily defined by the chosen material type and physics models.

Specification of the material type used in the simulation provides properties such as density, viscosity and conductivity, which are all used by the solver to calculate a solution. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 includes a database of common materials and allows you to modify material properties where necessary.

Defining Model Physics

Physics models determine the nature of the fluid, and can be described as either:

• Turbulent or Laminar

• Constant Density or Ideal Gas

Additional models can also be activated to meet the needs of various simulation requirements:

• Passive scalar

• Temperature

• Gravity

A region is defined as a volume domain in a simulation, surrounded by boundaries. Each region in the simulation must be represented by a part in the native CAD package. When multiple regions are required, multiple parts must be used within an assembly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 42

All regions must be assigned to a continuum, as they represent a volume of material in the simulation. Region settings can be used to define porous media, moving reference frames, and an energy source.

Specifying Boundary Conditions

To define boundary conditions you first need to select the surface or surfaces on the model to assign to a separate boundary.

A boundary is defined as a surface, which along with other boundaries, surround and characterize a region. Boundary conditions determine how the boundary will affect the material within a region, and consequently, the simulation as a whole.

Inlet boundaries determine how much fluid enters the region, using a velocity, mass flow rate or stagnation inlet. Outlet boundaries define the process for fluid leaving the region, which are defined with either a pressure or flow-split ratio. Wall boundaries contain the fluid, and can also be used to define a thermal specification that will influence the transfer of energy to or from the region. Symmetry boundaries can be used to avoid modeling the entire region where appropriate, and so reduce calculation time.

As boundary types can affect the way in which the volume mesh is constructed, it is important to set them before generating the mesh.

Specifying Mesh Settings

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver uses the finite volume method to obtain an approximate solution to the underlying equations of fluid flow. This requires a mesh to be created, which represents the fluid volume as a collection of much smaller volumes known as cells.

A surface mesh is first created based on the boundaries defining the regions in the simulation. Thereafter a volume mesh is created to discretize the entire model.

The accuracy of the results is directly affected by mesh quality. If it is necessary to improve the quality of the mesh, some of the ways in which this can be done are to:

• Increase the mesh density, that is, the number of cells

• Add further sub-surface prism layers to capture near wall flow

• Refine the mesh in areas where flow characteristics are expected to change rapidly

As volume mesh quality is largely governed by the surface mesh quality, it is common practice to create and inspect the surface mesh before creating a volume mesh.

Defining Solution Controls

Solution controls determine the level of accuracy the solver will work towards. As a high accuracy solution will take longer, it may be necessary to compromise on this in order to obtain a result in a shorter time.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 includes five predefined solver settings ranging from fast (with low accuracy) to slow (with high accuracy). Advanced options are also available to provide further control.

Running the Case

When the simulation has been fully defined, the volume mesh is sent to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ along with all the necessary data for running the simulation. The time to complete a simulation will vary depending on the mesh density and solution controls.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 43

As the solver is running, residuals showing the rate at which individual equations are converging are shown in a plot. A scalar scene displaying absolute pressure is displayed on completion of the simulation.

Post-Processing the Results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Post-processing of simulations is carried out using the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ interface. This allows the results to be taken from the solver and displayed in a variety of scenes and plots.

Making Modifications to the Settings or Geometry

As Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 is completely integrated within the CATIA environment, it is very simple to perform parametric studies that examine the response of the fluid to changes in geometry. Once the first analysis is complete, the boundary conditions, run settings and all other properties of the CFD model are stored within the CAD file. Any changes in the flow field due to design changes can be recalculated by generating a new mesh and running the solver.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 44

Connecting to Remote Machines

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses a client-server architecture, and as such the CAD client ( Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5) and the server (Simcenter STAR-CCM+) are not required to run on the same machine.

Using an SSH (secure shell) connection, you can connect the client and server on two different machines, even when these are on different platforms. Due to how the CAD client and server interact in the background, the SSH connection must not ask for a username or a password.

There are two ways that you can connect Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and Simcenter STAR-CCM+, depending on what your starting point is:

• You can start from the CAD client and launch the server on a remote machine. This method is useful for transferring CAD geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 running on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on Linux.

• You can start from the server and connect to the CAD client on a remote machine. This method is useful for connecting to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 to update the CAD geometry. With this method, you can perform a Design Manager analysis on a cluster while the geometry is updated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Contents:

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Starting from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, you can choose to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on a remote machine.

Using this method, you can set up the full CAE analysis in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 on your local machine, and then run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on the remote machine. You can also choose to transfer your geometry from the CAD client to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. This feature is useful if you want to import geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 running on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on Linux.

To configure Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 to launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on a remote machine:

1. Make sure that you have a working SSH connection between the two machines.

For the SSH connection, you require an SSH server on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and an SSH client on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5. The SSH connection to the remote machine must not ask for a username or a password. To avoid possible issues with a connection that still requires a password, add -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=0 to the SSH command. Setting this argument to zero stops the connection prompting for a password when one is needed — something that could cause the process to hang. See SSH Command.

2. In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 ribbon, click Preferences.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 45

3. In the Preferences panel, set Server Settings to Remote.

4. Set the remaining settings for your connection to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. See Server

Settings Panel.

This information is used to build a command-line in the background when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 invokes Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

5. If you are going to connect to the same remote host in future sessions, click Save as Default Settings.

The next time Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 invokes Simcenter STAR-CCM+, the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server launches on the specified remote machine. A Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client is also launched on the local machine to allow you to see the active session on the remote machine.

Server Settings Panel

Server Settings Panel

Specify the connection settings to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server using the Server Settings pane.

Parameter Description

Server Host Type Specifies whether to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on the local host, or on a remote host.

Local Runs the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on the same host as Simcenter STAR-CCM + Client for CATIA V5.

Remote Runs the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on the remote host that you specify.

SSH Command Specifies the absolute path to the SSH program. If the path to the SSH program exists in your Path environment variable, you can leave this parameter as the default entry.

You can include additional arguments in the SSH Command. The connection must not ask for a password or a username. To avoid possible issues with a connection that requires a password, add -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=0 to the SSH command. Setting this argument to zero stops the connection prompting for a password when one is needed, something that could cause the process to hang.

Server Host Specifies the remote host. You can enter the name, fully qualified domain name, IP address, or path to the host, depending on how your network is set up.

Sim File Directory Specifies the absolute path to the directory where you want to save the simulation file on the remote host. You must have read and write access to this directory. If a simulation file is present in this directory, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ will use this file. If no file is found in this directory, a new one is created. An example directory on a Linux machine is shown below:

/users/linuxbox/james/documents/cadClientCases

Server Executable Specifies the full path to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ executable on the remote host. An example path is shown below:

[STAR-CCM+_INSTALL_DIR]/star/bin/starccm+

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 46

Parameter Description

Save as Default Settings

Saves the server settings that you specify in this panel as the default settings. Save these changes if you want to connect to the same remote server in future sessions.

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

Starting from Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you can connect to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 on a remote machine.

This feature is useful if you have previously transferred your geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on Linux, and you want to reconnect the two.

To connect Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on the local machine to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 running on a remote machine:

1. Make sure that you have a working SSH connection between the two machines.

For the SSH connection, you require an SSH server on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and an SSH client on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+. The SSH connection to the remote machine must not ask for a username or a password.

2. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, expand the Geometry > CAD Client Models > [Model_Name] and set CAD-Client Update Mode to Remote.

The Remote CAD Client Settings node appears.

3. Set the remaining parameters for the CAD geometry. See CAD Geometry Settings.

4. Select the Remote CAD Client Settings node and set the connection setting for the remote CAD client. See

Remote CAD Client Settings.

5. If you are connecting from a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server that is running on a cluster, activate the Use Proxy Server option and set up the proxy server. See Proxy Server Settings.

When you make changes to the imported CAD geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, the changes are passed back to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 on the remote machine and the geometry is transferred back into Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Defining Materials and Physics

Defining the physical properties of a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 model involves specifying the materials, flow characteristics, operating conditions, and physics models.

These definitions and settings are accomplished through the use of continua and regions, which are described in the following sections.

Contents:

Working with Continua and Regions

Importing Geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for Visualization

Working with Continua and Regions

Continua and regions are used together to capture the physical and material properties of a model.

A continuum represents a material in combination with a set of physics models that will be used to simulate the response of the material to the conditions imposed upon it. A continuum also provides the facility to define reference and initial values.

A region represents one or more volumes within the overall model, not necessarily contiguous, which will share the same continuum and set of boundary conditions. Regions are defined using CAD parts, and will be discretized by the volume mesher.

As well as holding a set of boundary conditions, regions can also be used to model specific physical behavior, including porous resistance, moving reference frames and energy sources.

Parts can be imported into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes without affecting the analysis.

Continua are assigned to single or multiple regions, which can contain single or multiple parts. In part mode, only one continuum and one region are available, as there is only one part. In assembly mode, new continua can be added to represent different materials present in the simulation, and new regions can be added to represent the parts composed of these materials. Continua and regions can be deleted if they are not required, although the simulation must always contain at least one of each.

There is a well defined relationship between continua, regions, boundary conditions and CAD parts.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 50

• Every region must be associated with a continuum.

• Several regions can be associated with the same continuum.

• Every CAD part must belong to a region.

• Several CAD parts can be associated with the same region.

• Boundary conditions belong to regions, and cannot be shared between regions.

• Every CAD surface must have a boundary condition associated with it. A default wall boundary is applied to CAD surfaces that have not been specifically associated with a user-defined boundary condition.

The following series of illustrations depict the relationship between CAD parts, continua, and regions, for a circular steel duct containing a rotating fan, and surrounded by a layer of insulation.

• Initially we have a collection of CAD parts in an assembly. These must be imprinted where appropriate to ensure that interfaces between parts can be created correctly.

• Three continua are required to represent the three different materials present in the simulation: the fluid (for example, air), the steel pipe, and the insulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 51

• Two regions are required for the fluid portion of the simulation, as a rotating part is defined by applying a rotating frame of reference to a separate region surrounding the fan blades. Further regions are required for each of the solid parts (the steel pipe and insulating layer), which means a total of four separate regions overall.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 52

• A clearer picture can be given of the fan blade itself.

For an analysis containing a single part, for example a fluid-only case involving fluid flow through a converging-diverging pipe, the model will only require one continuum and one region in order to fully define

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 53

the physical and material properties of the model. In this case, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 automatically assigns the default continuum to the default region, and no further assignments are necessary.

To define different materials and associated physics for use in an assembly, you require additional continua. In each continuum you can specify a unique set of properties, such as a different material type or temperature. In assembly mode, continua are stored under a Continua node, as shown below.

To create an additional continuum:

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Initialization Panel.

Specifying initial conditions that are close to the expected solution can reduce the number of iterations required to reach a solution. You can set the initial conditions similar to the inlet conditions of the fluid domain.

Initial conditions are specified at a continuum level; if no initial conditions are specified, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 will use default values to initialize the solution.

Setting Up Regions

Additional regions are required when modelling multiple region physics, or when specific behavior such as porous resistance is required for a particular part within the same continuum. Assign parts from an assembly to regions. You can control the properties of these regions through the assigned continuum.

In assembly mode, regions are stored under the Regions node in the object tree, as shown below.

To create an additional region:

1. Right-click the Regions manager node in the object tree and select Add Region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 60

The Region Settings dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 61

2. In the Name property, enter a name for the region.

3. Select the parts that you want to include in the region.

You can select multiple parts from the graphics window or the CATIA feature tree.

Selected parts appear in the Supports field.

4. Select a continuum to apply to the region.

All available continua are listed here.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 62

Note: Assigning a continuum to a region causes the region to inherit the physical and material properties defined in the continuum

5. Activate any additional region physics for the region:

◦ Porous. See Defining a Porous Region.

◦ Moving Reference Frame. See Defining a Moving Reference Frame.

◦ Energy Source. See Defining an Energy Source.

6. If you want to import parts into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes, but do not want the region to be included in the CFD calculations, activate the Exclude from Analysis option. See Importing Geometry into STAR-CCM+ for Visualization.

7. Click OK.

A new region is added to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 object tree under the Regions node.

The parts that you assign to a region define the geometric extent of the region. Within this geometry, properties and behavior of the material is governed by the physics models and material properties defined in the region and continuum settings.

Note: Each region must be assigned at least one part, otherwise it will be ignored during the CFD analysis.

By default, every Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 model contains one continuum, and this is automatically assigned to the default region and each additional region that you create. If multiple continua

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 63

are defined in the model, you can choose a different continuum to assign to each region. This enables you to control the physical properties of each region, including varying material types.

All the parts in an assembly are assigned to the default region (this is the initial region created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5). When you assign a part to another region, it is automatically removed from the default region. If you remove a part from a region, it is reassigned back to the default region.

Importing Geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for Visualization

You can import CAD parts, that do not form part of the analysis, into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes.

Add these parts to a separate region—this region is excluded from the analysis. This feature is useful for showing the original geometry in a post-processing scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. For example, for an internal fluid volume of a pipe, the original geometry is the solid pipe.

To exclude CAD parts from the analysis:

1. In the Region Settings dialog, add the CAD parts that you want to use for visualization purposes.

2. Activate the Exclude From Analysis checkbox in the Advanced panel.

3. Click OK.

When you run the case, a surface mesh is generated for this region using the settings specified in the Mesh Pipeline.

Note: As is the case for all assemblies, you must imprint all parts that are used for visualization purposes onto any surface that they cut, otherwise you will not be able to generate the surface mesh.

Setting Boundary Conditions

Boundary conditions tell the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers how the substance within the region interacts with its environment. A velocity inlet boundary, for example, tells the solvers that an amount of substance is being added to the fluid domain at a certain rate.

A Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 boundary is made up of one or more CAD surfaces within the simulation which, along with other boundaries, surround and define a region.

The boundary is discretized by the surface mesher, which is then used by the volume mesher to mesh the entire region.

It is important to set the boundary conditions before creating the volume mesh, as some parts of the volume mesh, such as prism layers, depend on the type of boundary.

By default, each region contains only one boundary. To define more boundaries you need to add boundaries to the region. You can modify the properties of existing boundaries by editing its boundary node.

Some boundaries may require the specification of turbulence quantities, temperature, and passive scalar concentration, depending on whether these modeling options have been activated in Continuum Settings.

Stagnation Inlet Boundary

The stagnation inlet boundary is an inlet condition that is well-posed for compressible flows, although it is equally valid for incompressible flows. The stagnation conditions refer to the conditions in an imaginary plenum, far upstream, in which the flow is completely at rest. The stagnation inlet settings are displayed below.

Property Description

Stagnation Flow Normal to Surface

i Specify the direction components for the flow.

Outlet Boundary

An outlet boundary splits the flow between multiple outlets using a fraction of the total mass flow through each of the outlet boundaries. The outlet panel settings are provided below.

Property Description

Split Ratio Specifies the ratio of the split as a value between 0 and 1. The sum of all the flow-split ratio values in a region must equal 1. If you only have one flow-split boundary in the simulation, all the flow is assumed to exit through this boundary.

A pressure boundary is a flow outlet boundary at which you specify the pressure. The pressure outlet panel settings are provided below.

Property Description

Symmetry Plane Boundary

A symmetry plane boundary represents an imaginary plane of symmetry in the simulation. The solution that is obtained with a symmetry plane boundary is identical to the solution that would be obtained by mirroring the mesh about the symmetry plane (in half the resulting domain). There are no settings which are specific to symmetry plane boundaries.

Rotating Specifies the wall as a rotating impenetrable surface.

Custom Boundary

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, there are additional boundary types to those available in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5. The custom boundary in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 acts as a placeholder for a boundary that you will customize in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Common Boundary Conditions

Some boundary conditions are not specific to any boundary type and appear in multiple boundaries, so long as the physics model that is associated with the condition is activated.

Common Boundary Conditions on Inlet and Pressure Outlet Boundaries

Temperature, turbulence, and passive scalar boundary conditions are common to all inlet boundaries as well as the Pressure Outlet boundary.

Property Description

Temperature Specifies the temperature on the boundary surface. You can change the units using the drop-down menu.

Turbulence Intensity Specifies the turbulence intensity on the boundary surface. You can change the units using the dropdown menu.

Turbulent Length Scale Specifies the turbulent length scale on the boundary surface. You can change the units using the dropdown menu.

Passive Scalar Specifies the amount of passive scalar crossing the boundary. You can change the units using the dropdown menu.

Boundary Conditions on Wall Boundaries

When the energy equation is being solved, you can specify the thermal specification on wall boundaries.

Property Description

Adiabatic Specifies that no transfer of energy occurs between the boundary surface and the surrounding environment.

Convection Specifies the transfer of energy between the boundary surface and the fluid moving over the boundary surface.

Meshing the Model

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 provides options for generating polyhedral or trimmed volume meshes, with or without near-wall prism layers.

By default, prism layers are generated on all wall surfaces. The provision of a prism layer depends on the type of boundary that is applied to a face. As a consequence, it is recommended that you only generate the mesh after setting up the boundaries and regions.

The meshing process first creates a triangulated surface (the surface mesh) and thereafter converts it to the desired volume mesh (polyhedral or trimmer). As the quality of the volume mesh depends to a large extent on the quality of the surface mesh, it is prudent to check the surface mesh before proceeding with the volume mesh.

Although the entire meshing process can be launched with a single command (the Build And Run command from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu), it is possible to execute only single stages from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Mesh menu. Settings that are made in the Mesh Pipeline node govern the mesh generation process.

A mesh pipeline contains all the settings that are applied to the surface and volume meshes created on the CATIA parts to which it is applied. In single part mode, only one mesh pipeline is available. In assembly mode, multiple mesh pipelines can be created if necessary.

When mesh generation commences, each mesh pipeline will:

1. Extract geometry from CATIA.

2. Transfer the model to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3. Execute the surface remesher.

4. Execute the polyhedral or trimmer volume mesher with the prism layer mesher (if selected).

5. Create a mesh representation in the CATIA Graphics window.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 80

Controls on the top-level mesh pipeline node allow you to set the base sizes for the surface mesh, and control the prism layer. Further refinement to specific faces, parts, or volume shapes can be made by adding additional controls to the mesh pipeline.

Creation of Additional Surfaces in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ creates geometry part surfaces during the geometry transfer stage.

Initially, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 creates one part surface for each face in the CAD model. These part surfaces are then combined so that one surface per boundary remains. This outcome, however, is not possible for boundaries that contain CAD surfaces from more than one part. The final part surfaces appear in the Geometry > Parts node in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

The following items affect the number of part surfaces that are created in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

• The number of boundaries present in the model, including the default boundary. Each boundary in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 appears as a separate part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If, however, a boundary contains CAD surfaces from multiple parts, the part surfaces in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ cannot be combined.

• The number of mesh pipeline controls used (if any). Each CAD surface that is used to define a face mesh control in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 appears as a separate part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• The number of interfaces that are created during the meshing process (for assemblies only). All the CAD surfaces that define one interface between two parts in an assembly are grouped together under one part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. One part surface exists for each interface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Boundary Splitting due to Interface Generation

Interfaces are automatically created between two parts in an assembly during the mesh generation. A new boundary is created for each interface on the surfaces that share the interface.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 81

Boundary Splitting due to Face Mesh Controls and Part Mesh Controls

If you use a face mesh control or a part mesh control in your simulation, some boundaries may be split, depending on what faces are included in the mesh control. If a boundary and mesh control share the same faces, no splitting occurs. If a mesh control contains faces from multiple boundaries, splitting occurs and a new boundary is created. The name of the new boundary is derived from the original boundary.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 82

Working with Mesh Pipelines

When working with a single part, you will only have one mesh pipeline defined in the model tree. This will specify the mesh settings for the single part available. In assembly mode, multiple mesh pipelines can be created to give specific controls for different parts, and parts must be specifically associated with a mesh pipeline.

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

The mesh pipeline node contains the general mesh settings that will apply to all Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 parts associated within the pipeline in the absence of any further controls.

To set up the mesh pipeline:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 tree and select Mesh Pipeline object > Definition.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 83

2. In the Name field, enter the name of the mesh pipeline if required.

3. In the Part Selection box, specify the desired parts to use in the mesh pipeline.

This property is only available when working with assemblies.

4. From the Mesh Type tab, select the type of mesh that you want to generate:

▶Polyhedral

▶Trimmer

5. Set Base Size to the desired value.

The base size is a reference length used in other meshing parameters. It may be set to equal the length of the largest triangle you expect to have on your surface mesh, or to some other characteristic dimension.

The base size can be set as either a relative or absolute value. When it is set as a relative value, the reference size will be the diagonal of the bounding box enclosing the entire geometry. In the case of multiple parts in an assembly, the reference size will be calculated based on the diagonal length of the bounding box enclosing the entire assembly. This includes all parts from all mesh pipelines. The unit specification menu will become active when setting an absolute value.

6. Set Surface Mesh Size to the desired value.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 85

The surface mesh size is the base edge length of triangles on the surface mesh. Note that the ultimate length of some (or all) triangles on the surface mesh will depend on other factors such as surface curvature and edge proximity.

7. Set the prism layer settings. See Prism Layer Panel.

8. Set the advanced settings. See Mesh Pipeline Advanced Settings Panel.

9. If you selected to generate a trimmed mesh, set the Trimmer settings. See Trimmer Panel.

10.Click OK.

The advanced settings panel provides further customization of meshing parameters.

Property Description

Relative Minimum Surface Size Defines the minimum triangle size permitted on a feature curve. The minimum triangle size is set as a percentage of the surface mesh size. The default value is set to 25%. You must set the relative minimum surface size to a value greater than zero. If you set the relative minimum surface size to 100%, Simcenter STARCCM+ will not modify the triangle size when it detects curvature.

The figure below illustrates this behavior. Note that the base size was set to 20% in this example to emphasize the refinement on the curve.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 87

Property Description

Having a large value for the number of points on a circle property increases the mesh resolution on curved surfaces.

The transition between the fine mesh and coarse mesh areas is controlled by the growth ratio.

Growth Ratio Controls the rate at which triangle sizes change when moving from one triangle size to another. In the example below, the end faces of the block were set to have a smaller triangle size than the four side faces of the block. When the growth ratio is set to a low value, the transition between triangle size is very gradual. When a higher value is used, the transition is far more rapid.

The growth factor must be set to a value greater than 1.0. There is no upper limit for the growth factor.

Number of Points per Circle Controls the number of triangle edges that appear on a curved surface, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 88

Property Description

Regardless of the number of points per circle defined, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 will not permit the triangle edge length to shrink below 25% of the base size. The curvature length scale may also affect the number of edges on a curved surface.

Trimmer Panel

The trimmer mesh is controlled using the Trimmer Mesh Settings panel.

Property Description

Default Growth Rate Controls the stepping of the refinement from one cell size to the next. Five settings are available. By default, the Default Growth Rate is set to Fast, meaning that the fastest transition from the smallest cell size to the largest will be used. This usually equates to having only one layer of each cell size for each transition, which will result in the least number of cells being created for the supplied input values. The Medium, Slow, and Very Slow options further slow the transition from one cell size to the next in the mesh interior and therefore increase the overall cell count. In general, the medium option results in a minimum of two equal sized cell layers per transition, slow in four layers and the very slow option in eight layers.

Boundary Growth Rate Controls the number of cell layers to grow next to surfaces in the template. Five settings are available. By default, the Boundary Growth Rate is set to None, meaning that the setting used for the Default Growth Rate is used for controlling all transitions. If the Very Slow, Slow, Medium, or Fast options are selected then it will result in eight, four, two or one layers of

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 89

Property Description

cells respectively of the same size being created next to the geometry surfaces in the template.

Working with Mesh Controls

Mesh controls allow you to define custom mesh settings for a particular section of the model.

Multiple controls can be assigned to the same item to control different mesh parameters. If, for example, a face has two mesh controls assigned to it--one that controls the mesh size and another that controls the prism layer thickness, the final mesh will respect both the custom mesh size and the custom prism layer thickness. If two mesh controls set the same mesh parameter, the control created last will take precedence over the first.

Using a Face Mesh Control

A face mesh control allows you to set the surface mesh size and the prism layer parameters on a face. Custom settings made on a face control will take priority over settings in the parent mesh pipeline, and over settings made in any part mesh controls.

To add a face mesh control:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline > Mesh Controls node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 tree and select Add Face Mesh Control.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

The Face Mesh Control Settings dialog appears.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 91

2. Set Name to an appropriate value.

3. On the CAD geometry, select the desired faces to include in this mesh control.

4. If you want to specify a custom surface mesh size on the selected surfaces, activate the Custom Mesh Size option.

a) Set Mesh Size to the desired value.

You can enter this value as a percentage of the base size, or as an absolute value. If you select to enter the absolute value, you can select the units from the drop-down menu.

5. Set Prism Layer Custom Settings to the desired value:

▶Inherit Values: in the first instance, the face(s) will be assigned values from any part mesh control applied to the part to which the face(s) belong. If this does not apply, values will be taken from any applicable volumetric mesh control, and in the absence of this values will be taken from the parent mesh pipeline.

▶Use Custom Values: allows the prism layer parameters to be set directly on the face(s). See Prism Layer

Panel.

▶Disable: no prism layer will be generated on the face(s).

6. Click OK.

Using a Volumetric Mesh Control

A volumetric control permits mesh refinement within a user-defined box or sphere. Only the mesh size can be modified with a volumetric control; prism layer parameters are not affected.

To add a volumetric mesh control:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline > Mesh Controls node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 tree and select Add Volumetric Control.

The mesh size defines the triangle edge length for surface mesh within the volume shape, and the characteristic cell size for volume mesh. The custom mesh size will still affect the volume mesh in cases where the volume shape does not intersect any surfaces of the Pro/E geometry.

The mesh size can either be defined relative to the base size of the parent mesh pipeline, or as an absolute dimension with length units.

Meshing Behavior at Interfaces

The volume mesher will treat interfaces between two regions differently depending on what type of region (fluid or solid) these are.

If the interface lies between two fluid regions, no prism layers will be grown from both sides of the interface. If an interface lies between a solid region and a fluid region, prism layers will be grown from the interface. The default behavior of the prism layer generation can be overridden using a mesh control, so prism layers can be disabled on a solid-fluid interface. See Working With Mesh Controls.

There may be instances when the mesh generation fails. In most cases this will occur during the surface meshing phase. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 will try and identify the cause and suggest ways of rectifying this. This information will be printed in the Output tab of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 Info App window.

Setting Solution Controls

The solution you obtain from the solvers is a compromise between accuracy and processing time. You can manage the speed and accuracy of the solver from the Solution Controls dialog. The solution accuracy is also dependant on the mesh density.

To set up the solution controls in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5:

1. Either:

Siemens Digital Industries Software 105

2. Set the solution control parameters:

▶Using the slider, select one of the five pre-defined solver options. These options range from high accuracy and low speed, to low accuracy and high speed.

▶Click More... and set the solution control parameters manually. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings

Panel.

3. If you want to run a Java macro with the simulation, activate the Use Java File option. See Using Java

Macros with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

4. Click OK.

Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel

Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel

The advanced settings in the Solution Control dialog allow you to manually enter the values for the solution control parameters.

Parameter Description

Stopping Criteria

Iterations Specifies the maximum number of iterations for which the solver can run. When the Simcenter STARCCM+ solver reaches the specified number of

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 106

Parameter Description

iterations, it will stop. You can then post-process the results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Convergence Levels.

Convergence Specifies how many orders of magnitude the residuals should drop before the solver stops. See Convergence Levels.

Solution Accuracy

First Order This option is generally the quicker, but less accurate solver option. The first order scheme introduces a dissipative error that is stabilizing and helps the solver achieve robust convergence. However, it can also lead to the neglect and merging of discontinuities, meaning the solution is not fully captured.

Second Order This option is generally the more accurate, but slower solver option. The second order scheme attempts to minimize both dispersive and dissipative errors, providing a better representation of the simulation. However, in some situations, the lack of numerical dissipation can result in poorer convergence properties.

It is common practice to use the first order scheme initially to ensure the simulation is running as expected and then switch to second order.

Under-Relaxation Factors

Momentum Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the momentum equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

Pressure Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the pressurecorrection equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

Turbulence Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the turbulence equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

Fluid Temperature Specifies the fluid under-relaxation factor for the segregated energy solver. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

Solid Temperature Specifies the solid under-relaxation factor for the segregated energy solver. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 107

Convergence Level

The numerical method used by the solver requires an iterative process in order to obtain a solution. After each iteration, residuals are produced that indicate how well the governing equations for each solver quantity are being satisfied numerically. In general, the residual magnitude should decrease as the solution converges. When the magnitude of the residuals for all the quantities falls below the convergence level, the solver will stop iterating, and results will be exported for post-processing.

Note: In most cases, a drop of 3-5 orders of magnitude in the residuals is sufficient to obtain an accurate solution.

You can adjust the convergence level parameter to meet accuracy or process time requirements. However, if the residuals are no longer decreasing from one iteration to the next, it is likely that machine accuracy has been reached for that case. For a case that does not exhibit decreasing residuals, it would be necessary to reconsider the setup in case the volume mesh is too coarse, or boundary conditions have been set incorrectly.

Under-Relaxation Parameters

Under-relaxation parameters determine how quickly the solver reaches a solution for a particular equation, on a scale from 0 to 1, with 1 being the fastest.

Ideally, all under-relaxation parameters would be set to 1, however, doing so would likely cause solver instability due to the complex nature of most simulations. Hence the under-relaxation parameters should be set to values that compromise speed with stability.

Note: Adjust the under-relaxation parameters if changes to other solution controls such as Number of Iterations, Convergence Levels, and Solution Accuracy have failed to improve the behavior of the solver.

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

You can use Java macros with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to automate your simulation or to change a setting in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as selecting an alternative turbulence model, before the solver starts running.

An example of how to change a setting in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using a Java macro is outlined below:

1. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and set up the case.

Define the continuum settings, boundary conditions, mesh settings, and solution control settings.

2. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, start recording a macro and perform the desired operations, such as changing the physics models.

4. Stop recording the macro.

The macro saves at this point.

5. Close Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and do not save the simulation.

6. Return to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, open the Solution Controls dialog and activate the Use Java File checkbox.

A text entry field appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 108

7. Click Select Input File.

The Open dialog appears.

8. Navigate to your Java macro file and select it.

Selected files appear in the text entry field. The path in the entry field is displayed relative to the current CAD geometry file.

9. Click OK.

When you run the simulation, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ will launch and play the macro before starting the solver. This sequence allows you to set up and use additional Simcenter STAR-CCM+ physics models that are not available in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 monitors the active case for any errors in real-time and displays a
