Three areas are monitored by the live model checker:

• Continua. The continua checker makes sure that all necessary boundaries are present in the case, such as the presence of at least one inlet and one outlet.

• Regions and boundaries. The regions and boundaries checker covers issues specific to boundaries, such as a velocity inlet boundary having a zero value.

• Mesh pipelines. The mesh pipeline checker covers issues that are related to the mesh, such as the presence of multiple parts in a trimmed mesh pipeline.

Building and Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

Once you have defined the model physics, boundary conditions, mesh settings, and solver settings in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, you can build and run the case.

To build and run the case:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, select Solution > Build and Run.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 112

This action automatically generates the mesh, and runs the solver. When you run the solver, a new Residuals tab is added to the Info App dialog. You can use this residuals plot to monitor solution convergence. When the solver finishes, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and a scalar scene is automatically created for you.

Note: If a solution has already been computed in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, and the stopping criteria has been reached, clicking Build and Run clears the solution and starts running from the first iteration. If you want to run for more iterations, change the stopping criteria and click Run Solver, or click Run More Iterations.

Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5

If you have already generated a volume mesh for the model, you can run the case directly.

To run the solver:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, select Solution > Run Solver.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 113

Running for More Iterations

You may need to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers for more iterations than you originally set in the Number of Iterations stopping criterion. The Run More Iteration function runs the solver for an additional number of iterations as specified in the stopping criteria. Take, for example, a case where you have already run the simulation for 300 iterations. You specify 500 iterations in the Number of Iterations stopping criterion. When you next click Run for More Iterations, the simulation will run for 500 extra iterations, making 800 iterations in total. The solver runs until one of the stopping criteria is satisfied.

To run for more iterations:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, select Solution > Run for More Iterations in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu.

Clearing the Solution

You can clear all results that were calculated by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers using the Clear Solution function. All other Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 simulation settings remain intact.

Caution: This action is irreversible.

To clear the solution:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, select Solution > Clear Solution.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 114

The solution that was calculated by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers is deleted.

Visualizing the Solution

When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches after the solution is calculated, it automatically displays a scalar scene of the model that shows the Absolute Pressure field function.

To visualize the results, you can use this scene to display different scalar quantities, or use any of the other visualization tools in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as streamlines, plane sections and vector scenes.

You can import CAD parts into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes. These parts will not be taken into account during the analysis. This feature is useful for displaying the original geometry in a post-processing scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Importing Geometry Into STAR-CCM+ for Visualization.

Setting Up Sensors

You can define sensors on boundaries in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5. A sensor is an object that can be used to monitor solution data that is created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+. The sensor creates a CATIA parameter which can then be used within optimization loops.

Defining Sensors

You can create a sensor either before or after running a case. If you create it before running the case, the sensor will be evaluated when the case is run. If you create it after running the case, you will need to update the sensor.

To create a sensor:

1. Right-click Sensors.1 in the object tree and select Create CFD Sensor.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 115

The Create CFD Sensor dialog appears.

2. Select the type of report and the quantity to monitor.

3. Click Add.

A sensor object is created and added to the object tree.

Note: You can create multiple objects by clicking Add multiple times.

4. Click OK to close the dialog.

The sensor object contains an ! icon. This icon indicates that the sensor definition is incomplete.

5. Double click the sensor to edit it.

The Sensor Properties dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 116

6. Rename the sensor to something more appropriate in the Sensor Name property.

7. Select the boundaries that you want to associate with the sensor from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 object tree.

8. Click OK.

The sensor icon in the object tree will show if it requires an update. The sensor will be evaluated when the case is run or when an update is requested.

Updating Sensors

To update the sensor:

1. Right-click on the sensor in the object tree and select Update Sensor.

2. Click OK to dismiss the warning dialog.

The data for the sensor is calculated and a new report sub-node is added to the sensor.

Note: The units that are used in the sensor are CATIA working units, not Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 units.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 117

Viewing the Sensor Data

To view the sensor data after the solver has finished running:

The Edit Parameter dialog appears, displaying the report value.

2. Rename the report.

3. Click OK to close the report.

Working with Parameters

You can use CATIA’s formula editor to add numerical data together. You can find this feature in CATIA’s Knowledge toolbar.

To create a formula:

The Formulas dialog appears.

Exporting the Surface Mesh

You can export the surface mesh generated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 as a native CD-adapco surface mesh (.dbs) file. The .dbs file format is the recommended format to use when transferring surface data between CD-adapco programs, which are now part of Siemens. The boundary names and boundary types are retained by the file, as well as the interfaces that were automatically created between regions.

Exporting the Volume Mesh

You can export the volume mesh that you generated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 as a native CD-adapco volume mesh (.ccm) file. The .ccm file format is the recommended format to use when transferring volume meshes between CD-adapco programs, which are now part of Siemens. Guidelines

This section aims to provide guidance and assistance on making a geometry part suitable for CFD analysis using Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Contents:

Creating the Fluid Domain

Creating the Fluid Domain

In the majority of CAD models, the fluid domain for analysis must be extracted from the original part or assembly. The topics that are containing within this section demonstrate how to prepare the fluid domain.

Contents:

Internal Flow

External Flow

Multi Region Flow

Internal Flow

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for an internal flow are:

• Work in a product. If the original geometry contains only a single part, create a new product that contains the part.

• Create additional parts that close off any openings in the original geometry, we will call these parts the “caps”.

• Create an overall block part that encloses all the other parts, the “enclosure”. This will form the internal fluid volume.

• Subtract all parts from the enclosure. This will result in a solid block that contains a cavity.

• Delete the outer solid body--the remaining geometry is the fluid domain.

A worked example is provided below. In this case the assembly contains two parts: the valve (shown in red), and the valve housing (shown in blue).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 128

1. Load the part or product into CATIA. If the geometry is a part, add it to a product.

2. Insert a new part into the assembly by selecting Insert > New Part.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 129

3. Click on the root node in the assembly’s specification tree to insert the part into that assembly.

A dialog will appear asking whether a new origin for this part should be defined or not. Choose either option.

4. Give the new part an appropriate name, in this example the part is called Caps.

We will now close all the openings on the geometry--in this example two caps are needed as there are two openings.

5. Make the Caps part the active part by double-clicking on its Part Body node in the Specification Tree.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 130

The part will become active and the Part Design workbench appears. When parts are active these will be highlighted with a blue background in the specification tree.

6. Create a new sketch on a surface that contains an opening, as shown below.

7. In the Sketcher workbench, select the outermost edge of the face

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 131

8. Use the Project 3D Elements tool.

This will project the edge of the existing body onto the current sketch. The yellow color of the sketch means that it is associative, so if the diameter of the part changes, for example, the cap will automatically update to match the change.

9. Exit the Sketcher workbench and create a Pad from the sketch.

The length of the pad is not important, however ensure that the pad extends away from the geometry. If the pad is going inwards, use the Reverse Direction button in the Pad Definition dialog. In this example a Length of 5 mm is sufficient.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 132

The result of this operation is shown below.

10.Repeat the same steps for the other opening(s).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 133

Note that all the caps should be in the same part.

11.Double-click the root node in the specification tree to return to the Assembly Design workbench.

We will now insert a new part into the product. This part will become a composite of all the current parts, in this example the valve, the valve body, and the caps.

12.Insert a new part into the product as described previously. Give this new part a suitable name. In this example, the part was named Composite Part.

13.Double-click on the part file to activate it, as shown below.

14.Expand the nodes for all the parts to reveal the PartBody nodes and select them as shown below.

Hold down the <ctrl> key to select multiple items.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 135

15.Right-click on one of the highlighted PartBody nodes and select Copy.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 136

16.Paste these into the active Composite Part by right-clicking on it’s PartBody node as shown below, and selecting Paste Special...

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 137

The Paste Special dialog appears.

17.In the Paste Special dialog, select As Result With Link and click OK.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 138

This will paste all the selected parts into the active part without breaking the link to the original parts, meaning that if the original parts change, the pasted parts will also change--this is useful when analyzing different configurations in the product such as valve angle in this example.

The original parts are no longer required and will be hidden.

18.Return to the Assembly Design workbench by double-clicking on the root node in the specification tree.

19.Select the valve, valve body, and caps parts in the specification tree. Right-click on one of the nodes and select Hide/Show.

The parts’ nodes will become greyed out indicating they are hidden.

We will now insert a new part into the product. This will ultimately become the internal fluid volume. To begin with, we will create an enclosure that completely encloses the existing parts. The caps and valve assembly will then be subtracted from the enclosure which will result in two solid bodies, the outer enclosure and the internal fluid volume. The outer enclosure will then be deleted, leaving only the desired internal fluid volume.

20.Insert a new part into the assembly as described previously and rename it to Fluid Region.

21.Activate the Fluid Region part by double-clicking on it.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 139

22.Create a sketch on the top view plane.

23.Draw a rough sketch that encloses the entire assembly as shown below.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 141

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 144

This will remove the Composite Part from the Fluid Region using a boolean operation. The result will be a cavity. In the Remove dialog, ensure that the three parts from the Composite Part are listed in the Remove field and that the From field contains the Fluid Region’s PartBody as shown below.

28.Click OK to close the dialog.

The Fluid Region part now contains a cavity separating the internal fluid volume from the bulk solid.

29.Hide the Composite Part.

The outer bulk solid will be removed using the Remove Lump operation, resulting in only the internal fluid volume.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 145

30.Select Insert > Boolean Operations > Remove Lump.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 146

The face has to be a wetted face, such as the inside surface of the valve housing. To select hidden surfaces use <Ctrl> + <F11>.

34.Click OK to close the dialog.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 147

The internal fluid volume will appear as shown below.

The geometry is now ready for the CAD client analysis. Deactivated parts in an assembly will not be included in the analysis. Suppressed parts in an assembly will not be included in the analysis. In the above example, it is recommended that you extend the inlet and outlet regions to appropriate lengths so that a fully developed flow can be achieved before reaching the valve and to help reduce recirculation at the outlet.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

External Flow

The generation of a domain for external aerodynamics is generally easier than for internal flow cases but the sizing of the domain is more critical. As a guideline (assuming a specific situation is not being modelled i.e. flow in a wind tunnel) the domain should be sized as follows:

• Inlet: 2 x part length from the front of the part

• Outlet: 4 x part length from the rear of the part

• Sides: 3 x part width from the side of the part

• Ceiling: 4 x part height from the top of the part

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for an external flow are:

• Work in an assembly. If the original geometry contains only a single part, create a new assembly that contains the part.

• Create an overall block part that encloses all the other parts. The shape and size should correspond to the desired fluid domain.

• Subtract all parts from the overall block part - the remaining geometry is the fluid domain.

An example case is shown below. In this example a geometry of a car will be used.

1. Load the product file in CATIA. If the geometry is a part, insert it into a product.

2. If the part is symmetrical, this should be cut in half, as shown below, to reduce computational costs during the analysis.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 149

We will now insert a new part into the product. This will become the fluid domain.

3. Insert a new part into the product, Insert > New Part.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 150

4. Click on the Assembly root node in the specification tree to insert the part into the product. A dialog will appear asking whether a new origin should be defined for the part or not--you may choose either option.

5. Create a new sketch on any plane. In this example the sketch was created on the symmetry plane of the car.

6. Draw a profile with suitable dimensions--this sketch represents the profile of the fluid domain.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 151

7. Exit the Sketcher workbench and create a Pad from the sketch.

The length of the pad will correspond to the width of the fluid domain, as shown below.

We will now remove the car from the fluid domain using a boolean operation.

8. Select Insert > Boolean Operations > Remove...

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 152

9. In the Remove dialog that appears, select the car’s part body for the Remove field and the fluid domain for the From field.

10.Return to the assembly after the operation is complete and hide the car part, right-click the car node in the specification tree and select Show/Hide.

The area around the car in the final domain is shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 153

The geometry is now ready for the cad client analysis. Deactivated parts are not included in the analysis. If you make any changes to the car geometry, these will automatically be passed on to the fluid region, giving you an up-to-date fluid domain.

Multi Region Flow

This section shows how to create the fluid domain for multiple regions such as rotating machinery and porous media flow.

For the numerical assumptions made using the Moving Reference Frame (MRF) technique to hold true, a minimum of two cells need to be present between the rotating-static interface and any wall boundaries (for example the fan blades), and the rotating region must be circular in section. Where there is a large clearance between the rotating object and any static objects, it is advisable to avoid placing the interface too close to either hence facilitating a small cell size on the interface. Where there is a small clearance between the rotating and static parts, there is little choice but to place the interface approximately midway between the two.

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for multiple regions are:

• Work in an assembly. If the original geometry contains only a single part, create a new assembly that contains the part.

• Create an additional part that will enclose the rotating region (for example a fan) and subtract it from the part. In the case of a porous region, a separate part will be required for this as well.

• Create an additional part for the main static domain (the inlet and outlet regions) and subtract any obstructions/features that may be present there (for example the fan motor support arms on a fan casing).

In this example, a fan and fan case are used.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 154

1. Load the assembly in CATIA.

We will now insert a new part into the product. This will form the rotating region of the fluid domain.

2. Insert a new part into the assembly, Insert > New Part.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 155

3. Click on the Assembly node in the feature tree to insert the part into the assembly.

A dialog will pop up asking whether a new origin should be defined or not. Choose either option.

4. Rename the new part by right-clicking on it in the feature tree and selecting Properties.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 156

In the Properties dialog enter an appropriate name for the new part (in this case it will be called Rotating Region) and click OK to close the dialog.

5. Double-click the Rotating Region part body.

The part will become active and the Part Design workbench appears. When parts are active the part node will be highlighted in blue.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 157

6. Hide the fan casing, right-click on the feature tree or on the geometry and select Hide/Show.

7. Create a sketch on the contact face of the fan casing (where the fan and the fan casing are coincident).

If the part is a native CATIA geometry then this will be possible by simply clicking on the desired face, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 158

If the part is an imported geometry, a new plane will need to be created on the desired face before a sketch can be created.

8. Create a circle with the same center point as the fan casing - the diameter of the circle is not important at this stage as it will be made coincident with the fan casing in the next step.

9. Select the circle (shown in orange) and the inner-most edge on the fan casing (shown in red).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 159

13.Hide the fan casing part and show the fan part (using the Show/Hide option).

14.Create a pad from the sketch so that it encloses the fan, as shown below.

The fan can be visualized by changing the view to Shading with Edges and Hidden Edges

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 161

We will now remove the fan from this new pad using a boolean operation.

15.Change the view to Shaded with Edges.

16.Select Insert > Boolean Operations > Remove....

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 162

17.In the Remove dialog, select the fan part (from the feature tree) for the Remove field and the pad for the From field as shown below.

22.Enter the sketch workbench and select the front face of the Rotating Region.

23.Select the outermost edge of the face

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 164

24.Use the Project 3D Elements tool.

This will project the selected edge from the existing body onto the current sketch. The yellow color of the sketch means that it is associative, so if the diameter of the part changes (for example), the sketch will automatically update to match the change.

Imprinting Parts

Most CAD model assemblies are not suitable for meshing as the parts in the assembly are disjointed, where the coincident faces are overlapping. Attempting to generate a mesh with such an assembly will result in a meshing error. To rectify this problem, the parts in an assembly must be imprinted together.

Imprinting can also be used to split surfaces for boundary region applications. An example of such an application would be to model the area that a fan would occupy on the inside of computer case, such as in the third Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 tutorial, where a smaller section of the surface is needed to represent the fan, rather than the entire inner surface of the computer case.

Contents:

Imprinting Parts in an Assembly

Imprinting Surfaces on Parts for Boundary Region Applications

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 171

Imprinting Parts in an Assembly

In cases containing multiple adjacent parts, such as in Conjugate Heat Transfer cases, it is essential to imprint the profiles of the coincident faces of the smaller parts onto the face of the larger part. This will ensure that the volume mesh created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ contains interfaces between the adjacent parts.

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for multiple regions are:

• Work within the product, making the part that requires imprinting the work part.

• Extract the contact surfaces from the other components in the product.

• Sew the extracted surfaces onto the face you want to imprint.

The simple circuit board shown below requires imprinting before the mesh can be generated.

1. Load the product file in CATIA.

In this example, the green circuit board needs to be imprinted.

2. Right-click Base Board and select Define in Work Object.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 172

3. Switch to the Generative Shape Design workbench, by clicking on Start > Shape > Generative Shape Design.

4. Hide the base board by right-clicking on it in the specification tree and select Hide/Show.

5. Select all the contact faces on the other parts in the product, holding down the <Ctrl> key.

In this example the bottom surfaces of the capacitors and heat sinks are selected.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 173

We will now extract the selected faces.

6. Click on the Extract button.

Highlighting multiple faces before using the Extract function will automatically perform the same operation for each selection. If the Extract function was used first this would only allow one face to be selected at a time.

7. Switch back to the Part Design workbench, Mechanical Design > Part Design.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 174

8. Show the circuit board and hide the capacitors and heat sinks. The extracted faces will appear in yellow and overlap the existing top face of the circuit board.

We will now sew the extracted surfaces onto the face that we want to imprint.

9. Use the Sew function to sew one of the extracted surfaces to the base board.

Ensure that the Simplify Geometry option in the Sew Surface Definition dialog is cleared.

Also note that the sew direction arrow should be pointing towards the surface of the body to be sewn.

10.Repeat the same steps for the other extracted surfaces.

The base board face is imprinted with the contact edges of the capacitors and heat sinks, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 175

A high quality mesh with fully defined interfaces can now be successfully generated for this assembly. Deactivated parts are not included in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ analysis, so for CHT cases, such as the above example, ensure that all relevant parts are active.

Imprinting Surfaces on Parts for Boundary Region Applications

Faces in a part body can be split into smaller faces for boundary application.

The general procedure to follow is:

• Create a sketch on the surface you want to split. The shape of the sketch should correspond to the shape of the new face after it is split.

• Fill the sketch so that is becomes a surface.

• Sew the surface onto the face that requires imprinting.

A simple example of an aeration tank is shown below. The image shows the tank, the two air injectors need to be imprinted onto the base of the tank.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 176

1. Load the geometry part into CATIA.

2. Create a sketch on the face that requires imprinting.

In this case the air injectors are sketched onto the tank’s bottom face.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 177

3. Switch to the Generative Shape Design workbench, by clicking on StartShape > Generative Shape Design.

4. Use the Fill tool to create surfaces from the sketch profiles.

The Fill Surface Definition dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 178

5. Select the sketch that contains the profiles you want to imprint.

6. Click OK.

7. In the Multi-Result Management dialog, select the keep all the sub-elements radio button and click OK.

The sketches are now filled in with a planar surface as shown below.

8. Switch back to the Part Design workbench, Mechanical Design > Part Design.

9. Use the Sew function to sew the surfaces to the bottom face of the tank.

Ensure that the Simplify Geometry option in the Sew Surface Definition dialog is cleared.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 179

Also note that the sew direction arrow should be pointing towards the surface of the body to be sewn.

10.Hide the fill feature and the sketch on the feature tree by right-clicking and selecting Show/Hide.

The base of the tank is now imprinted with the air injector profiles. Selecting the bottom face shows that the injectors are now separate faces that can be selected independently from each other.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 180

The separate faces can now be defined as boundary regions.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Aircraft Wing Deicing System

This tutorial takes you through the steps that are required to run a CFD calculation in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 environment.

For this tutorial, the model is a modern deicing system that is used on aircraft wings. The hot air from the aircraft’s jet engine is used to heat the leading edge of the wing.

To download the tutorials bundle, go to https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/product/226870983/downloads, and follow the procedure outlined in the main STAR-CCM+ > Tutorials > Using Tutorial Macros and Files > Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal section of the user guide.

1. Copy the directory to your own disk space and open the part file piccoloAssem.CATProduct in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

See Launching STAR-CAT5.

The assembly is made up of two parts: the solid leading edge wing skin, and the internal air region.

2. Position the geometry as shown below.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu appears at the top of the screen.The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 object tree is located on the left of the screen.

Selecting Fluid Physics Models

The first step in setting up this tutorial is to modify the physics continuum that is used to model air. For this case, the flow is turbulent and thermal. Temperature calculations are on by default in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5.

Modify the initial conditions:

1. Right-click the Continua > Continuum node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 tree and select Continuum object > Definition....

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. Set Name to Air.

3. Set the Equation of State to Ideal Gas.

4. Click the Initialization tab.

5. Set Temperature to 400 K.

6. Click OK to close the dialog.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 231

Adding Solid Physics Models

The next step in setting up this tutorial is to define the physics continuum of the solid to be used.

1. Right-click the Continua node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 object tree and select Add Continuum.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. Set Name to Al.

3. Set Material to Solid and select Aluminum Alloy from the list.

4. Click the Initialization tab.

5. Set Temperature to 400 K.

6. Click OK.

Building and Running

The case is now ready to run.

Post-Processing Results

You perform all post-processing in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. By default, a scalar scene, Scalar Scene 1, automatically appears in the Graphics window when the solver finishes. This scene displays the absolute total pressure.

The results that are contained in the following sections are representative. You may see some variation in the results that you obtain, depending on what platform and package you are using.

Rotating Flow Inside a Graphics Card

This tutorial takes you through the steps that are required to run a CFD calculation in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 environment.

For this tutorial, the model is a fully sealed graphics card that is located inside an empty, idealized PC tower case. The geometry that is used in this tutorial has been simplified in order to decrease the computational cost. As a consequence the mesh is relatively coarse at approximately 200,000 cells compared to the 3-4 million cells used for an industrial analysis.

Geometry Transfer: CAD to Simulation

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 allows you to transfer geometry from CATIA to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ through a direct link between the two packages.

This feature provides you with a workflow that is tailored to design optimization. You can apply changes to the geometry in either Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and the changes are passed back to the other program. For example, you can make changes to the design after running an analysis in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ environment and these changes are passed back to the original CATIA file. This feature requires a CAD client license.

This tutorial demonstrates how to select the CAD parameters in your original geometry and transfer the geometry from CATIA to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you proceed to create a repeatable workflow (or pipeline) using mesh operations. After setting up this pipeline, you can make further changes to the geometry design and have STAR-CCM+ regenerate the corresponding volume mesh.

Contents:

Opening the CAD Model

Transferring the Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Creating the Shape Parts and Operations

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Modifying the Design

Opening the CAD Model

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation includes a directory containing the CAD geometry for this tutorial.

This directory is located in the starcat5 folder of the downloaded tutorials bundle. To download the tutorials bundle, go to https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/product/226870983/downloads, and follow the procedure outlined in the main STAR-CCM+ > Tutorials > Using Tutorial Macros and Files > Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal section of the user guide.

1. Copy the directory to your own disk space.

2. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 and open the product file cardAssem.CATProduct.

See Launching STAR-CAT5.

The assembly is made up of two parts: the card housing and the blower fan.

3. Position the geometry as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 318

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu appears at the top of the screen. The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 object tree is located on the left of the screen.

4. Save the analysis as cardAssem.CATAnalysis.

Transferring the Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5, choose the CAD parameters to expose to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and then transfer the geometry.

Specify the CAD parameters to transfer to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, click Design Data.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 319

The Design Data dialog appears.

2. In the CAD Parameters tab, select blowerFan\PartBody\CircPattern.1\AngularNumber.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 only recognizes native CAD features as CAD parameters.

The value of this parameter is displayed in the Parameter Value property.

3. Activate the Transfer to STAR-CCM+ option.

4. Click OK.

Transfer the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

5. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 menu, select Transfer Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and the CAD geometry is transferred over.

6. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, create a geometry scene and position the geometry as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 320

7. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, expand the Geometry node.

The transferred geometry appears under the Parts node. The properties that control the connection back to CATIA, including the CAD parameter value, appear under the CAD Client Models node.

When transferring geometry from CATIA to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, a link exists between the two software packages. This link allows data to be transferred between the two packages. To maintain this link, you must first save the geometry file in CATIA:

8. Switch to CATIA and save the geometry file.

In response, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ saves the simulation file with the name of the CATIA geometry file. Using this technique, you can rename or relocate both the geometry and simulation files without breaking the link between the two packages. You can also save the simulation file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ so long as you do not rename it or relocate it. Doing so will break the link between the packages.

Creating the Shape Parts and Operations

The transferred geometry consists of the card housing and the blower fan. To simulate this case, you require two regions: one static region that provides an enclosure for the simulation, and another for the rotating region around the fan.

The transferred geometry contains the solid parts. You require the fluid volume around these parts. The first stage in obtaining the fluid volume is to create part shapes that correspond to the two regions. To save time, you are provided with these part shapes, one for the enclosure, and another for the rotating region.

Import the shape parts:

1. Select File  > Import > Import Surface Mesh.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for CATIA V5 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 321

2. Import the part shapes:

a) In the Open dialog, navigate to the directory that you downloaded in the first section of this tutorial and select box.x_t and disc.x_t.

b) Click Open.

c) In the Import Surface Options dialog, deactivate the Open Geometry Scene After Import option.

d) Click OK.

The static region, box, is shown below in relation to the graphics card:

The rotating region, disc, is show below in relation to the graphics card:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Add-on provides you with straightforward access to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver from within the NX environment.

Standard physics models, including turbulence, ideal gas, heat transfer, and gravity are supported for single body cases. Multiple body simulations involving conjugate heat transfer, rotating reference frames, and porous media are also supported. Advanced physics models can be added to the simulation by either launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and selecting them directly, or by implementing additional Java macro commands.

This section contains the user guide and tutorials for the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX CAD client.

Introducing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX provides you with straightforward access to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver from within the NX environment.

Standard physics models, including turbulence, ideal gas, heat transfer, and gravity are supported for single body cases. Multiple body simulations involving conjugate heat transfer, rotating reference frames, and porous media are also supported. Advanced physics models can be added to the simulation by either launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and selecting them directly, or by implementing additional Java macro commands.

Contents:

What are the Capabilities?

Getting Started

Common Functions

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on Different Machines

See Also:

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

What are the Capabilities?

This section highlights the capabilities of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX enables you to:

• Define flow characteristics for the simulation

• Specify mesh parameters and controls

• Execute the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX, with specified solution controls

• Post-process results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

• Use parallel processing

Problem Definition

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX provides an interface for the specification of continua, regions, and boundaries in order to define the CFD simulation. This information is then used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to calculate a solution and present results.

The particular solver options that you can currently select through the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX interface include:

• Turbulence

◦ k-e Model

◦ Laminar

• Temperature

◦ Thermal Modelling

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 4

◦ Conjugate Heat Transfer

• Equation of State

◦ Constant Density

◦ Ideal Gas

• Porous Media

◦ Isotropic

◦ Uni-Directional

• Moving Reference Frames

• Energy Source

• Gravity

• Passive Scalar

Meshing

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX provides you with a transparent interface to Simcenter STAR-CCM+’s surface and volume meshing tools. This allows you to generate high-quality meshes using a solid model that was built within the NX environment. The specific meshing functionality includes:

• Surface meshing using the surface remesher for optimum mesh quality

• Prismatic subsurface meshing in the volume mesh for capturing near-wall boundary layers

• Volume meshing of parts with either:

◦ Tetrahedral core mesh generation

◦ Polyhedral core mesh generation

◦ Trimmed hexahedral core mesh generation

• Automatic handling of region-to-region interfaces

Running the Solver

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX allows the generation of solutions with varying accuracy and speed by providing the following solver controls:

• Number of iterations

• Stopping criterion at which to assume convergence

• Discretization scheme (1st or 2nd order)

• Solver under-relaxation factors

• Additional commands using Java macros

Post-processing

As post-processing is carried out in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, a wide range of tools are available for analysis. These include:

• Scalar scenes

• Vector scenes

• Streamlines

• Isosurfaces

• Plane sections

• Reports

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 5

• Plots

Parallel Processing

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX supports parallel processing for mesh generation and solver calculations. You can set up parallel processing in the Preferences dialog. The different Simcenter STAR-CCM+ licensing options can also be selected here. See Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Info App Window

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Info App window automatically appears when you start NX.

Initially, this window only contains the Status tab which displays the version and licensing information for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX. More tabs appear as you create or load geometry files in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX, allowing you to perform more actions.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6

You cannot close the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Info App window while NX or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX are running. Attempting to close the window by clicking the X button returns a message in the Status tab informing you of this. You can maximize and minimize the window by clicking the - and _ buttons respectively.

Use the Clear button to clear all the information that is displayed in a particular tab.

Use the Abort button to stop active processes, such as surface/volume meshing, or the solver. This button only appears when you can stop a process — it is grayed out at all other times.

A clock is displayed in the bottom-left of the window. This clock displays the current time on your machine. A progress bar is located next to the clock and reports the progress of various processes, such as mesh generation and the solver.

More information on the various tabs is provided in the following sections:

• The Status Tab

• The Output Tab

• The Model Checker Tab

• The Residuals Tab

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7

The Status Tab

The Status tab displays the licensing information for your current session, informing you whether the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX license checked out successfully. The version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX is also displayed in this tab. This tab appears by default when you launch NX without a geometry file.

The Output Tab

The Output tab appears once you create or open a geometry file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 8

During the meshing process, this tab displays status information along with a brief report on the generated mesh. If errors were encountered during the meshing process, they are reported here with suggestions as to what can be causing them.

When the solver is running, the Output tab behaves like the output window in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, displaying the data for each residual per iteration. When the solver finishes running, the same information is also displayed in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Output window.

You can control the amount of information that is displayed in the Output tab by editing the verbosity in the config.xml file. See Modifying the Config.xml File.

To abort the mesher or solver, click the Abort button.

The Model Checker Tab

The Model Checker tab displays information from the live model checker, where the case setup is actively monitored for any problems. See Checking the Model for Errors.

The following example reports that the case has no inlet boundary defined.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 9

The Residuals Tab

The Residuals tab appears when you launch the solver. Use the residuals to monitor the convergence of the solution being calculated.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 10

Typically, a drop in three to five orders of magnitude in the residuals indicates that the solution has converged to an acceptable level. The residuals that are displayed in this tab also appear in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ under the Plots node.

You can zoom in to the residuals by clicking and holding the left mouse button in the graph area and drawing a box around the area you want to view. To zoom out, right-click in the graph area. You can hide individual residuals from the Residuals tab by clicking their label at the top of the plot window.

Modifying the config.xml File

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ requires a configuration file to enable it to find the appropriate components to run correctly. This configuration file is created during installation. An explanation of the file and settings within it is given here.

The configuration file is called config.xml. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX searches for this file in the installation directory.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11

Typical config.xml content is shown below. In this example Simcenter STAR-CCM+ version 15.06.### is shown.

<CAD> <STAR_HOME>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\star</ STAR_HOME> <SOLVER>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\star\bin \starccm+.exe</SOLVER> <LOGFILE>starcad.log</LOGFILE> <WWHELP>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.### \win64\Intel11.1\wwhelp.exe</WWHELP> <MANDIR>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\doc\en \online</MANDIR> <VERBOSITY>Normal</VERBOSITY> <!-- Can be Verbose, Log or Normal. Default Normal --> </CAD>

You can edit the following lines:

• <SOLVER> provides the location of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver executable. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ licensing options are set in the Preferences dialog in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX user interface. See Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing.

• <LOGFILE> is the log file that will automatically be created and saved when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX is run. A path of your choice can be used.

• <VERBOSITY> is the verbosity of the output window in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Info App. This can be set to one of the following:

◦ Normal—This is the default setting and will display the least amount of information in the Output panel.

◦ Verbose—This will display a moderate amount of information in the Output panel.

◦ Log—This will display all available information in the Output panel.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Object Tree

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX uses an object tree as the primary method for setting parameters.

The object tree consists of nodes, each one of which represents a particular component of the simulation. This approach to the user interface complements the method that is used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+, allowing for an easy transition between the two software packages.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 14

The object tree appears slightly different in assembly mode as it must accommodate multiple parts, but the principles of operation remain the same.

Nodes are arranged in an order that follows the recommended workflow for setting up a simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX. At each stage, you typically right-click on a particular node in the tree and choose the appropriate action from the pop-up menu.

Certain functionality within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX applies to the simulation as a whole, rather than to individual objects. These operations are provided in the ribbon.

A complete list of all functions and their respective location is included in Understanding the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Interface.

Clicking on the Region node within the object tree will highlight all the relevant faces on the geometry model for that particular region. If different parts are assigned to multiple regions, then clicking on a region will only highlight the part and faces associated with that specific region. For example, clicking on the Fluid node below will highlight all the faces associated with the Fluid region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 15

Similarly, clicking on the Solid node highlights all the faces associated with the Solid region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 16

Clicking on a boundary node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX object tree highlights all the faces on the CAD geometry model that are associated with it. Note that clicking on the Default boundary node will not highlight any faces on the CAD geometry model. To stop highlighting the faces, you can either click on a blank space in the geometry window, or click on the root node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX object tree.

Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing

The licensing options and the options for setting up parallel processing are located in the Preferences dialog.

This dialog provides two sets of options: server preferences and server settings.

• Server preferences are applied whenever Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX starts a server.

• Server settings are saved in the CAD file and are applied only to that CAD file. Click Save as Default Server Settings to save the current server settings as the default settings to be applied to all CAD files.

To modify the run mode and licensing options:

1. Select Preferences from the ribbon.

The Preferences dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 17

2. Set up the licensing behavior for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX:

◦ To enable Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX in the current session, activate the Activate option. This action checks out the star-nx feature license. This option is activated by default.

◦ To automatically start Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX when you launch NX, activate the Activate on Startup option. This action checks out the star-nx feature license. This option is activated by default.

Note: If you update the geometry in disconnected mode then this setting is ignored.

3. Select the run mode:

▶For serial, set Run Mode to Serial (the default setting).

▶For parallel, set Run Mode to Parallel and Compute Processes to the desired number of cores.

You can use the up/down buttons or you can type in the number of cores that you want to use.

▶For advanced licensing options, such as Power on Demand, enter the appropriate argument in the Command field.

For Power on Demand, enter:

-licpath 1999@flex.cd-adapco.com -podkey <pod_key>

Where:

▪1999@flex.cd-adapco.com is the default CD-adapco Power on Demand server.

▪<pod_key> is the Power on Demand license key.

For more information on Power on Demand licensing, see the section User Guide > Using STAR-CCM + > STAR-CCM+ Licensing > Power on Demand Licensing.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 18

A full list of command-line arguments is available in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ User Guide at User Guide > Using STAR-CCM+ > Command-Line Reference.

The Command field updates automatically to reflect the selections you make. Manual entries are not affected by these selections.

4. Select a licensing option:

▶To use a Power Session license, select Power Session.

This license is designed for parallel simulations, where you can use an unlimited number of cores in this session.

▶To use a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Lite license, select Lite Session.

A limited set of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ features are provided when you activate this option.

If you select no licensing option, the default CAD client license is used.

5. Click OK.

If the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server is running when you modify the preferences, a message box appears informing you that both Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ must be closed for the changes to take effect.

6. Click OK to proceed.

7. Close the active Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ sessions.

8. Restart Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Note: The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server only starts when it is required, such as during surface meshing or volume meshing. It does not start when you launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

If an option in the Preferences dialog conflicts with an option in the config.xml file, the option that is set in the Preferences dialog takes precedence. An example of such a situation is if the Compute Processes property is set to 4 in the Preferences panel, while it is set to 2 in the config.xml file; the simulation runs using four processors. See Modifying the config.xml File

Note: IBM Platform MPI must be installed on your local machine for you to run in parallel. This program is included with the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ package installer.

Changing the Units System

You can use either the SI (International Standard) or USCS (United States Customary System) units system in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 19

To change the units system:

1. Bring up the Units System dialog:

▶Right-click the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX node within the object tree and select Set Units System.

▶Alternatively, from the ribbon, select Units System.

The Units System dialog appears.

2. Select the desired units system from the drop-down menu.

3. Click OK.

Automatic Unit Conversion in Dialog Panels

Changing the default units system converts existing values to the new units system. Ensure that you select the desired units system before you enter the value, otherwise you will need to re-enter it.

Note: Specific values that you have already modified the units on are not affected by a change of units system.

Transferring Units to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 20

Units that are used in the CAD geometry file are also used in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation. Less common units, such as those listed below, are not supported in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

• Micrometers

• Angstroms

• Nanometers

• Mils

• Microinches

• Footinches (this unit may be converted to inches in Simcenter STAR-CCM+)

• Miles

Note: This list may not be exhaustive and is subject to change.

Product Excellence Program

The Product Excellence Program collects information about our customers and their use of Siemens Digital Industries Software. This information helps us improve our product features and functionality to better meet customer needs. No personal or intellectual property information is collected or shared. Product performance is not affected and participation in the program is voluntary.

Privacy statement

The Product Excellence Program helps Siemens Digital Industries Software understand how customers use our products and assists us in improving our products. The program is anonymous and participation is voluntary.

The Product Excellence Program is designed to protect the privacy of the user and the intellectual property created through the use of Siemens Digital Industries Software products.

How does it work?

The Product Excellence Program is used to collect data about your installation, the features you use and how you use them. The data is sent to Siemens Digital Industries Software for analysis. By examining usage patterns from a large number of people, we gain insight into how the products are used and how to improve the software in future releases. Data collection occurs in the background as you use the software and does not affect performance or functionality.

What data is sent?

The data collected can vary by product and by release as we gain more insight or add new capabilities. The Product Excellence Program may collect information on the functions utilized, the operating environment (e.g.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 24

OS, RAM, graphics, etc.), product version, or other indications of user interaction. The data may also include the company name that is using the product. This data is solely for use by Siemens Digital Industries Software to improve our products and is never shared with any third party.

There is no contact information in the data and Siemens Digital Industries Software will not contact you by phone or email as a result of the data collected. No information about the data you create or manage is collected.

Participation is optional.

You can control your participation during installation or reinstallation of the software by using the Product Excellence Program option in the interactive installer.

Using Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX with Multiple Installed Versions of NX

If you have multiple versions of NX installed on your machine, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX is installed to work with the latest version.

Attempting to run a different version of NX results in an error message with the ugraf.exe executable.

Note: The error message can differ depending on what version of NX you are trying to run.

This error indicates that Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX is not set to work with the version of NX that you are trying to run. Clicking OK dismisses the message and allows you to work in that version of NX without Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

You can choose which version of NX Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX works with from the custom_dirs.dat file.

You can find the custom_dirs.dat file by checking the UGII_CUSTOM_DIRECTORY_FILE environment variable.

To specify which version of NX to use with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX:

1. Navigate to the folder that contains the custom_dirs.dat file.

The default location is:

C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-NX\

2. Locate and edit the custom_dirs.dat file using a text editor of your choice.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 25

Example custom_dirs.dat content is shown below. Depending on what versions of NX are installed on your machine, the contents of this file can differ:

// If uncommented, the following line supports STAR-NX with NX 9. C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-NX\win64\bin \STAR-NX9

// If uncommented, the following line supports STAR-NX with NX 8. // C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-NX\win64\bin \STAR-NX8

Uncomment the line that corresponds to the path of the version of NX that you want to use. In this example, NX8.

3. Comment out the lines that correspond to the path of any other versions of NX.

The final custom_dirs.dat content appears as follows:

// If uncommented, the following line supports STAR-NX with NX 9. // C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-NX\win64\bin \STAR-NX9

// If uncommented, the following line supports STAR-NX with NX 8. C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-NX\win64\bin\STARNX8

4. Save the file and exit the text editor.

Disabling Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

If for any reason you would like to temporarily disable Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX without having to uninstall it, do the following:

1. Change the variable name of the UGII_CUSTOM_DIRECTORY_FILE environmental variable. It is recommended that the variable value is not changed.

or

2. Navigate to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX installation folder and rename the custom_dirs.dat file.

The typical path is C:\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-NX

NX will now launch without Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX. To enable Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX again, undo the changes listed above.

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on Different Machines

You can run Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on two different machines.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ operates on a client-server architecture, where Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is the server and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX is the client. A benefit of client-server architectures is that the client and the server do not have to be running on the same machine. Typically, CAD packages run on Windows operating systems. You can choose to run Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on any remote machine with a supported or certified platform, including Linux platforms.

With Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX, you can transfer your CAD geometry directly to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ from within the NX environment. Along with the geometry data, you can also transfer design data, such as CAD parameters, CAD responses, coordinate systems, and reference planes.

Transferring Design Data to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Design data consists of CAD parameters, CAD responses, coordinate systems, and reference planes that you can transfer to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ along with the geometry.

CAD parameters control the feature dimensions, for example extrusion depth, and are useful for modifying the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ after running the analysis. CAD responses extract NX expressions such as those for volume, weight, moment of inertia, center of gravity, and mass. You can use reference planes in scalar scenes and reports in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. You can use coordinate systems to define motion in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation.

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, CAD parameters appear within the Expressions Editor dialog as single-values with units. You can select these for use in expressions, which in turn can be used in the following contexts:

• In 3D-CAD, for expressions that apply to design parameters

• Expression reports

• Coordinate parameters

Additionally, after transfer, you can set a CAD parameter in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to reference global scalar parameters.

To transfer design data to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Design Data.

The Design Data dialog appears.

▶CAD Responses—Click the CAD Responses tab and select the CAD responses that you want to transfer from the list.

▶Coordinate Systems—Click the Coordinate Systems tab and select the coordinate systems that you want to transfer from the list. You can select multiple items at once.

▶Reference Planes—Click the Reference Planes tab and select the planes that you want to transfer from the list. You can select multiple items at once.

3. In each tab, click the checkbox next to the selected item to activate it.

4. Click OK.

5. Transfer the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Transferring Geometry to STAR-CCM+.

The geometry, along with the specified design data, is transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Transferred CAD parameters are placed in the Geometry > CAD Client Models > [geometry_name] > CAD Parameters node. Transferred planes are placed in the Derived Parts node in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Transferred

coordinates systems are placed in the Tools > Coordinate Systems > Laboratory > Local Coordinate Systems node in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• The weight of a ship calculated through an expression in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX using the surface area and thickness of plates.

This workflow maintains an active link between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+. When working with Geometry Transfer, you can modify the geometry in either package and the geometry in the relevant package is updated accordingly.

Updating the Geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with NX Closed

You can close NX and continue working with the simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Doing so, however, breaks the link between the two software packages. Any further updates that you make to the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are not transferred back to the geometry in NX. Instead, these changes are stored in memory, which allows you to include the CAD parameters in your optimization scripts.

This workflow also allows you to release the NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX licenses when performing tasks in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In this case, the NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX licenses are temporarily checked out only when the updates to the geometry are stored in memory.

Transferring the geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX will overwrite the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Coincident Face Tolerance Specifies the tolerance, in meters, for geometry in adjacent faces to be considered coincident. The default value is 1.0E-3.

Create Part Contacts from Coincident Faces Controls whether the geometry transfer feature searches for pairs of coincident faces on the CAD faces. For each pair found, part contact data is created and stored in the Contacts property (in Simcenter STAR-CCM+). See the Creating Part

Contacts from Coincident Entities section in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ user guide.

Transfer Multi-Body Parts as Composites Specifies whether to transfer a single part containing multiple solid bodies as a composite part. Part contacts are created for each pair of coincident faces. Leaving this option deactivated merges all solid bodies in the part.

Transfer Hidden Geometry Specifies whether to transfer hidden parts. By default, hidden parts in NX are not transferred. For files saved in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX v10.06 and earlier, this option is activated by default.

Transfer Sheet Geometry Specifies whether to transfer sheet bodies as part of the transfer process. This option is turned off by default.

Check Parts' Validity Provides you with information on whether the bodies are geometrically and topologically valid, from the Parasolid geometry kernel point of view.

A simple message is displayed in the output window which states if the surface mesh is valid. For example: Body 2 is not valid.

Repair Invalid Bodies Attempts to repair invalid bodies. The number of invalid bodies that are successfully repaired is displayed in the output window.
