Understanding the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Process

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX the typical workflow for running a simulation is as follows:

1. Ensure that the CAD model is suitable for analysis

2. Extract the fluid volume

3. Define the material properties for each part of the model, for example, air, water, aluminum

4. Define model physics, for example, turbulence, temperature, gravity

5. Specify boundary conditions, for example, inlets, outlets, symmetry planes

6. Specify mesh settings

7. Define solution controls

8. Run the case

9. Post-process the results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Once you have obtained an initial solution you may wish to re-run the case with some different settings, or with some changes to the geometry. To do this you can:

1. Return to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and change settings or modify the geometry

2. Re-run the case

Using Suitable CAD Models in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX only supports the use of solid bodies. If a geometry is made up entirely of surfaces then it will not be possible to define any boundary conditions, and the meshing options will be greyed out.

It is good practice to create copies of the original geometry file(s) before importing them into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Suppressed or deactivated parts and features are not supported by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and will have no effect on the analysis. Hidden parts, however, are used in the analysis. Ensure that all desired parts and features are active before using them with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Extracting the Fluid Volume

A CAD model usually represents a component made from solid material. However, in the case of flow simulation, a model representing the fluid volume is needed, requiring a different CAD model to be created. This is illustrated below:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 44

In some instances, a simulation will require multiple regions, such as:

• Moving Reference Frames

For rotating flow, such as turbines.

• Porous Media

For representing regions with fine geometric structures

• Energy Source

For simulating thermal specifications, such as conjugate heat transfer

These types of simulation require each region to be represented by individual contiguous parts within an assembly.

Defining Material Properties

Continua determines the characteristics of the fluid and solid entities used within the simulation. The behavior of a single continuum is primarily defined by the chosen material type and physics models.

Specification of the material type used in the simulation provides properties such as density, viscosity and conductivity, which are all used by the solver to calculate a solution. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX includes a database of common materials and allows you to modify material properties where necessary.

Defining Model Physics

Physics models determine the nature of the fluid, and can be described as either:

• Turbulent or Laminar

• Constant Density or Ideal Gas

Additional models can also be activated to meet the needs of various simulation requirements:

• Passive scalar

• Temperature

• Gravity

A region is defined as a volume domain in a simulation, surrounded by boundaries. Each region in the simulation must be represented by a part in the native CAD package. When multiple regions are required, multiple parts must be used within an assembly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 45

All regions must be assigned to a continuum, as they represent a volume of material in the simulation. Region settings can be used to define porous media, moving reference frames, and an energy source.

Specifying Boundary Conditions

To define boundary conditions you first need to select the surface or surfaces on the model to assign to a separate boundary.

A boundary is defined as a surface, which along with other boundaries, surround and characterize a region. Boundary conditions determine how the boundary will affect the material within a region, and consequently, the simulation as a whole.

Inlet boundaries determine how much fluid enters the region, using a velocity, mass flow rate or stagnation inlet. Outlet boundaries define the process for fluid leaving the region, which are defined with either a pressure or flow-split ratio. Wall boundaries contain the fluid, and can also be used to define a thermal specification that will influence the transfer of energy to or from the region. Symmetry boundaries can be used to avoid modeling the entire region where appropriate, and so reduce calculation time.

As boundary types can affect the way in which the volume mesh is constructed, it is important to set them before generating the mesh.

Specifying Mesh Settings

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver uses the finite volume method to obtain an approximate solution to the underlying equations of fluid flow. This requires a mesh to be created, which represents the fluid volume as a collection of much smaller volumes known as cells.

A surface mesh is first created based on the boundaries defining the regions in the simulation. Thereafter a volume mesh is created to discretize the entire model.

The accuracy of the results is directly affected by mesh quality. If it is necessary to improve the quality of the mesh, some of the ways in which this can be done are to:

• Increase the mesh density, that is, the number of cells

• Add further sub-surface prism layers to capture near wall flow

• Refine the mesh in areas where flow characteristics are expected to change rapidly

As volume mesh quality is largely governed by the surface mesh quality, it is common practice to create and inspect the surface mesh before creating a volume mesh.

Defining Solution Controls

Solution controls determine the level of accuracy the solver will work towards. As a high accuracy solution will take longer, it may be necessary to compromise on this in order to obtain a result in a shorter time.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX includes five predefined solver settings ranging from fast (with low accuracy) to slow (with high accuracy). Advanced options are also available to provide further control.

Running the Case

When the simulation has been fully defined, the volume mesh is sent to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ along with all the necessary data for running the simulation. The time to complete a simulation will vary depending on the mesh density and solution controls.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 46

As the solver is running, residuals showing the rate at which individual equations are converging are shown in a plot. A scalar scene displaying absolute pressure is displayed on completion of the simulation.

Post-Processing the Results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Post-processing of simulations is carried out using the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ interface. This allows the results to be taken from the solver and displayed in a variety of scenes and plots.

Making Modifications to the Settings or Geometry

As Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX is completely integrated within the NX environment, it is very simple to perform parametric studies that examine the response of the fluid to changes in geometry. Once the first analysis is complete, the boundary conditions, run settings and all other properties of the CFD model are stored within the CAD file. Any changes in the flow field due to design changes can be recalculated by generating a new mesh and running the solver.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 47

Connecting to Remote Machines

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses a client-server architecture, and as such the CAD client ( Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX) and the server (Simcenter STAR-CCM+) are not required to run on the same machine.

Using an SSH (secure shell) connection, you can connect the client and server on two different machines, even when these are on different platforms. Due to how the CAD client and server interact in the background, the SSH connection must not ask for a username or a password.

There are two ways that you can connect Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+, depending on what your starting point is:

• You can start from the CAD client and launch the server on a remote machine. This method is useful for transferring CAD geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX running on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on Linux.

• You can start from the server and connect to the CAD client on a remote machine. This method is useful for connecting to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX to update the CAD geometry. With this method, you can perform a Design Manager analysis on a cluster while the geometry is updated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Contents:

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Starting from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX, you can choose to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on a remote machine.

Using this method, you can set up the full CAE analysis in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX on your local machine, and then run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on the remote machine. You can also choose to transfer your geometry from the CAD client to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. This feature is useful if you want to import geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX running on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on Linux.

To configure Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX to launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on a remote machine:

1. Make sure that you have a working SSH connection between the two machines.

For the SSH connection, you require an SSH server on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and an SSH client on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX. The SSH connection to the remote machine must not ask for a username or a password. To avoid possible issues with a connection that still requires a password, add -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=0 to the SSH command. Setting this argument to zero stops the connection prompting for a password when one is needed — something that could cause the process to hang. See SSH Command.

2. In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Preferences.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 48

3. In the Preferences panel, set Server Settings to Remote.

4. Set the remaining settings for your connection to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. See Server

Settings Panel.

This information is used to build a command-line in the background when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX invokes Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

5. If you are going to connect to the same remote host in future sessions, click Save as Default Settings.

The next time Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX invokes Simcenter STAR-CCM+, the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server launches on the specified remote machine. A Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client is also launched on the local machine to allow you to see the active session on the remote machine.

Defining Materials and Physics

Defining the physical properties of a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX model involves specifying the materials, flow characteristics, operating conditions, and physics models.

These definitions and settings are accomplished through the use of continua and regions, which are described in the following sections.

Contents:

Working with Continua and Regions

Importing Geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for Visualization

Working with Continua and Regions

Continua and regions are used together to capture the physical and material properties of a model.

A continuum represents a material in combination with a set of physics models that will be used to simulate the response of the material to the conditions imposed upon it. A continuum also provides the facility to define reference and initial values.

A region represents one or more volumes within the overall model, not necessarily contiguous, which will share the same continuum and set of boundary conditions. Regions are defined using CAD parts, and will be discretized by the volume mesher.

As well as holding a set of boundary conditions, regions can also be used to model specific physical behavior, including porous resistance, moving reference frames and energy sources.

Parts can be imported into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes without affecting the analysis.

Continua are assigned to single or multiple regions, which can contain single or multiple parts. In part mode, only one continuum and one region are available, as there is only one part. In assembly mode, new continua can be added to represent different materials present in the simulation, and new regions can be added to represent the parts composed of these materials. Continua and regions can be deleted if they are not required, although the simulation must always contain at least one of each.

There is a well defined relationship between continua, regions, boundary conditions and CAD parts.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 53

• Every region must be associated with a continuum.

• Several regions can be associated with the same continuum.

• Every CAD part must belong to a region.

• Several CAD parts can be associated with the same region.

• Boundary conditions belong to regions, and cannot be shared between regions.

• Every CAD surface must have a boundary condition associated with it. A default wall boundary is applied to CAD surfaces that have not been specifically associated with a user-defined boundary condition.

The following series of illustrations depict the relationship between CAD parts, continua, and regions, for a circular steel duct containing a rotating fan, and surrounded by a layer of insulation.

• Initially we have a collection of CAD parts in an assembly. These must be imprinted where appropriate to ensure that interfaces between parts can be created correctly.

• Three continua are required to represent the three different materials present in the simulation: the fluid (for example, air), the steel pipe, and the insulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 54

• Two regions are required for the fluid portion of the simulation, as a rotating part is defined by applying a rotating frame of reference to a separate region surrounding the fan blades. Further regions are required for each of the solid parts (the steel pipe and insulating layer), which means a total of four separate regions overall.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 55

• A clearer picture can be given of the fan blade itself.

For an analysis containing a single part, for example a fluid-only case involving fluid flow through a converging-diverging pipe, the model will only require one continuum and one region in order to fully define

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 56

the physical and material properties of the model. In this case, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX automatically assigns the default continuum to the default region, and no further assignments are necessary.

Setting Up Continua

To define different materials and associated physics for use in an assembly, you require additional continua. In each continuum you can specify a unique set of properties, such as a different material type or temperature. In assembly mode, continua are stored under a Continua node, as shown below.

To create an additional continuum:

1. Right-click the Continua node in the object tree and select Add Continuum.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. In the Name field, enter a name for the continuum.

3. In the Materials group, select the type of material that you want to define:

▶Gas

▶Liquid

▶Solid

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 57

4. Select a material from the list.

You can modify the properties of any material that you select.

Note: You can select only one material per continuum. If your simulation contains a number of materials, you must create additional continua. This action is only possible for assemblies.

5. In the Flow Characteristics group, select the type of flow that you want to model: Laminar or Turbulent. This group only appears for fluids.

6. In the Equation of State group, select the equation of state : Constant Density or Ideal Gas. This group only appears for gases.

7. In the Optional Physics Model group, activate any optional physics models: Passive Scalar and Temperature.

8. Define the material properties in the Material Properties group.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 58

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Material Properties Panel.

Note: You can change units of properties from the drop-down menu.

9. In the Reference Properties group, define the reference properties.

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Reference Properties Panel.

10.If you want to include the body force due to gravity when calculating the momentum equations in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, activate the gravity model in the Gravity group box.

See Activating the Gravity Model in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

11.Set the initial conditions in the Initialization group box.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 59

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Initialization Panel.

Specifying initial conditions that are close to the expected solution can reduce the number of iterations required to reach a solution. You can set the initial conditions similar to the inlet conditions of the fluid domain.

Initial conditions are specified at a continuum level; if no initial conditions are specified, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX will use default values to initialize the solution.

12.Click OK.

The continuum is added to the object tree.

Once you have created a continuum, you can assign it to a region.

Property Description

(Reference Pressure) The pressure values that are defined in the simulation are all relative to the reference pressure. For more information, see the What is the Reference Pressure? section.

(Reference Temperature) The reference temperature is used to define the operating temperature of the fluid in the buoyancy source term of the Boussinesq model. This parameter is used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ when the temperature, constant density, and gravity physics models are enabled.

(Reference Density) These quantities are not used as part of the CFD calculation, but is necessary to calculate the force coefficients when post-processing. (Reference Velocity)

(Reference Area)

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Initialization Panel

Specifying initial conditions that are close to the expected solution can reduce the number of iterations required to reach a solution. You can also set the initial conditions to match inlet conditions of the fluid domain. You can define the following continuum reference properties:

Property Description

(U Component of Velocity) The U direction vector for the initial velocity.

(V Component of Velocity) The V direction vectors for the initial velocity.

(W Component of Velocity) The W direction vectors for the initial velocity.

(Initial Pressure) The initial pressure. The physical value of the initial pressure defines the starting pressure in the regions to which the continuum is assigned. The initial pressure is specified with respect to the reference pressure. The default initial pressure is 0 Pa.

Property Description

(Turbulence Intensity) The initial turbulence intensity. The default value is 0.05 (5%)

(Turbulent Length Scale) The initial turbulent length scale. The default value is 0.01 m.

If you require the gravity model in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX, you can activate it in the Continuum Settings dialog:

1. In the Continuum Settings dialog, activate the Enable checkbox in the Gravity group.

2. Set the acceleration due to gravity in the (Acceleration due to gravity) box.

Setting Up Regions

Additional regions are required when modelling multiple region physics, or when specific behavior such as porous resistance is required for a particular part within the same continuum. Assign parts from an assembly to regions. You can control the properties of these regions through the assigned continuum.

In assembly mode, regions are stored under the Regions node in the object tree, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 62

To create an additional region:

1. Right-click the Regions manager node in the object tree and select Add Region.

The Region Settings dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 63

2. In the Name property, enter a name for the region.

3. Select the parts that you want to include in the region.

You can select multiple parts from the graphics window or the NX feature tree.

Selected parts appear in the Parts Selection group box field.

4. Select a continuum to apply to the region.

All available continua are listed here.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 64

Note: Assigning a continuum to a region causes the region to inherit the physical and material properties defined in the continuum

5. Activate any additional region physics for the region:

◦ Porous. See Defining a Porous Region.

◦ Moving Reference Frame. See Defining a Moving Reference Frame.

◦ Energy Source. See Defining an Energy Source.

6. If you want to import parts into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes, but do not want the region to be included in the CFD calculations, activate the Exclude from Analysis option. See Importing Geometry into STAR-CCM+ for Visualization.

7. Click OK.

A new region is added to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX object tree under the Regions node.

The parts that you assign to a region define the geometric extent of the region. Within this geometry, properties and behavior of the material is governed by the physics models and material properties defined in the region and continuum settings.

Note: Each region must be assigned at least one part, otherwise it will be ignored during the CFD analysis.

By default, every Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX model contains one continuum, and this is automatically assigned to the default region and each additional region that you create. If multiple continua are defined in the model, you can choose a different continuum to assign to each region. This enables you to control the physical properties of each region, including varying material types.

All the parts in an assembly are assigned to the default region (this is the initial region created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX). When you assign a part to another region, it is automatically removed from the default region. If you remove a part from a region, it is reassigned back to the default region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 65

Importing Geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for Visualization

You can import CAD parts, that do not form part of the analysis, into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes.

Add these parts to a separate region—this region is excluded from the analysis. This feature is useful for showing the original geometry in a post-processing scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. For example, for an internal fluid volume of a pipe, the original geometry is the solid pipe.

To exclude CAD parts from the analysis:

1. In the Region Settings dialog, add the CAD parts that you want to use for visualization purposes.

2. Activate the Exclude From Analysis checkbox in the Advanced panel.

Setting Boundary Conditions

Boundary conditions tell the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers how the substance within the region interacts with its environment. A velocity inlet boundary, for example, tells the solvers that an amount of substance is being added to the fluid domain at a certain rate.

A Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX boundary is made up of one or more CAD surfaces within the simulation which, along with other boundaries, surround and define a region.

The boundary is discretized by the surface mesher, which is then used by the volume mesher to mesh the entire region.

It is important to set the boundary conditions before creating the volume mesh, as some parts of the volume mesh, such as prism layers, depend on the type of boundary.

By default, each region contains only one boundary. To define more boundaries you need to add boundaries to the region. You can modify the properties of existing boundaries by editing its boundary node.

Some boundaries may require the specification of turbulence quantities, temperature, and passive scalar concentration, depending on whether these modeling options have been activated in Continuum Settings.

A symmetry plane boundary represents an imaginary plane of symmetry in the simulation. Meshing the Model

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX provides options for generating polyhedral or trimmed volume meshes, with or without near-wall prism layers.

By default, prism layers are generated on all wall surfaces. The provision of a prism layer depends on the type of boundary that is applied to a face. As a consequence, it is recommended that you only generate the mesh after setting up the boundaries and regions.

The meshing process first creates a triangulated surface (the surface mesh) and thereafter converts it to the desired volume mesh (polyhedral or trimmer). As the quality of the volume mesh depends to a large extent on the quality of the surface mesh, it is prudent to check the surface mesh before proceeding with the volume mesh.

Although the entire meshing process can be launched with a single command (the Build And Run command from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon), it is possible to execute only single stages from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NXribbon. Settings that are made in the Mesh Pipeline node govern the mesh generation process.

A mesh pipeline contains all the settings that are applied to the surface and volume meshes created on the NX parts to which it is applied. In single part mode, only one mesh pipeline is available. In assembly mode, multiple mesh pipelines can be created if necessary.

When mesh generation commences, each mesh pipeline will:

1. Extract geometry from NX.

2. Transfer the model to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3. Execute the surface remesher.

4. Execute the polyhedral or trimmer volume mesher with the prism layer mesher (if selected).

5. Create a mesh representation in the NX Graphics window.

Controls on the top-level mesh pipeline node allow you to set the base sizes for the surface mesh, and control the prism layer. Further refinement to specific faces, parts, or volume shapes can be made by adding additional controls to the mesh pipeline.

Creation of Additional Surfaces in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ creates geometry part surfaces during the geometry transfer stage.

Initially, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX creates one part surface for each face in the CAD model. These part surfaces are then combined so that one surface per boundary remains. This outcome, however, is not possible for boundaries that contain CAD surfaces from more than one part. The final part surfaces appear in the Geometry > Parts node in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

The following items affect the number of part surfaces that are created in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

• The number of boundaries present in the model, including the default boundary. Each boundary in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX appears as a separate part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If, however, a boundary contains CAD surfaces from multiple parts, the part surfaces in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ cannot be combined.

• The number of mesh pipeline controls used (if any). Each CAD surface that is used to define a face mesh control in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX appears as a separate part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• The number of interfaces that are created during the meshing process (for assemblies only). All the CAD surfaces that define one interface between two parts in an assembly are grouped together under one part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. One part surface exists for each interface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Boundary Splitting due to Interface Generation

Interfaces are automatically created between two parts in an assembly during the mesh generation. A new boundary is created for each interface on the surfaces that share the interface.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 83

Boundary Splitting due to Face Mesh Controls and Part Mesh Controls

If you use a face mesh control or a part mesh control in your simulation, some boundaries may be split, depending on what faces are included in the mesh control. If a boundary and mesh control share the same faces, no splitting occurs. If a mesh control contains faces from multiple boundaries, splitting occurs and a new boundary is created. The name of the new boundary is derived from the original boundary.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 84

Working with Mesh Pipelines

When working with a single part, you will only have one mesh pipeline defined in the model tree. This will specify the mesh settings for the single part available. In assembly mode, multiple mesh pipelines can be created to give specific controls for different parts, and parts must be specifically associated with a mesh pipeline.

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

The mesh pipeline node contains the general mesh settings that will apply to all Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX parts associated within the pipeline in the absence of any further controls.

To set up the mesh pipeline:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX tree and select Edit.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 85

The Mesh Pipeline Settings dialog appears.

2. In the Name field, enter the name of the mesh pipeline if required.

3. In the Part Selection box, specify the desired parts to use in the mesh pipeline.

This property is only available when working with assemblies.

4. From the Mesh Type tab, select the type of mesh that you want to generate:

▶Polyhedral

▶Trimmer

5. Set Base Size to the desired value.

The base size is a reference length used in other meshing parameters. It may be set to equal the length of the largest triangle you expect to have on your surface mesh, or to some other characteristic dimension.

The base size can be set as either a relative or absolute value. When it is set as a relative value, the reference size will be the diagonal of the bounding box enclosing the entire geometry. In the case of multiple parts in an assembly, the reference size will be calculated based on the diagonal length of the bounding box enclosing the entire assembly. This includes all parts from all mesh pipelines. The unit specification menu will become active when setting an absolute value.

6. Set Surface Mesh Size to the desired value.

The surface mesh size is the base edge length of triangles on the surface mesh. Note that the ultimate length of some (or all) triangles on the surface mesh will depend on other factors such as surface curvature and edge proximity.

7. Set the prism layer settings. See Prism Layer Panel.

8. Set the advanced settings. See Mesh Pipeline Advanced Settings Panel.

9. If you selected to generate a trimmed mesh, set the Trimmer settings. See Trimmer Panel.

10.Click OK.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 86

Mesh Pipeline Advanced Settings Panel

The advanced settings panel provides further customization of meshing parameters.

Property Description

Relative Minimum Surface Size Defines the minimum triangle size permitted on a feature curve. The minimum triangle size is set as a percentage of the surface mesh size. The default value is set to 25%. You must set the relative minimum surface size to a value greater than zero. If you set the relative minimum surface size to 100%, Simcenter STARCCM+ will not modify the triangle size when it detects curvature.

The figure below illustrates this behavior. Note that the base size was set to 20% in this example to emphasize the refinement on the curve.

Having a large value for the number of points on a circle property increases the mesh resolution on curved surfaces.

The transition between the fine mesh and coarse mesh areas is controlled by the growth ratio.

Growth Ratio Controls the rate at which triangle sizes change when moving from one triangle size to another. In the example below, the end faces of the block were set to have a smaller triangle size than the four side faces of the block. When the growth ratio is set to a low

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 88

Property Description

value, the transition between triangle size is very gradual. When a higher value is used, the transition is far more rapid.

The growth factor must be set to a value greater than 1.0. There is no upper limit for the growth factor.

Number of Points per Circle Controls the number of triangle edges that appear on a curved surface, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 89

Property Description

Regardless of the number of points per circle defined, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX will not permit the triangle edge length to shrink below 25% of the base size. The curvature length scale may also affect the number of edges on a curved surface.

Trimmer Panel

The trimmer mesh is controlled using the Trimmer panel.

Property Description

Default Growth Rate Controls the stepping of the refinement from one cell size to the next. Five settings are available. By default, the Default Growth Rate is set to Fast, meaning that the fastest transition from the smallest cell size to the largest will be used. This usually equates to having only one layer of each cell size for each transition, which will result in the least number of cells being created for the supplied input values. The Medium, Slow, and Very Slow options further slow the transition from one cell size to the next in the mesh interior and therefore increase the overall cell count. In general, the medium option results in a minimum of two equal sized cell layers per transition, slow in four layers and the very slow option in eight layers.

Boundary Growth Rate Controls the number of cell layers to grow next to surfaces in the template. Five settings are available. By default, the Boundary Growth Rate is set to None, meaning that the setting used for the Default Growth Rate is used for controlling all transitions. If the Very Slow, Slow, Medium, or Fast options are selected then it will result in eight, four, two or one layers of

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 90

Property Description

cells respectively of the same size being created next to the geometry surfaces in the template.

Working with Mesh Controls

Mesh controls allow you to define custom mesh settings for a particular section of the model.

Multiple controls can be assigned to the same item to control different mesh parameters. If, for example, a face has two mesh controls assigned to it--one that controls the mesh size and another that controls the prism layer thickness, the final mesh will respect both the custom mesh size and the custom prism layer thickness. If two mesh controls set the same mesh parameter, the control created last will take precedence over the first.

Using a Volumetric Mesh Control

Using a Face Mesh Control

A face mesh control allows you to set the surface mesh size and the prism layer parameters on a face. Custom settings made on a face control will take priority over settings in the parent mesh pipeline, and over settings made in any part mesh controls.

To add a face mesh control:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline > Mesh Controls node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX tree and select Add Face Mesh Control.

The Face Mesh Control Settings dialog appears.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 91

3. On the CAD geometry, select the desired faces to include in this mesh control.

4. If you want to specify a custom surface mesh size on the selected surfaces, activate the Custom Mesh Size option.

a) Set (Mesh Size) to the desired value.

You can enter this value as a percentage of the base size, or as an absolute value. If you select to enter the absolute value, you can select the units from the drop-down menu.

5. Set (Prism Layer Option) to the desired value:

▶Inherit Values: in the first instance, the face(s) will be assigned values from any part mesh control applied to the part to which the face(s) belong. If this does not apply, values will be taken from any applicable volumetric mesh control, and in the absence of this values will be taken from the parent mesh pipeline.

▶Use Custom Values: allows the prism layer parameters to be set directly on the face(s). See Prism Layer

Panel.

Mesh generation will be carried out automatically when you issue the Build and Run command.

Visualizing the Mesh

Meshing Behavior at Interfaces

Visualizing the Mesh

Surface and volume meshes will automatically be displayed on first creation. If required, they can be hidden from view.

To hide a generated mesh in the geometry view:

1. From Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX the ribbon, click Show/Hide Mesh.

Meshing Behavior at Interfaces

The volume mesher will treat interfaces between two regions differently depending on what type of region (fluid or solid) these are.

If the interface lies between two fluid regions, no prism layers will be grown from both sides of the interface. If an interface lies between a solid region and a fluid region, prism layers will be grown from the interface. The default behavior of the prism layer generation can be overridden using a mesh control, so prism layers can be disabled on a solid-fluid interface. See Working With Mesh Controls.

See Also:

Working with Mesh Controls

Common Causes for Meshing Failures

There may be instances when the mesh generation fails. In most cases this will occur during the surface meshing phase. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX will try and identify the cause and suggest ways of rectifying this. This information will be printed in the Output tab of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Info App window.

The Parts in an Assembly are not Imprinted

Obtaining a Solution

The following section details the execution of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers in order to obtain a solution.

Contents:

Setting Solution Controls

Checking the Model for Errors

Building and Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

Clearing the Solution

Visualizing the Solution

Setting Solution Controls

The solution you obtain from the solvers is a compromise between accuracy and processing time. You can manage the speed and accuracy of the solver from the Solution Controls dialog. The solution accuracy is also dependant on the mesh density.

To set up the solution controls in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX:

1. Either:

▶Right-click on the STAR-NX node within the object tree and select Set Solution Controls.

▶From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, select Solution Controls.

The Solution Controls dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 102

2. Set the solution control parameters:

▶Using the slider, select one of the five pre-defined solver options. These options range from high accuracy and low speed, to low accuracy and high speed.

▶Click to expand the Advanced Settings tab and set the solution control parameters manually. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

3. If you want to run a Java macro with the simulation, activate the Use Java File option. See Using Java

Macros with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

4. Click OK.

Contents:

Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel

The advanced settings in the Solution Control dialog allow you to manually enter the values for the solution control parameters.

Parameter Description

Stopping Criteria

(Number of Iterations) Specifies the maximum number of iterations for which the solver can run. When the Simcenter STARCCM+ solver reaches the specified number of iterations, it will stop. You can then post-process the results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Convergence Levels.

(Convergence Level) Specifies how many orders of magnitude the residuals should drop before the solver stops. See Convergence Levels.

Solution Accuracy

First Order This option is generally the quicker, but less accurate solver option. The first order scheme introduces a dissipative error that is stabilizing and helps the solver achieve robust convergence. However, it can also

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 103

Parameter Description

lead to the neglect and merging of discontinuities, meaning the solution is not fully captured.

Second Order This option is generally the more accurate, but slower solver option. The second order scheme attempts to minimize both dispersive and dissipative errors, providing a better representation of the simulation. However, in some situations, the lack of numerical dissipation can result in poorer convergence properties.

It is common practice to use the first order scheme initially to ensure the simulation is running as expected and then switch to second order.

Under-Relaxation Factors

(Momentum Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the momentum equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Pressure Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the pressurecorrection equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Turbulence Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the turbulence equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Fluid Temperature Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the fluid under-relaxation factor for the segregated energy solver. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Solid Temperature Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the solid under-relaxation factor for the segregated energy solver. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

Convergence Level

The numerical method used by the solver requires an iterative process in order to obtain a solution. After each iteration, residuals are produced that indicate how well the governing equations for each solver quantity are being satisfied numerically. In general, the residual magnitude should decrease as the solution converges. When the magnitude of the residuals for all the quantities falls below the convergence level, the solver will stop iterating, and results will be exported for post-processing.

Note: In most cases, a drop of 3-5 orders of magnitude in the residuals is sufficient to obtain an accurate solution.

You can adjust the convergence level parameter to meet accuracy or process time requirements. However, if the residuals are no longer decreasing from one iteration to the next, it is likely that machine accuracy has been reached for that case. For a case that does not exhibit decreasing residuals, it would be necessary to reconsider the setup in case the volume mesh is too coarse, or boundary conditions have been set incorrectly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 104

Under-Relaxation Parameters

Under-relaxation parameters determine how quickly the solver reaches a solution for a particular equation, on a scale from 0 to 1, with 1 being the fastest.

Ideally, all under-relaxation parameters would be set to 1, however, doing so would likely cause solver instability due to the complex nature of most simulations. Hence the under-relaxation parameters should be set to values that compromise speed with stability.

Note: Adjust the under-relaxation parameters if changes to other solution controls such as Number of Iterations, Convergence Levels, and Solution Accuracy have failed to improve the behavior of the solver.

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

You can use Java macros with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to automate your simulation or to change a setting in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as selecting an alternative turbulence model, before the solver starts running.

An example of how to change a setting in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using a Java macro is outlined below:

1. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and set up the case.

Define the continuum settings, boundary conditions, mesh settings, and solution control settings.

2. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, start recording a macro and perform the desired operations, such as changing the physics models.

4. Stop recording the macro.

The macro saves at this point.

5. Close Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and do not save the simulation.

6. Return to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX, open the Solution Controls dialog and activate the Use Java File checkbox.

A text entry field appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 105

7. Click (Select Input File).

The Open dialog appears.

8. Navigate to your Java macro file and select it.

Selected files appear in the text entry field. The path in the entry field is displayed relative to the current CAD geometry file.

9. Click OK.

When you run the simulation, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ will launch and play the macro before starting the solver. This sequence allows you to set up and use additional Simcenter STAR-CCM+ physics models that are not available in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Checking the Model for Errors

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX monitors the active case for any errors in real-time and displays a warning

triangle next to any nodes for which there is a problem.

Three areas are monitored by the live model checker:

• Continua. The continua checker makes sure that all necessary boundaries are present in the case, such as the presence of at least one inlet and one outlet.

• Regions and boundaries. The regions and boundaries checker covers issues specific to boundaries, such as a velocity inlet boundary having a zero value.

• Mesh pipelines. The mesh pipeline checker covers issues that are related to the mesh, such as the presence of multiple parts in a trimmed mesh pipeline.

To see the cause of an error:

1. Right-click on an node displaying the warning triangle, and select Show Errors...

A dialog appears describing the error, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 107

2. Click OK to close the dialog.

The Show Errors... right-click menu is available for any node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX object tree that contains a warning triangle. Selecting it will show errors for that node and its sub-nodes.

To see a complete list of issues for the case, right-click on the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX root node and select Show Errors...

You can also manually check for errors.

To perform a manual check:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Check Model for Errors.

If errors are found in the case set up, these are displayed in the Model Checker tab of the Info App dialog. See The Model Checker Tab.

Building and Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

Once you have defined the model physics, boundary conditions, mesh settings, and solver settings in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX, you can build and run the case.

To build and run the case:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Build and Run.

This action automatically generates the mesh, and runs the solver. When you run the solver, a new Residuals tab is added to the Info App dialog. You can use this residuals plot to monitor solution convergence. When the solver finishes, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and a scalar scene is automatically created for you.

Note: If a solution has already been computed in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, and the stopping criteria has been reached, clicking Build and Run clears the solution and starts running from the first iteration. If you want to run for more iterations, change the stopping criteria and click Run Solver, or click Run More Iterations.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 108

Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX

If you have already generated a volume mesh for the model, you can run the case directly.

To run the solver:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Run Solver.

Running for More Iterations

You may need to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers for more iterations than you originally set in the Number of Iterations stopping criterion. The Run More Iteration function runs the solver for an additional number of iterations as specified in the stopping criteria. Take, for example, a case where you have already run the simulation for 300 iterations. You specify 500 iterations in the Number of Iterations stopping criterion. When you next click Run for More Iterations, the simulation will run for 500 extra iterations, making 800 iterations in total. The solver runs until one of the stopping criteria is satisfied.

To run for more iterations:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Run For More Iterations.

Clearing the Solution

You can clear all results that were calculated by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers using the Clear Solution function. All other Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX simulation settings remain intact.

Caution: This action is irreversible.

To clear the solution:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, select Clear Solution.

The solution that was calculated by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers is deleted.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 109

Visualizing the Solution

When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches after the solution is calculated, it automatically displays a scalar scene of the model that shows the Absolute Pressure field function.

To visualize the results, you can use this scene to display different scalar quantities, or use any of the other visualization tools in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as streamlines, plane sections and vector scenes.

You can import CAD parts into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes. These parts will not be taken into account during the analysis. This feature is useful for displaying the original geometry in a post-processing scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Importing Geometry Into STAR-CCM+ for Visualization.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Exporting the Surface Mesh

You can export the surface mesh generated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX as a native CD-adapco surface mesh (.dbs) file. The .dbs file format is the recommended format to use when transferring surface data between CD-adapco programs, which are now part of Siemens. The boundary names and boundary types are retained by the file, as well as the interfaces that were automatically created between regions.

To export the surface mesh:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Export > Surface Mesh (.dbs).

Exporting the Volume Mesh

You can export the volume mesh that you generated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX as a native CDadapco volume mesh (.ccm) file. The .ccm file format is the recommended format to use when transferring volume meshes between CD-adapco programs, which are now part of Siemens. The region and boundary names, and region and boundary types are retained in this file. The interfaces that were automatically created interfaces between regions are also retained in this file.

To export the volume mesh:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Export > Volume Mesh (.ccm).

Guidelines

This section aims to provide guidance and assistance on making a geometry part suitable for CFD analysis using Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Contents:

Creating the Fluid Domain

Imprinting Parts

Creating the Fluid Domain

In the majority of CAD models, the fluid domain for analysis must be extracted from the original part or assembly. The topics that are containing within this section demonstrate how to prepare the fluid domain.

Contents:

Internal Flow

External Flow

Multi Region Flow

Internal Flow

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for an internal flow are:

• Work in an assembly. If the original geometry contains only a single part, create a new assembly that contains the part.

• Create an additional part that will close off any openings in the original geometry, these are called “caps”.

• Unite all parts with the caps to obtain one solid part.

• Create an overall block part that encloses all the other parts, this is the “enclosure”.

• Subtract all parts from the enclosure and delete the outer solid body--the remaining geometry is the fluid domain.

A worked example is provided below. In this case the assembly contains two parts: the valve (shown in red), and the valve housing (shown in blue).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 116

1. Load the assembly into NX. If the geometry is a part, insert it into an assembly.

We will now insert a new component into the assembly. This part will close any openings in the assembly using caps.

2. Insert a new component into the assembly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 117

Give this component an appropriate name and then accept the default placement settings. In this case the new component was given the name cap.

3. Make the new component the work part.

4. Select the Extrusion tool and select the outer edge of one of the openings on the geometry, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 118

Ensure that the Type Filter is set to No Selection Filter and that the Selection Scope is set to Entire Assembly, as shown below, otherwise you will only be able to select features from the active part.

5. Perform the same actions for all other openings.

6. Use the Unite operation to join all the parts and form one solid.

In the Unite dialog, select one of the caps you created in the previous step as the Target. Select the other parts (the other cap, valve and valve housing) as the Tool.

7. Hide the original valve and valve housing parts by going to the Assembly Navigator and clicking on the red tick besides each part. These should become greyed out as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 119

The part will appear as shown below.

8. Return the to the assembly and make the assembly the work part.

A new component will be inserted into the assembly. A sketch that encloses the entire assembly will then be created and extruded. The valve, valve housing, and caps will then be subtracted from this, leaving two bodies. The outer body will be deleted, leaving only the internal fluid volume.

9. Insert another component into the assembly and make it the work part.

10.Create a sketch on any plane and sketch a bounding box that will, when extruded, enclose the entire assembly, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 120

11.Subtract the cap part from the internal fluid part.

Select the fluid box as the Target and the caps as the Tool. To be able to select parts through solids, click on the

Highlight Hidden Edges button. Moving the mouse over the geometry will then highlight internal bodies in brown (the default color), as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 121

12.Use the Extract Bodies tool to extract the internal fluid region.

With the Extract Body dialog active, click on any face on the outer body to select it. Note that there is another free-floating solid body enclosed within this body, which will not get selected -- this is the internal fluid volume.

13.Hide the caps geometry.

14.Go to the Part Navigator and suppress the Extracted Body feature. This is done by clicking on the tick next to the feature--when suppressed the tick besides the node will disappear.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 122

15.Suppress the components that you do not want to take part in the analysis, such as the valve, valve housing and caps, by right-clicking on these and selecting Suppression...

16.In the Suppression dialog that appears set the component to Always Suppressed and click on OK.

The extracted internal fluid volume is shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 123

The geometry is now ready for the CAD client analysis. Deactivated parts in an assembly will not be included in the analysis. Suppressed parts in an assembly will not be included in the analysis. In the above example, it is recommended that you extend the inlet and outlet regions to appropriate lengths so that a fully developed flow can be achieved before reaching the valve and to help reduce recirculation at the outlet.

External Flow

The generation of a domain for external aerodynamics is generally easier than for internal flow cases but the sizing of the domain is more critical. As a guideline (assuming a specific situation is not being modelled i.e. flow in a wind tunnel) the domain should be sized as follows:

• Inlet: 2 x part length from the front of the part

• Outlet: 4 x part length from the rear of the part

• Sides: 3 x part width from the side of the part

• Ceiling: 4 x part height from the top of the part

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for an external flow are:

• Work in an assembly. If the original geometry contains only a single part, create a new assembly that contains the part.

• Create an overall block part that encloses all the other parts. The shape and size should correspond to the desired fluid domain.

• Subtract all parts from the overall block part - the remaining geometry is the fluid domain.

An example case is shown below. In this example a geometry of a car will be used.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 124

1. Load the assembly in NX. If the geometry is a part file, insert this into an assembly.

2. If the geometry is symmetrical, cut this in half to save on computation costs.

The easiest way of doing this is to perform an extrusion to remove the unwanted half.

3. Insert a new component into the assembly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 125

4. Give this component an appropriate name and then accept the default placement settings. In this example, the component was called domain.

5. Make the new component the active part, right click on it in the feature tree and select Make Work Part.

6. Create a sketch on the symmetry plane of the geometry. This sketch will represent the fluid domain profile.

7. Extrude the sketch to an appropriate length to complete the domain creation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 126

8. Subtract the car geometry from the domain geometry. This is done using the Subtract feature.

9. In the Subtract dialog, select the domain as the Target and the car as the Tool.

Ensure that the Type Filter is set to No Selection Filter and that the Selection Scope is set to Entire Assembly, as shown below, otherwise you will only be able to select the active part.

10.Hide the car part, by clicking on the tick next to the part. Once done, the tick will be greyed out.

The final result is shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 127

Multi Region Flow

This section shows how to create the fluid domain for multiple regions such as rotating machinery and porous media flow.

For the numerical assumptions made using the Moving Reference Frame (MRF) technique to hold true, a minimum of two cells need to be present between the rotating-static interface and any wall boundaries (for example the fan blades), and the rotating region must be circular in section. Where there is a large clearance between the rotating object and any static objects, it is advisable to avoid placing the interface too close to either hence facilitating a small cell size on the interface. Where there is a small clearance between the rotating and static parts, there is little choice but to place the interface approximately midway between the two.

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for multiple regions are:

• Work in an assembly. If the original geometry contains only a single part, create a new assembly that contains the part.

• Create an additional part that will enclose the rotating region (for example a fan) and subtract it from the part. In the case of a porous region, a separate part will be required for this as well.

• Create an additional part for the main static domain (the inlet and outlet regions) and subtract any obstructions/features that may be present there (for example the fan motor support arms on a fan casing).

In this example, a fan and fan case are used.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 128

1. Load the assembly into NX.

2. Insert a new empty component into the assembly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 129

Give this component an appropriate name and then accept the default placement settings. In this example the new component was given the name Rotating Region.

3. Make the new component the work part by right-clicking on its node in the assembly navigator and selecting Make Work Part.

4. Hide the Fan part by going to the assembly navigator and clicking on the red tick besides the part.

The tick will turn grey and the part will not be visible in the geometry window.

5. Create a sketch on the contact face of the fan casing (where the fan and the fan casing are coincident).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 130

6. If the continuous auto dimensioning feature of NX is turned on, disable it by clicking on the Continuous Auto Dimensioning button in the toolbar.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 131

7. Draw a circle that shares the same center point as the sketch plane face.

The size of the circle is not important at this stage as it will be made coincident with the innermost edge of the fan casing in a later step.

8. Ensure that the Type Filter is set to No Selection Filter and that the Selection Scope is set to Entire Assembly, as shown below, otherwise you will not be able to select edges from other parts.

9. Click on the Project Curve button in the toolbar

If this button is missing from the toolbar, you may need to click on the (Open in Sketch Task Environment) button to open the active sketch in the sketch task environment.

The Project Curve dialog appears.

10.Select the innermost edge of the fan casing.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 132

11.Exit the dialog.

A message will appear warning you that the projection will not be associative. Click on Yes to accept and close the dialog.

12.Right-click on the projected edge and select Convert to Reference.

13.Click on the Constraints button in the toolbar.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 133

The Constraints dialog will appear.

14.Select the circle and the innermost edge of the fan casing, as shown below.

This will add new options in the Constraints dialog.

15.Click on the Equal Radius button to make the circle and the projected edge have the same radius.

The circle will snap to the projected edge, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 134

16.Hide the fan casing and show the fan.

17.Extrude the sketch so that it fully encloses the fan.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 135

Ensure that no boolean operations are set to take place in the Extrude dialog -- these might result in an error during the extrusion.

18.Use the boolean subtract operation to remove the fan from the Rotating Region.

You can use the See-Thru view with the Highlight Hidden Edges button to see and select the fan inside the Rotating Region.

Hiding the fan and using the See-Thru view will show the result of this operation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 136

19.Return to the assembly and make the assembly the work part.

20.Hide the fan part; this will no longer be required.

21.Insert another component into the assembly as previously described and make that the work part.

22.Use the Extrude tool and select the existing outer edge on the front face of the Rotating Region. To make it easier to see which is the front face, use the see-thru tool.

The preview of the extrude is shown below.

Imprinting Parts

Most CAD model assemblies are not suitable for meshing as the parts in the assembly are disjointed, where the coincident faces are overlapping. Attempting to generate a mesh with such an assembly will result in a meshing error. To rectify this problem, the parts in an assembly must be imprinted together.

Imprinting can also be used to split surfaces for boundary region applications. An example of such an application would be to model the area that a fan would occupy on the inside of computer case, such as in the third Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX tutorial, where a smaller section of the surface is needed to represent the fan, rather than the entire inner surface of the computer case.

Contents:

Imprinting Parts in an Assembly

Imprinting Surfaces on Parts for Boundary Region Applications

Imprinting Parts in an Assembly

In cases containing multiple adjacent parts, such as in Conjugate Heat Transfer cases, it is essential to imprint the profiles of the coincident faces of the smaller parts onto the face of the larger part. This will ensure that the volume mesh created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ contains interfaces between the adjacent parts.

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for multiple regions are:

• Work within the assembly, making the part that requires imprinting the work part.

• Create a sketch on the face you want to imprint, and project the contact edges of the other components in the assembly onto this sketch.

• Split the face you want to imprint using the sketch created in the previous step.

The simple circuit board shown below requires imprinting before the mesh can be generated.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 141

In this example, the capacitors and heat sinks are not imprinted to the circuit board. This would result in a failure when attempting to generate a mesh.

To imprint the capacitors and heat sinks onto the circuit board follow the steps outlined below:

1. Load the assembly file in NX.

2. Make the part that will be imprinted the Work Part, right click on the part’s node in the feature tree.

In this example this is the base board.

3. Use the See-Thru button from the toolbar to make the other parts translucent.

4. Create a new sketch on the surface that requires imprinting.

5. Click on the Project Curve button on the toolbar.

If this button is missing from the toolbar, you may need to click on the (Open in Sketch Task Environment) button to open the active sketch in the sketch task environment.

The Project Curve dialog will appear.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 142

6. Click on the contact face of the other parts to select the contact edges, as shown below.

7. Clicking OK in the Project Curve dialog will bring up message informing you that the projected edges will not be associative. Click on Yes to accept and continue.

8. Click on the Divide Face button in the toolbar.

The Divide Face dialog will appear.

9. In the Faces to Divide box, select the face you want to imprint.

10.In the Dividing Objects box, select the sketch that contains the contact edges of the other parts.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 143

11.Ensure that the projection direction (the arrow in the geometry window) is pointing towards the face to be imprinted.

This can be reversed by clicking on the Reverse Direction button in the Projection Direction box.

12.Return to the assembly and make the assembly the work part.

The contact edges of the capacitors and heat sinks have now been imprinted onto the base board. This can be verified by the parts in the assembly.

A high quality mesh with fully defined interfaces can now be successfully generated for this assembly. Suppressed parts are not included in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ analysis, so for CHT cases, such as the above example, ensure that all relevant parts are active.

Imprinting Surfaces on Parts for Boundary Region Applications

Faces in a part body can be split into smaller faces for boundary application.

The general procedure to follow is:

• Create a sketch on the surface you want to split. The shape of the sketch should correspond to the shape of the new face after it is split.

• Split the face that requires imprinting with the sketch containing the profiles.

A simple example of an aeration tank is shown below. The image shows the tank, the two air injectors need to be imprinted onto the base of the tank.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 144

1. Load the part into NX.

2. Create a sketch on the face that requires imprinting.

In this case the bottom face of the tank needs imprinting.

3. Draw the profile of the boundary you want imprinted.

In this case, the air injectors are circular in profile.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 145

You can use <Shift> + <F8> to change the view so that it is normal to the sketch plane.

4. Use the Divide Face function to split the face.

Select the face you want to divide for the Faces to Divide field, and the sketch profile(s) you created in the previous step as the Dividing Objects.

The face is now imprinted; each face can be selected independently of each other, and can be used when defining boundaries.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 146

The separate faces can now be defined as boundary regions.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 147

This tutorial takes you through the steps that are required to run a CFD calculation in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX environment.

For this tutorial, the model is a modern deicing system that is used on aircraft wings. The hot air from the aircraft’s jet engine is used to heat the leading edge of the wing.

Opening the CAD Model

This directory is located in the starnx folder of the downloaded tutorials bundle. To download the tutorials bundle, go to https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/product/226870983/downloads, and follow the procedure outlined in the main STAR-CCM+ > Tutorials > Using Tutorial Macros and Files > Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal section of the user guide.

1. Copy the directory to your own disk space and open the part file piccoloAssem.prt in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

The assembly is made up of two parts: the solid leading edge wing skin, and the internal air region.

The imported geometry is shown below.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon appears at the top of the screen.The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX object tree is located on the left of the screen.

To switch to this object tree:

2. Click (STAR Tree).

If these items are not visible, refer to Launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Manually.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 188

Selecting Fluid Physics Models

The first step in setting up this tutorial is to modify the physics continuum that is used to model air. For this case, the flow is turbulent and thermal. Temperature calculations are on by default in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Modify the initial conditions:

1. Right-click the Continua > Continuum node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX tree and select Edit.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. Set Name to Air.

3. Set the Equation of State to Ideal Gas.

4. Click to expand the Initialization tab.

5. Set (Temperature) to 400 K.

6. Click OK to close the dialog.

Adding Solid Physics Models

The next step in setting up this tutorial is to define the physics continuum of the solid to be used.

1. Right-click the Continua node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX object tree and select Add Continuum.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. Set Name to Al.

3. Set Material Type to Solid.

4. Set Material Name to Aluminum Alloy

5. Click to expand the Initialization tab.

6. Set (Temperature) to 400 K.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 189

7. Click OK.

Setting the Solid Region

Create a new solid region for the wing skin:

1. Right-click the Regions node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX object tree and select Add Region.

The Region Settings dialog appears.

2. Select the wing skin as shown below.

Once selected, the part becomes highlighted.

3. Set Name to Leading Edge.

4. Set Continuum Selection to Al.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 190

This action assigns the aluminum alloy that you created earlier as the material for this region.

5. Click OK.

Now that the solid region of the wing is defined, rename the default region to something more appropriate:

6. Right-click the Regions > Region node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX tree and select Rename.

7. Enter Internal Air as the new name.

8. Click a blank area to accept the name change.

Defining Boundary Conditions for the Fluid Region

Create the inlet and outlet boundary conditions. Use symmetry boundaries on the side walls to extend the simulation domain. Use a wall boundary with a fixed temperature to model the piccolo walls.

Create the inlet boundary first:

1. Right-click the Regions > Internal Air > Boundaries node and select Add Boundary.

The Boundary Settings dialog appears.

2. On the CAD model, select the three faces that are highlighted below.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 191

These selections are reported in the Face Selection box in the Boundary Settings dialog.

3. Set the following properties:

Type Velocity Inlet

Boundary Name Inlet

(Normal Velocity ) 90 m/s

(Temperature) 460 K

(Turbulence Intensity) 0.135

(Turbulent Length Scale ) 2.2e-005 m

4. Click OK.

Create the outlet boundary:

6. Select the face that is highlighted below.

Defining Boundary Conditions for the Solid Region

Use the convection boundary condition to model the heat propagation from the solid wing.

The convective boundary condition models ambient conditions on the outside of the domain. Use convection to model the heat propagation in the solid wing skin.

Create the symmetry boundary first:

1. Right-click the Regions > Leading Edge > Boundaries node and select Add Boundary.

The Boundary Settings dialog appears.

2. Select the two faces highlighted below, one on either side of the geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 195

3. Set the following parameters:

Parameter Value

Type Symmetry Plane

Name Solid Symmetry

4. Click OK.

Modify the default boundary so that it uses convection:

5. Right-click the Regions > Leading Edge > Boundaries > Default node and select Edit.

The Boundary Settings dialog appears.

6. Set the following properties:

Parameter Value

Thermal Specification Convection

(Heat Transfer Coefficient ) 100 W/m^2.K

(Temperature ) 228 K

7. Click OK.

8. Save your progress.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Setting the Coincident Faces Tolerance

The geometry that is used in this tutorial has large changes in feature size and requires you to reduce the Coincident Faces Detection Tolerance.

1. Right-click Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and select Geometry Transfer Settings.

The Geometry Transfer Settings dialog appears.

2. Set (Coincident Faces Tolerance) to 0.0001.
