Creating a Part Mesh Control

Create a part mesh control to disable the prism layer generation in the solid region. Solid regions do not require prism layers.

1. Right-click Mesh Pipelines > Mesh Pipeline > Mesh Controls in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX tree and select Add Part Mesh Control.

The Part Mesh Control Settings dialog appears.

2. Select the solid wing region on the CAD model.

The selection is added to the Part Selection box.

3. Set Name to Solid Region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 200

4. In the Prism Layer box, set (Prism layer option) to Disable using the drop-down menu.

5. Click OK.

Creating a Face Mesh Control

Create a face mesh control to reduce the size of the prism layer thickness at the inlet boundary.

1. Right-click Mesh Pipelines > Mesh Pipeline > Mesh Controls in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX tree and select Add Face Mesh Control.

The Face Mesh Control Settings dialog appears.

2. Select the cylindrical faces that are perpendicular to the inlet boundary, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 201

3. Set Name to Inlet Refinement.

4. Activate the Custom Mesh Size option.

5. Activate the Absolute option.

6. Set (Mesh Size) to 0.00025 m.

7. In the Prism Layer box, set (Prism Layer Option) to Use Custom Values.

8. Set Layer Thickness Option to Absolute.

9. Set (Layer Thickness) to 0.0002 m.

10.Click OK.

Modifying Solution Controls

Modify the maximum number of iterations and the solution accuracy. To help accelerate convergence, edit the solid under-relaxation factor:

1. Click Solution Controls on the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 202

The Solution Controls dialog appears.

2. Set the following parameters:

Parameter Value

(Number of Iterations) 500

(Convergence Level) 0.01

(Solid Temperature Under-Relaxation Factor) 0.9999

3. Click OK.

4. Save your progress.

Building and Running

The case is now ready to run.

To run the simulation:

1. From the ribbon, click Build and Run.

The Residuals plot appears in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX Output window. You can use this plot to monitor the convergence of the solution.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 205

When the solver is done, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches.

Post-Processing Results

You perform all post-processing in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. By default, a scalar scene, Scalar Scene 1, automatically appears in the Graphics window when the solver finishes. This scene displays the absolute total pressure.

The results that are contained in the following sections are representative. You may see some variation in the results that you obtain, depending on what platform and package you are using.

1. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, click File > Save to save the simulation.

Creating A Scalar Scene

Create a scalar scene containing a cross-section of the model. Plot temperature on this section to demonstrate how the hot gas coming from the piccolo tube affects the wing skin and the air inside the wing.

To create the scene:

1. Right-click the Scenes node in the explorer pane and select New Scene > Scalar.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 206

A new scalar scene, Scalar Scene 2, is created and selected in the Graphics window.

2. Right-click the Derived Parts node and select New Part > Section > Plane....

The Create Plane Section dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 207

3. Set the origin coordinates to [0.0 mm, 0.0 mm, 18.4 mm].

4. Set the normal vector to [0.0 mm, 0.0 mm, 1.0 mm].

5. In the Display group box, select Existing Displayer, and select Scalar 1 from the drop-down menu.

6. Click Create followed by Close.

Change the scalar field to display temperature contours:

7. Click Scene/Plot.

8. Navigate to Scalar Scene 2 > Scalar 1 > Scalar Field.

9. Set Function to Temperature.

Modify the contour style to have a smooth transition between the different temperature values in the scene:

10.Navigate to Scalar Scene 2 > Scalar 1.

11.Set Contour Style to Smooth Filled.

Adjust the outlines in the scene to show only the plane section:

12.Right-click Scalar Scene 2 > Outline 1 > Parts and select Edit....

The Parts dialog appears.

13.Right-click on a blank area and choose Deselect All.

14.Select the Derived Parts > plane section node.

15.Click OK.

16.Position the scene to show the side view of the geometry.

17.Click simulation.

18.Click (Save) to save the simulation.

The finished scene is shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 208

Visualizing the Wing Skin Temperature

Create another scalar scene to display the temperature on the wing skin geometry.

To create another scalar scene:

1. Right-click the Scenes node in the explorer pane and select New Scene > Scalar.

A new scalar scene, Scalar Scene 3, is created and selected in the Graphics window.

2. Click Scene/Plot.

3. Right-click Scalar Scene 3 > Scalar 1 > Parts and select Edit....

The Parts dialog appears.

4. Expand the Regions node and select the Leading Edge node.

5. Click OK.

6. Navigate to Scalar Scene 3 > Scalar 1 > Scalar Field.

7. Set Function to Temperature.

To have a smooth transition between the different temperature values, edit the contour style:

8. Navigate to Scalar Scene 3 > Scalar 1.

9. Set Contour Style to Smooth Filled.

Adjust the outlines to appear on the solid region only:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 209

10.Right-click Scalar Scene 3 > Outline 1 > Parts and select Edit....

11.In the Parts dialog, expand the Regions node and deselect the Internal Air node.

12.Click OK.

13.Reorient the geometry to get a better view of the leading edge.

14.Click Simulation.

15.Save the simulation.

The finished scene is shown below.

Creating a Streamlines Scene

Create streamlines to get a better understanding of how the hot air flows inside the leading edge of the wing.

First, create a geometry scene:

1. Right-click the Scenes node in the object tree and select New Scene > Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 210

A new geometry scene, Geometry Scene 1, is created and selected in the Graphics window.

2. Click Scene/Plot.

3. Navigate to the Geometry Scene 1 > Surface 1 node.

4. Set Opacity to 0.1.

Next, create the streamlines:

5. Click Simulation.

6. Right-click the Derived Parts node and select New Part > Streamline....

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 211

The Create Streamline dialog appears.

7. In the Input Parts box, click Select....

8. In the Select Objects dialog, expand the Regions node and deselect Leading Edge.

9. Click OK to close the Select Objects dialog.

10.Make sure that Part Seed is selected in the Seed Mode section.

11.Set Seed Parts to Regions > Internal Air > Boundaries > Inlet.

12.Set Part U-Resolution to 10.

13.Set Part V-Resolution to 10.

14.Make sure that New Streamline Displayer is selected in the Display section.

15.Click Create followed by Close.

The streamlines do not yet appear in the geometry scene. Follow the steps that are outlined below to modify the streamlines:

16.Navigate to Derived Parts > Streamline > Source Seed.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 212

17.Activate the Randomize option.

18.Navigate to Derived Parts > Streamline > 2nd Order Integrator.

19.Set Maximum Propagation to 0.3.

Adjust the appearance of the streamlines to display tubes instead of the default lines:

20.Click Scene/Plot.

21.Navigate to Geometry Scene 1 > Streamline Stream 1.

22.Set Mode to Tubes and Width to 0.00025.

Adjust the scalar field of the streamlines to display temperature:

23.Navigate to Geometry Scene 1 > Streamline Stream 1 > Scalar Field.

24.Set Function to Temperature.

Turn off the outlines in the geometry scene to have a better view of the streamlines.

25.Right-click the Geometry Scene 1 > Outline 1 and select Toggle Visibility.

26.Reorient the geometry to get a better view of the leading edge.

27.Save the simulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 213

The finished scene is shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 214

Rotating Flow Inside a Graphics Card

This tutorial takes you through the steps that are required to run a CFD calculation in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX environment.

For this tutorial, the model is a fully sealed graphics card that is located inside an empty, idealized PC tower case. The geometry that is used in this tutorial has been simplified in order to decrease the computational cost. As a consequence the mesh is relatively coarse at approximately 200,000 cells compared to the 3-4 million cells used for an industrial analysis.

Opening the CAD Model

A directory containing the CAD geometry is provided with the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ distribution.

This directory is located in the starnx folder of the downloaded tutorials bundle. To download the tutorials bundle, go to https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/product/226870983/downloads, and follow the procedure outlined in the main STAR-CCM+ > Tutorials > Using Tutorial Macros and Files > Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal section of the user guide.

1. Copy the directory to your own disk space and open the part file gpuAssem.prt in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

The assembly is made up of two parts: the PC tower case (including the GPU housing), and the rotating region that encloses the blower fan of the GPU.

The imported geometry is shown below.

Selecting Fluid Physics Models

The first step in setting up this tutorial is to define the physics of the problem. For this case, the flow is turbulent and isothermal. Temperature calculations are on by default in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 217

To turn temperature calculations off:

1. Right-click the Continua > Continuum node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX tree and select Edit.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. Deactivate the Temperature option in the Optional Physics Models box.

3. Click OK.

Setting the Rotating Region

Create the rotating region that contains the GPU fan:

1. Right-click the Regions node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX object tree and select Add Region.

The Region Settings dialog appears.

2. Select the disc that is located inside the graphics card housing.

You can select this part from within the PC tower by right-clicking the disc and selecting Select from List... > Solid Body in GPUBLOWERFAN from the Quick Pick dialog.

Once selected, the part becomes highlighted as shown below.

Property Value

Y -1.9434

Geometry Transfer: CAD to Simulation

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX allows you to transfer geometry from NX to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ through a direct link between the two packages.

This feature provides you with a workflow that is tailored to design optimization. You can apply changes to the geometry in either Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and the changes are passed back to the other program. For example, you can make changes to the design after running an analysis in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ environment and these changes are passed back to the original NX file. This feature requires a CAD client license.

This tutorial demonstrates how to select the CAD parameters in your original geometry and transfer the geometry from NX to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you proceed to create a repeatable workflow (or pipeline) using mesh operations. After setting up this pipeline, you can make further changes to the geometry design and have STAR-CCM+ regenerate the corresponding volume mesh.

Contents:

Opening the CAD Model

Transferring the Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Creating the Shape Parts and Operations

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Modifying the Design

Opening the CAD Model

To download the tutorials bundle, go to https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/product/226870983/downloads, and follow the procedure outlined in the main STAR-CCM+ > Tutorials > Using Tutorial Macros and Files > Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal section of the user guide.

2. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and open the assembly file cardAssem.prt.

Transferring the Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX, choose the CAD parameters to expose to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and then transfer the geometry.

Specify the CAD parameters to transfer to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

The Design Data dialog appears.

6. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, create a geometry scene and position the geometry as shown below.

7. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, expand the Geometry node.

The transferred geometry appears under the Parts node. The properties that control the connection back to NX, including the CAD parameter value, appear under the CAD Client Models node.

When transferring geometry from NX to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, a link exists between the two software packages. This link allows data to be transferred between the two packages. To maintain this link, you must first save the geometry file in NX:

8. Switch to NX and save the geometry file.

In response, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ saves the simulation file with the name of the NX geometry file. Using this technique, you can rename or relocate both the geometry and simulation files without breaking the

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 265

link between the two packages. You can also save the simulation file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ so long as you do not rename it or relocate it. Doing so will break the link between the packages.

Creating the Shape Parts and Operations

The transferred geometry consists of the card housing and the blower fan. To simulate this case, you require two regions: one static region that provides an enclosure for the simulation, and another for the rotating region around the fan.

The transferred geometry contains the solid parts. You require the fluid volume around these parts. The first stage in obtaining the fluid volume is to create part shapes that correspond to the two regions. To save time, you are provided with these part shapes, one for the enclosure, and another for the rotating region.

Import the shape parts:

1. Select File  > Import > Import Surface Mesh.

2. Import the part shapes:

a) In the Open dialog, navigate to the directory that you downloaded in the first section of this tutorial and select box.x_t and disc.x_t.

b) Click Open.

c) In the Import Surface Options dialog, deactivate the Open Geometry Scene After Import option.

d) Click OK.

The static region, box, is shown below in relation to the graphics card:

The rotating region, disc, is show below in relation to the graphics card:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 266

Now subtract the solid CAD geometry from these shape parts to obtain the final fluid volume. Begin by subtracting the blower fan geometry from the disc part:

3. Right-click the Operations node and select New > Boolean > Subtract.

Property Setting

Input Parts disc

cardAssem > blowerFan

Target Parts disc

5. Click OK.

6. Rename the Operations > Subtract node to Fan Subtraction.

7. Rename Parts > Subtract node to Rotating Region.

Subtract the card housing geometry and the disc part from the static region:

Property Setting

Input Parts box

disc

cardAssem > cardCase

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 267

Property Setting

Target Parts box

9. Rename Operations > Subtract node to Card Subtraction.

10.Rename Parts > Subtract node to Static Region.

To get a conformal mesh between the two regions, imprint both fluid volumes together:

12.In the Create Imprint Operation dialog, select Rotating Region and Static Region and click OK.

The transferred geometry contains CAD data. To ensure best results, instruct all operations to use the CAD data where available:

13.Under the Operations node, multi-select the Fan Subtraction and Card Subtraction nodes and activate the Perform CAD Boolean option.

14.Select the Operations > Imprint node and set Merge/Imprint Method to CAD Imprint.

The contacts between the two parts are created. These contacts are used while creating the regions to define the interfaces between the regions.

Execute all operations:

15.Right-click on the Operations node and select Execute All.

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Assign the parts to regions and create the automated mesh operation.

Assign the fluid parts to regions:

1. Expand the Geometry > Parts node and multi-select the Rotating Region and Static Region nodes.

2. Right-click on one of the selected parts and choose Assign Parts to Regions....

a) Select Create a Region for Each Part.

b) Select Create a Boundary for Each Part Surface.

c) Click Apply and Close.

Create the automated mesh operation:

5. In the Create Automated Mesh Operation dialog:

a) From the Parts list, select Rotating Region and Static Region.

b) Select the following meshers, in order:

Group Mesher

An automated mesh operation is added to the Operations node. Refine the mesh settings for this case:

8. Select the Prism Layer Total Thickness node and set Percentage of Base to 20.

Generate the volume mesh:

◦ Rotating Region > Boundaries > cardAssem.blowerFan.Faces

◦ Static Region > Boundaries > cardAssem.cardCase.Faces

You can exit Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and NX and maintain the link between the two packages. To demonstrate, in the following steps you save the simulation and exit both applications. In the next section, you will resume the simulation and continue where you left off.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

In this tutorial, you modify the number of blades on the graphics card blower fan from 10 to 15 blades.

To re-establish the link between NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you must load the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX first and transfer the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Resume the analysis and re-establish the link between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. Launch NX with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX and load cardAssem.prt.

2. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX ribbon, click Transfer Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and the CAD geometry is transferred over.

3. Switch to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

4. Open the geometry scene to visualize the initial geometry representation.

5. Expand the Geometry > CAD Client Models > cardAssem.prt > CAD Parameters node.

6. Select the blowerFan.prt\p60 node and set Parameter Value to 15.

A yellow warning icon appears on the CAD parameter node as well as the assembly node. This icon indicates that the CAD Client Model is out of date.

To update the model:

7. Right-click the cardAssem.prt node and select Update Model.

The geometry updates in the scene. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ passes the change in the design back to NX.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 270

8. Switch back to NX and view the updated geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for NX 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 271

The pipeline you set up is fully repeatable. To update the volume mesh:

9. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, open the mesh scene.

10.Click (Generate Volume Mesh).

The volume mesh updates to reflect the changes in the design.

All boundaries and boundary conditions that you set are maintained after this change. This feature reduces the amount of work that is required when analyzing multiple designs.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Add-on provides you with straightforward access to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver from within the Creo environment.

Standard physics models, including turbulence, ideal gas, heat transfer, and gravity are supported for single body cases. Multiple body simulations involving conjugate heat transfer, rotating reference frames, and porous media are also supported. Advanced physics models can be added to the simulation by either launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and selecting them directly, or by implementing additional Java macro commands.

This section contains the user guide and tutorials for the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo CAD client.

You can use Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo to transfer your CAD geometry directly into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ without transferring the CAE settings. This method is an alternate way importing geometry to using the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ CAD translators. See Transferring Geometry to STAR-CCM+.

Introducing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo provides you with straightforward access to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver from within the Creo environment.

Standard physics models, including turbulence, ideal gas, heat transfer, and gravity are supported for single body cases. Multiple body simulations involving conjugate heat transfer, rotating reference frames, and porous media are also supported. Advanced physics models can be added to the simulation by either launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and selecting them directly, or by implementing additional Java macro commands.

Contents:

What are the Capabilities?

Getting Started

Common Functions

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on Different Machines

See Also:

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

What are the Capabilities?

This section highlights the capabilities of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo enables you to:

• Define flow characteristics for the simulation

• Specify mesh parameters and controls

• Execute the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, with specified solution controls

• Post-process results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

• Use parallel processing

Problem Definition

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo provides an interface for the specification of continua, regions, and boundaries in order to define the CFD simulation. This information is then used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to calculate a solution and present results.

The particular solver options that you can currently select through the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo interface include:

• Turbulence

◦ k-e Model

◦ Laminar

• Temperature

◦ Thermal Modelling

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 4

◦ Conjugate Heat Transfer

• Equation of State

◦ Constant Density

◦ Ideal Gas

• Porous Media

◦ Isotropic

◦ Uni-Directional

• Moving Reference Frames

• Energy Source

• Gravity

• Passive Scalar

Meshing

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo provides you with a transparent interface to Simcenter STAR-CCM+’s surface and volume meshing tools. This allows you to generate high-quality meshes using a solid model that was built within the Creo environment. The specific meshing functionality includes:

• Surface meshing using the surface remesher for optimum mesh quality

• Prismatic subsurface meshing in the volume mesh for capturing near-wall boundary layers

• Volume meshing of parts with either:

◦ Tetrahedral core mesh generation

◦ Polyhedral core mesh generation

◦ Trimmed hexahedral core mesh generation

• Automatic handling of region-to-region interfaces

Running the Solver

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo allows the generation of solutions with varying accuracy and speed by providing the following solver controls:

• Number of iterations

• Stopping criterion at which to assume convergence

• Discretization scheme (1st or 2nd order)

• Solver under-relaxation factors

• Additional commands using Java macros

Post-processing

As post-processing is carried out in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, a wide range of tools are available for analysis. These include:

• Scalar scenes

• Vector scenes

• Streamlines

• Isosurfaces

• Plane sections

• Reports

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 5

• Plots

Parallel Processing

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo supports parallel processing for mesh generation and solver calculations. You can set up parallel processing in the Preferences dialog. The different Simcenter STAR-CCM+ licensing options can also be selected here. See Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing.

Launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Manually

By default, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo starts automatically when you launch Creo. The STAR-Creo Info App window appears, along with the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo object tree and ribbon.

If this does not happen, you can manually launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo by following the steps outlined below:

1. Start Creo.

2. Create an empty part or load an existing part.

3. In the ribbon, select Auxiliary Applications from the Tools tab.

The Auxiliary Applications dialog appears.

4. Click Register....

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6

5. Browse to the protk.dat file in your Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo installation directory.

Typically this file is located in C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\STARCAD[VERSION]\STAR-Creo.

6. Select this file and click Open.

A entry stating that starproe.dllNot Running appears in the Auxiliary Applications dialog.

7. Select this entry and click Start.

The STAR-Creo Info App window appears and the checks for licensing begin. If everything is in order, a Licensing successful message appears in the Status page of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Info App window, and the StarCreo.dll Not Running message vanishes from the Auxiliary Applications dialog.

8. Click Close in the Auxiliary Applications dialog.

9. Close the open geometry file and reopen it again.

The ( Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo) icon appears on the left of the screen when you load or create a geometry file. Click on this icon to display the object tree.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon also appears.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Info App Window

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Info App window automatically appears when you start Creo.

Initially, this window only contains the Status tab which displays the version and licensing information for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo. More tabs appear as you create or load geometry files in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, allowing you to perform more actions.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7

You cannot close the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Info App window while Creo or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo are running. Attempting to close the window by clicking the X button returns a message in the Status tab informing you of this. You can maximize and minimize the window by clicking the - and _ buttons respectively.

Use the Clear button to clear all the information that is displayed in a particular tab.

Use the Abort button to stop active processes, such as surface/volume meshing, or the solver. This button only appears when you can stop a process — it is grayed out at all other times.

A clock is displayed in the bottom-left of the window. This clock displays the current time on your machine. A progress bar is located next to the clock and reports the progress of various processes, such as mesh generation and the solver.

More information on the various tabs is provided in the following sections:

• The Status Tab

• The Output Tab

• The Model Checker Tab

• The Residuals Tab

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 8

The Status Tab

The Status tab displays the licensing information for your current session, informing you whether the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo license checked out successfully. The version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo is also displayed in this tab. This tab appears by default when you launch Creo without a geometry file.

The Output Tab

The Output tab appears once you create or open a geometry file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 9

During the meshing process, this tab displays status information along with a brief report on the generated mesh. If errors were encountered during the meshing process, they are reported here with suggestions as to what can be causing them.

When the solver is running, the Output tab behaves like the output window in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, displaying the data for each residual per iteration. When the solver finishes running, the same information is also displayed in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Output window.

You can control the amount of information that is displayed in the Output tab by editing the verbosity in the config.xml file. See Modifying the Config.xml File.

To abort the mesher or solver, click the Abort button.

The Model Checker Tab

The Model Checker tab displays information from the live model checker, where the case setup is actively monitored for any problems. See Checking the Model for Errors.

The following example reports that the case has no inlet boundary defined.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 10

The Residuals Tab

The Residuals tab appears when you launch the solver. Use the residuals to monitor the convergence of the solution being calculated.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11

Typically, a drop in three to five orders of magnitude in the residuals indicates that the solution has converged to an acceptable level. The residuals that are displayed in this tab also appear in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ under the Plots node.

You can zoom in to the residuals by clicking and holding the left mouse button in the graph area and drawing a box around the area you want to view. To zoom out, right-click in the graph area. You can hide individual residuals from the Residuals tab by clicking their label at the top of the plot window.

Modifying the config.xml File

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ requires a configuration file to enable it to find the appropriate components to run correctly. This configuration file is created during installation. An explanation of the file and settings within it is given here.

The configuration file is called config.xml. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo searches for this file in the installation directory.

Typical config.xml content is shown below. In this example Simcenter STAR-CCM+ version 15.06.### is shown.

<CAD> <STAR_HOME>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\star</ STAR_HOME> <SOLVER>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\star\bin \starccm+.exe</SOLVER>

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 12

<LOGFILE>starcad.log</LOGFILE> <WWHELP>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.### \win64\Intel11.1\wwhelp.exe</WWHELP> <MANDIR>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\doc\en \online</MANDIR> <VERBOSITY>Normal</VERBOSITY> <!-- Can be Verbose, Log or Normal. Default Normal --> </CAD>

You can edit the following lines:

• <SOLVER> provides the location of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver executable. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ licensing options are set in the Preferences dialog in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo user interface. See Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing.

• <LOGFILE> is the log file that will automatically be created and saved when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo is run. A path of your choice can be used.

• <VERBOSITY> is the verbosity of the output window in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Info App. This can be set to one of the following:

◦ Normal—This is the default setting and will display the least amount of information in the Output panel.

◦ Verbose—This will display a moderate amount of information in the Output panel.

◦ Log—This will display all available information in the Output panel.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Object Tree

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo uses an object tree as the primary method for setting parameters.

The object tree consists of nodes, each one of which represents a particular component of the simulation. This approach to the user interface complements the method that is used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+, allowing for an easy transition between the two software packages.

The object tree appears slightly different in assembly mode as it must accommodate multiple parts, but the principles of operation remain the same.

Nodes are arranged in an order that follows the recommended workflow for setting up a simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo. At each stage, you typically right-click on a particular node in the tree and choose the appropriate action from the pop-up menu.

Certain functionality within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo applies to the simulation as a whole, rather than to individual objects. These operations are provided in the ribbon.

A complete list of all functions and their respective location is included in Understanding the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Interface.

Clicking on the Region node within the object tree will highlight all the relevant faces on the geometry model for that particular region. If different parts are assigned to multiple regions, then clicking on a region will only highlight the part and faces associated with that specific region. For example, clicking on the Fluid node below will highlight all the faces associated with the Fluid region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 16

Similarly, clicking on the Solid node highlights all the faces associated with the Solid region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 17

Clicking on a boundary node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo object tree highlights all the faces on the CAD geometry model that are associated with it. Note that clicking on the Default boundary node will not highlight any faces on the CAD geometry model. To stop highlighting the faces, you can either click on a blank space in the geometry window, or click on the root node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo object tree.

Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing

The licensing options and the options for setting up parallel processing are located in the Preferences dialog.

This dialog provides two sets of options: server preferences and server settings.

• Server preferences are applied whenever Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo starts a server.

• Server settings are saved in the CAD file and are applied only to that CAD file. Click Save as Default Server Settings to save the current server settings as the default settings to be applied to all CAD files.

To modify the run mode and licensing options:

1. Select Preferences from the ribbon.

The Preferences dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 18

2. Set up the licensing behavior for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo:

◦ To enable Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo in the current session, activate the Activate option. This action checks out the star-proe feature license. This option is activated by default.

◦ To automatically start Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo when you launch Creo, activate the Activate on Startup option. This action checks out the star-proe feature license. This option is activated by default.

Note: If you update the geometry in disconnected mode then this setting is ignored.

3. Select the run mode:

▶For serial, set Run Mode to Serial (the default setting).

▶For parallel, set Run Mode to Parallel and Compute Processes to the desired number of cores.

You can use the up/down buttons or you can type in the number of cores that you want to use.

▶For advanced licensing options, such as Power on Demand, enter the appropriate argument in the Command field.

For Power on Demand, enter:

-licpath 1999@flex.cd-adapco.com -podkey <pod_key>

Where:

▪1999@flex.cd-adapco.com is the default CD-adapco Power on Demand server.

▪<pod_key> is the Power on Demand license key.

For more information on Power on Demand licensing, see the section User Guide > Using STAR-CCM + > STAR-CCM+ Licensing > Power on Demand Licensing.

A full list of command-line arguments is available in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ User Guide at User Guide > Using STAR-CCM+ > Command-Line Reference.

The Command field updates automatically to reflect the selections you make. Manual entries are not affected by these selections.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 19

4. Select a licensing option:

▶To use a Power Session license, select Power Session.

This license is designed for parallel simulations, where you can use an unlimited number of cores in this session.

▶To use a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Lite license, select Lite Session.

A limited set of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ features are provided when you activate this option.

If you select no licensing option, the default CAD client license is used.

5. Click OK.

If the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server is running when you modify the preferences, a message box appears informing you that both Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ must be closed for the changes to take effect.

6. Click OK to proceed.

7. Close the active Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ sessions.

8. Restart Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

Note: The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server only starts when it is required, such as during surface meshing or volume meshing. It does not start when you launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

If an option in the Preferences dialog conflicts with an option in the config.xml file, the option that is set in the Preferences dialog takes precedence. An example of such a situation is if the Compute Processes property is set to 4 in the Preferences panel, while it is set to 2 in the config.xml file; the simulation runs using four processors. See Modifying the config.xml File

Note: IBM Platform MPI must be installed on your local machine for you to run in parallel. This program is included with the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ package installer.

Changing the Units System

You can use either the SI (International Standard) or USCS (United States Customary System) units system in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

To change the units system:

1. Bring up the Units System dialog:

▶Right-click the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo node within the object tree and select Set Units System.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 20

▶Alternatively, from the ribbon, select Units System.

The Units System dialog appears.

2. Select the desired units system from the drop-down menu.

3. Click OK.

Automatic Unit Conversion in Dialog Panels

Changing the default units system converts existing values to the new units system. Ensure that you select the desired units system before you enter the value, otherwise you will need to re-enter it.

Note: Specific values that you have already modified the units on are not affected by a change of units system.

Transferring Units to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Units that are used in the CAD geometry file are also used in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation. Less common units, such as those listed below, are not supported in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

• Micrometers

• Angstroms

• Nanometers

• Mils

• Microinches

• Footinches (this unit may be converted to inches in Simcenter STAR-CCM+)

• Miles

Note: This list may not be exhaustive and is subject to change.

These units are converted to meters when the CAD geometry is imported into Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Transferring the CAE Model to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

You can transfer your geometry and the simulation setup to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ at any time from within the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo environment. If you want to transfer only the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, refer to Transferring Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

To transfer the geometry with the simulation set up:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Transfer CAE Model.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 21

The version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ that is affiliated with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo launches.

Note: A surface mesh is required in order to visualize the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If you have not generated a mesh before clicking Transfer CAE Model, the geometry is tessellated with a medium density.

Using Creo Mouse Controls in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ offers the ability to set the mouse interactor style to match that of Creo; this could make geometry manipulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ more natural if you are used to working with Creo.

To change the mouse interactor style:

1. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

2. Click Tools and select Options from the menu.

The Options dialog appears.

3. Expand the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ node and select Visualization.

4. In the Properties panel, set Interactor Style topro-E / NX using the drop-down menu.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 22

5. Click Close.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ will now use this mouse interactor style each time it launches.

Editing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Settings While the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client is Running

If you make a change in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo while the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client is running, such as adding or deleting a boundary, you may need to update the volume mesh.

Scenes in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ session will not display the model correctly unless you keep the volume mesh up to date. A list of changes that require you to re-mesh the geometry is provided below:

• For boundaries and regions: changing the type, adding or deleting

• For mesh pipelines and mesh controls: editing, adding or deleting

When adding or removing regions and boundaries in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, the scenes in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ may be missing some parts, as shown below, even after re-meshing the geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 23

To update the scene, you need to manually add the modified regions and boundaries to the scene in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client. You can do this by dragging and dropping the region or part from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ object tree, or by adding the region or part using the Part Selector. An alternative method would be to create a new scene, as this will automatically pick up the new regions and boundaries added to the simulation.

Product Excellence Program

The Product Excellence Program collects information about our customers and their use of Siemens Digital Industries Software. This information helps us improve our product features and functionality to better meet customer needs. No personal or intellectual property information is collected or shared. Product performance is not affected and participation in the program is voluntary.

Privacy statement

The Product Excellence Program helps Siemens Digital Industries Software understand how customers use our products and assists us in improving our products. The program is anonymous and participation is voluntary.

The Product Excellence Program is designed to protect the privacy of the user and the intellectual property created through the use of Siemens Digital Industries Software products.

How does it work?

The Product Excellence Program is used to collect data about your installation, the features you use and how you use them. The data is sent to Siemens Digital Industries Software for analysis. By examining usage patterns from a large number of people, we gain insight into how the products are used and how to improve the software in future releases. Data collection occurs in the background as you use the software and does not affect performance or functionality.

What data is sent?

The data collected can vary by product and by release as we gain more insight or add new capabilities. The Product Excellence Program may collect information on the functions utilized, the operating environment (e.g.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 25

OS, RAM, graphics, etc.), product version, or other indications of user interaction. The data may also include the company name that is using the product. This data is solely for use by Siemens Digital Industries Software to improve our products and is never shared with any third party.

There is no contact information in the data and Siemens Digital Industries Software will not contact you by phone or email as a result of the data collected. No information about the data you create or manage is collected.

Participation is optional.

You can control your participation during installation or reinstallation of the software by using the Product Excellence Program option in the interactive installer.

Using Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo with Multiple Installed Versions of Creo

If you have multiple versions of Creo installed on your machine, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo is installed to work with the latest version.

You can manually integrate Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo with an older supported version of Creo:

1. In the installation directory of the older version of Creo, navigate to the folder that contains the config.pro file.

The default location is:

C:\Program Files\PTC\Creo X.0\Common Files\XXXX\text

2. Locate and edit the config.pro file using a text editor of your choice.

You require administrator privileges to edit the config.pro file.

3. Enter the following line at the end of the file:

protkdat C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-Creo \protk.dat

This line contains the full path to the protk.dat file in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo installation directory. Make sure to enter the correct full version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

4. Save the file and exit the text editor.

Disabling Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

If for any reason you would like to temporarily disable Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo without having to uninstall it, do the following:

1. Go to the text folder in the Creo installation directory.

The typical path is C:\Program Files\PTC\Creo X.0\Common Files\XXXX\text.

2. Locate and edit the config.pro file using a text editor of your choice.

3. Comment out the following line with an “!”:

protkdat C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-Creo \protk.dat

so that it looks like this:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 26

!protkdat C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CAD15.06.###\STAR-Creo \protk.dat15.06.###

Creo will now launch without Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo. To enable Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo again, undo the changes listed above.

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on Different Machines

You can run Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on two different machines.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ operates on a client-server architecture, where Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is the server and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo is the client. A benefit of client-server architectures is that the client and the server do not have to be running on the same machine. Typically, CAD packages run on Windows

operating systems. You can choose to run Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on any remote machine with a supported or certified platform, including Linux platforms.

Transferring Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

With Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, you can transfer your CAD geometry directly to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ from within the Creo environment. Along with the geometry data, you can also transfer design data, such as CAD parameters, coordinate systems, and reference planes.

The Transfer Geometry feature imports your geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+. This function provides an alternative method to the CAD translator add-ons for importing geometry. This method of transferring geometry can provide a faster workflow when performing a design analysis.

To transfer geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Transfer Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and imports the CAD geometry. You are now at the same stage in the workflow as if you imported the surface mesh directly into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using the CAD translators (File > Import > Import Surface Mesh...).

2. Set up your case in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Caution: Do not click Transfer CAE Model if you have previously used the Transfer Geometry method and set up your case in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. This action results in the loss of your settings in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Transferring Design Data to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Design data consists of CAD parameters, coordinate systems, and reference planes that you can transfer to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ along with the geometry.

CAD parameters control the feature dimensions, for example extrusion depth, and are useful for modifying the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ after running the analysis. You can use reference planes in scalar scenes and reports in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. You can use coordinate systems to define motion in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation.

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, CAD parameters appear within the Expressions Editor dialog as single-values with units. You can select these for use in expressions, which in turn can be used in the following contexts:

• In 3D-CAD, for expressions that apply to design parameters

• Expression reports

• Coordinate parameters

Additionally, after transfer, you can set a CAD parameter in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to reference global scalar parameters.

This workflow maintains an active link between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+. When working with Geometry Transfer, you can modify the geometry in either package and the geometry in the relevant package is updated accordingly.

Updating the Geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Creo Closed

You can close Creo and continue working with the simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Doing so, however, breaks the link between the two software packages. Any further updates that you make to the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are not transferred back to the geometry in Creo. Instead, these changes are stored in memory, which allows you to include the CAD parameters in your optimization scripts.

This workflow also allows you to release the Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo licenses when performing tasks in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In this case, the Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo licenses are temporarily checked out only when the updates to the geometry are stored in memory.

Transferring the geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo will overwrite the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Understanding the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Process

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo the typical workflow for running a simulation is as follows:

1. Ensure that the CAD model is suitable for analysis

2. Extract the fluid volume

3. Define the material properties for each part of the model, for example, air, water, aluminum

4. Define model physics, for example, turbulence, temperature, gravity

5. Specify boundary conditions, for example, inlets, outlets, symmetry planes

6. Specify mesh settings

7. Define solution controls

8. Run the case

9. Post-process the results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Once you have obtained an initial solution you may wish to re-run the case with some different settings, or with some changes to the geometry. To do this you can:

1. Return to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and change settings or modify the geometry

2. Re-run the case

Using Suitable CAD Models in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo only supports the use of solid bodies. If a geometry is made up entirely of surfaces then it will not be possible to define any boundary conditions, and the meshing options will be greyed out.

It is good practice to create copies of the original geometry file(s) before importing them into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

Suppressed or deactivated parts and features are not supported by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and will have no effect on the analysis. Hidden parts, however, are used in the analysis. Ensure that all desired parts and features are active before using them with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

Extracting the Fluid Volume

A CAD model usually represents a component made from solid material. However, in the case of flow simulation, a model representing the fluid volume is needed, requiring a different CAD model to be created. This is illustrated below:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 45

In some instances, a simulation will require multiple regions, such as:

• Moving Reference Frames

For rotating flow, such as turbines.

• Porous Media

For representing regions with fine geometric structures

• Energy Source

For simulating thermal specifications, such as conjugate heat transfer

These types of simulation require each region to be represented by individual contiguous parts within an assembly.

Defining Material Properties

Continua determines the characteristics of the fluid and solid entities used within the simulation. The behavior of a single continuum is primarily defined by the chosen material type and physics models.

Specification of the material type used in the simulation provides properties such as density, viscosity and conductivity, which are all used by the solver to calculate a solution. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo includes a database of common materials and allows you to modify material properties where necessary.

Defining Model Physics

Physics models determine the nature of the fluid, and can be described as either:

• Turbulent or Laminar

• Constant Density or Ideal Gas

Additional models can also be activated to meet the needs of various simulation requirements:

• Passive scalar

• Temperature

• Gravity

A region is defined as a volume domain in a simulation, surrounded by boundaries. Each region in the simulation must be represented by a part in the native CAD package. When multiple regions are required, multiple parts must be used within an assembly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 46

All regions must be assigned to a continuum, as they represent a volume of material in the simulation. Region settings can be used to define porous media, moving reference frames, and an energy source.

Specifying Boundary Conditions

To define boundary conditions you first need to select the surface or surfaces on the model to assign to a separate boundary.

A boundary is defined as a surface, which along with other boundaries, surround and characterize a region. Boundary conditions determine how the boundary will affect the material within a region, and consequently, the simulation as a whole.

Inlet boundaries determine how much fluid enters the region, using a velocity, mass flow rate or stagnation inlet. Outlet boundaries define the process for fluid leaving the region, which are defined with either a pressure or flow-split ratio. Wall boundaries contain the fluid, and can also be used to define a thermal specification that will influence the transfer of energy to or from the region. Symmetry boundaries can be used to avoid modeling the entire region where appropriate, and so reduce calculation time.

As boundary types can affect the way in which the volume mesh is constructed, it is important to set them before generating the mesh.

Specifying Mesh Settings

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver uses the finite volume method to obtain an approximate solution to the underlying equations of fluid flow. This requires a mesh to be created, which represents the fluid volume as a collection of much smaller volumes known as cells.

A surface mesh is first created based on the boundaries defining the regions in the simulation. Thereafter a volume mesh is created to discretize the entire model.

The accuracy of the results is directly affected by mesh quality. If it is necessary to improve the quality of the mesh, some of the ways in which this can be done are to:

• Increase the mesh density, that is, the number of cells

• Add further sub-surface prism layers to capture near wall flow

• Refine the mesh in areas where flow characteristics are expected to change rapidly

As volume mesh quality is largely governed by the surface mesh quality, it is common practice to create and inspect the surface mesh before creating a volume mesh.

Defining Solution Controls

Solution controls determine the level of accuracy the solver will work towards. As a high accuracy solution will take longer, it may be necessary to compromise on this in order to obtain a result in a shorter time.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo includes five predefined solver settings ranging from fast (with low accuracy) to slow (with high accuracy). Advanced options are also available to provide further control.

Running the Case

When the simulation has been fully defined, the volume mesh is sent to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ along with all the necessary data for running the simulation. The time to complete a simulation will vary depending on the mesh density and solution controls.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 47

As the solver is running, residuals showing the rate at which individual equations are converging are shown in a plot. A scalar scene displaying absolute pressure is displayed on completion of the simulation.

Post-Processing the Results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Post-processing of simulations is carried out using the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ interface. This allows the results to be taken from the solver and displayed in a variety of scenes and plots.

Making Modifications to the Settings or Geometry

As Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo is completely integrated within the Creo environment, it is very simple to perform parametric studies that examine the response of the fluid to changes in geometry. Once the first analysis is complete, the boundary conditions, run settings and all other properties of the CFD model are stored within the CAD file. Any changes in the flow field due to design changes can be recalculated by generating a new mesh and running the solver.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 48

Working with Simplified Representations in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

In Creo, simplified representations control which parts of an assembly are visible in a session. The purpose of a simplified representation is to improve the performance of large assemblies in Creo by excluding components or substituting them for another.

A complete model representation is known as the master representation. The procedure for transferring geometry with simplified representations to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is the same as the procedure for transferring geometry with a master representation. The difference is that features which are excluded in the simplified representation are not transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Assembly models with simplified representations can have components with the following status:

• Exclude Representation

• Geometry Representation

• Graphics Representation

• Light Graphics Representation

• Symbolic Representation

• Boundary Box Only Representation

• Default Envelope Only Representation

• Substitute Representation

If the status is Substitute Representation, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo checks for its type. If the type is Interchange, then the substitute geometry is transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Components with other status types (in the list above) are not transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If the status of a component is set to master representation, then the component is transferred to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

If you are setting up a CAE simulation within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, simplified representations can affect the way in which boundaries are displayed in the Graphics window. If you change between representations, you may require to click off the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo tree.

If you want to load simplified representations in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo while running in disconnected (batch) mode, you must create a configuration file and place that in the folder containing the files with the simplified representation:

1. In the directory that contains the geometry files with the simplified representation, create a readable text file.

2. Open the text file using a text editor and add the following line:

open_simplified_rep_by_default [SIMPLIFIED_REP_NAME]

Where [SIMPLIFIED_REP_NAME] is the simplified representation name of the assembly model.

3. Save the text file.

4. Rename the text file to config.pro.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 49

Connecting to Remote Machines

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses a client-server architecture, and as such the CAD client ( Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo) and the server (Simcenter STAR-CCM+) are not required to run on the same machine.

Using an SSH (secure shell) connection, you can connect the client and server on two different machines, even when these are on different platforms. Due to how the CAD client and server interact in the background, the SSH connection must not ask for a username or a password.

There are two ways that you can connect Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and Simcenter STAR-CCM+, depending on what your starting point is:

• You can start from the CAD client and launch the server on a remote machine. This method is useful for transferring CAD geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo running on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on Linux.

• You can start from the server and connect to the CAD client on a remote machine. This method is useful for connecting to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo to update the CAD geometry. With this method, you can perform a Design Manager analysis on a cluster while the geometry is updated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

Contents:

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Starting from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, you can choose to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on a remote machine.

Using this method, you can set up the full CAE analysis in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo on your local machine, and then run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on the remote machine. You can also choose to transfer your geometry from the CAD client to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. This feature is useful if you want to import geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo running on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on Linux.

To configure Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo to launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on a remote machine:

1. Make sure that you have a working SSH connection between the two machines.

For the SSH connection, you require an SSH server on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and an SSH client on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo. The SSH connection to the remote machine must not ask for a username or a password. To avoid possible issues with a connection that still requires a password, add -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=0 to the SSH command. Setting this argument to zero stops the connection prompting for a password when one is needed — something that could cause the process to hang. See SSH Command.

2. In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Preferences.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 50

3. In the Preferences panel, set Server Settings to Remote.

4. Set the remaining settings for your connection to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. See Server

Settings Panel.

This information is used to build a command-line in the background when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo invokes Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

5. If you are going to connect to the same remote host in future sessions, click Save as Default Settings.

The next time Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo invokes Simcenter STAR-CCM+, the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server launches on the specified remote machine. A Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client is also launched on the local machine to allow you to see the active session on the remote machine.

To connect Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on the local machine to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo running on a remote machine:

Defining Materials and Physics

Defining the physical properties of a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo model involves specifying the materials, flow characteristics, operating conditions, and physics models.

These definitions and settings are accomplished through the use of continua and regions, which are described in the following sections.

Contents:

Working with Continua and Regions

Importing Geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for Visualization

Working with Continua and Regions

Continua and regions are used together to capture the physical and material properties of a model.

A continuum represents a material in combination with a set of physics models that will be used to simulate the response of the material to the conditions imposed upon it. A continuum also provides the facility to define reference and initial values.

A region represents one or more volumes within the overall model, not necessarily contiguous, which will share the same continuum and set of boundary conditions. Regions are defined using CAD parts, and will be discretized by the volume mesher.

As well as holding a set of boundary conditions, regions can also be used to model specific physical behavior, including porous resistance, moving reference frames and energy sources.

Parts can be imported into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes without affecting the analysis.

Continua are assigned to single or multiple regions, which can contain single or multiple parts. In part mode, only one continuum and one region are available, as there is only one part. In assembly mode, new continua can be added to represent different materials present in the simulation, and new regions can be added to represent the parts composed of these materials. Continua and regions can be deleted if they are not required, although the simulation must always contain at least one of each.

There is a well defined relationship between continua, regions, boundary conditions and CAD parts.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 55

• Every region must be associated with a continuum.

• Several regions can be associated with the same continuum.

• Every CAD part must belong to a region.

• Several CAD parts can be associated with the same region.

• Boundary conditions belong to regions, and cannot be shared between regions.

• Every CAD surface must have a boundary condition associated with it. A default wall boundary is applied to CAD surfaces that have not been specifically associated with a user-defined boundary condition.

The following series of illustrations depict the relationship between CAD parts, continua, and regions, for a circular steel duct containing a rotating fan, and surrounded by a layer of insulation.

• Initially we have a collection of CAD parts in an assembly. These must be imprinted where appropriate to ensure that interfaces between parts can be created correctly.

• Three continua are required to represent the three different materials present in the simulation: the fluid (for example, air), the steel pipe, and the insulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 56

• Two regions are required for the fluid portion of the simulation, as a rotating part is defined by applying a rotating frame of reference to a separate region surrounding the fan blades. Further regions are required for each of the solid parts (the steel pipe and insulating layer), which means a total of four separate regions overall.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 57

• A clearer picture can be given of the fan blade itself.

For an analysis containing a single part, for example a fluid-only case involving fluid flow through a converging-diverging pipe, the model will only require one continuum and one region in order to fully define

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 58

the physical and material properties of the model. In this case, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo automatically assigns the default continuum to the default region, and no further assignments are necessary.

Contents:

Setting Up Continua

Setting Up Regions

Setting Up Continua

To define different materials and associated physics for use in an assembly, you require additional continua. In each continuum you can specify a unique set of properties, such as a different material type or temperature. In assembly mode, continua are stored under a Continua node, as shown below.

To create an additional continuum:

1. Right-click the Continua node in the object tree and select Add Continuum.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. In the Name field, enter a name for the continuum.

3. In the Materials group, select the type of material that you want to define:

▶Gas

▶Liquid

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 59

▶Solid

4. Select a material from the list.

You can modify the properties of any material that you select.

Note: You can select only one material per continuum. If your simulation contains a number of materials, you must create additional continua. This action is only possible for assemblies.

5. In the Flow Characteristics group, select the type of flow that you want to model: Laminar or Turbulent. This group only appears for fluids.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 60

6. In the Equation of State group, select the equation of state : Constant Density or Ideal Gas. This group only appears for gases.

7. In the Optional Physics Model group, activate any optional physics models: Passive Scalar and Temperature.

8. Define the material properties in the Material Properties group.

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Material Properties Panel.

Note: You can change units of properties from the drop-down menu.

9. In the Reference Properties group, define the reference properties.

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Reference Properties Panel.

10.If you want to include the body force due to gravity when calculating the momentum equations in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, activate the gravity model in the Gravity group box.

See Activating the Gravity Model in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

11.Set the initial conditions in the Initialization group box.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 61

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Initialization Panel.

Specifying initial conditions that are close to the expected solution can reduce the number of iterations required to reach a solution. You can set the initial conditions similar to the inlet conditions of the fluid domain.

Initial conditions are specified at a continuum level; if no initial conditions are specified, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo will use default values to initialize the solution.

12.Click OK.

The continuum is added to the object tree.

Once you have created a continuum, you can assign it to a region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Continuum Properties

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Continuum Properties

The continuum dialog has a number of properties that you can define. This section provides a description for each property.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Material Properties Panel

You can define the following material properties in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo:

Property Description

Density Available for all types of materials. For gases, this property is available when you use the Constant Density equation of state.

Specific Heat Available for all material types when you activate the Temperature physics model.

Molecular Viscosity Only available for fluids.

Conductivity Available for all materials when you activate the temperature physics model.

Molecular Weight Only applies to gases. This property is available when you use the Ideal Gas equation of state.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Reference Properties Panel

You can define the following continuum reference properties:

Property Description

(Reference Pressure) The pressure values that are defined in the simulation are all relative to the reference pressure. For more information, see the What is the Reference Pressure? section.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 62

Property Description

(Reference Temperature) The reference temperature is used to define the operating temperature of the fluid in the buoyancy source term of the Boussinesq model. This parameter is used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ when the temperature, constant density, and gravity physics models are enabled.

(Reference Density) These quantities are not used as part of the CFD calculation, but is necessary to calculate the force coefficients when post-processing. (Reference Velocity)

(Reference Area)

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Initialization Panel

Specifying initial conditions that are close to the expected solution can reduce the number of iterations required to reach a solution. You can also set the initial conditions to match inlet conditions of the fluid domain. You can define the following continuum reference properties:

Property Description

(U Component of Velocity) The U direction vector for the initial velocity.

(V Component of Velocity) The V direction vectors for the initial velocity.

(W Component of Velocity) The W direction vectors for the initial velocity.

(Initial Pressure) The initial pressure. The physical value of the initial pressure defines the starting pressure in the regions to which the continuum is assigned. The initial pressure is specified with respect to the reference pressure. The default initial pressure is 0 Pa.

(Initial Temperature) The initial temperature. This physical value of the initial temperature defines the starting temperature throughout any region to which the continuum is assigned. The default initial temperature is 300 K.

(Turbulence Intensity) The initial turbulence intensity. The default value is 0.05 (5%)

(Turbulent Length Scale) The initial turbulent length scale. The default value is 0.01 m.

Activating the Gravity Model in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

If you require the gravity model in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, you can activate it in the Continuum Settings dialog:

1. In the Continuum Settings dialog, activate the Enable checkbox in the Gravity group.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 63

2. Set the acceleration due to gravity in the (Acceleration due to gravity) box.

You can change the units from the drop-down list.
