Setting Up Regions

Additional regions are required when modelling multiple region physics, or when specific behavior such as porous resistance is required for a particular part within the same continuum. Assign parts from an assembly to regions. You can control the properties of these regions through the assigned continuum.

In assembly mode, regions are stored under the Regions node in the object tree, as shown below.

To create an additional region:

1. Right-click the Regions manager node in the object tree and select Add Region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 64

The Region Settings dialog appears.

2. In the Name property, enter a name for the region.

3. Select the parts that you want to include in the region.

You can select multiple parts from the graphics window or the Creo feature tree.

Selected parts appear in the Parts Selection group box field.

4. Select a continuum to apply to the region.

All available continua are listed here.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 65

Note: Assigning a continuum to a region causes the region to inherit the physical and material properties defined in the continuum

5. Activate any additional region physics for the region:

◦ Porous. See Defining a Porous Region.

◦ Moving Reference Frame. See Defining a Moving Reference Frame.

◦ Energy Source. See Defining an Energy Source.

6. If you want to import parts into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes, but do not want the region to be included in the CFD calculations, activate the Exclude from Analysis option. See Importing Geometry into STAR-CCM+ for Visualization.

7. Click OK.

A new region is added to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo object tree under the Regions node.

The parts that you assign to a region define the geometric extent of the region. Within this geometry, properties and behavior of the material is governed by the physics models and material properties defined in the region and continuum settings.

Note: Each region must be assigned at least one part, otherwise it will be ignored during the CFD analysis.

By default, every Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo model contains one continuum, and this is automatically assigned to the default region and each additional region that you create. If multiple continua are defined in the model, you can choose a different continuum to assign to each region. This enables you to control the physical properties of each region, including varying material types.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 66

All the parts in an assembly are assigned to the default region (this is the initial region created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo). When you assign a part to another region, it is automatically removed from the default region. If you remove a part from a region, it is reassigned back to the default region.

Importing Geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for Visualization

You can import CAD parts, that do not form part of the analysis, into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes.

Add these parts to a separate region—this region is excluded from the analysis. This feature is useful for showing the original geometry in a post-processing scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. For example, for an internal fluid volume of a pipe, the original geometry is the solid pipe.

To exclude CAD parts from the analysis:

1. In the Region Settings dialog, add the CAD parts that you want to use for visualization purposes.

2. Activate the Exclude From Analysis checkbox in the Advanced panel.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 71

3. Click OK.

When you run the case, a surface mesh is generated for this region using the settings specified in the Mesh Pipeline.

Note: As is the case for all assemblies, you must imprint all parts that are used for visualization purposes onto any surface that they cut, otherwise you will not be able to generate the surface mesh.

An example of this feature is shown in the following section, where a valve and valve body geometry are imported into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization.

Setting Up a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Scene to Display Imported Geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

You can visualize geometry that is not included in the analysis. For example, you can add the valve and valve housing geometry to a Geometry Scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, even though this does not have any effect to the flow.

To use parts that are excluded from the analysis in a scene:

1. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, create a new scene.

In the following example, a Geometry Scene is used.

2. Create a streamlines derived part.

3. Click on the scene/plot button.

The object tree switches to the scene nodes.

4. Double-click on the Geometry Scene > Displayers > Geometry > Parts node.

5. In the Edit dialog:

a) Deactivate the Regions node.

b) Expand the Parts node and activate the part that corresponds to the valve body.

This is the region that you chose to exclude from the analysis in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

6. Click OK.

7. Select the Geometry node and set Representation to Geometry.

The imported geometry only contains a surface mesh and does not appear by default (the default Representation is set to Volume). This is why you must change the Representation to Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 73

Setting Boundary Conditions

Boundary conditions tell the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers how the substance within the region interacts with its environment. A velocity inlet boundary, for example, tells the solvers that an amount of substance is being added to the fluid domain at a certain rate.

A Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo boundary is made up of one or more CAD surfaces within the simulation which, along with other boundaries, surround and define a region.

The boundary is discretized by the surface mesher, which is then used by the volume mesher to mesh the entire region.

It is important to set the boundary conditions before creating the volume mesh, as some parts of the volume mesh, such as prism layers, depend on the type of boundary.

By default, each region contains only one boundary. To define more boundaries you need to add boundaries to the region. You can modify the properties of existing boundaries by editing its boundary node.

Some boundaries may require the specification of turbulence quantities, temperature, and passive scalar concentration, depending on whether these modeling options have been activated in Continuum Settings.

The Boundary Settings dialog appears.

Meshing the Model

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo provides options for generating polyhedral or trimmed volume meshes, with or without near-wall prism layers.

By default, prism layers are generated on all wall surfaces. The provision of a prism layer depends on the type of boundary that is applied to a face. As a consequence, it is recommended that you only generate the mesh after setting up the boundaries and regions.

The meshing process first creates a triangulated surface (the surface mesh) and thereafter converts it to the desired volume mesh (polyhedral or trimmer). As the quality of the volume mesh depends to a large extent on the quality of the surface mesh, it is prudent to check the surface mesh before proceeding with the volume mesh.

Although the entire meshing process can be launched with a single command (the Build And Run command from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon), it is possible to execute only single stages from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creoribbon. Settings that are made in the Mesh Pipeline node govern the mesh generation process.

A mesh pipeline contains all the settings that are applied to the surface and volume meshes created on the Creo parts to which it is applied. In single part mode, only one mesh pipeline is available. In assembly mode, multiple mesh pipelines can be created if necessary.

When mesh generation commences, each mesh pipeline will:

1. Extract geometry from Creo.

2. Transfer the model to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3. Execute the surface remesher.

4. Execute the polyhedral or trimmer volume mesher with the prism layer mesher (if selected).

5. Create a mesh representation in the Creo Graphics window.

Controls on the top-level mesh pipeline node allow you to set the base sizes for the surface mesh, and control the prism layer. Further refinement to specific faces, parts, or volume shapes can be made by adding additional controls to the mesh pipeline.

Creation of Additional Surfaces in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ creates geometry part surfaces during the geometry transfer stage.

Initially, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo creates one part surface for each face in the CAD model. These part surfaces are then combined so that one surface per boundary remains. This outcome, however, is not possible for boundaries that contain CAD surfaces from more than one part. The final part surfaces appear in the Geometry > Parts node in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

The following items affect the number of part surfaces that are created in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

• The number of boundaries present in the model, including the default boundary. Each boundary in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo appears as a separate part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If, however, a boundary contains CAD surfaces from multiple parts, the part surfaces in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ cannot be combined.

• The number of mesh pipeline controls used (if any). Each CAD surface that is used to define a face mesh control in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo appears as a separate part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• The number of interfaces that are created during the meshing process (for assemblies only). All the CAD surfaces that define one interface between two parts in an assembly are grouped together under one part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. One part surface exists for each interface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Boundary Splitting due to Interface Generation

Interfaces are automatically created between two parts in an assembly during the mesh generation. A new boundary is created for each interface on the surfaces that share the interface.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 84

Boundary Splitting due to Face Mesh Controls and Part Mesh Controls

If you use a face mesh control or a part mesh control in your simulation, some boundaries may be split, depending on what faces are included in the mesh control. If a boundary and mesh control share the same faces, no splitting occurs. If a mesh control contains faces from multiple boundaries, splitting occurs and a new boundary is created. The name of the new boundary is derived from the original boundary.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 85

Working with Mesh Pipelines

When working with a single part, you will only have one mesh pipeline defined in the model tree. This will specify the mesh settings for the single part available. In assembly mode, multiple mesh pipelines can be created to give specific controls for different parts, and parts must be specifically associated with a mesh pipeline.

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

The mesh pipeline node contains the general mesh settings that will apply to all Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo parts associated within the pipeline in the absence of any further controls.

To set up the mesh pipeline:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo tree and select Edit.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 86

The Mesh Pipeline Settings dialog appears.

2. In the Name field, enter the name of the mesh pipeline if required.

3. In the Part Selection box, specify the desired parts to use in the mesh pipeline.

This property is only available when working with assemblies.

4. From the Mesh Type tab, select the type of mesh that you want to generate:

▶Polyhedral

▶Trimmer

5. Set Base Size to the desired value.

The base size is a reference length used in other meshing parameters. It may be set to equal the length of the largest triangle you expect to have on your surface mesh, or to some other characteristic dimension.

The base size can be set as either a relative or absolute value. When it is set as a relative value, the reference size will be the diagonal of the bounding box enclosing the entire geometry. In the case of multiple parts in an assembly, the reference size will be calculated based on the diagonal length of the bounding box enclosing the entire assembly. This includes all parts from all mesh pipelines. The unit specification menu will become active when setting an absolute value.

6. Set Surface Mesh Size to the desired value.

The surface mesh size is the base edge length of triangles on the surface mesh. Note that the ultimate length of some (or all) triangles on the surface mesh will depend on other factors such as surface curvature and edge proximity.

7. Set the prism layer settings. See Prism Layer Panel.

8. Set the advanced settings. See Mesh Pipeline Advanced Settings Panel.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 87

9. If you selected to generate a trimmed mesh, set the Trimmer settings. See Trimmer Panel.

10.Click OK.

Prims layers improve the simulation near non-slip walls, particularly when a turbulence model is active.

Property Description

Layer Thickness Defines the overall depth of the prism layer, which includes all of the individual layers, as illustrated below.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 88

Property Description

Mesh Pipeline Advanced Settings Panel

The advanced settings panel provides further customization of meshing parameters.

Property Description

Relative Minimum Surface Size Defines the minimum triangle size permitted on a feature curve. The minimum triangle size is set as a percentage of the surface mesh size. The default value is set to 25%. You must set the relative minimum surface size to a value greater than zero. If you set the relative minimum surface size to 100%, Simcenter STARCCM+ will not modify the triangle size when it detects curvature.

The figure below illustrates this behavior. Note that the base size was set to 20% in this example to emphasize the refinement on the curve.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 89

Property Description

Having a large value for the number of points on a circle property increases the mesh resolution on curved surfaces.

The transition between the fine mesh and coarse mesh areas is controlled by the growth ratio.

Growth Ratio Controls the rate at which triangle sizes change when moving from one triangle size to another. In the example below, the end faces of the block were set to have a smaller triangle size than the four side faces of the block. When the growth ratio is set to a low value, the transition between triangle size is very gradual. When a higher value is used, the transition is far more rapid.

The growth factor must be set to a value greater than 1.0. There is no upper limit for the growth factor.

Number of Points per Circle Controls the number of triangle edges that appear on a curved surface, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 90

Property Description

Regardless of the number of points per circle defined, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo will not permit the triangle edge length to shrink below 25% of the base size. The curvature length scale may also affect the number of edges on a curved surface.

Trimmer Panel

The trimmer mesh is controlled using the Trimmer panel.

Property Description

Default Growth Rate Controls the stepping of the refinement from one cell size to the next. Five settings are available. By default, the Default Growth Rate is set to Fast, meaning that the fastest transition from the smallest cell size to the largest will be used. This usually equates to having only one layer of each cell size for each transition, which will result in the least number of cells being created for the supplied input values. The Medium, Slow, and Very Slow options further slow the transition from one cell size to the next in the mesh interior and therefore increase the overall cell count. In general, the medium option results in a minimum of two equal sized cell layers per transition, slow in four layers and the very slow option in eight layers.

Boundary Growth Rate Controls the number of cell layers to grow next to surfaces in the template. Five settings are available. By default, the Boundary Growth Rate is set to None, meaning that the setting used for the Default Growth Rate is used for controlling all transitions. If the Very Slow, Slow, Medium, or Fast options are selected then it will result in eight, four, two or one layers of

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 91

Property Description

cells respectively of the same size being created next to the geometry surfaces in the template.

Working with Mesh Controls

Mesh controls allow you to define custom mesh settings for a particular section of the model.

Multiple controls can be assigned to the same item to control different mesh parameters. If, for example, a face has two mesh controls assigned to it--one that controls the mesh size and another that controls the prism layer thickness, the final mesh will respect both the custom mesh size and the custom prism layer thickness. If two mesh controls set the same mesh parameter, the control created last will take precedence over the first.

Using a Face Mesh Control

A face mesh control allows you to set the surface mesh size and the prism layer parameters on a face. Custom settings made on a face control will take priority over settings in the parent mesh pipeline, and over settings made in any part mesh controls.

To add a face mesh control:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline > Mesh Controls node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo tree and select Add Face Mesh Control.

The Face Mesh Control Settings dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 92

2. Set Name to an appropriate value.

3. On the CAD geometry, select the desired faces to include in this mesh control.

4. If you want to specify a custom surface mesh size on the selected surfaces, activate the Custom Mesh Size option.

a) Set (Custom Mesh Size) to the desired value.Set (Mesh Size) to the desired value.

You can enter this value as a percentage of the base size, or as an absolute value. If you select to enter the absolute value, you can select the units from the drop-down menu.

5. Set (Prism Layer Option) to the desired value:

▶Inherit Values: in the first instance, the face(s) will be assigned values from any part mesh control applied to the part to which the face(s) belong. If this does not apply, values will be taken from any applicable volumetric mesh control, and in the absence of this values will be taken from the parent mesh pipeline.

▶Use Custom Values: allows the prism layer parameters to be set directly on the face(s). See Prism Layer

Panel.

▶Disable: no prism layer will be generated on the face(s).

6. Click OK.

Visualizing the Mesh

Surface and volume meshes will automatically be displayed on first creation. If required, they can be hidden from view.

To hide a generated mesh in the geometry view:

1. From Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo the ribbon, click Show/Hide Mesh.

Meshing Behavior at Interfaces

The volume mesher will treat interfaces between two regions differently depending on what type of region (fluid or solid) these are.

If the interface lies between two fluid regions, no prism layers will be grown from both sides of the interface. If an interface lies between a solid region and a fluid region, prism layers will be grown from the interface. The default behavior of the prism layer generation can be overridden using a mesh control, so prism layers can be disabled on a solid-fluid interface. See Working With Mesh Controls.

See Also:

Common Causes for Meshing Failures

There may be instances when the mesh generation fails. In most cases this will occur during the surface meshing phase. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo will try and identify the cause and suggest ways of rectifying this. This information will be printed in the Output tab of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Info App window.

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel

The advanced settings in the Solution Control dialog allow you to manually enter the values for the solution control parameters.

Parameter Description

Stopping Criteria

(Number of Iterations) Specifies the maximum number of iterations for which the solver can run. When the Simcenter STARCCM+ solver reaches the specified number of iterations, it will stop. You can then post-process the results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Convergence Levels.

(Convergence Level) Specifies how many orders of magnitude the residuals should drop before the solver stops. See Convergence Levels.

Solution Accuracy

First Order This option is generally the quicker, but less accurate solver option. The first order scheme introduces a dissipative error that is stabilizing and helps the solver achieve robust convergence. However, it can also

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 104

Parameter Description

lead to the neglect and merging of discontinuities, meaning the solution is not fully captured.

Second Order This option is generally the more accurate, but slower solver option. The second order scheme attempts to minimize both dispersive and dissipative errors, providing a better representation of the simulation. However, in some situations, the lack of numerical dissipation can result in poorer convergence properties.

It is common practice to use the first order scheme initially to ensure the simulation is running as expected and then switch to second order.

Under-Relaxation Factors

(Momentum Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the momentum equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Pressure Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the pressurecorrection equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Turbulence Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the turbulence equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Fluid Temperature Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the fluid under-relaxation factor for the segregated energy solver. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Solid Temperature Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the solid under-relaxation factor for the segregated energy solver. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

Convergence Level

The numerical method used by the solver requires an iterative process in order to obtain a solution. After each iteration, residuals are produced that indicate how well the governing equations for each solver quantity are being satisfied numerically. In general, the residual magnitude should decrease as the solution converges. When the magnitude of the residuals for all the quantities falls below the convergence level, the solver will stop iterating, and results will be exported for post-processing.

Note: In most cases, a drop of 3-5 orders of magnitude in the residuals is sufficient to obtain an accurate solution.

You can adjust the convergence level parameter to meet accuracy or process time requirements. However, if the residuals are no longer decreasing from one iteration to the next, it is likely that machine accuracy has been reached for that case. For a case that does not exhibit decreasing residuals, it would be necessary to reconsider the setup in case the volume mesh is too coarse, or boundary conditions have been set incorrectly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 105

Under-Relaxation Parameters

Under-relaxation parameters determine how quickly the solver reaches a solution for a particular equation, on a scale from 0 to 1, with 1 being the fastest.

Ideally, all under-relaxation parameters would be set to 1, however, doing so would likely cause solver instability due to the complex nature of most simulations. Hence the under-relaxation parameters should be set to values that compromise speed with stability.

Note: Adjust the under-relaxation parameters if changes to other solution controls such as Number of Iterations, Convergence Levels, and Solution Accuracy have failed to improve the behavior of the solver.

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

You can use Java macros with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to automate your simulation or to change a setting in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as selecting an alternative turbulence model, before the solver starts running.

An example of how to change a setting in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using a Java macro is outlined below:

1. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and set up the case.

Define the continuum settings, boundary conditions, mesh settings, and solution control settings.

2. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, start recording a macro and perform the desired operations, such as changing the physics models.

4. Stop recording the macro.

The macro saves at this point.

5. Close Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and do not save the simulation.

6. Return to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, open the Solution Controls dialog and activate the Use Java File checkbox.

A text entry field appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 106

7. Click (Select Input File).

The Open dialog appears.

8. Navigate to your Java macro file and select it.

Selected files appear in the text entry field. The path in the entry field is displayed relative to the current CAD geometry file.

9. Click OK.

When you run the simulation, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ will launch and play the macro before starting the solver. This sequence allows you to set up and use additional Simcenter STAR-CCM+ physics models that are not available in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

Checking the Model for Errors

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo monitors the active case for any errors in real-time and displays a

warning triangle next to any nodes for which there is a problem.

Three areas are monitored by the live model checker:

• Continua. The continua checker makes sure that all necessary boundaries are present in the case, such as the presence of at least one inlet and one outlet.

• Regions and boundaries. The regions and boundaries checker covers issues specific to boundaries, such as a velocity inlet boundary having a zero value.

• Mesh pipelines. The mesh pipeline checker covers issues that are related to the mesh, such as the presence of multiple parts in a trimmed mesh pipeline.

To see the cause of an error:

1. Right-click on an node displaying the warning triangle, and select Show Errors...

A dialog appears describing the error, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 108

2. Click OK to close the dialog.

The Show Errors... right-click menu is available for any node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo object tree that contains a warning triangle. Selecting it will show errors for that node and its sub-nodes.

To see a complete list of issues for the case, right-click on the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo root node and select Show Errors...

You can also manually check for errors.

To perform a manual check:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Check Model for Errors.

If errors are found in the case set up, these are displayed in the Model Checker tab of the Info App dialog. See The Model Checker Tab.

Building and Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

Once you have defined the model physics, boundary conditions, mesh settings, and solver settings in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, you can build and run the case.

To build and run the case:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Build and Run.

This action automatically generates the mesh, and runs the solver. When you run the solver, a new Residuals tab is added to the Info App dialog. You can use this residuals plot to monitor solution convergence. When the solver finishes, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and a scalar scene is automatically created for you.

Note: If a solution has already been computed in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, and the stopping criteria has been reached, clicking Build and Run clears the solution and starts running from the first iteration. If you want to run for more iterations, change the stopping criteria and click Run Solver, or click Run More Iterations.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 109

Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo

If you have already generated a volume mesh for the model, you can run the case directly.

To run the solver:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Run Solver.

Running for More Iterations

You may need to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers for more iterations than you originally set in the Number of Iterations stopping criterion. The Run More Iteration function runs the solver for an additional number of iterations as specified in the stopping criteria. Take, for example, a case where you have already run the simulation for 300 iterations. You specify 500 iterations in the Number of Iterations stopping criterion. When you next click Run for More Iterations, the simulation will run for 500 extra iterations, making 800 iterations in total. The solver runs until one of the stopping criteria is satisfied.

To run for more iterations:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Run For More Iterations.

Clearing the Solution

You can clear all results that were calculated by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers using the Clear Solution function. All other Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo simulation settings remain intact.

Caution: This action is irreversible.

To clear the solution:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, select Clear Solution.

The solution that was calculated by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers is deleted.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 110

Visualizing the Solution

When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches after the solution is calculated, it automatically displays a scalar scene of the model that shows the Absolute Pressure field function.

To visualize the results, you can use this scene to display different scalar quantities, or use any of the other visualization tools in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as streamlines, plane sections and vector scenes.

You can import CAD parts into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes. These parts will not be taken into account during the analysis. This feature is useful for displaying the original geometry in a post-processing scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Importing Geometry Into STAR-CCM+ for Visualization.

Exporting the Surface Mesh

You can export the surface mesh generated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo as a native CD-adapco surface mesh (.dbs) file. The .dbs file format is the recommended format to use when transferring surface data between CD-adapco programs, which are now part of Siemens. The boundary names and boundary types are retained by the file, as well as the interfaces that were automatically created between regions.

To export the surface mesh:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Export > Surface Mesh (.dbs).

Exporting the Volume Mesh

You can export the volume mesh that you generated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo as a native CDadapco volume mesh (.ccm) file. The .ccm file format is the recommended format to use when transferring volume meshes between CD-adapco programs, which are now part of Siemens. The region and boundary names, and region and boundary types are retained in this file. The interfaces that were automatically created interfaces between regions are also retained in this file.

To export the volume mesh:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Export > Volume Mesh (.ccm).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Exporting an Engineering Report

You can export a summary of the simulation settings and results in HTML format to two individual files:

• The first will be given a user-specified file name, and contains results from the simulation.

• The second will be given a user-specified file name appended with _caseinfo, and contains details on the simulation set-up.

Note: You can only export an engineering report after you obtain a solution.

To export an engineering report:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Export > Engineering Report (.html,.csv).

Selecting Fluid Physics Models

The first step in setting up this tutorial is to modify the physics continuum that is used to model air. For this case, the flow is turbulent and thermal. Temperature calculations are on by default in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

Modify the initial conditions:

1. Right-click the Continua > Continuum node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo tree and select Edit.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. Set Name to Air.

3. Set the Equation of State to Ideal Gas.

4. Click to expand the Initialization tab.

5. Set (Temperature) to 400 K.

6. Click OK to close the dialog.

Adding Solid Physics Models

The next step in setting up this tutorial is to define the physics continuum of the solid to be used.

1. Right-click the Continua node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo object tree and select Add Continuum.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 159

2. Set Name to Al.

3. Set Material Type to Solid.

4. Set Material Name to Aluminum Alloy

5. Click to expand the Initialization tab.

6. Set (Temperature) to 400 K.

7. Click OK.

5. Set Continuum Selection to Al.

This action assigns the aluminum alloy that you created earlier as the material for this region.

6. Click OK.

Now that the solid region of the wing is defined, rename the default region to something more appropriate:

Rotating Flow Inside a Graphics Card

This tutorial takes you through the steps that are required to run a CFD calculation in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo environment.

For this tutorial, the model is a fully sealed graphics card that is located inside an empty, idealized PC tower case. The geometry that is used in this tutorial has been simplified in order to decrease the computational cost. As a consequence the mesh is relatively coarse at approximately 200,000 cells compared to the 3-4 million cells used for an industrial analysis.

Selecting Fluid Physics Models

The first step in setting up this tutorial is to define the physics of the problem. For this case, the flow is turbulent and isothermal. Temperature calculations are on by default in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

To turn temperature calculations off:

1. Right-click the Continua > Continuum node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo tree and select Edit.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. Deactivate the Temperature option in the Optional Physics Models box.

3. Click OK.

Geometry Transfer: CAD to Simulation

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo allows you to transfer geometry from Creo to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ through a direct link between the two packages.

This feature provides you with a workflow that is tailored to design optimization. You can apply changes to the geometry in either Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and the changes are passed back to the other program. For example, you can make changes to the design after running an analysis in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ environment and these changes are passed back to the original Creo file. This feature requires a CAD client license.

This tutorial demonstrates how to select the CAD parameters in your original geometry and transfer the geometry from Creo to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you proceed to create a repeatable workflow (or pipeline) using mesh operations. After setting up this pipeline, you can make further changes to the geometry design and have STAR-CCM+ regenerate the corresponding volume mesh.

Opening the CAD Model

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ installation includes a directory containing the CAD geometry for this tutorial.

This directory is located in the starcreo folder of the downloaded tutorials bundle. To download the tutorials bundle, go to https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/product/226870983/downloads, and follow the procedure outlined in the main STAR-CCM+ > Tutorials > Using Tutorial Macros and Files > Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal section of the user guide.

1. Copy the directory to your own disk space.

2. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo and open the assembly file cardassem.asm in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo.

The assembly is made up of two parts: the card housing and the blower fan.

The imported geometry is shown below.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon appears at the top of the screen. The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo object tree is located on the left of the screen.

To switch to the object tree:

3. Click (STAR Tree).

If these items are not visible, refer to Launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo Manually.

Transferring the Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo, choose the CAD parameters to expose to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and then transfer the geometry.

Specify the CAD parameters to transfer to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Design Data.

The Design Data dialog appears.

2. In the CAD Parameters tab, select blowerfan.prt > p14 = 10.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo only recognizes native CAD features as CAD parameters.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 235

The value of this parameter is displayed in the Value property.

3. Click the checkbox next to the selected parameter to activate it.

4. Click OK.

Transfer the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

5. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo ribbon, click Transfer Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and the CAD geometry is transferred over.

6. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, create a geometry scene and position the geometry as shown below.

7. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, expand the Geometry node.

The transferred geometry appears under the Parts node. The properties that control the connection back to Creo, including the CAD parameter value, appear under the CAD Client Models node.

When transferring geometry from Creo to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, a link exists between the two software packages. This link allows data to be transferred between the two packages. To maintain this link, you must first save the geometry file in Creo:

8. Switch to Creo and save the geometry file.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Creo 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 236

In response, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ saves the simulation file with the name of the Creo geometry file. Using this technique, you can rename or relocate both the geometry and simulation files without breaking the link between the two packages. You can also save the simulation file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ so long as you do not rename it or relocate it. Doing so will break the link between the packages.

Creating the Shape Parts and Operations

The transferred geometry consists of the card housing and the blower fan. To simulate this case, you require two regions: one static region that provides an enclosure for the simulation, and another for the rotating region around the fan.

The transferred geometry contains the solid parts. You require the fluid volume around these parts. The first stage in obtaining the fluid volume is to create part shapes that correspond to the two regions. To save time, you are provided with these part shapes, one for the enclosure, and another for the rotating region.

Import the shape parts:

1. Select File  > Import > Import Surface Mesh.

2. Import the part shapes:

a) In the Open dialog, navigate to the directory that you downloaded in the first section of this tutorial and select box.x_t and disc.x_t.

b) Click Open.

c) In the Import Surface Options dialog, deactivate the Open Geometry Scene After Import option.

d) Click OK.

The static region, box, is shown below in relation to the graphics card:

Siemens Digital Industries Software 237

The rotating region, disc, is show below in relation to the graphics card:

Now subtract the solid CAD geometry from these shape parts to obtain the final fluid volume. Begin by subtracting the blower fan geometry from the disc part:

3. Right-click the Operations node and select New > Boolean > Subtract.

4. In the Create Subtract Operation dialog, set the following properties:

Property Setting

Input Parts disc

CARDASSEM > BLOWERFAN

Target Parts disc

5. Click OK.

6. Rename the Operations > Subtract node to Fan Subtraction.

7. Rename Parts > Subtract node to Rotating Region.

Subtract the card housing geometry and the disc part from the static region:

8. Create another subtract operation with the following settings:

Property Setting

Input Parts box

disc

CARDASSEM > CARDCASE

Siemens Digital Industries Software 238

Property Setting

Target Parts box

9. Rename Operations > Subtract node to Card Subtraction.

10.Rename Parts > Subtract node to Static Region.

To get a conformal mesh between the two regions, imprint both fluid volumes together:

11.Right-click the Operations node and select New > Boolean > Imprint.

12.In the Create Imprint Operation dialog, select Rotating Region and Static Region and click OK.

The transferred geometry contains CAD data. To ensure best results, instruct all operations to use the CAD data where available:

13.Under the Operations node, multi-select the Fan Subtraction and Card Subtraction nodes and activate the Perform CAD Boolean option.

14.Select the Operations > Imprint node and set Merge/Imprint Method to CAD Imprint.

The contacts between the two parts are created. These contacts are used while creating the regions to define the interfaces between the regions.

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Assign the parts to regions and create the automated mesh operation.

Assign the fluid parts to regions:

1. Expand the Geometry > Parts node and multi-select the Rotating Region and Static Region nodes.

2. Right-click on one of the selected parts and choose Assign Parts to Regions....

3. In the Assign Parts to Regions dialog:

a) Select Create a Region for Each Part.

b) Select Create a Boundary for Each Part Surface.

c) Click Apply and Close.

Create the automated mesh operation:

4. Right-click the Operations node and select New > Mesh > Automated Mesh.

5. In the Create Automated Mesh Operation dialog:

a) From the Parts list, select Rotating Region and Static Region.

b) Select the following meshers, in order:

Group Mesher

Surface Meshers Surface Remesher

Core Volume Meshers Polyhedral Mesher

Optional Boundary Layer Meshers Prism Layer Mesher

c) Click OK.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 239

An automated mesh operation is added to the Operations node. Refine the mesh settings for this case:

6. Expand the Automated Mesh > Default Controls node.

7. Select the Base Size node and set Value to 16 mm.

8. Select the Prism Layer Total Thickness node and set Percentage of Base to 20.

Generate the volume mesh:

9. Click (Generate Volume Mesh).

10.When the volume mesh is generated, create a mesh scene that displays the following parts:

◦ Rotating Region > Boundaries > CARDASSEM.BLOWERFAN.Faces

◦ Static Region > Boundaries > CARDASSEM.CARDCASE.Faces

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Add-on provides you with straightforward access to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver from within the Inventor environment.

Standard physics models, including turbulence, ideal gas, heat transfer, and gravity are supported for single body cases. Multiple body simulations involving conjugate heat transfer, rotating reference frames, and porous media are also supported. Advanced physics models can be added to the simulation by either launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and selecting them directly, or by implementing additional Java macro commands.

This section contains the user guide and tutorials for the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor CAD client.

This section assumes that you have previous experience in using Inventor, and only describes the additional features available as part of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

You can use Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor to transfer your CAD geometry directly into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ without transferring the CAE settings. This method is an alternate way importing geometry to using the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ CAD translators. See Transferring Geometry to STAR-CCM+.

Introducing Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor provides you with straightforward access to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver from within the Inventor environment.

Standard physics models, including turbulence, ideal gas, heat transfer, and gravity are supported for single body cases. Multiple body simulations involving conjugate heat transfer, rotating reference frames, and porous media are also supported. Advanced physics models can be added to the simulation by either launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and selecting them directly, or by implementing additional Java macro commands.

What are the Capabilities?

This section highlights the capabilities of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor enables you to:

• Define flow characteristics for the simulation

• Specify mesh parameters and controls

• Execute the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor, with specified solution controls

• Post-process results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

• Use parallel processing

Problem Definition

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor provides an interface for the specification of continua, regions, and boundaries in order to define the CFD simulation. This information is then used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to calculate a solution and present results.

The particular solver options that you can currently select through the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor interface include:

• Turbulence

◦ k-e Model

◦ Laminar

• Temperature

◦ Thermal Modelling

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 4

◦ Conjugate Heat Transfer

• Equation of State

◦ Constant Density

◦ Ideal Gas

• Porous Media

◦ Isotropic

◦ Uni-Directional

• Moving Reference Frames

• Energy Source

• Gravity

• Passive Scalar

Meshing

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor provides you with a transparent interface to Simcenter STAR-CCM+’s surface and volume meshing tools. This allows you to generate high-quality meshes using a solid model that was built within the Inventor environment. The specific meshing functionality includes:

• Surface meshing using the surface remesher for optimum mesh quality

• Prismatic subsurface meshing in the volume mesh for capturing near-wall boundary layers

• Volume meshing of parts with either:

◦ Tetrahedral core mesh generation

◦ Polyhedral core mesh generation

◦ Trimmed hexahedral core mesh generation

• Automatic handling of region-to-region interfaces

Running the Solver

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor allows the generation of solutions with varying accuracy and speed by providing the following solver controls:

• Number of iterations

• Stopping criterion at which to assume convergence

• Discretization scheme (1st or 2nd order)

• Solver under-relaxation factors

• Additional commands using Java macros

Post-processing

As post-processing is carried out in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, a wide range of tools are available for analysis. These include:

• Scalar scenes

• Vector scenes

• Streamlines

• Isosurfaces

• Plane sections

• Reports

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 5

• Plots

Parallel Processing

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor supports parallel processing for mesh generation and solver calculations. You can set up parallel processing in the Preferences dialog. The different Simcenter STAR-CCM+ licensing options can also be selected here. See Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Info App Window

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Info App window automatically appears when you start Inventor.

Initially, this window only contains the Status tab which displays the version and licensing information for Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor. More tabs appear as you create or load geometry files in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor, allowing you to perform more actions.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 6

You cannot close the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Info App window while Inventor or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor are running. Attempting to close the window by clicking the X button returns a message in the Status tab informing you of this. You can maximize and minimize the window by clicking the - and _ buttons respectively.

Use the Clear button to clear all the information that is displayed in a particular tab.

Use the Abort button to stop active processes, such as surface/volume meshing, or the solver. This button only appears when you can stop a process — it is grayed out at all other times.

A clock is displayed in the bottom-left of the window. This clock displays the current time on your machine. A progress bar is located next to the clock and reports the progress of various processes, such as mesh generation and the solver.

More information on the various tabs is provided in the following sections:

• The Status Tab

• The Output Tab

• The Model Checker Tab

• The Residuals Tab

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 7

The Status Tab

The Status tab displays the licensing information for your current session, informing you whether the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor license checked out successfully. The version of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor is also displayed in this tab. This tab appears by default when you launch Inventor without a geometry file.

The Output Tab

The Output tab appears once you create or open a geometry file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 8

During the meshing process, this tab displays status information along with a brief report on the generated mesh. If errors were encountered during the meshing process, they are reported here with suggestions as to what can be causing them.

When the solver is running, the Output tab behaves like the output window in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, displaying the data for each residual per iteration. When the solver finishes running, the same information is also displayed in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Output window.

You can control the amount of information that is displayed in the Output tab by editing the verbosity in the config.xml file. See Modifying the Config.xml File.

To abort the mesher or solver, click the Abort button.

The Model Checker Tab

The Model Checker tab displays information from the live model checker, where the case setup is actively monitored for any problems. See Checking the Model for Errors.

The following example reports that the case has no inlet boundary defined.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 9

The Residuals Tab

The Residuals tab appears when you launch the solver. Use the residuals to monitor the convergence of the solution being calculated.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 10

Typically, a drop in three to five orders of magnitude in the residuals indicates that the solution has converged to an acceptable level. The residuals that are displayed in this tab also appear in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ under the Plots node.

You can zoom in to the residuals by clicking and holding the left mouse button in the graph area and drawing a box around the area you want to view. To zoom out, right-click in the graph area. You can hide individual residuals from the Residuals tab by clicking their label at the top of the plot window.

Modifying the config.xml File

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ requires a configuration file to enable it to find the appropriate components to run correctly. This configuration file is created during installation. An explanation of the file and settings within it is given here.

The configuration file is called config.xml. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor searches for this file in the installation directory.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 11

Typical config.xml content is shown below. In this example Simcenter STAR-CCM+ version 15.06.### is shown.

<CAD> <STAR_HOME>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\star</ STAR_HOME> <SOLVER>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\star\bin \starccm+.exe</SOLVER> <LOGFILE>starcad.log</LOGFILE> <WWHELP>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.### \win64\Intel11.1\wwhelp.exe</WWHELP> <MANDIR>C:\Program Files\CD-adapco\15.06.###\STAR-CCM+15.06.###\doc\en \online</MANDIR> <VERBOSITY>Normal</VERBOSITY> <!-- Can be Verbose, Log or Normal. Default Normal --> </CAD>

You can edit the following lines:

• <SOLVER> provides the location of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver executable. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ licensing options are set in the Preferences dialog in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor user interface. See Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing.

• <LOGFILE> is the log file that will automatically be created and saved when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor is run. A path of your choice can be used.

• <VERBOSITY> is the verbosity of the output window in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Info App. This can be set to one of the following:

◦ Normal—This is the default setting and will display the least amount of information in the Output panel.

◦ Verbose—This will display a moderate amount of information in the Output panel.

◦ Log—This will display all available information in the Output panel.

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Object Tree

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor uses an object tree as the primary method for setting parameters.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 14

The object tree consists of nodes, each one of which represents a particular component of the simulation. This approach to the user interface complements the method that is used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+, allowing for an easy transition between the two software packages.

The object tree appears slightly different in assembly mode as it must accommodate multiple parts, but the principles of operation remain the same.

Nodes are arranged in an order that follows the recommended workflow for setting up a simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor. At each stage, you typically right-click on a particular node in the tree and choose the appropriate action from the pop-up menu.

Certain functionality within Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor applies to the simulation as a whole, rather than to individual objects. These operations are provided in the ribbon.

A complete list of all functions and their respective location is included in Understanding the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Interface.

Clicking on the Region node within the object tree will highlight all the relevant faces on the geometry model for that particular region. If different parts are assigned to multiple regions, then clicking on a region will only highlight the part and faces associated with that specific region. For example, clicking on the Fluid node below will highlight all the faces associated with the Fluid region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 15

Similarly, clicking on the Solid node highlights all the faces associated with the Solid region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 16

Clicking on a boundary node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor object tree highlights all the faces on the CAD geometry model that are associated with it. Note that clicking on the Default boundary node will not highlight any faces on the CAD geometry model. To stop highlighting the faces, you can either click on a blank space in the geometry window, or click on the root node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor object tree.

Setting Up Parallel Processing and Licensing

The licensing options and the options for setting up parallel processing are located in the Preferences dialog.

This dialog provides two sets of options: server preferences and server settings.

• Server preferences are applied whenever Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor starts a server.

• Server settings are saved in the CAD file and are applied only to that CAD file. Click Save as Default Server Settings to save the current server settings as the default settings to be applied to all CAD files.

To modify the run mode and licensing options:

1. Select Preferences from the ribbon.

Siemens Digital Industries Software 17

The Preferences dialog appears.

2. Select the run mode:

▶For serial, set Run Mode to Serial (the default setting).

You can use the up/down buttons or you can type in the number of cores that you want to use.

▶For advanced licensing options, such as Power on Demand, enter the appropriate argument in the Command field.

3. Select a licensing option:

This license is designed for parallel simulations, where you can use an unlimited number of cores in this session.

▶To use a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Lite license, select Lite Session.

6. Close the active Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ sessions.

7. Restart Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

Note: The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server only starts when it is required, such as during surface meshing or volume meshing. It does not start when you launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

If an option in the Preferences dialog conflicts with an option in the config.xml file, the option that is set in the Preferences dialog takes precedence. An example of such a situation is if the Compute Processes property is set to 4 in the Preferences panel, while it is set to 2 in the config.xml file; the simulation runs using four processors. See Modifying the config.xml File

Saving Files in Inventor

Product Excellence Program

The Product Excellence Program collects information about our customers and their use of Siemens Digital Industries Software. This information helps us improve our product features and functionality to better meet customer needs. No personal or intellectual property information is collected or shared. Product performance is not affected and participation in the program is voluntary.

Privacy statement

The Product Excellence Program helps Siemens Digital Industries Software understand how customers use our products and assists us in improving our products. The program is anonymous and participation is voluntary.

The Product Excellence Program is designed to protect the privacy of the user and the intellectual property created through the use of Siemens Digital Industries Software products.

How does it work?

The Product Excellence Program is used to collect data about your installation, the features you use and how you use them. The data is sent to Siemens Digital Industries Software for analysis. By examining usage patterns from a large number of people, we gain insight into how the products are used and how to improve the software in future releases. Data collection occurs in the background as you use the software and does not affect performance or functionality.

What data is sent?

The data collected can vary by product and by release as we gain more insight or add new capabilities. The Product Excellence Program may collect information on the functions utilized, the operating environment (e.g.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 23

OS, RAM, graphics, etc.), product version, or other indications of user interaction. The data may also include the company name that is using the product. This data is solely for use by Siemens Digital Industries Software to improve our products and is never shared with any third party.

There is no contact information in the data and Siemens Digital Industries Software will not contact you by phone or email as a result of the data collected. No information about the data you create or manage is collected.

Participation is optional.

You can control your participation during installation or reinstallation of the software by using the Product Excellence Program option in the interactive installer.

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on Different Machines

You can run Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on two different machines.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 30

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ operates on a client-server architecture, where Simcenter STAR-CCM+ is the server and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor is the client. A benefit of client-server architectures is that the client and the server do not have to be running on the same machine. Typically, CAD packages run on Windows operating systems. You can choose to run Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on any remote machine with a supported or certified platform, including Linux platforms.

Transferring Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

With Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor, you can transfer your CAD geometry directly to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ from within the Inventor environment. Along with the geometry data, you can also transfer design data, such as CAD parameters, coordinate systems, and reference planes.

The Transfer Geometry feature imports your geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+. This function provides an alternative method to the CAD translator add-ons for importing geometry. This method of transferring geometry can provide a faster workflow when performing a design analysis.

To transfer geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Transfer Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and imports the CAD geometry. You are now at the same stage in the workflow as if you imported the surface mesh directly into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using the CAD translators (File > Import > Import Surface Mesh...).

2. Set up your case in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Caution: Do not click Transfer CAE Model if you have previously used the Transfer Geometry method and set up your case in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. This action results in the loss of your settings in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Transferring Design Data to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Design data consists of CAD parameters, coordinate systems, and reference planes that you can transfer to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ along with the geometry.

CAD parameters control the feature dimensions, for example extrusion depth, and are useful for modifying the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ after running the analysis. You can use reference planes in scalar scenes and reports in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. You can use coordinate systems to define motion in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ simulation.

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, CAD parameters appear within the Expressions Editor dialog as single-values with units. You can select these for use in expressions, which in turn can be used in the following contexts:

• In 3D-CAD, for expressions that apply to design parameters

• Expression reports

• Coordinate parameters

Additionally, after transfer, you can set a CAD parameter in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to reference global scalar parameters.

This workflow maintains an active link between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+. When working with Geometry Transfer, you can modify the geometry in either package and the geometry in the relevant package is updated accordingly.

Updating the Geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Inventor Closed

You can close Inventor and continue working with the simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. Doing so, however, breaks the link between the two software packages. Any further updates that you make to the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ are not transferred back to the geometry in Inventor. Instead, these changes are stored in memory, which allows you to include the CAD parameters in your optimization scripts.

This workflow also allows you to release the Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor licenses when performing tasks in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In this case, the Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor licenses are temporarily checked out only when the updates to the geometry are stored in memory.

Transferring the geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor will overwrite the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

contacts are created for each pair of coincident faces. Leaving this option deactivated merges all solid bodies in the part.

Understanding the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Process

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor the typical workflow for running a simulation is as follows:

1. Ensure that the CAD model is suitable for analysis

2. Extract the fluid volume

3. Define the material properties for each part of the model, for example, air, water, aluminum

4. Define model physics, for example, turbulence, temperature, gravity

5. Specify boundary conditions, for example, inlets, outlets, symmetry planes

6. Specify mesh settings

7. Define solution controls

8. Run the case

9. Post-process the results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Once you have obtained an initial solution you may wish to re-run the case with some different settings, or with some changes to the geometry. To do this you can:

1. Return to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and change settings or modify the geometry

2. Re-run the case

Using Suitable CAD Models in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor only supports the use of solid bodies. If a geometry is made up entirely of surfaces then it will not be possible to define any boundary conditions, and the meshing options will be greyed out.

It is good practice to create copies of the original geometry file(s) before importing them into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

Suppressed or deactivated parts and features are not supported by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and will have no effect on the analysis. Hidden parts, however, are used in the analysis. Ensure that all desired parts and features are active before using them with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

Extracting the Fluid Volume

A CAD model usually represents a component made from solid material. However, in the case of flow simulation, a model representing the fluid volume is needed, requiring a different CAD model to be created. This is illustrated below:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 41

In some instances, a simulation will require multiple regions, such as:

• Moving Reference Frames

For rotating flow, such as turbines.

• Porous Media

For representing regions with fine geometric structures

• Energy Source

For simulating thermal specifications, such as conjugate heat transfer

These types of simulation require each region to be represented by individual contiguous parts within an assembly.

Defining Material Properties

Continua determines the characteristics of the fluid and solid entities used within the simulation. The behavior of a single continuum is primarily defined by the chosen material type and physics models.

Specification of the material type used in the simulation provides properties such as density, viscosity and conductivity, which are all used by the solver to calculate a solution. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor includes a database of common materials and allows you to modify material properties where necessary.

Defining Model Physics

Physics models determine the nature of the fluid, and can be described as either:

• Turbulent or Laminar

• Constant Density or Ideal Gas

Additional models can also be activated to meet the needs of various simulation requirements:

• Passive scalar

• Temperature

• Gravity

A region is defined as a volume domain in a simulation, surrounded by boundaries. Each region in the simulation must be represented by a part in the native CAD package. When multiple regions are required, multiple parts must be used within an assembly.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 42

All regions must be assigned to a continuum, as they represent a volume of material in the simulation. Region settings can be used to define porous media, moving reference frames, and an energy source.

Specifying Boundary Conditions

To define boundary conditions you first need to select the surface or surfaces on the model to assign to a separate boundary.

A boundary is defined as a surface, which along with other boundaries, surround and characterize a region. Boundary conditions determine how the boundary will affect the material within a region, and consequently, the simulation as a whole.

Inlet boundaries determine how much fluid enters the region, using a velocity, mass flow rate or stagnation inlet. Outlet boundaries define the process for fluid leaving the region, which are defined with either a pressure or flow-split ratio. Wall boundaries contain the fluid, and can also be used to define a thermal specification that will influence the transfer of energy to or from the region. Symmetry boundaries can be used to avoid modeling the entire region where appropriate, and so reduce calculation time.

As boundary types can affect the way in which the volume mesh is constructed, it is important to set them before generating the mesh.

Specifying Mesh Settings

The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solver uses the finite volume method to obtain an approximate solution to the underlying equations of fluid flow. This requires a mesh to be created, which represents the fluid volume as a collection of much smaller volumes known as cells.

A surface mesh is first created based on the boundaries defining the regions in the simulation. Thereafter a volume mesh is created to discretize the entire model.

The accuracy of the results is directly affected by mesh quality. If it is necessary to improve the quality of the mesh, some of the ways in which this can be done are to:

• Increase the mesh density, that is, the number of cells

• Add further sub-surface prism layers to capture near wall flow

• Refine the mesh in areas where flow characteristics are expected to change rapidly

As volume mesh quality is largely governed by the surface mesh quality, it is common practice to create and inspect the surface mesh before creating a volume mesh.

Defining Solution Controls

Solution controls determine the level of accuracy the solver will work towards. As a high accuracy solution will take longer, it may be necessary to compromise on this in order to obtain a result in a shorter time.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor includes five predefined solver settings ranging from fast (with low accuracy) to slow (with high accuracy). Advanced options are also available to provide further control.

Running the Case

When the simulation has been fully defined, the volume mesh is sent to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ along with all the necessary data for running the simulation. The time to complete a simulation will vary depending on the mesh density and solution controls.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 43

As the solver is running, residuals showing the rate at which individual equations are converging are shown in a plot. A scalar scene displaying absolute pressure is displayed on completion of the simulation.

Post-Processing the Results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Post-processing of simulations is carried out using the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ interface. This allows the results to be taken from the solver and displayed in a variety of scenes and plots.

Making Modifications to the Settings or Geometry

As Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor is completely integrated within the Inventor environment, it is very simple to perform parametric studies that examine the response of the fluid to changes in geometry. Once the first analysis is complete, the boundary conditions, run settings and all other properties of the CFD model are stored within the CAD file. Any changes in the flow field due to design changes can be recalculated by generating a new mesh and running the solver.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 44

Connecting to Remote Machines

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses a client-server architecture, and as such the CAD client ( Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor) and the server (Simcenter STAR-CCM+) are not required to run on the same machine.

Using an SSH (secure shell) connection, you can connect the client and server on two different machines, even when these are on different platforms. Due to how the CAD client and server interact in the background, the SSH connection must not ask for a username or a password.

There are two ways that you can connect Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+, depending on what your starting point is:

• You can start from the CAD client and launch the server on a remote machine. This method is useful for transferring CAD geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor running on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on Linux.

• You can start from the server and connect to the CAD client on a remote machine. This method is useful for connecting to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor to update the CAD geometry. With this method, you can perform a Design Manager analysis on a cluster while the geometry is updated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

Contents:

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

Running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor with Remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Starting from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor, you can choose to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on a remote machine.

Using this method, you can set up the full CAE analysis in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor on your local machine, and then run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server on the remote machine. You can also choose to transfer your geometry from the CAD client to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. This feature is useful if you want to import geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor running on Windows to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on Linux.

To configure Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor to launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ on a remote machine:

1. Make sure that you have a working SSH connection between the two machines.

For the SSH connection, you require an SSH server on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and an SSH client on the machine running Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor. The SSH connection to the remote machine must not ask for a username or a password. To avoid possible issues with a connection that still requires a password, add -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=0 to the SSH command. Setting this argument to zero stops the connection prompting for a password when one is needed — something that could cause the process to hang. See SSH Command.

2. In the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Preferences.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 45

3. In the Preferences panel, set Server Settings to Remote.

4. Set the remaining settings for your connection to the remote Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server. See Server

Settings Panel.

This information is used to build a command-line in the background when Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor invokes Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

5. If you are going to connect to the same remote host in future sessions, click Save as Default Settings.

The next time Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor invokes Simcenter STAR-CCM+, the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ server launches on the specified remote machine. A Simcenter STAR-CCM+ client is also launched on the local machine to allow you to see the active session on the remote machine.
