Defining Materials and Physics

Defining the physical properties of a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor model involves specifying the materials, flow characteristics, operating conditions, and physics models.

These definitions and settings are accomplished through the use of continua and regions, which are described in the following sections.

Contents:

Working with Continua and Regions

Importing Geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for Visualization

Working with Continua and Regions

Continua and regions are used together to capture the physical and material properties of a model.

A continuum represents a material in combination with a set of physics models that will be used to simulate the response of the material to the conditions imposed upon it. A continuum also provides the facility to define reference and initial values.

A region represents one or more volumes within the overall model, not necessarily contiguous, which will share the same continuum and set of boundary conditions. Regions are defined using CAD parts, and will be discretized by the volume mesher.

As well as holding a set of boundary conditions, regions can also be used to model specific physical behavior, including porous resistance, moving reference frames and energy sources.

Parts can be imported into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes without affecting the analysis.

Continua are assigned to single or multiple regions, which can contain single or multiple parts. In part mode, only one continuum and one region are available, as there is only one part. In assembly mode, new continua can be added to represent different materials present in the simulation, and new regions can be added to represent the parts composed of these materials. Continua and regions can be deleted if they are not required, although the simulation must always contain at least one of each.

There is a well defined relationship between continua, regions, boundary conditions and CAD parts.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 50

• Every region must be associated with a continuum.

• Several regions can be associated with the same continuum.

• Every CAD part must belong to a region.

• Several CAD parts can be associated with the same region.

• Boundary conditions belong to regions, and cannot be shared between regions.

• Every CAD surface must have a boundary condition associated with it. A default wall boundary is applied to CAD surfaces that have not been specifically associated with a user-defined boundary condition.

The following series of illustrations depict the relationship between CAD parts, continua, and regions, for a circular steel duct containing a rotating fan, and surrounded by a layer of insulation.

• Initially we have a collection of CAD parts in an assembly. These must be imprinted where appropriate to ensure that interfaces between parts can be created correctly.

• Three continua are required to represent the three different materials present in the simulation: the fluid (for example, air), the steel pipe, and the insulation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 51

• Two regions are required for the fluid portion of the simulation, as a rotating part is defined by applying a rotating frame of reference to a separate region surrounding the fan blades. Further regions are required for each of the solid parts (the steel pipe and insulating layer), which means a total of four separate regions overall.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 52

• A clearer picture can be given of the fan blade itself.

For an analysis containing a single part, for example a fluid-only case involving fluid flow through a converging-diverging pipe, the model will only require one continuum and one region in order to fully define

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 53

the physical and material properties of the model. In this case, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor automatically assigns the default continuum to the default region, and no further assignments are necessary.

Setting Up Continua

To define different materials and associated physics for use in an assembly, you require additional continua. In each continuum you can specify a unique set of properties, such as a different material type or temperature. In assembly mode, continua are stored under a Continua node, as shown below.

To create an additional continuum:

1. Right-click the Continua node in the object tree and select New.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. In the Name field, enter a name for the continuum.

3. In the Materials group, select the type of material that you want to define:

▶Gas

▶Liquid

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 54

▶Solid

4. Select a material from the list.

You can modify the properties of any material that you select.

Note: You can select only one material per continuum. If your simulation contains a number of materials, you must create additional continua. This action is only possible for assemblies.

5. In the Flow Characteristics group, select the type of flow that you want to model: Laminar or Turbulent. This group only appears for fluids.

6. In the Equation of State group, select the equation of state : Constant Density or Ideal Gas. This group only appears for gases.

7. In the Optional Physics Model group, activate any optional physics models: Passive Scalar and Temperature.

8. Define the material properties in the Material Properties group.

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Material Properties Panel.

Note: You can change units of properties from the drop-down menu.

9. In the Reference Properties group, define the reference properties.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 55

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Reference Properties Panel.

10.If you want to include the body force due to gravity when calculating the momentum equations in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, activate the gravity model in the Gravity group box.

See Activating the Gravity Model in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

11.Set the initial conditions in the Initialization group box.

See Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Initialization Panel.

Specifying initial conditions that are close to the expected solution can reduce the number of iterations required to reach a solution. You can set the initial conditions similar to the inlet conditions of the fluid domain.

Initial conditions are specified at a continuum level; if no initial conditions are specified, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor will use default values to initialize the solution.

12.Click OK.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 56

The continuum is added to the object tree.

Once you have created a continuum, you can assign it to a region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Material Properties Panel

You can define the following material properties in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor:

Property Description

Density Available for all types of materials. For gases, this property is available when you use the Constant Density equation of state.

Specific Heat Available for all material types when you activate the Temperature physics model.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Reference Properties Panel

You can define the following continuum reference properties:

Property Description

(Reference Pressure) The pressure values that are defined in the simulation are all relative to the reference pressure. For more information, see the What is the Reference Pressure? section.

(Reference Temperature) The reference temperature is used to define the operating temperature of the fluid in the buoyancy source term of the Boussinesq model. This parameter is used by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ when the temperature, constant density, and gravity physics models are enabled.

(Reference Density) These quantities are not used as part of the CFD calculation, but is necessary to calculate the force

Siemens Digital Industries Software 57

Property Description

(Reference Velocity) coefficients when post-processing.

(Reference Area)

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Initialization Panel

Specifying initial conditions that are close to the expected solution can reduce the number of iterations required to reach a solution. You can also set the initial conditions to match inlet conditions of the fluid domain. You can define the following continuum reference properties:

Property Description

(U Component of Velocity) The U direction vector for the initial velocity.

(V Component of Velocity) The V direction vectors for the initial velocity.

(W Component of Velocity) The W direction vectors for the initial velocity.

(Initial Pressure) The initial pressure. The physical value of the initial pressure defines the starting pressure in the regions to which the continuum is assigned. The initial pressure is specified with respect to the reference pressure. The default initial pressure is 0 Pa.

(Initial Temperature) The initial temperature. This physical value of the initial temperature defines the starting temperature throughout any region to which the continuum is assigned. The default initial temperature is 300 K.

(Turbulence Intensity) The initial turbulence intensity. The default value is 0.05 (5%)

(Turbulent Length Scale) The initial turbulent length scale. The default value is 0.01 m.

Setting Up Regions

Additional regions are required when modelling multiple region physics, or when specific behavior such as porous resistance is required for a particular part within the same continuum. Assign parts from an assembly to regions. You can control the properties of these regions through the assigned continuum.

In assembly mode, regions are stored under the Regions node in the object tree, as shown below.

To create an additional region:

1. Right-click the Regions node in the object tree and select New.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 59

The Region Settings dialog appears.

2. In the Name property, enter a name for the region.

3. Select the parts that you want to include in the region.

You can select multiple parts from the graphics window or the Inventor feature tree.

Selected parts appear in the Parts Selection group box field.

4. Select a continuum to apply to the region.

All available continua are listed here.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 60

Note: Assigning a continuum to a region causes the region to inherit the physical and material properties defined in the continuum

5. Activate any additional region physics for the region:

◦ Porous. See Defining a Porous Region.

◦ Moving Reference Frame. See Defining a Moving Reference Frame.

◦ Energy Source. See Defining an Energy Source.

6. If you want to import parts into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes, but do not want the region to be included in the CFD calculations, activate the Exclude from Analysis option. See Importing Geometry into STAR-CCM+ for Visualization.

7. Click OK.

A new region is added to the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor object tree under the Regions node.

The parts that you assign to a region define the geometric extent of the region. Within this geometry, properties and behavior of the material is governed by the physics models and material properties defined in the region and continuum settings.

Note: Each region must be assigned at least one part, otherwise it will be ignored during the CFD analysis.

By default, every Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor model contains one continuum, and this is automatically assigned to the default region and each additional region that you create. If multiple continua are defined in the model, you can choose a different continuum to assign to each region. This enables you to control the physical properties of each region, including varying material types.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 61

All the parts in an assembly are assigned to the default region (this is the initial region created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor). When you assign a part to another region, it is automatically removed from the default region. If you remove a part from a region, it is reassigned back to the default region.

Importing Geometry into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for Visualization

You can import CAD parts, that do not form part of the analysis, into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes.

Add these parts to a separate region—this region is excluded from the analysis. This feature is useful for showing the original geometry in a post-processing scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. For example, for an internal fluid volume of a pipe, the original geometry is the solid pipe.

To exclude CAD parts from the analysis:

1. In the Region Settings dialog, add the CAD parts that you want to use for visualization purposes.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 67

2. Activate the Exclude From Analysis checkbox in the Advanced panel.

3. Click OK.

When you run the case, a surface mesh is generated for this region using the settings specified in the Mesh Pipeline.

Note: As is the case for all assemblies, you must imprint all parts that are used for visualization purposes onto any surface that they cut, otherwise you will not be able to generate the surface mesh.

An example of this feature is shown in the following section, where a valve and valve body geometry are imported into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization.

Contents:

Setting Up a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Scene to Display Imported Geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

Setting Up a Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Scene to Display Imported Geometry from Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

You can visualize geometry that is not included in the analysis. For example, you can add the valve and valve housing geometry to a Geometry Scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor, even though this does not have any effect to the flow.

To use parts that are excluded from the analysis in a scene:

1. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, create a new scene.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 68

In the following example, a Geometry Scene is used.

2. Create a streamlines derived part.

3. Click on the scene/plot button.

Setting Boundary Conditions

Boundary conditions tell the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers how the substance within the region interacts with its environment. A velocity inlet boundary, for example, tells the solvers that an amount of substance is being added to the fluid domain at a certain rate.

A Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor boundary is made up of one or more CAD surfaces within the simulation which, along with other boundaries, surround and define a region.

The boundary is discretized by the surface mesher, which is then used by the volume mesher to mesh the entire region.

It is important to set the boundary conditions before creating the volume mesh, as some parts of the volume mesh, such as prism layers, depend on the type of boundary.

By default, each region contains only one boundary. To define more boundaries you need to add boundaries to the region. You can modify the properties of existing boundaries by editing its boundary node.

Some boundaries may require the specification of turbulence quantities, temperature, and passive scalar concentration, depending on whether these modeling options have been activated in Continuum Settings.

Symmetry Plane Boundary

A symmetry plane boundary represents an imaginary plane of symmetry in the simulation. The solution that is obtained with a symmetry plane boundary is identical to the solution that would be obtained by mirroring the mesh about the symmetry plane (in half the resulting domain). There are no settings which are specific to symmetry plane boundaries.

Meshing the Model

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor provides options for generating polyhedral or trimmed volume meshes, with or without near-wall prism layers.

By default, prism layers are generated on all wall surfaces. The provision of a prism layer depends on the type of boundary that is applied to a face. As a consequence, it is recommended that you only generate the mesh after setting up the boundaries and regions.

The meshing process first creates a triangulated surface (the surface mesh) and thereafter converts it to the desired volume mesh (polyhedral or trimmer). As the quality of the volume mesh depends to a large extent on the quality of the surface mesh, it is prudent to check the surface mesh before proceeding with the volume mesh.

Although the entire meshing process can be launched with a single command (the Build And Run command from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon), it is possible to execute only single stages from the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventorribbon. Settings that are made in the Mesh Pipeline node govern the mesh generation process.

A mesh pipeline contains all the settings that are applied to the surface and volume meshes created on the Inventor parts to which it is applied. In single part mode, only one mesh pipeline is available. In assembly mode, multiple mesh pipelines can be created if necessary.

When mesh generation commences, each mesh pipeline will:

1. Extract geometry from Inventor.

2. Transfer the model to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3. Execute the surface remesher.

4. Execute the polyhedral or trimmer volume mesher with the prism layer mesher (if selected).

5. Create a mesh representation in the Inventor Graphics window.

Controls on the top-level mesh pipeline node allow you to set the base sizes for the surface mesh, and control the prism layer. Further refinement to specific faces, parts, or volume shapes can be made by adding additional controls to the mesh pipeline.

Creation of Additional Surfaces in Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ creates geometry part surfaces during the geometry transfer stage.

Initially, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor creates one part surface for each face in the CAD model. These part surfaces are then combined so that one surface per boundary remains. This outcome, however, is not possible for boundaries that contain CAD surfaces from more than one part. The final part surfaces appear in the Geometry > Parts node in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

The following items affect the number of part surfaces that are created in Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

• The number of boundaries present in the model, including the default boundary. Each boundary in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor appears as a separate part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. If, however, a boundary contains CAD surfaces from multiple parts, the part surfaces in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ cannot be combined.

• The number of mesh pipeline controls used (if any). Each CAD surface that is used to define a face mesh control in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor appears as a separate part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

• The number of interfaces that are created during the meshing process (for assemblies only). All the CAD surfaces that define one interface between two parts in an assembly are grouped together under one part surface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. One part surface exists for each interface in Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Boundary Splitting due to Interface Generation

Interfaces are automatically created between two parts in an assembly during the mesh generation. A new boundary is created for each interface on the surfaces that share the interface.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 80

Boundary Splitting due to Face Mesh Controls and Part Mesh Controls

If you use a face mesh control or a part mesh control in your simulation, some boundaries may be split, depending on what faces are included in the mesh control. If a boundary and mesh control share the same faces, no splitting occurs. If a mesh control contains faces from multiple boundaries, splitting occurs and a new boundary is created. The name of the new boundary is derived from the original boundary.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 81

Working with Mesh Pipelines

When working with a single part, you will only have one mesh pipeline defined in the model tree. This will specify the mesh settings for the single part available. In assembly mode, multiple mesh pipelines can be created to give specific controls for different parts, and parts must be specifically associated with a mesh pipeline.

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

The mesh pipeline node contains the general mesh settings that will apply to all Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor parts associated within the pipeline in the absence of any further controls.

To set up the mesh pipeline:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor tree and select Edit.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 82

The Mesh Pipeline Settings dialog appears.

2. In the Name field, enter the name of the mesh pipeline if required.

3. In the Part Selection box, specify the desired parts to use in the mesh pipeline.

This property is only available when working with assemblies.

4. From the Mesh Type tab, select the type of mesh that you want to generate:

▶Polyhedral

▶Trimmer

5. Set Base Size to the desired value.

The base size is a reference length used in other meshing parameters. It may be set to equal the length of the largest triangle you expect to have on your surface mesh, or to some other characteristic dimension.

The base size can be set as either a relative or absolute value. When it is set as a relative value, the reference size will be the diagonal of the bounding box enclosing the entire geometry. In the case of multiple parts in an assembly, the reference size will be calculated based on the diagonal length of the bounding box enclosing the entire assembly. This includes all parts from all mesh pipelines. The unit specification menu will become active when setting an absolute value.

6. Set Surface Mesh Size to the desired value.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 83

The surface mesh size is the base edge length of triangles on the surface mesh. Note that the ultimate length of some (or all) triangles on the surface mesh will depend on other factors such as surface curvature and edge proximity.

7. Set the prism layer settings. See Prism Layer Panel.

8. Set the advanced settings. See Mesh Pipeline Advanced Settings Panel.

9. If you selected to generate a trimmed mesh, set the Trimmer settings. See Trimmer Panel.

10.Click OK.

Property Description

Siemens Digital Industries Software 84

Mesh Pipeline Advanced Settings Panel

The advanced settings panel provides further customization of meshing parameters.

Property Description

Relative Minimum Surface Size Defines the minimum triangle size permitted on a feature curve. The minimum triangle size is set as a percentage of the surface mesh size. The default value is set to 25%. You must set the relative minimum surface size to a value greater than zero. If you set the relative minimum surface size to 100%, Simcenter STARCCM+ will not modify the triangle size when it detects curvature.

The figure below illustrates this behavior. Note that the base size was set to 20% in this example to emphasize the refinement on the curve.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 85

Property Description

Having a large value for the number of points on a circle property increases the mesh resolution on curved surfaces.

The transition between the fine mesh and coarse mesh areas is controlled by the growth ratio.

Growth Ratio Controls the rate at which triangle sizes change when moving from one triangle size to another. In the example below, the end faces of the block were set to have a smaller triangle size than the four side faces of the block. When the growth ratio is set to a low value, the transition between triangle size is very gradual. When a higher value is used, the transition is far more rapid.

The growth factor must be set to a value greater than 1.0. There is no upper limit for the growth factor.

Number of Points per Circle Controls the number of triangle edges that appear on a curved surface, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 86

Property Description

Regardless of the number of points per circle defined, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor will not permit the triangle edge length to shrink below 25% of the base size. The curvature length scale may also affect the number of edges on a curved surface.

Trimmer Panel

The trimmer mesh is controlled using the Trimmer panel.

Property Description

Default Growth Rate Controls the stepping of the refinement from one cell size to the next. Five settings are available. By default, the Default Growth Rate is set to Fast, meaning that the fastest transition from the smallest cell size to the largest will be used. This usually equates to having only one layer of each cell size for each transition, which will result in the least number of cells being created for the supplied input values. The Medium, Slow, and Very Slow options further slow the transition from one cell size to the next in the mesh interior and therefore increase the overall cell count. In general, the medium option results in a minimum of two equal sized cell layers per transition, slow in four layers and the very slow option in eight layers.

Boundary Growth Rate Controls the number of cell layers to grow next to surfaces in the template. Five settings are available. By default, the Boundary Growth Rate is set to None, meaning that the setting used for the Default Growth Rate is used for controlling all transitions. If the Very Slow, Slow, Medium, or Fast options are selected then it will result in eight, four, two or one layers of

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 87

Property Description

cells respectively of the same size being created next to the geometry surfaces in the template.

Working with Mesh Controls

Mesh controls allow you to define custom mesh settings for a particular section of the model.

Multiple controls can be assigned to the same item to control different mesh parameters. If, for example, a face has two mesh controls assigned to it--one that controls the mesh size and another that controls the prism layer thickness, the final mesh will respect both the custom mesh size and the custom prism layer thickness. If two mesh controls set the same mesh parameter, the control created last will take precedence over the first.

Contents:

Using a Face Mesh Control

Using a Volumetric Mesh Control

Using a Part Mesh Control

Using a Face Mesh Control

A face mesh control allows you to set the surface mesh size and the prism layer parameters on a face. Custom settings made on a face control will take priority over settings in the parent mesh pipeline, and over settings made in any part mesh controls.

To add a face mesh control:

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline > Mesh Controls node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor tree and select New Face Mesh Control.

The Face Mesh Control dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 88

2. Set Name to an appropriate value.

3. On the CAD geometry, select the desired faces to include in this mesh control.

4. If you want to specify a custom surface mesh size on the selected surfaces, activate the Custom Surface Mesh Size option.

a) Set (Custom Surface Mesh Size) to the desired value.

You can enter this value as a percentage of the base size, or as an absolute value. If you select to enter the absolute value, you can select the units from the drop-down menu.

5. Set Prism Layer Settings to the desired value:

▶Inherit Values: in the first instance, the face(s) will be assigned values from any part mesh control applied to the part to which the face(s) belong. If this does not apply, values will be taken from any applicable volumetric mesh control, and in the absence of this values will be taken from the parent mesh pipeline.

▶Use Custom Values: allows the prism layer parameters to be set directly on the face(s). See Prism Layer

Panel.

▶Disable: no prism layer will be generated on the face(s).

6. Click OK.

Using a Volumetric Mesh Control

A volumetric control permits mesh refinement within a user-defined box or sphere. Only the mesh size can be modified with a volumetric control; prism layer parameters are not affected.

To add a volumetric mesh control:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 89

1. Right-click the Mesh Pipeline > Mesh Controls node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor tree and select New Volumetric Control.

The Volumetric Control dialog appears.

2. Set Name to an appropriate value.

3. Set Custom Surface Mesh Size to the desired value.

The mesh size defines the triangle edge length for surface mesh within the volume shape, and the characteristic cell size for volume mesh. The custom mesh size will still affect the volume mesh in cases where the volume shape does not intersect any surfaces of the Pro/E geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 90

The mesh size can either be defined relative to the base size of the parent mesh pipeline, or as an absolute dimension with length units.

4. Select the type of volumetric control to create:

▶Box

▶Sphere

5. Enter the parameters for the volumetric shape:

▶If you are creating a box, enter the coordinates for Point 1 and Point 2.

X, Y, and Z coordinates of the two opposite corners of the box are required by the panel. These coordinates can either be entered manually, or taken from existing points within the Pro/E window. To use an existing point, click Choose Point 1 or Choose Point 2 and use the Inventor point selection operation to select the appropriate point.

▶If you are creating a sphere, enter the coordinates for the center point and the radius of the sphere.

The sphere shape is defined by a center point and a radius. The center point can be set either by entering the coordinates directly, or by clicking the Choose Point button and using the Pro/E point selection procedure to choose an existing point in the Pro/E window. The coordinates of the existing point will be used to populate the panel.

6. Click Create.

The shape is added to the Shapes list.

7. Click OK.

Controlling the Mesh Depth

The Depth option controls the mesh visualization (mesh depth). If the mesh appears to be hidden behind the geometry surface and is hard to see (particularly when zooming in closer, as shown in the screenshot below), changing the mesh Depth option may help improve mesh visualization.

Increasing the Depth value will improve the mesh definition.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 95

To change the depth of the mesh:

1. Click Depth = Default in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon and select the desired depth from the drop-down list.

The higher the number the more pronounced the mesh will be, however increasing this value too much will cause the mesh from behind the geometry to start appearing (particularly near the edges). For thin geometries, a high depth number should be avoided as the entire mesh will be visible, including the mesh from behind the geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 96

The default setting (Depth = Default) should work well with most geometries. The original Pro/E value is stored in the Depth = Original setting--this tends to hide the mesh when zooming in and is not recommended for most cases.

Meshing Behavior at Interfaces

The volume mesher will treat interfaces between two regions differently depending on what type of region (fluid or solid) these are.

If the interface lies between two fluid regions, no prism layers will be grown from both sides of the interface. If an interface lies between a solid region and a fluid region, prism layers will be grown from the interface. The default behavior of the prism layer generation can be overridden using a mesh control, so prism layers can be disabled on a solid-fluid interface. See Working With Mesh Controls.

See Also:

Working with Mesh Controls

Common Causes for Meshing Failures

There may be instances when the mesh generation fails. In most cases this will occur during the surface meshing phase. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor will try and identify the cause and suggest ways of rectifying this. This information will be printed in the Output tab of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Info App window.

The Parts in an Assembly are not Imprinted

The parts in an assembly should be imprinted together so that there is a common contact area between them.

A simple example of when imprinting is required is shown below.

Obtaining a Solution

The following section details the execution of the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers in order to obtain a solution.

Contents:

Setting Solution Controls

Checking the Model for Errors

Building and Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

Clearing the Solution

Visualizing the Solution

Setting Solution Controls

The solution you obtain from the solvers is a compromise between accuracy and processing time. You can manage the speed and accuracy of the solver from the Solution Controls dialog. The solution accuracy is also dependant on the mesh density.

To set up the solution controls in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor:

1. Either:

▶Right-click on the STAR-Inventor node within the object tree and select Solution Controls.

▶From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, select Solution Controls.

The Solution Controls dialog appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 102

2. Set the solution control parameters:

▶Using the slider, select one of the five pre-defined solver options. These options range from high accuracy and low speed, to low accuracy and high speed.

▶Click the Advanced tab and set the solution control parameters manually. See Solution Controls

Advanced Settings Panel.

3. If you want to run a Java macro with the simulation, activate the Use Java File option. See Using Java

Macros with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

4. Click OK.

Contents:

Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel

The advanced settings in the Solution Control dialog allow you to manually enter the values for the solution control parameters.

Parameter Description

Stopping Criteria

(Number of Iterations) Specifies the maximum number of iterations for which the solver can run. When the Simcenter STARCCM+ solver reaches the specified number of iterations, it will stop. You can then post-process the results in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Convergence Levels.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 103

Parameter Description

(Convergence Level) Specifies how many orders of magnitude the residuals should drop before the solver stops. See Convergence Levels.

Solution Accuracy

First Order This option is generally the quicker, but less accurate solver option. The first order scheme introduces a dissipative error that is stabilizing and helps the solver achieve robust convergence. However, it can also lead to the neglect and merging of discontinuities, meaning the solution is not fully captured.

Second Order This option is generally the more accurate, but slower solver option. The second order scheme attempts to minimize both dispersive and dissipative errors, providing a better representation of the simulation. However, in some situations, the lack of numerical dissipation can result in poorer convergence properties.

It is common practice to use the first order scheme initially to ensure the simulation is running as expected and then switch to second order.

Under-Relaxation Factors

(Momentum Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the momentum equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Pressure Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the pressurecorrection equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Turbulence Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the under-relaxation factor for the turbulence equation. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Fluid Temperature Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the fluid under-relaxation factor for the segregated energy solver. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

(Solid Temperature Under-Relaxation Factor) Specifies the solid under-relaxation factor for the segregated energy solver. See Solution Controls Advanced Settings Panel.

Convergence Level

The numerical method used by the solver requires an iterative process in order to obtain a solution. After each iteration, residuals are produced that indicate how well the governing equations for each solver quantity are being satisfied numerically. In general, the residual magnitude should decrease as the solution converges.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 104

When the magnitude of the residuals for all the quantities falls below the convergence level, the solver will stop iterating, and results will be exported for post-processing.

Note: In most cases, a drop of 3-5 orders of magnitude in the residuals is sufficient to obtain an accurate solution.

You can adjust the convergence level parameter to meet accuracy or process time requirements. However, if the residuals are no longer decreasing from one iteration to the next, it is likely that machine accuracy has been reached for that case. For a case that does not exhibit decreasing residuals, it would be necessary to reconsider the setup in case the volume mesh is too coarse, or boundary conditions have been set incorrectly.

Under-Relaxation Parameters

Under-relaxation parameters determine how quickly the solver reaches a solution for a particular equation, on a scale from 0 to 1, with 1 being the fastest.

Ideally, all under-relaxation parameters would be set to 1, however, doing so would likely cause solver instability due to the complex nature of most simulations. Hence the under-relaxation parameters should be set to values that compromise speed with stability.

Note: Adjust the under-relaxation parameters if changes to other solution controls such as Number of Iterations, Convergence Levels, and Solution Accuracy have failed to improve the behavior of the solver.

Using Java Macros in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

You can use Java macros with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to automate your simulation or to change a setting in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as selecting an alternative turbulence model, before the solver starts running.

An example of how to change a setting in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ using a Java macro is outlined below:

1. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and set up the case.

Define the continuum settings, boundary conditions, mesh settings, and solution control settings.

2. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

3. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, start recording a macro and perform the desired operations, such as changing the physics models.

4. Stop recording the macro.

The macro saves at this point.

5. Close Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and do not save the simulation.

6. Return to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor, open the Solution Controls dialog and activate the Use Java File checkbox.

A text entry field appears.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 105

7. Click More Commands....

The Open dialog appears.

8. Navigate to your Java macro file and select it.

Selected files appear in the text entry field. The path in the entry field is displayed relative to the current CAD geometry file.

9. Click OK.

When you run the simulation, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ will launch and play the macro before starting the solver. This sequence allows you to set up and use additional Simcenter STAR-CCM+ physics models that are not available in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

Checking the Model for Errors

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor monitors the active case for any errors in real-time and displays a

warning triangle next to any nodes for which there is a problem.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 106

Three areas are monitored by the live model checker:

• Continua. The continua checker makes sure that all necessary boundaries are present in the case, such as the presence of at least one inlet and one outlet.

• Regions and boundaries. The regions and boundaries checker covers issues specific to boundaries, such as a velocity inlet boundary having a zero value.

• Mesh pipelines. The mesh pipeline checker covers issues that are related to the mesh, such as the presence of multiple parts in a trimmed mesh pipeline.

To see the cause of an error:

1. Right-click on an node displaying the warning triangle, and select Show Errors...

A dialog appears describing the error, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 107

2. Click OK to close the dialog.

The Show Errors... right-click menu is available for any node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor object tree that contains a warning triangle. Selecting it will show errors for that node and its sub-nodes.

To see a complete list of issues for the case, right-click on the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor root node and select Show Errors...

You can also manually check for errors.

To perform a manual check:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click t Check.

If errors are found in the case set up, these are displayed in the Model Checker tab of the Info App dialog. See The Model Checker Tab.

Building and Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

Once you have defined the model physics, boundary conditions, mesh settings, and solver settings in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor, you can build and run the case.

To build and run the case:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Build and Run.

This action automatically generates the mesh, and runs the solver. When you run the solver, a new Residuals tab is added to the Info App dialog. You can use this residuals plot to monitor solution convergence. When the solver finishes, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and a scalar scene is automatically created for you.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 108

Note: If a solution has already been computed in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, and the stopping criteria has been reached, clicking Build and Run clears the solution and starts running from the first iteration. If you want to run for more iterations, change the stopping criteria and click Run Solver, or click Run More Iterations.

Running the Simulation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor

If you have already generated a volume mesh for the model, you can run the case directly.

To run the solver:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Run Solver.

Running for More Iterations

You may need to run the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers for more iterations than you originally set in the Number of Iterations stopping criterion. The Run More Iteration function runs the solver for an additional number of iterations as specified in the stopping criteria. Take, for example, a case where you have already run the simulation for 300 iterations. You specify 500 iterations in the Number of Iterations stopping criterion. When you next click Run for More Iterations, the simulation will run for 500 extra iterations, making 800 iterations in total. The solver runs until one of the stopping criteria is satisfied.

To run for more iterations:

• From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Run For More Iterations.

Clearing the Solution

You can clear all results that were calculated by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers using the Clear Solution function. All other Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor simulation settings remain intact.

Caution: This action is irreversible.

To clear the solution:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, select Clear Solution.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 109

The solution that was calculated by the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ solvers is deleted.

Visualizing the Solution

When Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches after the solution is calculated, it automatically displays a scalar scene of the model that shows the Absolute Pressure field function.

To visualize the results, you can use this scene to display different scalar quantities, or use any of the other visualization tools in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, such as streamlines, plane sections and vector scenes.

You can import CAD parts into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes. These parts will not be taken into account during the analysis. This feature is useful for displaying the original geometry in a post-processing scene in Simcenter STAR-CCM+. See Importing Geometry Into STAR-CCM+ for Visualization.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Exporting the Surface Mesh

You can export the surface mesh generated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor as a native CD-adapco surface mesh (.dbs) file. The .dbs file format is the recommended format to use when transferring surface data between CD-adapco programs, which are now part of Siemens. The boundary names and boundary types are retained by the file, as well as the interfaces that were automatically created between regions.

To export the surface mesh:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Export > Surface Mesh (.dbs).

Exporting the Volume Mesh

You can export the volume mesh that you generated in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor as a native CD-adapco volume mesh (.ccm) file. The .ccm file format is the recommended format to use when transferring volume meshes between CD-adapco programs, which are now part of Siemens. The region and boundary names, and region and boundary types are retained in this file. The interfaces that were automatically created interfaces between regions are also retained in this file.

To export the volume mesh:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Export > Volume Mesh (.ccm).

Guidelines

This section aims to provide guidance and assistance on making a geometry part suitable for CFD analysis using Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

Contents:

Creating the Fluid Domain

Imprinting Parts

Creating the Fluid Domain

In the majority of CAD models, the fluid domain for analysis must be extracted from the original part or assembly. The topics that are containing within this section demonstrate how to prepare the fluid domain.

Contents:

Internal Flow

External Flow

Multi Region Flow

Internal Flow

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for an internal flow are:

• Work in a part. Import the original geometry into the new part (by making the new part derived), ensuring that all parts are maintained as separate solid bodies.

• Close any openings by creating “caps”.

• Create an overall block that encloses all the other geometry parts, the “enclosure”.

• Subtract all parts from the enclosure and delete the outer solid body--the remaining geometry is the fluid domain.

• Create a new assembly from the multi body derived part.

A worked example is provided below. In this case the assembly contains two parts: the valve (shown in red), and the valve housing (shown in blue).

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 116

1. Create a new part file in CATIA and name it Internal Fluid Volume.

By default CATIA will open a sketch--close this sketch.

We will make this part file derived and import the assembly we want to extract the internal fluid volume from. During the import operation we can choose to import each part of the assembly as separate bodies. This is useful if you want to visualize the original components or perform a conjugate heat transfer analysis.

2. Click on the Derive button in the Create panel of the ribbon.

3. Locate and select the assembly or part file where you want to create the internal volume.

The Derived Assembly dialog appears.

4. In the Derived Assembly dialog, click (Maintain each body as a solid body).

This will keep the solids in the assembly as separate bodies. The default option is to merge all solids into one solid body.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 117

Notice that two bodies were imported into the part file under the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree.

5. Rename the imported bodies to something more representative--in this example the two bodies were renamed to Valve Housing and Valve respectively.

Hovering the mouse pointer over the body nodes will highlights the corresponding body in the geometry window, this makes it easier to identify the bodies when renaming them.

We will now cap any openings.

6. Create a sketch on one of the faces containing an opening, as shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 118

By default, CATIA automatically converts any edges that lie on the sketch plane into sketch entities. These will appear in orange.

7. In this case we only require the outer edge, so click on the inner edge and delete it by pressing <Delete>.

If the automatic projection option was turned off, you will need to manually project the outer edge of the face onto the sketch.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 119

8. Create an extrusion from the sketch to cap the opening. The length of the extrusion is not important.

In the Extrude dialog, click on the (New solid) button to make the cap a new body rather than merge it with the existing body it is in contact with.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 120

9. A new body will be added to the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree; rename this to Cap1.

10.Using the same technique, cap any other openings on the geometry, and rename the new bodies in the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 121

We will now create a solid block that completely encloses the other parts. This block will be added as a separate solid body in the part file.

11.Create a sketch that completely encloses the assembly, as shown below.

12.Extrude the sketch so that it completely encloses the geometry.

In the Extrusion dialog, click on the (New Solid) button, otherwise the geometry contained within the extrusion would be merged with the extrusion.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 122

13.Note that a new solid is added to the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree, rename this to Internal Fluid Volume.

We will now subtract the original assembly and caps from the solid block. The result will be a solid block that contains a cavity separating the outer solid from the inner solid (the internal fluid volume).

14.Click on Combine in the Modify panel of the ribbon.

The Combine dialog will appear.

15.Click on the (Cut) button, and select the enclosure as the Base.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 123

16.Now select the other bodies (the original assembly parts and the caps) as the Toolbody.

A dashed outline will appear when the mouse pointer hovers over hidden parts, as shown below. Click to select these parts.

17.In the Combine dialog, activate the Keep Toolbody option.

By default the toolbody parts are consumed by this operation, however we want to keep them.

We will now delete the outer solid. The remaining solid is the internal fluid volume.

18.Click on the Delete Face button in the Surface panel of the ribbon.

The Delete Face dialog will appear.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 124

19.Click on the (Select lump or void) button, and select the solid body in the geometry window--this will delete the outer solid body and leave the internal fluid volume.

The internal fluid volume of the geometry is shown below.

The last step is to export the bodies from this multi body part into an assembly, where they can be selected for use in STAR-CAT5.

20.Save the current part file using a suitable name.

21.Make the original assembly components visible by right-clicking on these in the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree and selecting Visibility.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 125

22.Click on the Manage tab of the ribbon.

23.Click on the Make Components button in the Layout panel of the ribbon.

The Make Components : Selection dialog appears.

24.Select the internal fluid volume and the original components from the geometry window. These will be added to the dialog.

25.Click Next.

The Make Components : Bodies dialog appears.

26.Give the new assembly (and parts) a suitable name and click OK.

The new assembly will be opened automatically.

27.Save the new assembly.

The derived part is associative, meaning that if the original part/assembly is modified, the derived part can be updated to reflect this. The up-to-date derived part can then be exported to an assembly, as described above, where it can be used with STAR-CAT5.

The geometry is now ready for the CAD client analysis. Suppressed parts in an assembly will not be included in the analysis. In the above example, it is recommended that you extend the inlet and outlet regions to appropriate lengths so that a fully developed flow can be achieved before reaching the valve and to help reduce recirculation at the outlet.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 126

External Flow

The generation of a domain for external aerodynamics is generally easier than for internal flow cases but the sizing of the domain is more critical. As a guideline (assuming a specific situation is not being modelled i.e. flow in a wind tunnel) the domain should be sized as follows:

• Inlet: 2 x part length from the front of the part

• Outlet: 4 x part length from the rear of the part

• Sides: 3 x part width from the side of the part

• Ceiling: 4 x part height from the top of the part

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for an external flow are:

• Work in a part file. If the original geometry contains an assembly then create a new part and make it derived, loading the assembly into this part.

• Create an overall block that encloses all the other parts. Ensure that this block is a separate solid body in the part. The shape and size should correspond to the desired fluid domain.

• Subtract all parts from the overall block part - the remaining geometry is the fluid domain.

An example case is shown below. In this example a geometry of a car will be used.

1. Create a new part file and make this a derived part.

2. Load the assembly into the part file, using the default import options. The assembly parts will be merged into one solid body.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 127

3. If the geometry is symmetrical, as is the case with the car in this example, cut it in half to save on computational costs.

We will now create the fluid domain for the case.

4. Create a sketch on a suitable plane, in this example the symmetry plane of the car will do.

5. Draw the bounding box of the fluid domain using appropriate dimensions. In this case the sketch will represent the profile of the fluid domain, as shown below.

6. Extrude the sketch to the appropriate thickness for the domain.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 128

The Extrude dialog appears.

7. Click on the (New Body) button to create a new solid body from this extrusion--the default option would merge all solids together. Note that a new solid body is added to the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree.

8. Click on Combine in the Modify panel of the ribbon.

The Combine dialog appears.

9. Click on the (Cut) button, and select the domain as the Base, and the car as the Toolbody.

A dashed outline will appear when the mouse pointer hovers over hidden parts, as shown below; click on this to select the hidden body.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 129

The fluid domain is now complete. A close-up of the car in the fluid domain is shown below.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 130

The geometry is now ready for the cad client analysis. Deactivated parts are not included in the analysis.Suppressed parts are not included in the analysis. If you make any changes to the car geometry, these will automatically be passed on to the fluid region, giving you an up-to-date fluid domain.

Multi Region Flow

This section shows how to create the fluid domain for multiple regions such as rotating machinery and porous media flow.

For the numerical assumptions made using the Moving Reference Frame (MRF) technique to hold true, a minimum of two cells need to be present between the rotating-static interface and any wall boundaries (for example the fan blades), and the rotating region must be circular in section. Where there is a large clearance between the rotating object and any static objects, it is advisable to avoid placing the interface too close to either hence facilitating a small cell size on the interface. Where there is a small clearance between the rotating and static parts, there is little choice but to place the interface approximately midway between the two.

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for multiple regions are:

• Create a new derived part, importing the original geometry into this part. Ensure that all parts are maintained as separate solid bodies.

• Create a new body that encloses the rotating component, and subtract the rotating component from the solid. This is now the rotating region.

• Create additional bodies that will form the inlet and outlet regions, and subtract any obstructions/features that may be present. An example would be the support arms of the fan motor in a fan casing.

• Create a new assembly from the multi body derived part.

In this example, a fan and fan case are used.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 131

1. Create a new part file in Inventor. Name this new part Fluid Domain.

Make this part derived and import the assembly for which you want to create the fluid domain for.

2. Click on the Derive button in the Create panel of the ribbon.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 132

3. Locate and select the assembly or part file you want to create the fluid domain for.

4. In the Derived Assembly dialog, click on the (Maintain each body as a solid body) button.

This will keep the solids in the assembly as separate bodies. The default option is to merge all solids into one solid body.

Notice that two bodies were imported into the part file under the = > Solid Bodies node in the feature tree.

5. Rename the imported bodies to something more representative--in this example the two bodies were renamed to Casing and Fan respectively.

Hovering the mouse pointer over the body nodes highlights the corresponding body in the geometry window, this makes it easier to identify the bodies when renaming them.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 133

We will now create a solid body that will enclose the rotating component, this body will become the rotating region.

6. Hide the fan by right-clicking on its corresponding body sub-node in the Solid Bodies node and clear the checkbox next to Visibility.

To make a body visible again, right-click on it in the feature tree and tick the Visibility option.

7. Create a sketch on the circular face of the fan casing.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 134

By default Inventor automatically adds any edges that lie on the sketch plane to the current sketch--these appear in orange. Delete this edge.

8. Draw a circle that shares the same center point as the fan casing. The edge of the circle should coincide with the innermost edge of the fan casing.

To achieve this, select both the circle sketch and the innermost edge on the fan casing and click on the Equal button in the Constrain panel of the ribbon.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 135

The result of this operation is shown below--the circle will snap to the selected edge.

9. Hide the fan casing and show the fan again.

10.Extrude the sketch until it completely encloses the fan.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 136

The Extrude dialog appears.

11.Click on the (New Body) button to create a new solid body from this extrusion--the default option would merge all solids together.

12.Upon completing the operation, a new solid body will be added to the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree. Rename this body to Rotating Region.

We will now subtract the fan from the rotating region.

13.Click on Combine in the Modify panel of the ribbon.

The Combine dialog will appear.

14.Click on the (Cut) button, and select the rotating region as the Base, and the fan as the Toolbody.

A dashed outline appears when the mouse pointer hovers over hidden parts, as shown below; click on this to select the hidden body.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 137

15.In the Combine dialog, tick the Keep Toolbody checkbox to keep the toolbody.

If this is not selected, the toolbody will be consumed by this operation. Keeping the bodies is useful if you want to import these into Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for visualization purposes.

We will now create a new body that will extend upstream of the rotating region. This will be the inlet region.

16.Create a sketch on the front face of the rotating region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 138

By default Inventor automatically adds any edges that lie on the sketch plane to the current sketch; these appear in orange. Keep this sketch and exit the sketch. If this feature of Inventor was turned off, you can select the outermost edge on the body and click on the Project Geometry button on the Draw panel of the ribbon.

17.Extrude the sketch to a suitable length for the case.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 139

In the Extrude dialog, click on the (New Body) button to create a new solid body from this extrusion-- the default option would merge all solids together.

Note that a new solid body was added to the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree,> Rename this to Inlet Region.

We will now create a new body that will extend downstream of the rotating region. This will be the outlet region.

18.Create a sketch on the back face of the rotating region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 140

By default Inventor automatically adds any edges that lie on the sketch plane to the current sketch; these appear in orange. We only need the outer edge, so the inner edge can be deleted. If this option was turned off, you can manually project the outermost edge as previously described.

19.Extrude the sketch to a suitable length for the case.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 141

The Extrude dialog appears.

20.Click on the (New solid) button to create a new solid body from this extrusion--the default option would merge all solids together.

Note that a new solid body was added to the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree, rename this to Outlet Region.

In this example, the fan casing contains support arms that hold the base of the motor. We need to subtracted these from the outlet region.

21.Hide the rotating region and the inlet region, leaving only the outlet region visible.

22.Make the fan casing body visible.

23.Click on Combine in the Modify panel of the ribbon.

The Combine dialog appears.

24.Click on the (Cut) button, select the outlet region as the Base, and the fan casing as the Toolbody.

25.In the Combine dialog, tick the Keep Toolbody checkbox to keep the toolbody.

The toolbody will be hidden automatically after the operation completes.

26.Show the rotating region and the inlet region.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 142

The multi-region fluid domain is complete. A cross-section of the fluid domain is shown below (note that the fan and fan casing were set to visible for this screenshot), where the fan is shown in red, the fan casing is shown in white, and the multi-region fluid domain is shown in grey.

The last step is to export the bodies from this multi body part into an assembly, where they can be selected for use in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

27.Save the current part file using a suitable name.

28.Make the original assembly components visible by right-clicking on these in the Solid Bodies node in the feature tree and selecting Visibility.

29.Click on the Manage tab of the ribbon.

30.Click on the Make Components button in the Layout panel of the ribbon.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 143

The Make Components : Selection dialog appears.

31.Select the internal fluid volume and the original components from the geometry window.

These will be added to the dialog.

32.Click Next.

The Make Components : Bodies dialog appears.

33.Give the new assembly (and parts) a suitable name and click OK.

The new assembly will be opened automatically.

34.Save the new assembly.

The derived part is associative, meaning that if the original part/assembly is modified, the derived part can be updated to reflect this. The up-to-date derived part can then be exported to an assembly, as described above, where it can be used with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

The geometry is now ready for cad client analysis. Suppressed parts will not be included in the analysis. The three regions that form the fluid domain all have a conformal match, so it will be possible to create the interfaces and obtain a topologically valid mesh in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ without any further modifications to the geometry.

Imprinting Parts

Most CAD model assemblies are not suitable for meshing as the parts in the assembly are disjointed, where the coincident faces are overlapping. Attempting to generate a mesh with such an assembly will result in a meshing error. To rectify this problem, the parts in an assembly must be imprinted together.

Imprinting can also be used to split surfaces for boundary region applications. An example of such an application would be to model the area that a fan would occupy on the inside of computer case, such as in the third Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor tutorial, where a smaller section of the surface is needed to represent the fan, rather than the entire inner surface of the computer case.

Contents:

Imprinting Parts in an Assembly

Imprinting Surfaces on Parts for Boundary Region Applications

Imprinting Parts in an Assembly

In cases containing multiple adjacent parts, such as in Conjugate Heat Transfer cases, it is essential to imprint the profiles of the coincident faces of the smaller parts onto the face of the larger part. This will ensure that the volume mesh created by Simcenter STAR-CCM+ contains interfaces between the adjacent parts.

In general, the steps to follow in creating the fluid domain for multiple regions are:

• Work within the assembly, making the part that requires imprinting the work part.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 144

• Create a sketch on the face you want to imprint, and project the contact edges of the other components in the assembly onto this sketch.

• Split the face you want to imprint using the sketch created in the previous step.

The simple circuit board shown below requires imprinting before the mesh can be generated.

In this example, the capacitors and heat sinks are not imprinted to the circuit board. This would result in a failure when attempting to generate a mesh.

To imprint the capacitors and heat sinks onto the circuit board follow the steps outlined below:

1. Load the assembly into Inventor.

2. Double-click on the node of the part that you want to imprint.

This will make it the active part; all other parts in the assembly will become transparent.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 145

3. Create a sketch on the face that requires imprinting.

We will now project the intersecting edges of the other components onto the active sketch.

4. Click on the Project Cut Edges button in the Draw panel of the ribbon.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 146

5. Hover the mouse pointer over one of the transparent parts, this will become highlighted in white--click to select it.

The contact edges of the part are added to the sketch; these appear colored in blue.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 147

6. Exit the sketch when done.

We will imprint the face with the sketch containing the contact edges of the other components.

7. Click on the Split button in the Modify panel of the ribbon.

The Split dialog appears.

8. Select the sketch containing the contact edges to act as the Split Tool.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 148

Note that the sketch containing the profile will be consumed by this operation.

9. Select the face you want to imprint using the Faces to be Split tool.

10.Repeat the above steps (obtaining the profiles and splitting the face) for all the other components in the assembly.

11.Return to the assembly by double-clicking on the root node in the feature tree.

To verify that the face was correctly imprinted, we can hide the other parts by right-clicking on the imprinted part and selecting Isolate.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 149

A high quality mesh with fully defined interfaces can now be successfully generated for this assembly. Suppressed parts are not included in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ analysis, so for CHT cases, such as the above example, ensure that all relevant parts are active.

Imprinting Surfaces on Parts for Boundary Region Applications

Faces in a part body can be split into smaller faces for boundary application.

The general procedure to follow is:

• Create a sketch on the surface you want to split. The shape of the sketch should correspond to the shape of the new face after it is split.

• Split the face that requires imprinting with the sketch containing the profiles.

A simple example of an aeration tank is shown below. The image shows the tank, the two air injectors need to be imprinted onto the base of the tank.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 150

1. Load the part into Inventor.

2. Create a sketch on the face that requires imprinting.

By default Inventor will automatically project edges that lie on the sketch plane--these will appear in orange. Delete these sketch entities.

3. Draw the profile of the faces you want to imprint.

In this example, the air injector profiles are circular in shape.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 151

4. Click on the Split button in the Modify panel of the ribbon.

The Split dialog appears.

5. Select one of the profiles you created in the previous step to act as the Split Tool.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 152

Note that the sketch containing the profile will be consumed by this operation.

6. Select the face you want to imprint using the Faces to be Split tool.

7. Repeat the above steps (creating the profiles and completing the split) for all the new boundaries you want to add.

The face is now imprinted; each face can be selected independently of each other, and can be used when defining boundaries.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 153

The separate faces can now be defined as boundary regions.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 154

Selecting Fluid Physics Models

The first step in setting up this tutorial is to modify the physics continuum that is used to model air. For this case, the flow is turbulent and thermal. Temperature calculations are on by default in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

3. Set the Equation of State to Ideal Gas.

4. Click the Initialization tab.

5. Set (Temperature) to 400 K.

6. Click OK to close the dialog.

Adding Solid Physics Models

The next step in setting up this tutorial is to define the physics continuum of the solid to be used.

3. Set Material to Solid and select Aluminum Alloy from the list.

5. Set (Temperature) to 400 K.

6. Click OK.

Rotating Flow Inside a Graphics Card

This tutorial takes you through the steps that are required to run a CFD calculation in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor environment.

For this tutorial, the model is a fully sealed graphics card that is located inside an empty, idealized PC tower case. The geometry that is used in this tutorial has been simplified in order to decrease the computational cost. As a consequence the mesh is relatively coarse at approximately 200,000 cells compared to the 3-4 million cells used for an industrial analysis.

To download the tutorials bundle, go to https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/product/226870983/downloads, and follow the procedure outlined in the main STAR-CCM+ > Tutorials > Using Tutorial Macros and Files > Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal section of the user guide.

1. Copy the directory to your own disk space and open the part file gpuAssem.iam in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

The assembly is made up of two parts: the PC tower case (including the GPU housing), and the rotating region that encloses the blower fan of the GPU.

Selecting Fluid Physics Models

The first step in setting up this tutorial is to define the physics of the problem. For this case, the flow is turbulent and isothermal. Temperature calculations are on by default in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor.

To turn temperature calculations off:

1. Right-click the Continua > Continuum node in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor tree and select Edit.

The Continuum Settings dialog appears.

2. Deactivate the Temperature option in the Optional Physics Models box.

3. Click OK.

Geometry Transfer: CAD to Simulation

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor allows you to transfer geometry from Inventor to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ through a direct link between the two packages.

This feature provides you with a workflow that is tailored to design optimization. You can apply changes to the geometry in either Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor or Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and the changes are passed back to the other program. For example, you can make changes to the design after running an analysis in the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ environment and these changes are passed back to the original Inventor file. This feature requires a CAD client license.

This tutorial demonstrates how to select the CAD parameters in your original geometry and transfer the geometry from Inventor to Simcenter STAR-CCM+. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you proceed to create a repeatable workflow (or pipeline) using mesh operations. After setting up this pipeline, you can make further changes to the geometry design and have STAR-CCM+ regenerate the corresponding volume mesh.

Contents:

Opening the CAD Model

Transferring the Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

Creating the Shape Parts and Operations

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Modifying the Design

To download the tutorials bundle, go to https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/product/226870983/downloads, and follow the procedure outlined in the main STAR-CCM+ > Tutorials > Using Tutorial Macros and Files > Downloading the Tutorial Files from the Support Center Portal section of the user guide.

1. Copy the directory to your own disk space.

2. Launch Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and open the assembly file cardAssem.iam.
