The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon appears at the top of the screen. The Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor object tree is located on the left of the screen.

To switch to the object tree:

3. Click Model and select STAR-Inventor.

If these items are not visible, refer to Launching Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor Manually.

Transferring the Geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+

In Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor, choose the CAD parameters to expose to Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and then transfer the geometry.

Specify the CAD parameters to transfer to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Design Data.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 277

The Design Data dialog appears.

2. In the CAD Parameters tab, select blowerFan.ipt\d15.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor only recognizes native CAD features as CAD parameters.

The value of this parameter is displayed in the Parameter Value property.

3. Activate the Transfer to STAR-CCM+ option.

4. Click OK.

Transfer the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

5. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Transfer Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and the CAD geometry is transferred over.

6. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, create a geometry scene and position the geometry as shown below.

7. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, expand the Geometry node.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 278

The transferred geometry appears under the Parts node. The properties that control the connection back to Inventor, including the CAD parameter value, appear under the CAD Client Models node.

When transferring geometry from Inventor to Simcenter STAR-CCM+, a link exists between the two software packages. This link allows data to be transferred between the two packages. To maintain this link, you must first save the geometry file in Inventor:

8. Switch to Inventor and save the geometry file.

In response, Simcenter STAR-CCM+ saves the simulation file with the name of the Inventor geometry file. Using this technique, you can rename or relocate both the geometry and simulation files without breaking the link between the two packages. You can also save the simulation file in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ so long as you do not rename it or relocate it. Doing so will break the link between the packages.

Creating the Shape Parts and Operations

The transferred geometry consists of the card housing and the blower fan. To simulate this case, you require two regions: one static region that provides an enclosure for the simulation, and another for the rotating region around the fan.

The transferred geometry contains the solid parts. You require the fluid volume around these parts. The first stage in obtaining the fluid volume is to create part shapes that correspond to the two regions. To save time, you are provided with these part shapes, one for the enclosure, and another for the rotating region.

Import the shape parts:

1. Select File  > Import > Import Surface Mesh.

2. Import the part shapes:

a) In the Open dialog, navigate to the directory that you downloaded in the first section of this tutorial and select box.x_t and disc.x_t.

b) Click Open.

c) In the Import Surface Options dialog, deactivate the Open Geometry Scene After Import option.

d) Click OK.

The static region, box, is shown below in relation to the graphics card:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 279

The rotating region, disc, is show below in relation to the graphics card:

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 280

Now subtract the solid CAD geometry from these shape parts to obtain the final fluid volume. Begin by subtracting the blower fan geometry from the disc part:

3. Right-click the Operations node and select New > Boolean > Subtract.

4. In the Create Subtract Operation dialog, set the following properties:

Property Setting

Input Parts disc

cardAssem.iam > blowerFan:1

Target Parts disc

5. Click OK.

6. Rename the Operations > Subtract node to Fan Subtraction.

7. Rename Parts > Subtract node to Rotating Region.

Subtract the card housing geometry and the disc part from the static region:

8. Create another subtract operation with the following settings:

Property Setting

Input Parts box

disc

cardAssem.iam > cardCase:1

Target Parts box

9. Rename Operations > Subtract node to Card Subtraction.

10.Rename Parts > Subtract node to Static Region.

To get a conformal mesh between the two regions, imprint both fluid volumes together:

11.Right-click the Operations node and select New > Boolean > Imprint.

12.In the Create Imprint Operation dialog, select Rotating Region and Static Region and click OK.

The transferred geometry contains CAD data. To ensure best results, instruct all operations to use the CAD data where available:

13.Under the Operations node, multi-select the Fan Subtraction and Card Subtraction nodes and activate the Perform CAD Boolean option.

14.Select the Operations > Imprint node and set Merge/Imprint Method to CAD Imprint.

The contacts between the two parts are created. These contacts are used while creating the regions to define the interfaces between the regions.

Execute all operations:

15.Right-click on the Operations node and select Execute All.

Setting Up the Mesh Pipeline

Assign the parts to regions and create the automated mesh operation.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 281

Assign the fluid parts to regions:

1. Expand the Geometry > Parts node and multi-select the Rotating Region and Static Region nodes.

2. Right-click on one of the selected parts and choose Assign Parts to Regions....

3. In the Assign Parts to Regions dialog:

a) Select Create a Region for Each Part.

b) Select Create a Boundary for Each Part Surface.

c) Click Apply and Close.

Create the automated mesh operation:

4. Right-click the Operations node and select New > Mesh > Automated Mesh.

5. In the Create Automated Mesh Operation dialog:

a) From the Parts list, select Rotating Region and Static Region.

b) Select the following meshers, in order:

Group Mesher

Surface Meshers Surface Remesher

Core Volume Meshers Polyhedral Mesher

Optional Boundary Layer Meshers Prism Layer Mesher

c) Click OK.

An automated mesh operation is added to the Operations node. Refine the mesh settings for this case:

6. Expand the Automated Mesh > Default Controls node.

7. Select the Base Size node and set Value to 16 mm.

8. Select the Prism Layer Total Thickness node and set Percentage of Base to 20.

Generate the volume mesh:

9. Click (Generate Volume Mesh).

10.When the volume mesh is generated, create a mesh scene that displays the following parts:

◦ Rotating Region > Boundaries > cardAssem.iam.blowerFan:1.<all_faces>

◦ Static Region > Boundaries > cardAssem.iam.cardCase:1.<all_faces>

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 282

You can exit Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and Inventor and maintain the link between the two packages. To demonstrate, in the following steps you save the simulation and exit both applications. In the next section, you will resume the simulation and continue where you left off.

11.Save the simulation.

12.Exit Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

13.Exit Inventor

Modifying the Design

Modify the number of blades on the blower fan using the CAD parameter.

In this tutorial, you modify the number of blades on the graphics card blower fan from 10 to 15 blades.

To re-establish the link between Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+, you must load the geometry in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor first and transfer the geometry to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

Resume the analysis and re-establish the link between Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and Simcenter STAR-CCM+:

1. Launch Inventor with Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor and load cardAssem.iam.

2. From the Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor ribbon, click Transfer Geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 283

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ launches and the CAD geometry is transferred over.

3. Switch to Simcenter STAR-CCM+.

4. Open the geometry scene to visualize the initial geometry representation.

5. Expand the Geometry > CAD Client Models > cardAssem.iam > CAD Parameters node.

6. Select the blowerFan.ipt\d15 node and set Parameter Value to 15.

A yellow warning icon appears on the CAD parameter node as well as the assembly node. This icon indicates that the CAD Client Model is out of date.

To update the model:

7. Right-click the cardAssem.iam node and select Update Model.

The geometry updates in the scene. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ passes the change in the design back to Inventor.

8. Switch back to Inventor and view the updated geometry.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 284

The pipeline you set up is fully repeatable. To update the volume mesh:

9. In Simcenter STAR-CCM+, open the mesh scene.

10.Click (Generate Volume Mesh).

The volume mesh updates to reflect the changes in the design.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+ Client for Inventor 2020.3  |  User Guide

Siemens Digital Industries Software 285

All boundaries and boundary conditions that you set are maintained after this change. This feature reduces the amount of work that is required when analyzing multiple designs.
